In the beginning, those scoundrels had relied on those children to plead for mercy from the town mayor of that era. Out of momentary softness, the former mayor tacitly allowed them to live there.

As a result... they festered into a malignant tumor. If a real war broke out now, their town would have to pay a heavy price.

Whenever Wolf Four mentioned this Chaotic Zone, it filled him with itching hatred.

Shang Feifan was all too familiar with this kind of situation; countless parallel scenarios existed in the real world.

"They don't dare to offend the town and nearby villages too severely, and they wouldn't dare pull off anything too outrageous—at the very least, they wouldn't dare rush out to engage in wholesale pillaging. Although Moyue Valley is dangerous, it's also a place rich in resources. These people survive by venturing into the valley, exploring the surrounding mountains and wilderness for materials, and trading those finds with nearby folks for food and survival supplies," Hu Bushuai's attitude was far more neutral.

"However, due to poor management inside, it is indeed terribly chaotic. Once we go in, if anyone tries to strike up a conversation with you, it's best to ignore them," Hu Bushuai warned.

Following closely behind the two, Shang Feifan passed through the wide-open bone gate. The moment he stepped inside, he felt an atmosphere and environment drastically different from Moyue Town.

First was the air quality.

It was utterly bizarre. Outside the gate, when he looked up, he could still see a blue sky, but upon entering this place, the sky above was a dreary, ash-gray.

The sky formed a distinct dividing line right at the bone gate’s wall—one side gloomy, the other clear.

The air here smelled faintly of foul sewage and dry earth.

Second were the houses and roads.

The buildings here were haphazardly constructed without any urban planning. Although most were made of stone, they weren't neat, orderly bricks; instead, they were piled together from rubble and mud, looking dangerously like condemned buildings. There were also makeshift shanties built from animal pelts and skeletal frames.

No sewage systems were visible along the roads, and residents casually dumped their household garbage and excrement right onto the pathways.

There were no straight roads, only winding alleys weaving through the shanties. Every single path was made of dirt.

And finally, the people.

Flies and mosquitoes buzzed around the garbage and the beastmen. Young, ignorant beastmen were still running and chasing each other in the streets, but whether in human-like form or beast form, every single one of them was filthy, as if no one had given them a bath or washed their clothes in ages.

There were unclothed infant beastmen and drunkards collapsed by the roadside...

chunks.chapterTitle: 第10章 信中的莫约山谷 (Part 2)
chunks.chineseText:
感觉信中提到的莫约山谷更像是这里，而不是莫约镇。不过信中似乎也确实没有提到镇子这样的词。

商非凡想着他是不是跑错地方，其实应该到这里来等待和寻找拉斐尔？

这里的兽人们看到三人进来，有人赶紧把家里好东西拿出来放到门口，期待三人能看中什么。

有人冷漠。有人直接对三人吐唾沫，满脸妒忌和仇恨。还有人站在家门口和路边上搔首弄姿……

虎不帅暗中观察诺曼霍希尔的神情，发现他像是看多了这种环境一样，脸上没有任何波动，眼中也没有厌恶和鄙视。

绝大多数大城市里来的兽人都会下意识排斥和厌恶这种棚户区。

这是无法避免的，任何一个习惯了干净整洁有秩序生活环境的人，乍然来到这样肮脏混乱的地方，谁都会有不适感。

除非这个虎兽人经常出入类似的地方。

虎不帅垂下眼睑。

狼四领头，把速度压得很慢，只比正常行人慢跑的速度稍微快一点。

“这里的人不太友好，这里的道路也不好，我们的巨虫身体巨大，如果从他们的屋顶和墙上奔跑，很容易压塌他们的房屋，他们就会有理由攻击我们。巨虫一旦遭受攻击，也会反击，到时候很可能变成混战。”

虎不帅像是特意和商非凡解释说。

商非凡随口问：“那我们为什么非要从这里穿行？从外面走不行吗？”

虎不帅：“你说你从黑森林城来这里是要办一点事，而我刚好知道黑森林城遇到了一连串诡异的怪案，经过初步调查，有人怀疑这些案件的背后有一个组织操纵。当时黑森林城的管理者对疑似这个组织的人进行大肆抓捕，但不少人逃出了黑森林城。之后黑森林城就派出了一些特别调查员去追捕逃跑的兽人和调查该组织在其他地方的情况。”

商非凡拉着缰绳，转头看虎不帅：“你以为我是特别调查员，就是为了追捕逃跑兽人才来到这里？”

虎不帅：“黑森林城的某些上层人士似乎认定那个组织的人和各地混乱区有关。正好王都也有意要大力收拾各地混乱区。”

原来这样的混乱区并不是特例。

商非凡低笑：“王都想要收拢王权？收拾混乱区只是借口，他们想要借着收拾混乱区进而把混乱区附近的大小地方政权给收拾掉才是真的？而我们都知道，很多混乱区都是地方政权放纵才会出现。”

虎不帅看着他：“所以你是吗？”

商非凡：“如果我是，我就不会想要留在这里开个修理铺。”

“有人会做长线调查和长期埋伏。”

“你担心我对莫约镇……对你姨父一家不利？”

虎不帅直接道：“我会盯着你。”

商非凡哈哈大笑：“好啊，欢迎。”

三人顺利穿行过混乱区，从混乱区最后面与山谷相接的羊肠小道进入真正的莫约山谷。

羊肠小道有一道小得多的骨头大门，终日关闭。

狼四掏出钱币扔给看守者。

看守者这才打开大门。

虎不帅看商非凡踏上羊肠小道却没有任何动作，掏出一条布巾递给他。

商非凡接过布巾，眼中打出一个问号。

狼四这时也拉住巨虫，掏出一条布巾系在脸上。

“山谷里的空气有毒。混乱区的空气就是受到山谷空气影响。”虎不帅简单解释。

商非凡学着两人把布巾系到口鼻处，闻到了浓郁的药草味。

随着逐渐深入山谷，商非凡发现这里的天空越来越灰暗，走了没一会儿，三人身上和巨虫身上都落了一层薄薄的黑灰。

商非凡看到山谷中和山上似乎有很多像是被大火焚烧后的黑色枯木。

那些黑灰好像就是从那些枯木上飘出来的。

地面柔软，黑灰像雪层一样堆积得极厚。

巨虫的长脚落进去，一插就是一个洞。

狼四做了个手势，停在路边等两人。

“不腐尸还在更里面。从这里开始，小心周围一切，这里有很多外面没有的怪物，但在白天，只要你不惊扰它们，它们也不会主动攻击你。跟紧我的脚步，不要特意操控你的巨虫，它不止一次来过这里，知道这里哪条路安全，如果你和我们走散，就让巨虫带着你走。”

狼四特意叮嘱的是商非凡。

虎不帅对这里显然也不陌生。

商非凡点头。

狼四这才重新领头出发。

虎不帅让商非凡走中间。

商非凡接受了这份好意。

刚拐过一个弯，商非凡脸上陡然露出不可置信的神情。

那是什么？！

作者有话说：

商非凡：被保护和被监视了，果然虎不帅帮我是有目的的，而不是看我长得帅……
chunks.englishText:
It felt as though the Moyue Valley mentioned in the letter closely resembled this place rather than Moyue Town. Yet, the letter didn't seem to mention any word like "town," either.

Shang Feifan wondered if he had come to the wrong place—should he have actually come here to wait for and search for Raphael?

Seeing the three of them enter, some beastmen here hurriedly brought out their best belongings and placed them right at their doorways, hoping the trio might take a fancy to something.

Others remained indifferent. Some even spat directly at the three of them, their faces twisted with envy and hatred. Others still stood at their doorsteps and along the roadside, striking seductive poses...

Hu Bushuai secretly observed Norman Horsiel's expression and discovered that he acted as though he were accustomed to such an environment; his face showed not a single ripple of fluctuation, and his eyes held neither disgust nor contempt.

The vast majority of beastmen hailing from major cities would instinctively reject and loathe this kind of slum.

This was unavoidable. Anyone accustomed to a clean, tidy, and orderly living environment would inevitably feel a sense of discomfort upon suddenly arriving in such a filthy, chaotic place.

Unless this tiger beastman frequented similar places on a regular basis.

Hu Bushuai lowered his eyelids.

Taking the lead, Wolf Four kept their pace very slow, just slightly faster than a normal pedestrian's jog.

"The people here aren't very friendly, and the roads here are terrible. Our giant bugs have massive bodies; if they were to run across these people's rooftops and walls, they could easily collapse their houses, giving them a pretext to attack us. Once a giant bug is attacked, it will retaliate, and by then, it could easily spiral into a chaotic brawl."

Hu Bushuai spoke as if he were specifically explaining this to Shang Feifan.

Shang Feifan asked casually, "Then why must we ride through here? Can't we just walk around the outside?"

Hu Bushuai answered, "You said you came here from Black Forest City to take care of some business, and I happen to know that Black Forest City has experienced a string of bizarre, mysterious cases. Preliminary investigations suggest that someone suspects an organization is pulling the strings behind these incidents. At the time, the administrators of Black Forest City launched a massive crackdown on suspected members of this organization, but quite a few people managed to flee Black Forest City. Afterward, Black Forest City dispatched several special investigators to track down the escaped beastmen and investigate the organization's activities elsewhere."

Reining in his mount, Shang Feifan turned his head to look at Hu Bushuai. "Do you take me for a special investigator who came here precisely to hunt down escaped beastmen?"

Hu Bushuai replied, "Certain upper-echelons in Black Forest City seem convinced that members of that organization are connected to the Chaotic Zones across various regions. Just in time, the Royal Capital also intends to heavily clean up these Chaotic Zones everywhere."

So, Chaotic Zones like this weren't isolated exceptions.

Shang Feifan let out a low chuckle. "The Royal Capital wants to consolidate royal authority? Cleaning up the Chaotic Zones is merely an excuse; their true goal is to use the clean-up as leverage to dismantle the local and regional regimes surrounding these zones, isn't it? And as we all know, many Chaotic Zones only exist because local authorities turned a blind eye."

Hu Bushuai looked right at him. "So, are you one of them?"

Shang Feifan replied, "If I were, I wouldn't be trying to stay here and open a repair shop."

"Some people engage in long-term investigations and deep undercover operations."

"Are you worried that I might pose a threat to Moyue Town... or to your uncle's family?"

Hu Bushuai stated bluntly, "I will keep my eyes on you."

Shang Feifan laughed heartily. "Wonderful, you're welcome to try."

The three of them successfully traversed the Chaotic Zone, passing through the narrow, twisting footpath at the very rear where the zone met the valley, officially entering the true Moyue Valley.

That narrow footpath was guarded by a much smaller bone gate, which remained locked day and night.

Wolf Four fished out some coins and tossed them to the guard.

Only then did the guard open the gate.

Seeing Shang Feifan step onto the footpath without making any moves, Hu Bushuai pulled out a piece of cloth and handed it to him.

Shang Feifan accepted the cloth, a silent question mark hanging in his eyes.

At the same time, Wolf Four reined in his giant bug and tied a piece of cloth around his face.

"The air in the valley is poisonous. The air in the Chaotic Zone is affected by the valley's air," Hu Bushuai explained briefly.

Mimicking the two of them, Shang Feifan tied the cloth over his mouth and nose, instantly catching a rich, pungent scent of medicinal herbs.

As they penetrated deeper into the valley, Shang Feifan noticed that the sky above grew increasingly dim and gloomy. After walking for just a short while, a thin layer of black ash had settled over their bodies and their giant bugs.

Shang Feifan spotted what looked like numerous black, withered trees scattered across the valley floor and mountainsides, as if they had been scorched by a massive wildfire.

That black ash seemed to be drifting down from those charred trees.

The ground was soft, with the black ash piled up as thickly as a layer of snow.

When the giant bugs' long legs stepped down, every single stride punched out a deep hole.

Making a hand gesture, Wolf Four halted by the roadside to wait for the other two.

"The uncorrupted corpses are further inside. From this point on, be careful of everything around you. There are many monsters here that don't exist outside, but during the day, as long as you don't provoke them, they won't actively attack you. Stay close to my footsteps, and don't try to deliberately steer your giant bug; it has been here more than once and knows which paths are safe. If you get separated from us, let the giant bug lead you."

Wolf Four directed this warning specifically at Shang Feifan.

Hu Bushuai, for his part, was clearly no stranger to this place either.

Shang Feifan nodded.

Only then did Wolf Four resume his lead, setting off once more.

Hu Bushuai arranged for Shang Feifan to ride in the middle.

Shang Feifan readily accepted this goodwill gesture.

Just as they rounded a bend, an expression of sheer disbelief abruptly surfaced on Shang Feifan's face.

What on earth is that?!

Author's Note:

Shang Feifan: Protected and monitored simultaneously. Sure enough, Hu Bushuai helped me with an ulterior motive, not because of how handsome I am...

chunks.chineseText:
第11章 游戏初死

他看到了一面巨大无比的镜子，就这么嵌入山体中，山有多高，这面镜子就有多高。

镜子中，他看到自己被包裹在一个满是粘液的半透明茧子中，他的头脸露了出来。

兽人世界的他，他自己判断与他现实世界的真实容颜相像程度达到七成。

该游戏不能捏脸，人形取模用的就是现实世界的面孔，经过游戏世界自动调整。

他的头发和眼睛瞳孔的颜色变了，发色就像挑染一样，黑色和金色掺杂在一起，眼睛瞳孔颜色则特别的黑，如果情绪激动就会转为金色，到了晚上不知道是不是会变成绿色？

嘴唇比现实中的要稍微厚一些，人形的他还把略长的头发扎了个小揪揪，

虽然调整的不多，但只见过他几面，不是非常熟悉他的人绝对无法在游戏中认出他，顶多觉得有点眼熟。

何况他还多了兽耳和兽尾，身高也从一米八七增加到了两米出头，肌肉层也厚了很多。

商非凡敢打赌，就是让伏向军来看这个兽人，也不会一眼认出这就是他。

但自己认出自己的脸还是没问题的。

他因为工作缘故，经常需要修改自己的容颜五官，对自己的五官异常熟悉。

镜子中那个被包裹在茧子中的人就是他！

但那是什么一个情况？

为什么有一根细长的管子插入镜子中的他的脑子里，像是正在吸食他的脑浆？

“诺曼先生？”

“诺曼霍希尔，你怎么了？你看到了什么？”

“他好像是看到了什么幻像。”

“瞳孔扩散……坏了，他没有呼吸了！是诅咒！”

“诺曼！诺曼……”

耳边，虎不帅的声音越来越遥远。

莫约山谷的一切变得模糊、虚幻、不再真实。

又出了游戏bug吗？

不是。

刚刚游戏系统在他脑子里宣布——

他死了。

被诅咒而死。

商非凡……对着空气默默竖起中指。

“这可是游戏！玩家出现负面状态都没有一个提醒吗？”

他骑上巨虫前还查看过自己的生命值和精力值，都近乎满值。

结果就这么一会儿，他就莫名其妙死了。

哦，也算不上莫名其妙，他是被诅咒死的。

但他以为在迪莉娅夫人没有特别说明的情况下，他的诅咒应该不会那么快发作。

或者是诅咒者知道他去找了迪莉娅夫人，特意又对他加重了诅咒？

商非凡从来没有死得这么郁闷过。

好吧，他是第一次死亡。

大概是全息游戏的缘故，虽然这次死亡没有见血、没有任何痛苦，但这种徘徊在死地的感觉太糟糕了，就跟他真的死掉了一样。

这里就是游戏的死后空间？

怎么没有听玩家说过？

他记得伏向军好像跟他提过，玩家在游戏里死亡就是眼前一黑，然后就直接掉线。接着就要等七十二小时的死亡惩罚，七十二小时后才能再次上线。

因为死亡惩罚比较严重，玩家们都不敢像在其他游戏中一样随便浪费自己的生命。

别的游戏有这么长的死亡惩罚时间，玩家早就跑光了，但这可是第一个也是全球唯一一个百分百真实体感的全息游戏，还不是单机，而是多玩家待在同一个服务器里。死亡惩罚那就真的是惩罚，玩游戏上头的玩家们没有谁愿意那么长时间不接触游戏。

可他现在为什么没有掉线？

这里是哪里？

这里不是莫约山谷，是一个巨大的黑色空间，他现在就像是悬浮在半空中，但能走能坐能动。

难道被诅咒死亡就会有这样的特殊场景出现？

对了，他死之前看到的是什么？

现在他依然能看到同样的景象，那面巨大的镜子就漂浮在他前方！

这说明这副景象并不是他在莫约山谷中看到，而就是只有死亡或即将死亡时才能看到的特有幻象。

镜子中的那个他依旧被吸食着脑浆。

不管这是真是假，都太糟糕了。

“醒过来兄弟！”

“睁开你的眼睛！”

“有东西在吸食你的大脑！赶紧醒过来摆脱它！”

镜子中的他眼皮急速抖动，似乎就要睁开眼睛。

商非凡握紧拳头：“抗争！抗争！”

啪！镜子中的他真的睁开了眼睛。

就在这时，一股庞大的力道突然把鼓劲的他拉扯了过去。

这次商非凡明显感觉到什么叫“眼前一黑”。

但很快，也许连一秒钟也没有，他就再次看到了光线。

……这又是什么见鬼的地方？

他好像和镜子中的那个他合二为一了。

商非凡用力挣扎，先挣出被茧子裹紧的双手，用力撕裂茧皮，又用手去摸自己的头顶，摸到了一根滑溜溜的触手，又像是软管。

商非凡反手抓住触手用力往外拔。

他感觉不到任何痛苦，但他能感觉到有什么东西正在脱离他的大脑。

啪！

触手完全被拔了出来。

商非凡手指在头顶摸来摸去，没有摸到任何伤口。

太古怪了！

但他现在的体感非常真实。

商非凡没有急着下线，而是先撕开茧子，把自己从茧子中解放出来。

周围的光线有点黑暗，他和茧子好像位于一个池子中。

池子里有透明粘液。

商非凡走到池子边沿，发现这个池子并不算深，只到他腰间。

单手按住池边轻轻一跳，他就从池子里跳了出来。

粘液从他身上往下滴落。

周围隐约可见很多个小池子，但这时那些池子都空着。

再转头，他刚刚拔出来的触手已经消失无踪，就连他撕开的茧子也消失了，不知道是不是化作了池中粘液。

商非凡低头看自己，就见身上穿着一套玩家固定的初生装：一件背心和一条及膝短裤。

他的背心口袋里还放着什么东西。

商非凡抽出来一看，是一本B5皮质笔记本。

翻开笔记本首页，一阵微微光芒闪过。

一行字出现在笔记本的第一页纸上。

【欢迎玩家‘你皇退休了’进入天河星兽人大陆，下面是游戏引导，请仔细观看……】

商非凡：这不是传说中游戏的正确打开方式吗？

等他耐心看完笔记本上浮现的动图指引，主要是介绍游戏规则和一些注意事项。

笔记本自动翻到第二页。

这一页是目录页，上面罗列了七个大类：游戏规则、个人数据、任务、地图、技能、经验值、存档。

目录页最下方还有一排跳动的年月日时分秒显示，每一秒跳动一下。

根据时间来看，他才“刚刚出生”不到十分钟。

任务项发出光亮。

商非凡轻轻点击了一下。

笔记本又自动往后翻，翻到任务页面。

空白的页面上浮现了第一个任务。

【任务一！请玩家‘你皇退休了’离开神殿出生池，前往神殿外面探索新世界。完成后奖励5铜达铢，请到玩家自建营地天残谷一号营地杂货铺领取。】

不太明亮的神殿中浮现出带着光芒的箭头。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 11: First Death in the Game

He saw a mirror of gargantuan proportions embedded right into the mountain face; as tall as the mountain itself, so stood the mirror.

Within the mirror's reflection, he saw himself encased within a translucent cocoon filled with viscous slime, with only his head and face exposed.

His appearance in the beastman world, by his own estimation, bore a seventy-percent resemblance to his true face in the real world.

The game did not allow for face-sculpting; the humanoid avatar model was taken directly from his real-world face, subjected to automatic adjustments by the game world.

The color of his hair and pupils had changed; his hair featured highlights woven together like alternating streaks of black and gold, while his pupils were an exceptionally deep black that would shift to gold whenever he experienced intense emotions—wondering if they might turn green come nighttime?

His lips were slightly thicker than those in reality, and his humanoid form also sported his slightly lengthened hair tied up into a small ponytail.

Though the adjustments were minor, anyone who had only met him a few times and wasn't intimately familiar with him would utterly fail to recognize him in the game, at most feeling a vague sense of familiarity.

Furthermore, he now possessed beast ears and a beast tail, his height had surged from one meter eighty-two to just over two meters, and his muscle mass had thickened considerably.

Shang Feifan would bet all he had that even if Fu Xiangjun were brought here to look at this beastman, he would never instantly recognize that this was him.

Yet, recognizing his own face presented no problem whatsoever.

Due to the nature of his work, he frequently needed to alter his facial features and appearance, making him abnormally familiar with his own visage.

That person wrapped inside the cocoon within the mirror was undoubtedly him!

But what kind of bizarre situation was this?

Why was a slender tube inserted straight into the brain of his reflection in the mirror, as if it were actively sucking out his brain matter?

"Mr. Norman?"

"Norman Horsiel, what's wrong with you? What did you see?"

"It looks like he's seeing some kind of hallucination."

"Pupils dilated... Oh no, he's stopped breathing! It's a curse!"

"Norman! Norman..."

By his ears, Hu Bushuai's voice grew increasingly distant.

Everything in Moyue Valley grew blurred, illusory, and devoid of reality.

Had another game bug struck?

No.

Just a moment ago, the game system had announced inside his head—

He was dead.

Killed by a curse.

Shang Feifan... silently raised his middle finger toward the empty air.

"This is supposed to be a game! Is there really not even a single warning when a player contracts a negative status effect?"

Right before mounting the giant bug, he had checked his health and stamina bars; both had been nearly full.

And yet, just like that, he had died for no apparent reason.

Well, it wasn't entirely without reason; he had been killed by a curse.

However, he had assumed that since Lady Delia hadn't explicitly stated otherwise, his curse shouldn't have flared up so quickly.

Or perhaps the caster of the curse knew he had gone to see Lady Delia and deliberately intensified the curse upon him?

Shang Feifan had never died a death so frustratingly vexing.

Fine, this was his first time dying anyway.

Likely due to the nature of a full-dive holographic game, although this death lacked bloodshed and physical pain, the lingering sensation of hovering in death's domain felt utterly wretched—it felt every bit as real as actual death.

Was this the game's afterlife space?

Why had he never heard any other players mention it?

He recalled Fu Xiangjun mentioning that when a player died in the game, their vision would simply go black, followed by an immediate disconnection. After that, they would have to endure a seventy-two-hour death penalty, remaining unable to log back in until those seventy-two hours had elapsed.

Because the death penalty was relatively severe, players dared not waste their lives carelessly as they might in other games.

In any other game with such a punishingly long death penalty, players would have long since abandoned it. But this was the first and globally unique one-hundred-percent realistic sensory holographic game—and it wasn't a single-player title either, but a massive multiplayer server shared by countless individuals. The death penalty here was genuinely a punishment, and none of the game-addicted players were willing to stay away from the game for that long.

So why hadn't he been disconnected right now?

Where on earth was this?

This wasn't Moyue Valley; it was a massive, pitch-black space. He felt as though he were suspended mid-air, yet he could walk, sit, and move around freely.

Did dying from a curse trigger such a special scenario?

Right, what had he seen right before he died?

He could still see that exact same imagery right now—that gigantic mirror was floating directly in front of him!

This proved that this vision hadn't been something he witnessed in Moyue Valley, but rather a unique hallucination that only manifested upon death or the threshold of dying.

His reflection in the mirror was still having its brain matter sucked away.

Regardless of whether this was real or fake, it was thoroughly wretched.

"Wake up, brother!"

"Open your eyes!"

"Something is sucking out your brain! Wake up quickly and shake it off!"

The eyelids of his reflection in the mirror flickered rapidly, as if it were about to open its eyes.

Shang Feifan clenched his fists. "Fight back! Fight back!"

*Snap!* His reflection in the mirror truly opened its eyes.

At that exact moment, a colossal, overwhelming force suddenly yanked him—the one pumping himself up—forward.

This time, Shang Feifan distinctly experienced what it meant to have his "vision go black."

Yet, a moment later—perhaps not even a full second—light flooded back into his view.

...What in the hell-spawned place was this now?

He seemed to have merged into one with that reflection in the mirror.

Struggling with all his might, Shang Feifan first wrenched his cocoon-bound hands free, forcefully tearing apart the cocoon's skin before reaching up to pat his own head. His fingers brushed against a slippery, tentacle-like appendage, resembling a soft tube.

Reaching backward, Shang Feifan grabbed the tentacle and yanked it outward with all his strength.

He felt no physical pain whatsoever, yet he could vividly sense something detaching itself from his brain.

*Squelch!*

The tentacle was completely pulled out.

Shang Feifan felt around his head with his fingers, finding not a single wound.

How utterly bizarre!

Yet his sensory perception right now was exceptionally real.

Without rushing to log off, Shang Feifan first tore open the remaining cocoon, freeing himself entirely from its confines.

The ambient light was rather dim; he and the cocoon seemed to be located inside a pool.

The pool was filled with a transparent viscous slime.

Wading over to the edge of the pool, Shang Feifan discovered that it wasn't particularly deep, reaching only up to his waist.

Pressing a single hand against the rim, he gave a light spring and vaulted straight out of the pool.

Slime dripped down continuously from his body.

In the surrounding gloom, numerous other small pools were faintly visible, though all of them were currently empty.

Turning his head again, he saw that the tentacle he had just pulled out had vanished completely without a trace, and even the cocoon he had torn open had disappeared—perhaps transformed into the slime filling the pool.

Looking down at himself, Shang Feifan saw that he was clad in a standard set of introductory player starting gear: a simple tank top and knee-length shorts.

Something seemed to be tucked inside his tank top pocket.

Reaching in to pull it out, Shang Feifan found a B5-sized leather-bound notebook.

As he flipped open to the cover page, a faint flash of light swept across it.

A line of text materialized on the very first page of the notebook:

[Welcome, player 'Your Emperor Has Retired', to the Tianhe Star Beastman Continent. Below is the game tutorial; please view it carefully...]

Shang Feifan thought: Isn't this the legendary, correct way for a game to open?

Once he patiently finished reading through the animated diagrams that emerged on the notebook—which primarily introduced the game rules and a few essential precautions—

The notebook automatically flipped to the second page.

This page served as a table of contents, listing seven major categories: Game Rules, Personal Stats, Quests, Map, Skills, Experience Points, and Save Data.

At the very bottom of the table of contents page, a row of ticking digits displayed the current year, month, day, hour, minute, and second, advancing once every second.

Judging by the time, he had been "newly born" for less than ten minutes.

The "Quests" entry began to emit a soft glow.

Shang Feifan gently tapped on it.

The notebook automatically flipped forward again, landing on the quest page.

On the previously blank page, the first quest materialized:

[Quest One! Player 'Your Emperor Has Retired', please leave the Temple Birth Pool and venture outside the temple to explore the new world. Upon completion, you will be rewarded with 5 Copper Dazhu; please collect it from the grocery store in the player-built encampment, Heavenly Remnant Valley Camp No. 1.]

Luminous arrows began to glow and drift within the dimly lit temple.

chunks.chineseText:
商非凡没再继续翻看笔记本，而是抬脚向箭头指示的方向走去。

忽然，他感到有什么不对，伸手摸向身后。

……他的尾巴呢？

他那条又粗又长的虎尾到哪里去了？

之前他还不习惯屁股后面摇着一根长尾巴，但现在缺了它，却又觉得哪哪都不对劲，感觉平衡感都差了点。

难道死一次会掉尾巴？

门缝透进光芒。

商非凡暂时把尾巴放到一边，推开陈旧破烂的大门，下意识抬手挡住眼睛。

外面正是大中午，太阳光刺眼。

等到眼睛适应光线，商非凡慢慢走下台阶。

他在游戏论坛看过出生点的画面。

从外面看很是残破的小神殿，周围荒草萋萋，死去的藤蔓交缠在低矮灌木上，地上石砖碎的碎、失踪的失踪，到处坑坑洼洼，曾经也许美丽宏伟的建筑和装饰变成一块块残石倒在地上，真实却荒凉。

神殿后面是禁区，有玩家试图绕到神殿后面查看，但总是走进一片浓雾，绕一圈又会走回神殿正前方。

按照游戏策划的说法，那是待开发的秘境副本，暂时还不开放。

顺着神殿前面的破碎石砖小路走个两百多米就能看到一座残缺的石拱门。

从剩下的部分来看，这座拱门造型十分精致。

越过石拱门，再往前就能看到新手村。

伏向军说，这个新手村相当排斥玩家，想要在这里领到任务可不容易。

反而有不少玩家因为对当地土著兽人不了解，初死就死在新手村的NPC兽人手里。

新手村的土著兽人看到了他。

他们看他的脸色并不友好。

商非凡一步跨过石拱门。

叮咚。

【玩家成功拓展新地图，奖励贡献点1点。想要获得更多贡献点数，请更深入和广泛地探索新地图区域。】

【检测到玩家死亡速度过快，为避免资源浪费，请玩家善用游戏商城。】

商非凡停住脚步。

这不是皮质笔记本上的游戏在提醒他，这是他脑中的游戏系统在提醒他！

商非凡抽出皮质笔记本，翻开。

他的任务页面上没有之前任何任务的痕迹，他的第一个任务就是走出神殿出生池。

正这么想，笔记本上的任务页面闪烁了一下。

紧接着，任务页面上就浮现出新的文字。

【恭喜玩家‘你皇退休了’顺利完成第一个任务，请记得到玩家自建营地天残谷一号营地杂货铺领取奖励。】

商非凡啪地合上笔记本。

他需要整理一下他的大脑。

也许他的脑浆真的被人吸食过，他感觉他脑子现在特别混乱。
chunks.englishText:
Shang Feifan did not continue flipping through the notebook. Instead, he lifted his foot and walked in the direction indicated by the arrow.

Suddenly, he felt something was amiss and reached behind his back.

...Where was his tail?

Where had that thick, long tiger tail of his gone?

Earlier, he hadn't been used to having a long tail swishing behind his buttocks, but now that it was missing, everything felt wrong, and even his sense of balance seemed slightly off.

Could dying once make you lose your tail?

Light seeped through the crack of the door.

Shang Feifan momentarily put the tail issue aside, pushed open the dilapidated, rotting heavy door, and instinctively raised a hand to shield his eyes.

Outside was high noon, and the sunlight was dazzling.

Waiting for his eyes to adjust to the brightness, Shang Feifan slowly descended the steps.

He had seen the footage of the spawn points on the game forums.

Viewed from the outside, it was a terribly ruined small shrine. Weeds grew wild all around, dead vines intertwined with low shrubs, and the stone bricks on the ground were either shattered or missing. Potholes were everywhere, and what might have once been magnificent, beautiful architecture and decorations now lay scattered on the ground as blocks of broken stone—desolate yet realistic.

Behind the shrine was a restricted zone. Some players had attempted to skirt around to the back of the shrine to investigate, but they would always walk into a thick fog and loop right back around to the front of the shrine.

According to the game planners, that was a secret realm dungeon awaiting development and was temporarily closed.

Following the broken stone-brick path in front of the shrine for a little over two hundred meters led to a ruined stone archway.

Judging from the remaining parts, this archway had been exquisitely crafted.

Crossing the stone archway and moving further ahead would bring one to the novice village.

Fu Xiangjun had said that this novice village was quite xenophobic toward players, and trying to secure quests here would be no easy feat.

Instead, quite a few players, due to their ignorance of the local aboriginal beastmen, had suffered their very first death at the hands of the NPC beastmen in the novice village.

The aboriginal beastmen of the novice village spotted him.

The expressions on their faces as they looked at him were hardly friendly.

Shang Feifan took a step past the stone archway.

*Ding-dong.*

[Player has successfully expanded a new map, rewarding 1 Contribution Point. To obtain more Contribution Points, explore the new map region more deeply and extensively.]

[Detected that the player's death speed was excessively fast. To avoid wasting resources, players are advised to make good use of the game mall.]

Shang Feifan came to a halt.

This wasn't the game within the leather-bound notebook reminding him; this was the game system inside his very brain giving him a prompt!

Shang Feifan pulled out the leather-bound notebook and flipped it open.

His quest page bore no trace of any previous quests; his very first quest was simply to walk out of the shrine's spawn pool.

As he thought this, the quest page on the notebook flickered.

Immediately afterward, new text materialized on the quest page.

[Congratulations to player 'Your Emperor Has Retired' for successfully completing the first quest. Please remember to collect your reward at the grocery store in Camp No. 1, Tiancan Valley, a player-built settlement.]

Shang Feifan snapped the notebook shut with a sharp *thwack*.

He needed to sort out his brain.

Perhaps his brain matter really had been sucked out by something; his mind felt exceptionally chaotic right now.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第12章 退游是不可能退游的 (Part 1)
chunks.chineseText:
第12章 退游是不可能退游的

天残村的土著兽人们就看到那个不明种族的高大兽人在石拱门边上盘膝坐下，面对他们，却目光放空，也不知在想些什么。

“不用担心。这次就一个，如果他敢做什么，我们就杀了他。”一名身上有鳞片的兽人目光狠厉地盯着商非凡。

村长走过来：“这些刚走出来的活尸很弱，杀起来不难。阿蓝、阿瓶，你们负责盯着他，别让村中孩子接近他。如果他有异动，就吹响骨哨。”

“是！”

“不如直接杀了他。”另一名兽人握着大铁叉子跃跃欲试。

“不急，先看看他想干什么。”

商非凡并不知道土著兽人正谋算着宰了他，他正在思考他为什么会有两套游戏系统，以及死亡后为什么不是直接下线，而像是刚刚进入游戏一样从神殿出生池出生。

这种问题最简单的就是问游戏GM，或者把这种情况当做游戏bug提交给游戏商。

但商非凡没那么单纯，他虽然是第一次玩游戏，但他经历过的奇葩和凶险事情太多，遇到任何事，他更习惯先想一想根源在哪里、对他是否有害，以及如何解决才能从事件中谋取最大利益。

这事如果反应给游戏商，他可能会得到一些游戏中的补偿，也许是一套低级神装，也许是一匹坐骑，也许是经验值翻倍，甚至只是补偿一堆游戏币。

那些东西不说他自己可以从游戏中弄到更好的，以后开通现实货币和游戏币的兑换，他氪点金也能买到。

况且他的直觉告诉他，他身上的情况也许不能简单用游戏bug来解释。

皮质笔记本型的游戏系统还可以说是通过视力神经来让大脑进行判断，本质和VR眼镜的游戏系统并没有太大区别。

直接作用于大脑的游戏系统那就完全是两码事了。

他能想到的最可能阴谋就是——游戏商有意找玩家测试更先进的脑载型光脑游戏系统，却为了节省经费或其他原因，没有取得玩家许可。

也有可能这种抽取某个玩家做小白鼠的事只是个别游戏开发者的行为？

商非凡甚至还脑洞大开，想到会不会是游戏系统里的主脑“活”了，背着游戏开发商搞事，拿人类当小白鼠。

这些猜想都有可能。

而不管是游戏商本身的锅，还是内部员工个人行为，或者是主脑行为，他去找游戏商，游戏商只会想法糊弄他、想法把这件事给彻底掩盖掉。

所以去找游戏商反应bug这条路，能让他获得的利益并不大，先丢到一边。

要想获得最大的实际利益，那就是拿到实际证据去控告游戏商对玩家大脑进行非法实验，进而拿到巨额赔偿。

赔偿的方式可以多种多样，合作也可以……这些以后再想。

重点是得拿到证据！

既然是实验就不可能就他一个人，肯定还有其他玩家也遇到了同样的事情，他得找到这些玩家。这是拿到证据的第一步。

第二步，拿自己做实验，看这种脑载型游戏系统对人体到底有什么样的影响，找医学界脑科专家监控他的身体和精神变化，做好数据记录。

第三步就是设法找到脑载型游戏系统的痕迹，搞清楚这种系统是如何被下载到人类大脑里又是如何运行的。

还有第四步，设法找到游戏开发商和游戏运营商的实体，目前这两者都躲得很好，竟然没有哪家公司站出来承认他们有了这么伟大的发明。

这件事本身就很奇怪。

这也是他们会关注这个游戏的原因之一。

思考到此，基调就定下来了，他会继续玩这个游戏，也不会把拥有两套游戏系统的事反应给游戏商。

当然，他选择不立刻退游、拿自己当实验体，很可能遭遇变成植物人、变成精神病、甚至直接脑死之类的危险。

但原本他和伏向军两人玩这个游戏，就有拿自己当实验体的意思。

所以这和他们的初期计划并不矛盾，只不过他需要承担的风险更大一些。

也许他可以借此多申请一些退休金？

再说他原本来玩游戏只是无聊下的打发时间，以及对全息游戏的好奇。没想到这个游戏这么好玩（危险），反而激起了他更大兴趣。

他渴求安宁生活，但他同样需要刺激。否则生活岂不是太无聊？

第一个问题解决。

现在就来思考第二个大问题。

他为什么会在初死后没有直接下线，而是出现在天残谷新手村的神殿出生池？

为什么这时候他才像是刚登陆游戏一样拥有了皮质笔记本？

如果顺着之前的思路思考……

也许有谁故意打了个时间差，抢先一步截住他，就是为了先测试脑载型游戏系统在他身上的效果。

当他在游戏中死亡后，游戏主脑系统捕捉到了他的脑波信息，认为他是刚上游戏的玩家，就把他送到了神殿出生池？

如果这样想的话，感觉两套系统的开发者都不一样，而且前者还瞒着后者。

所以第二个大问题的关键就是找到给他下载脑载型游戏系统的幕后黑手。

对此，他需要小心的是对他下载脑载型游戏系统的幕后黑手在察觉他发现真相后，会不会想要对他进行灭口处理？比如利用那个游戏头盔，让他直接脑死？

而想要不惊动幕后黑手对他下狠手，最好的方法就是退游，从此不再碰那个游戏头盔。

但退游是不可能退游的，所以……他就只有假装什么都不知道，甚至“傻乎乎”地以为这是游戏中的某种奇遇设定，继续玩他的游戏。

商非凡按揉太阳穴。

别人来玩游戏都是来放松和寻找第二人生感的，他玩游戏却要把脑子给玩烧了。

还有第三个问题，为什么他会在被诅咒死亡后看到那面巨大镜子？

以及镜子中的景象又代表了什么？

那到底是真的被什么东西吸食了脑浆，还是只是游戏系统正在生成玩家身体的过程？

商非凡决定下线去检查一下自己的大脑，如果大脑的反应数据和之前一样，那他看到的景象就是游戏系统正在生成玩家身体的过程。

商非凡本身也比较偏向于这种推测。

但让他挥之不去的是，他为什么会看到这一幕？

这是脑载型游戏系统给予的特别福利？还是真的游戏bug？

那一幕其实挺恐怖的，胆大的玩家还好，胆小的玩家看到这一幕恐怕会吓得不敢继续玩游戏，就算不被吓到也会胡思乱想。

所以应该不是游戏开发商特意让玩家看到这一幕。

这个问题除了游戏出bug外，他暂时想不到其他答案，总不能是脑载型游戏系统特意让他看到这一幕吧？

那又为什么要他看到这一幕？

商非凡原地跳起。

想不通的问题就暂时放一放，也许以后自然而然就会知道答案。

下线前他想先把这个天残谷新手村和玩家一号营地给转一遍，接触一下其他玩家，看都是什么情况。

跳起时总觉得少了什么的商非凡又想到了自己的粗长虎尾。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 12: Quitting the Game is Simply Impossible

The indigenous beastmen of Tiancan Village watched as that tall beastman of an unidentified race sat cross-legged by the stone archway. He faced them, yet his gaze was vacant, and who knew what he was pondering.

"Don't worry. There's only one this time. If he dares to pull anything, we'll kill him." A beastman with scales on his body stared fiercely at Shang Feifan.

The village chief walked over. "These walking corpses that just crawled out are very weak; killing them won't be hard. A-Lan, A-Ping, you two are responsible for keeping an eye on him. Don't let the village children get close to him. If he makes any suspicious moves, blow the bone whistle."

"Understood!"

"We might as well just kill him outright." Another beastman gripped a large iron pitchfork, eager to try.

"No rush. Let's see what he's up to first."

Shang Feifan had no idea that the indigenous beastmen were plotting to slaughter him. At that moment, he was contemplating why he possessed two sets of game systems, and why upon dying he hadn't simply logged off, but instead spawned from the shrine's spawning pool just like someone entering the game for the very first time.

The simplest way to resolve such a question was to ask a game GM, or submit this anomaly to the game developer as a bug.

However, Shang Feifan was not that naive. Although this was his first time playing a game, he had experienced too many bizarre and perilous situations. Whenever he encountered anything, he was more accustomed to first figuring out where the root cause lay, whether it was harmful to him, and how to resolve it to extract the maximum benefit from the incident.

If he reported this matter to the game developer, he might receive some in-game compensation—perhaps a set of low-tier divine gear, a mount, doubled experience points, or even just a pile of game currency.

Leaving aside the fact that he could acquire even better items himself within the game, once real-money-to-game-currency exchange opened up in the future, he could simply whale a bit and buy them.

Furthermore, his intuition told him that his current situation could not simply be explained away as a game bug.

The leather-bound notebook game system could still be described as a device that stimulated the optic nerve to let the brain make judgments, differing little in essence from a VR headset game system.

A game system that acted directly upon the brain, however, was an entirely different matter.

The most probable conspiracy he could think of was that the game developer had intentionally tested a more advanced brain-interfaced optical-brain game system on players, yet for the sake of saving costs or other reasons, had done so without obtaining the players' consent.

Could it also be that such an act of using a player as a guinea pig was merely the rogue behavior of an individual game developer?

Shang Feifan's imagination even ran wild, wondering if the master brain within the game system had "come alive," acting behind the backs of the developers and treating humans as lab rats.

All of these conjectures were possible.

And whether it was the game developer's own fault, an internal employee's individual misconduct, or the master brain's actions, if he went to the game developer, they would only try to brush him off and find a way to completely cover the matter up.

Therefore, the path of reporting the bug to the game developer would yield him very little actual benefit, so he tossed it aside for now.

To gain the maximum practical benefit, he needed to secure concrete evidence to sue the game developer for illegal experimentation on a player's brain, and thereby extort massive compensation.

The form of compensation could vary, and cooperation was also an option... he would think about those later.

The key point was obtaining evidence!

Since it was an experiment, it couldn't just be him; there had to be other players who had encountered the exact same thing. He needed to find these players—that was the first step to securing evidence.

The second step was to use himself as an experiment to see what kind of impact this brain-interfaced game system actually had on the human body, and find medical brain-science experts to monitor his physical and mental changes while keeping proper data records.

The third step was to find a way to trace the remnants of the brain-interfaced game system, figuring out how such a system was downloaded into the human brain and how it operated.

Then there was the fourth step: finding the physical entities of the game developer and the game operator. Currently, both were hiding so well that not a single company had stepped forward to claim credit for such a magnificent invention.

This fact alone was quite strange.

And this was precisely one of the reasons they had taken an interest in this game in the first place.

With these thoughts, the tone was set: he would continue playing this game, and he would not report the fact that he possessed two game systems to the developers.

Of course, choosing not to log off immediately and using himself as a test subject carried severe risks—he could potentially turn into a vegetable, a mental patient, or suffer immediate brain death.

Yet originally, when Fu Xiangjun and he played this game, they had intended to use themselves as experimental subjects anyway.

Thus, this did not contradict their initial plan; it was simply that the risks he had to bear were somewhat greater.

Perhaps he could use this to apply for a higher pension?

Besides, he had originally only come to play the game to pass the time out of boredom and out of curiosity about holographic gaming. To his surprise, this game was so fun (and dangerous) that it instead sparked even greater interest.

He craved a peaceful life, but he also needed excitement. Otherwise, wouldn't life be far too dull?

The first problem was solved.

Now, let's ponder the second major problem.

Why, after his initial death, did he not log off directly, but instead appear at the shrine's spawning pool in the Tiancan Valley Novice Village?

Why was it only at this moment that he possessed a leather-bound notebook, just as if he were logging into the game for the very first time?

If he followed his previous line of reasoning...

Perhaps someone had deliberately played with the timing, intercepting him a step ahead precisely to test the effects of the brain-interfaced game system on him.

When he died in the game, the game's master brain system captured his brainwave information, assumed he was a newly logged-in player, and sent him to the shrine's spawning pool?

Thinking along these lines, it felt as though the developers of the two systems were completely different entities, with the former even keeping things hidden from the latter.

Therefore, the crux of the second major problem was finding the mastermind who had downloaded the brain-interfaced game system into him.

Regarding this, what he needed to be careful about was whether the mastermind who installed the system would, upon discovering that he had uncovered the truth, attempt to silence him—for instance, by using that gaming helmet to cause direct brain death?

And the best way to avoid alerting the mastermind into dealing a ruthless blow to him was to quit the game and never touch that gaming helmet again.

However, quitting the game was simply impossible, so... his only option was to pretend he knew nothing, and even play along "foolishly" as if this were some kind of special in-game encounter setting, continuing to play his game.

Shang Feifan massaged his temples.

Other people came to games to relax and seek a second lease on life, but his gaming sessions were practically going to fry his brain.

There was also a third question: why had he seen that gigantic mirror after dying from the curse?

And what did the scene inside the mirror represent?

Was his brain matter genuinely being sucked out by something, or was it merely the game system generating the player's physical body?

Shang Feifan decided to log off and inspect his own brain. If the brain response data matched what it was before, then the scene he had witnessed was simply the game system generating a player's body.

Shang Feifan himself leaned somewhat toward this hypothesis.

Yet, what lingered stubbornly in his mind was: why had he seen that particular spectacle?

Was this a special perk granted by the brain-interfaced game system? Or was it truly a game bug?

That scene was actually quite terrifying. Bold players might brush it off, but timid ones would probably be scared out of their wits and dare not continue playing; even if not frightened, they would let their imaginations run wild.

So it shouldn't have been something the game developers deliberately let players witness.

Aside from a game glitch, he could temporarily find no other answer to this question. It couldn't possibly be that the brain-interfaced system had deliberately made him see it, could it?

And if so, why would it want him to see it?

Shang Feifan leaped up from the spot.

Unresolved questions would have to be put aside for now; perhaps the answers would reveal themselves naturally in time.

Before logging off, he wanted to tour this Tiancan Valley Novice Village and Player Camp No. 1 first, mingling with other players to see what their situations were like.

As he jumped, Shang Feifan, who always felt like something was missing, thought once more of his thick, long tiger tail.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第12章 退游是不可能退游的 (Part 2)
chunks.chineseText:
他在天残谷出生点这边出生的身体都和之前的身体不一样！

继而商非凡想到了伏向军和论坛上对于玩家的介绍——出生就是天残。

天残兽人不能在兽形和人形之间自由转换，或者是天生就有身体残缺。

他现在这具身体就没有尾巴，符合天残说法。

商非凡还试着让自己转变成小虎崽，但不管他怎么想，他的身体都没有动静。不知道是他还没有掌握兽形和人形的转换方法，还是压根就不能转换。

如果是这样的话，那不是说他之前的游戏身体和现在的游戏身体就不是同一具身体？

叮咚。

【检测到玩家正处于死亡惩罚时间，七十二小时内，玩家将失去尾巴和失去在兽形与人形之间互相转换的能力。请玩家珍惜生命，建议玩家善用游戏商城，开启buff监测等相关功能。】

商非凡：……这个补丁解释来得可真及时。

另外这个说明也又一次证明脑载型游戏系统和皮质笔记本型游戏系统就是两个不同系统！

两者之间连死亡惩罚都不一样。而且脑载型游戏系统从来不叫他的玩家名字。

就是他为什么从脑载系统的反应中感觉到一丝丝无耻？

就好像这个系统不愿意浪费自己的资源给玩家重生身体，直接就利用了笔记本系统的再生功能？

然后为了隐瞒笔记本系统，还故意搞出了一个七十二小时的“天残惩罚”。

但脑载系统就不怕七十二小时后他身体恢复，可以双形转变，被笔记本系统发现不对？

还是说脑载系统能够推算出七十二小时后会有办法解决这个问题？

商非凡突然想到游戏系统几次提到要善用游戏商城……

商非凡就顺手打开了游戏商城，找到搜索栏。这个游戏商城竟然还有搜索功能，这就方便多了。

他输入状态一词，打算找不到就再输入buff一词。

商城页面给出了搜索结果。

没想到跳出来的商品还挺多，就是大多都是灰色。

比如能显示出身体状态的装备武器最低价都在一百贡献点以上。

还有些天赋技能也能做到显示身体状态，比如：

天赋技能，【瞳术】。激活【瞳术】，学习第一级观测之眼，即可随时观测自身身体状态。

天赋技能，【不死之身】。激活【不死之身】，学习第一级快速恢复术，即可随时修复自身状态至最佳状态。

我靠！不死之身！

商非凡眼馋得眼睛都红了，但一看要激活这个天赋技能需要的贡献点数，他就……以后再说吧。

开启初级炼金术只要一百点，但想要激活天赋技能不死之身，只是激活就要一千贡献点！

还有职业技能，【医师】可学习初级诊断学，诊断身体状态。【治疗祭司】学习初级感知学，能随时感知身体状态……

总之，有类似功能的天赋技能和职业技能很多，但无一例外都很贵！看着就让他想骂游戏商吝啬，给贡献点就给那么一点点。

商非凡又精简条件，去掉所有超过4个贡献点的商品。

这次剩下来的商品就不多了。

只有四个，且都属于特殊物品类别。

【残破的红巾】，据说这是一条从最终战场捡来的垃圾，不知道原主人是谁，系在左胳膊上可以随时侦测你的身体状态，但偶尔会失灵。只要3个贡献点，你就可以带回家。

【破旧的手镯】，据一名低级鉴定师学徒鉴定，这只手镯很有可能属于炼金大师鼠田泉的早年作品，戴在身上会产生颜色变化，不同的颜色代表你不同的身体状态。红色请小心，这说明你就快死了。3个贡献点。

【碎裂的玻璃球】，据说这只看起来像是眼睛的玻璃球原本属于一名极端邪恶的诅咒大巫，只有有缘人才能得到。现在只要4个贡献点，你就能成为它的有缘人。哦，它的功能很多，帮忙诅咒只是之一，它还能帮你监测别人对你的诅咒情况并反馈给你，包括你的身体状态。你如果快死了，它也会让你知道。同时它还能遮掩你的身体状态。使用它，小心被拉入黑暗世界。

【破盒子】，这很有可能是从大繁华纪留下的高科技物品，名为医疗诊断箱，可以用来诊断身体状况和病情，但需要充能才能使用。没有使用说明书，但冲着它来自大繁华纪，它也最少值4个贡献点。卖给那些喜爱大繁华纪物品的古董商人，说不定能大赚一笔。

更好的商品不是没有，但是他买不起。

是现在就买残次品，将来有更好的再替换。还是把贡献点攒着，要买就买最好的？

不远处，草丛晃动。

商非凡看过去，就看到一只方头方脑的小毛茸茸躲在草丛中正在偷瞧他。
chunks.englishText:
The body he had spawned with here at the Tiancan Valley spawning point was completely different from his previous one!

Following that, Shang Feifan thought of Fu Xiangjun and the descriptions of players on the forum—they were born with physical flaws (Tiancan).

Tiancan beastmen could not freely transform between beast form and human form, or they were born with congenital physical defects.

His current body possessed no tail at all, which fit the description of a Tiancan.

Shang Feifan even tried to transform himself into a small tiger cub, but no matter what he willed, his body remained completely motionless. He didn't know whether he simply hadn't mastered the method of transforming between beast and human forms, or if transformation was utterly impossible.

If that was the case, didn't it mean his previous game body and his current game body were not the exact same body?

*Ding-dong.*

[Detected that the player is currently in the death penalty period. Within seventy-two hours, the player will lose their tail and the ability to mutually transform between beast and human forms. Please cherish your life; it is recommended that the player make good use of the game shop and activate related functions such as buff monitoring.]

Shang Feifan: ...This patch explanation sure came in timely.

Moreover, this description once again proved that the brain-interfaced game system and the leather-bound notebook game system were two entirely separate systems!

Even their death penalties didn't match. Besides, the brain-interfaced system never addressed him by his player name.

Why, though, did he sense a trace of shamelessness from the brain-interfaced system's feedback?

It was as if this system was unwilling to waste its own resources to regenerate a physical body for the player, and instead directly hijacked the notebook system's regeneration function?

Then, to conceal the notebook system, it deliberately concocted a seventy-two-hour "Tiancan Penalty."

Yet, wasn't the brain-interfaced system afraid that after seventy-two hours, once his body recovered and dual-form transformation became possible, the notebook system would discover something was amiss?

Or could it be that the brain-interfaced system had calculated that it would find a way to resolve this issue by the time seventy-two hours were up?

Shang Feifan suddenly recalled how the game system had mentioned several times that he should make good use of the game shop...

Shang Feifan casually opened the game shop and found the search bar. This game shop actually had a search function, which made things much more convenient.

He typed in the word "status," intending to enter "buff" next if nothing turned up.

The shop page displayed the search results.

To his surprise, quite a few items popped up, though the majority were grayed out.

For instance, equipment and weapons capable of displaying physical status had a minimum price starting at over one hundred contribution points.

There were also certain innate skills that could achieve body-status displays, such as:

Innate Skill: [Pupil Technique]. Activate [Pupil Technique] and learn Level 1 Observation Eye to monitor your own physical status at any time.

Innate Skill: [Undying Body]. Activate [Undying Body] and learn Level 1 Rapid Recovery to restore your physical condition to its optimal state at any moment.

Holy crap! An undying body!

Shang Feifan's eyes turned red with envy, but the moment he saw the contribution points required to activate this innate skill, he... decided to talk about it later in life.

Unlocking Elementary Alchemy only cost one hundred points, but to activate the Undying Body innate skill, just the activation alone required one thousand contribution points!

There were also profession skills: [Physician] could learn Elementary Diagnostics to diagnose physical conditions; [Healing Priest] could learn Elementary Perception to sense physical conditions at any time...

In short, there were plenty of innate and profession skills with similar functions, but without exception, they were all exorbitantly expensive! Just looking at them made him want to curse the developers for being so stingy, giving out such measly amounts of contribution points.

Shang Feifan refined his filter criteria, removing all items exceeding 4 contribution points.

This time, the remaining items weren't many.

There were only four, all belonging to the special item category.

[Tattered Red Scarf]: Rumored to be a piece of trash picked up from the final battlefield. The original owner is unknown. Tying it around your left arm allows you to detect your physical status at any time, though it occasionally malfunctions. For just 3 contribution points, you can take it home.

[Dilapidated Bracelet]: Authenticated by a low-tier appraiser apprentice as likely belonging to the early works of Alchemy Master Shu Tianquan. Wearing it will cause color changes, with different colors representing different physical states. Red means proceed with caution—it indicates you are about to die. 3 contribution points.

[Shattered Glass Orb]: Rumored to look like an eyeball, this glass orb originally belonged to an extremely evil Cursed Arch-Mage and can only be obtained by someone destined. Now, for just 4 contribution points, you can become that destined person. Oh, it has many functions; helping cast curses is merely one of them. It can also help monitor curses placed on you by others and feed that information back to you, including your physical status. If you're about to die, it will let you know as well. At the same time, it can conceal your physical status. Use it with caution, lest you be dragged into the dark world.

[Broken Box]: Highly likely to be a high-tech item left over from the Great Prosperous Era, named a Medical Diagnostic Kit. It can be used to diagnose physical conditions and illnesses, but requires charging to operate. It comes with no instruction manual, but given that it hails from the Great Prosperous Era, it is worth at least 4 contribution points. Selling it to antique dealers who adore items from the Great Prosperous Era might net you a hefty profit.

Better items weren't nonexistent, but he couldn't afford them.

Should he buy a defective item now and replace it later when something better came along? Or should he hoard his contribution points and only buy the absolute best when the time came?

Not far away, the bushes rustled.

Shang Feifan looked over and spotted a square-headed, fluffy little creature hiding in the brush, secretly peeking at him.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第13章 我是到处跑的修理商 (Part 1)
chunks.chineseText:
第13章 我是到处跑的修理商

“喵呜~，你是我爸爸吗？”奶声奶气的毛茸茸大着胆子探出一颗小脑袋。

商非凡对养宠物无感，对毛茸茸也不是特别喜欢，但小家伙这声喵呜，不是特别心狠手辣反社会的，真对他心硬不起来。

商非凡看小家伙仰着脑袋很吃力的样子，就伸手想把它托起来。

小家伙竟然真的跳到他的手掌上，小屁屁往他手掌心一坐，摆出了一个蹲坐的造型。

像个幼崽玩偶，还是藏狐和兔狲的混合种。

但这个幼崽玩偶不是可爱型，而是奇葩型。

脑袋方方的也就算了，身上灰白色的小绒毛稀稀拉拉，小小年纪就斑秃了。

而且小家伙很脏，应该很久没有大人给他舔毛和清理，身上不多的毛发一条条地黏在一起，裸-露出的皮肤也有不少被蚊虫叮咬出来的疙瘩，还有一些小伤疤。

“抱歉，我不是你爸爸。”虽然到处找爸爸的小家伙很可怜，但商非凡心够硬，还是一口戳破小家伙的期望。

小家伙的眼神略微黯淡了一些，但也没有太失望，大概是失望太多次，已经习惯。

“你可以帮我找我爸爸吗？村长伯伯说他出门打猎迷路了，一直没能找到回家的路。我可以付你报酬，我藏了两枚果子……”

“你妈妈呢？”商非凡不想接这个任务，迅速打断小家伙。

“我妈妈被咕噜巨兽吃掉了。”

“咕噜巨兽？”

“那是一种非常非常可怕的巨兽，它总是吃不饱，肚子老是发出咕噜咕噜的叫声，它可以一口就把我们都吞了！”小家伙举起爪子张大嘴，做出恐吓模样。

“嘿！你在干什么？放下我们村的幼崽！”远处传来一声爆喝。

当即就有三个兽人提着铁叉就冲了过来。

商非凡：搞嘛？

“快放下他！”

“他是我爸爸~”

不是。商非凡想把小家伙放到地上，但小家伙伸出爪子抱紧了他的手腕。

他这是被碰瓷了吗？

同一时间，莫约山谷。

虎不帅收拾起诺曼掉落的衣裤和钱袋，连同那根骨杖一起，扎成一个包裹扎在巨虫身上。

“不帅少爷？那个人就这么消失了？这不像是诅咒……”狼四脸色沉重，眼中满是不解。

虎不帅也想不通，就在那虎兽人瞳孔扩散失去呼吸没有几秒，他的身体上方突然出现一个黑洞，没等他和狼四反应过来，那虎兽人的身体就被吸进了黑洞中。

诡异的是，当虎兽人身体被吸进黑洞的同时，他身上穿着的衣裤鞋袜和所有身外物全都掉落到地上。

然后黑洞就消失了。

整个过程非常快，全部可能都不到一两秒。

“我们回去。”他要回去问问他小姨，诅咒能否做到这种效果，以及虎兽人为什么会死得那么快。

回头再看天残谷天残村。

三名兽人包围了商非凡，举着铁叉喝令他放下幼崽。

商非凡略微提起右手，表示没有恶意：“你们也看见了，不是我不想放开他，是他不肯放开我。”

“你会说人话？”身上有鳞片的兽人惊讶。

商非凡：“我跟人自然说人话，你不是人吗？”

三名兽人互看。

更多的兽人发现这边动静不对，往这边跑了过来。

还有人吹响了骨哨。

商非凡听到锐利的骨哨声，再看到一个高壮兽人带着一群手持各种武器的兽人往这边跑，瞥小家伙：“你可真会给我找麻烦。”

小家伙露出呆滞表情。

商非凡没注意到，他看向带着兽人跑过来的高壮兽人，先发制人：“日安，诸位，我是诺曼霍希尔，一名出来赚钱的修理商，我来自莫约山谷镇。请问你们这里有什么需要修理的东西吗？另外，我还想买一些提炼过的金属矿石。”

“莫约山谷镇？没听过。你们谁听过吗？”

“应该不是这附近。”

“他说他是一名修理商，他还有一个正式的名字，不像前面那些活尸，不会说人话，连名字都说不出来。”

商非凡：那是因为他们不好意思说出他们的游戏名。

不过玩家不会说人话是怎么回事？

等等，他想起来了，他在论坛好像看到过，游戏策划说是为了更有真实感，也为了防止玩家刚进游戏不懂分寸就会跟土著们胡说八道，所以玩家可以听懂当地兽人说的语言，却无法说出来，必须通过学习。

学习兽人世界通用语的时间，也是玩家适应和融入这个世界的时间，到那时他们基本都会知道什么该说什么不该说。

可他不但一开始就能听懂当地语言，他还能说能读，应该也能写。

“你说你是莫约山谷镇来的修理商，那你为什么会从古墓地出来？”村长走上前来，质问。

“古墓地？”商非凡看向身后，“你是说那个老破小神殿？”

“对，那个神殿就是祭祀古墓地无数怨灵之用。除了祭司，不会有活人去那里。”

“我不知道。”商非凡一脸无辜：“我醒来就在神殿外面，身上的行李、武器和钱袋都不见了，只剩下一套不属于我的内衣。”

村长和周围几名兽人互看。

“他说他在神殿外面。”

“那就好。不是从神殿里面出来的应该不是活尸。”

兽人们窃窃私语。

“我知道了。他肯定是被那些活尸给打劫了。”

“那些活尸竟然没有杀了他，还给他换上了它们的衣服。”

“可能是想借刀杀人，想让我们以为他也是活尸然后杀了他？”

“这应该就是一个倒霉的商人，他看起来和那些活尸一点都不一样。像是大城市来的。”

兽人们都觉得商非凡看起来不像是那些刚从神殿走出来的活尸。

那些活尸怎么说呢，就像是刚来到这个世界的幼崽一样，看到什么都好奇，但又比幼崽危险，行为古里古怪，啃土的、吃草的、捏自己的、打人的、跳舞的、喃喃自语的、还有冲上来就想抱他们幼崽的……什么都有，在当地兽人眼中就是一群神经病。

“阿呆不怕他。他应该不是坏人。”

“阿呆懂什么，那就是一个小呆子！”

“先把阿呆抱回来。其他的再说。”

村长伸手：“能把我们村的幼崽还给我们吗？”

商非凡也伸出手臂：“那你们谁来帮个忙，把他从我胳膊上撕下来？”

噗！几个兽人发出闷笑。

村长脸色也缓和许多。现场谁都能看出来，那个高大的陌生兽人并没有控制阿呆，反倒是阿呆四肢都缠在了高大兽人的手臂上，抱得贼紧。

“阿呆！”村长轻喝。

阿呆扭头，表情呆呆。

“快过来，那不是我们村的人。”

“爸爸！”阿呆抱紧商非凡手臂。

村长特别无奈：“他不是你爸爸，他只是路过这里的游商。”

阿呆扭头不理睬。

商非凡空着的手弹了弹小家伙的额头：“你先下来。你不是要我帮你找爸爸吗？如果你肯下来，那么这事还有的谈，否则……”

小家伙仍旧抱紧他手臂不动。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 13: I'm a Traveling Repairman

"Meow~, are you my daddy?" A tiny, squeaky, furry little head poked out timidly.

Shang Feifan was indifferent to raising pets and wasn't particularly fond of furry things either, but with the little fellow's pitiful "meow," unless someone was truly ruthless and sociopathic, it was impossible to stay hard-hearted against it.

Seeing the little creature tilting its head up with a very strenuous look, Shang Feifan reached out, intending to lift it up.

To his surprise, the little thing actually hopped onto his palm, planted its tiny butt right in the center, and struck a squatting pose.

It looked like a baby doll, or perhaps a hybrid between a Pallas's cat and a Tibetan fox.

Yet, this baby doll wasn't cute; it was utterly bizarre.

Having a square head was one thing, but the sparse, grayish-white fuzz on its body was patchy, and it was suffering from alopecia at such a tender age.

Moreover, the little creature was quite filthy. It must have been a long time since an adult licked its fur and cleaned it; the meager hair it had was clumped together in strands, and its exposed skin bore numerous mosquito bites, bumps, and small scars.

"Sorry, I'm not your daddy." Although a little creature running around searching everywhere for its dad was pitiful, Shang Feifan's heart was tough enough to puncture the little one's expectations in one breath.

The little creature's eyes dimmed slightly, though not with excessive disappointment—likely because it had been let down too many times and had grown accustomed to it.

"Can you help me find my daddy? Village Chief Uncle said he got lost hunting and hasn't been able to find his way back home. I can pay you a reward; I've hidden two fruits..."

"What about your mother?" Shang Feifan had no desire to take on this quest and swiftly interrupted the little fellow.

"My mother was eaten by a Gulu Behemoth."

"A Gulu Behemoth?"

"It's a very, very scary giant beast. It's never full, its belly is always making a gurgling sound, and it can swallow all of us in one bite!" The little creature raised its paws and opened its mouth wide, striking a threatening pose.

"Hey! What are you doing? Put down our village's cub!" A furious roar echoed from a distance.

Immediately, three orcs came charging over, brandishing iron forks.

Shang Feifan: What is going on here?

"Put him down right now!"

"He's my daddy~"

No, I am not. Shang Feifan wanted to place the little thing on the ground, but it extended its claws and hugged his wrist tightly.

Was he being scammed by a professional porcelain-toucher?

At the same time, in the Moyue Valley.

Hu Bushuai packed up the clothes, pants, and money pouch dropped by Norman, along with that bone staff, and tied them into a bundle strapped onto the giant insect.

"Young Master Bushuai? That guy just vanished like that? This doesn't look like a curse..." Lang Si's expression was grave, his eyes full of incomprehension.

Hu Bushuai couldn't figure it out either. Just seconds after the tiger orc's pupils dilated and he stopped breathing, a black hole suddenly appeared right above his body. Before he and Lang Si could react, the tiger orc's body was sucked straight into the black hole.

What was bizarre was that the moment the tiger orc's body was sucked into the black hole, the clothes, pants, shoes, socks, and all external belongings he was wearing fell clean to the ground.

Then the black hole vanished.

The entire process happened at lightning speed, lasting less than a second or two.

"Let's head back." He needed to go back and ask his little aunt whether a curse could achieve such an effect, and why the tiger orc had died so quickly.

Looking back at the Heavenly Defect Valley and Heavenly Defect Village.

The three orcs surrounded Shang Feifan, brandishing their iron forks and shouting at him to put down the cub.

Shang Feifan raised his right hand slightly to indicate he meant no harm: "You saw it yourselves, it's not that I don't want to let him go; it's that he refuses to let go of me."

"You can speak the common tongue?" The orc with scales on his body asked in surprise.

Shang Feifan: "I naturally speak human words to humans. Aren't you human?"

The three orcs looked at each other.

More orcs noticed the commotion and came running over.

Someone even blew a bone whistle.

Hearing the sharp blast of the bone whistle and watching a tall, muscular orc lead a crowd of orcs armed with various weapons charging toward them, Shang Feifan glanced down at the little fellow: "You really know how to cause me trouble."

The little creature wore a vacant expression.

Unaware of it, Shang Feifan looked at the tall, muscular orc leading the charge and took the initiative: "Good day, everyone. I am Norman Hoaxier, a traveling repairman looking to make some money. I come from Moyue Valley Town. Do you have anything here that needs repairing? Additionally, I'd like to buy some refined metal ores."

"Moyue Valley Town? Never heard of it. Has anyone here heard of it?"

"Shouldn't be anywhere nearby."

"He says he's a repairman, and he even has a proper name. Unlike those walking corpses from earlier, who couldn't speak human words and couldn't even state their names."

Shang Feifan: That's because they were too embarrassed to say their gaming handles.

However, what was going on with players not being able to speak human words?

Wait, he remembered seeing something on the forums: the game developers supposedly implemented this for greater realism and to prevent players from talking nonsense with the natives before they understood the boundaries of the new game. Therefore, players could understand the language spoken by the local orcs, but were unable to speak it until they learned it.

The time spent learning the Orcish lingua franca was also the adaptation and integration period for players in this world. By then, they would basically know what should and shouldn't be said.

Yet, not only could he understand the local language right from the start, but he could also speak, read, and presumably write it.

"You say you're a repairman from Moyue Valley Town, so why did you come out of the ancient graveyard?" The village chief stepped forward and questioned him.

"Ancient graveyard?" Shang Feifan looked behind him. "You mean that old, dilapidated temple?"

"Right, that temple is used to sacrifice to the countless grievances of the ancient graveyard. Aside from priests, no living person goes there."

"I have no idea." Shang Feifan put on an innocent look. "When I woke up, I was outside the temple. My luggage, weapons, and money pouch were all gone, leaving me with only a set of undergarments that don't belong to me."

The village chief and several surrounding orcs exchanged glances.

"He said he was outside the temple."

"That's fine then. Anyone who didn't come from inside the temple shouldn't be a walking corpse."

The orcs whispered among themselves.

"I get it. He must have been robbed by those walking corpses."

"Those walking corpses actually didn't kill him and even changed him into their clothes."

"Could it be they wanted to use a borrowed knife to kill someone, making us think he's a walking corpse and kill him instead?"

"This must just be an unlucky merchant. He looks completely different from those walking corpses. He looks like he's from a big city."

The orcs all agreed that Shang Feifan didn't look like those walking corpses that had just walked out of the temple.

How should they describe those walking corpses? They were like infants who had just arrived in this world—curious about everything, yet more dangerous than infants, with bizarre behaviors. Some gnawed on dirt, some ate grass, some pinched themselves, some beat people up, some danced, some muttered to themselves, and others rushed up trying to hug their cubs... They did all sorts of things, appearing to the local orcs as a bunch of lunatics.

"Ah-Dai isn't afraid of him. He shouldn't be a bad person."

"What does Ah-Dai know? He's just a little simpleton!"

"Pull Ah-Dai back first. We'll talk about the rest later."

The village chief reached out: "Can you return our village's cub to us?"

Shang Feifan also extended his arms: "Then which of you wants to lend a hand and peel him off my arm?"

Pfft! Several orcs emitted muffled chuckles.

The village chief's expression also softened considerably. Anyone on the scene could see that the tall, strange orc wasn't controlling Ah-Dai; rather, Ah-Dai had wrapped all four limbs tightly around the tall orc's arm, hugging on for dear life.

"Ah-Dai!" The village chief shouted softly.

Ah-Dai turned his head, looking blank.

"Come over here quickly. He's not from our village."

"Daddy!" Ah-Dai hugged Shang Feifan's arm even tighter.

The village chief was extremely helpless: "He's not your daddy. He's just a traveling merchant passing through."

Ah-Dai turned his head away and ignored him.

Shang Feifan flicked the little fellow's forehead with his free hand: "Get down first. Didn't you want me to help you find your daddy? If you're willing to get down, then we can talk about this matter; otherwise..."

The little creature still hugged his arm tightly and refused to budge.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第13章 我是到处跑的修理商 (Part 2)
chunks.chineseText:
商非凡看向村长。

村长干咳一声：“你说你叫？”

“诺曼霍希尔，你们可以叫我诺曼。我的钱财都没了，但我的手艺没丢。你们村有什么东西需要修理吗，我修理费可以打五折。”商非凡很坦诚地说：“我需要赚点钱回家，今年我们那片土地受到虫族诅咒影响，收成不太好，我弟还在等我带钱回家买粮食。”

听商非凡这么一说，兽人们警惕的神情几乎都消失了，甚至不少兽人脸上对他露出同情的神情。

“该死的虫族！”还有几个兽人同仇敌忾地呸呸吐唾沫。

“该死的活尸！尸体会复活，肯定是虫族在搞鬼。”

“死去的尸体就不该再醒来。”

“对。可惜我们人手太少，否则一定要把那些活尸建设的营地给毁掉！”

“对了，这个人不是从外面来的吗，让他把消息带回大城市，让那些大城市的兽人派兵过来消灭那些活尸。”

半个小时后，商非凡坐在了村长家的谷仓里。

村长妻子给他送来了一壶水和一个烤出来的死面饼。

被叫做阿呆的方头小幼崽也总算肯从商非凡的胳膊上下来，但村长让他离开，他却紧挨着商非凡不肯走。

商非凡也没驱赶这小东西。

商非凡表示自己不想白吃白喝，村长很理解地在谷仓里找了一个刚刚用坏掉的打麦粒工具——连枷，交给他修理。

叮咚。

商非凡同时接到了两个游戏系统的任务，都是让他帮助天残村村长修复打麦工具连枷。

商非凡：……行吧，同一个任务，他可以赚1点贡献点，外加5个铜达铢。比起其他玩家，他应该算是赚了？

这种简单农具，天残村的成年兽人几乎人人都会修理。

村长也就是给商非凡找点事干，顺便看看他是不是真的会修理各种工具。

商非凡看到这么古老的打麦工具……好吧，他在很多战区部落混过，那里的发展比原始社会也好不到哪里去，他经常在那种地方一待就是几个月，这些古老工具倒也见过不少。

但他还真没修理过。

不过话已经说出口，作为到处跑赚生活费的小修理商，他怎么可能连这么常见的农业工具都不能修理？

好在连枷构造简单，看起来就像是双截棍，动手能力强的人多琢磨一会儿就能知道原理。

商非凡跟村长借用了几件常用工具，刷刷就修理起来。

因为这把连枷使用时间比较长，负责打麦的骨棍需要更换了。

这里的兽人似乎很喜欢使用骨头当材料。

商非凡就把陈旧腐朽的骨棍换下来，换上新的，再打孔固定。

顺便他还改进了一下村长家的连枷，给连枷头绑上了三根骨棍，三根骨棍平排，可以让拍打面积更大一些。

虽然这样改造会更沉重一些，但商非凡相信那些健壮的兽人不会觉得改造后的连枷用起来有多吃力。

比起连枷，当然还是脱粒机更好用，但商非凡看了一圈都没看到适合做脱粒机的材料，只好略微改进了下连枷。

商非凡修理连枷时，小兽人阿呆就坐在一边专心致志地看着。

商非凡把水壶和麦饼推给他。

小家伙也没客气，撕下一块就着清水塞进嘴里用力咀嚼。

村长中途过来，看到商非凡不但修理了他家的连枷，还改进了，试了试，觉得很好用，顿时对商非凡多了几分亲热。

“你做的这个连枷应该可以提高不少打麦效率，介意我给其他村人看看吗？”

“当然可以。我一个人又做不过来。如果有人自己会做，那就自己做。”

年轻健壮的村长伸手拍拍商非凡的肩膀，感叹：“兄弟，你是个好人。我们差点误会你。”

“爸爸。”阿呆吧唧抱住商非凡的小腿。

商非凡低头：“能说说这小东西是怎么回事吗？”

村长未语先叹气：“其实我们村像阿呆的小家伙很多。你应该已经看出来了吧，我们这里是天残村。”
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 13: I'm a Traveling Repairman (Part 2)

Shang Feifan looked toward the village elder.

The village elder gave a dry cough: "You said your name is?"

"Norman Hochschild, you can call me Norman. All my money and belongings are gone, but my craftsmanship hasn't. Does your village have anything that needs repairing? I can offer a fifty-percent discount on my repair fees," Shang Feifan said very candidly. "I need to earn some money to go back home. This year, our land was affected by the Zerg curse, and the harvest wasn't very good. My younger brother is still waiting for me to bring money home to buy food."

Hearing Shang Feifan put it this way, the guarded expressions of the beastmen nearly vanished entirely, and many even cast looks of sympathy toward him.

"Damn the Zerg!" A few beastmen also spat in solidarity against a common enemy.

"Damn the living corpses! Corpses rising from the dead—it's definitely the Zerg making trouble."

"Dead corpses shouldn't be waking back up again."

"Right. It's a pity our numbers are too small, otherwise we'd definitely destroy the camp those living corpses built!"

"Right, isn't this person from the outside? Let him take the word back to the big cities and have the beastmen there dispatch troops to wipe out those living corpses."

Half an hour later, Shang Feifan was seated inside the village elder's granary.

The elder's wife had brought him a flask of water and a baked unleavened flatbread.

The square-headed little cub called A-Dai was finally willing to climb down from Shang Feifan's arm, but when the elder told him to leave, he stayed pressed right against Shang Feifan's side, refusing to budge.

Shang Feifan didn't drive the little thing away, either.

Stating that he didn't want to eat and drink for free, Shang Feifan was met with the village elder's understanding. The elder searched the granary and handed him a recently broken threshing tool—a flail—for him to repair.

*Ding-dong.*

Shang Feifan received two game system quests simultaneously, both instructing him to help the Tiancan Village elder repair the threshing flail.

Shang Feifan: *...Fine then. For the exact same quest, I get to earn 1 contribution point plus 5 copper dalars. Compared to other players, I suppose I'm making a profit?*

Such simple farm tools could be repaired by almost every adult beastman in Tiancan Village.

The village elder was simply giving Shang Feifan something to do, while incidentally testing whether he could genuinely repair all sorts of tools.

Seeing such an ancient threshing tool... well, he had mixed among many warzone tribes where development was no better than a primitive society, and he had often spent months at a time in places like that, so he had indeed seen quite a few of these ancient tools.

However, he had truly never repaired one before.

Yet since the words were already out of his mouth, as a traveling little repairman trying to earn a living, how could he possibly fail to mend such a common agricultural tool?

Fortunately, the flail had a simple structure, looking rather like a nunchaku. Anyone with good hands-on skills could figure out the mechanics after pondering it for a little while.

Borrowing a few common tools from the village elder, Shang Feifan set to work, his movements brisk.

Because this flail had been used for quite a long time, the bone stick responsible for beating the grain needed to be replaced.

The beastmen here seemed very fond of using bones as materials.

Shang Feifan promptly removed the aged, decaying bone stick, fitted a new one in its place, and drilled holes to secure it.

By the way, he even made a few improvements to the elder's flail, binding three bone sticks to the flail head side-by-side in a row, which would allow for a larger striking surface.

Though this modification would make it somewhat heavier, Shang Feifan believed that the robust beastmen wouldn't find the modified flail tiring to use.

Compared to a flail, a threshing machine was naturally much easier to use, but Shang Feifan had looked around and found no materials suitable for building a threshing machine, so he had to settle for slightly improving the flail.

As Shang Feifan repaired the flail, the little beastman A-Dai sat right beside him, watching with rapt attention.

Shang Feifan pushed the water flask and wheat cake toward him.

The little fellow didn't stand on ceremony either, tearing off a piece and shoving it into his mouth along with some plain water, chewing hard.

The village elder came over midway and saw that Shang Feifan had not only repaired his family's flail but had also improved it. After testing it out and finding it remarkably easy to use, a surge of warmth toward Shang Feifan instantly bloomed in his heart.

"This flail you made should be able to boost grain-threshing efficiency quite a bit. Do you mind if I show it to the other villagers?"

"Of course not. I can't possibly make them all by myself. If anyone knows how to make it, let them make it themselves."

The young and sturdy village elder reached out to pat Shang Feifan's shoulder, sighing, "Brother, you're a good person. We almost misunderstood you."

"Daddy," A-Dai babbled, hugging Shang Feifan's lower leg.

Shang Feifan lowered his head: "Can you tell me what's going on with this little thing?"

The village elder sighed before speaking: "Actually, there are many little ones like A-Dai in our village. You should have already noticed by now—this is Tiancan Village."

chunks.chineseText:
第14章 活尸传说

村长当着阿呆的面说出阿呆的身世。

“阿呆不能转变为人形，反应还有些迟钝。他在三年前被人扔到我们天残谷外面，还被人下了药，大概是怕他醒来。等我们发现他，他差点被冻死。”

“我们把他带回村，但他身体一直不太好，长得也比同龄兽人瘦小。另外，我们也不知道他的迟钝是天生，还是药物造成。”

商非凡觉得当着小家伙的面就这么说出他的身世是不是不太好，但村长一脸稀松平常。

“我们从来不会隐瞒这些孩子他们的真正身世。难道想让他们对抛弃他们的人还继续心存幻想吗？”

村长脸上露出冷笑。

“可他跟我说他父亲出门打猎迷路、母亲被咕噜兽吃掉……”

“哈！那都是我们村小孩子瞎编出来的。一开始是村里大人为了哄孩子，后来那些小孩都学会自己骗自己，哪怕我们跟他们说了他们是被抛弃的，他们还是会幻想，甚至会编一个身世来哄自己。说父母被怪兽吃掉、打猎迷路、在外行商还没回来是最常见的。但也就小时候会这样，等他们长大了就不会再自己骗自己。”

商非凡看向阿呆，发现这小东西表情呆愣愣，似乎不知道两个大人正在聊他的身世。

有点古怪，这小东西刚开始和他说话时可没有这么呆。

“这么说这些被遗弃的孤儿都是村人里在养育？”

“也谈不上养育，就是给口饭吃。有些人生不出孩子或者比较喜欢小孩子，会收-养。但大多数都是村里一同养育，等长大一些，村里会统-一-教他们生存知识。”

村长蹲下，揉揉阿呆的脑袋：“这也是我们天残村自古就有的规矩，我们虽然没办法顾得上所有天残，但只要被扔到这里的，我们都会想法给口饭吃，让他们能尽量长到成年，然后选择自己的未来。”

商非凡看村长说得冷漠，但从这个村子的兽人对小兽人的紧张程度来看，他们对这些被遗弃的孤儿也许不能做到像对自己亲生儿女一样关照爱护，也放在了心上。

商非凡心想怪不得玩家出生点会安排在这里，这简直就是最好的“帮扶”对象和发展地。

可惜这里的土著兽人也不知对玩家产生了什么误会，竟然对玩家十分警惕和仇视。

玩家甚至也没有留在这个村子发展，而是跑去外面建设了玩家营地。

或者这种发展原本就是游戏背景设定？

如果是设定的话，游戏策划为什么非要玩家和当地土著一上来就对立？

还是说这个村子还有更大的秘密可以挖掘？

“你们说的活尸是怎么回事？”商非凡想要趁机了解一下情况。

“你不问，我也要跟你说。这件事，还需要你帮个忙，帮忙不要把我们这里出现活尸的事说出去。”村长索性坐到地上。

咦？他还以为村长会让他帮忙传递消息给外面，让外面人想办法来消灭活尸。

“为什么？”商非凡直接问出来。

村长坦言：“因为我们不想村子里的人跟着一起被消灭。”

最重要的是那些活尸虽然让他们头疼，却也没有真的伤害到他们。

商非凡：这是个非常强大的理由。而村长说的情况也确实非常有可能出现。

“我答应你们。实际上我出现在这里，我就和你们绑到一块儿。我如果对外说出这里有活尸，说不定就有人觉得我也沾上了活尸病毒，想要以防万一的杀掉我。”

村长重重点头：“就是这样！如果那些活尸真的很危险，我们自然会派人把消息传递出去。”

商非凡再次明确表示他也不想沾上麻烦。

村长从商非凡的神情看出他没有说谎，这才放松心神开始跟商非凡侃大山。

“你知道我们这个天残谷的由来吗？”

商非凡理所当然摇头。

村长也猜到对方不知道，他只是用这种方式打开话头：“我们天残谷后方，也就是你今天出来的神殿后方曾经是坟地。在很久很久以前，传说是战毁纪甚至是大战纪时期，那里就是坟地。”

商非凡：战毁纪？大战纪？他记得好像还有一个大繁华纪？那现在是什么纪元？复原纪？

这个游戏世界背景设定得还挺复杂。

村长不知道商非凡不知道他们兽人世界的历史，继续按照他自己的节奏述说：“而我们天残谷附近一片，据说在大繁华纪原本是一座极为繁华的大城市，附近还有很多附属城村镇。但是大战纪来临，城市被摧毁，死了很多很多人。这些人就被掩埋在天残谷后方。”

“之后战毁纪期间附近死人也都会埋在那里。那时这里还有很多人居住，据说战毁纪的兽人们就是靠残留下来的遗迹里的东西支撑，直到毒雾纪来临。”

村长提到毒雾纪，脸上不由自主露出恐惧不安和厌恶的神情：“没人知道那些毒雾是怎么冒出来的，就在一天晚上整个兽人世界都冒出了毒雾。因为毒雾，好不容易支撑到战毁纪的兽人们又死了很多很多。”

“有人说那些毒雾来自虫族诅咒，只是谁也无法证明这点。在毒雾中勉强活下来的兽人把附近的死人都集中掩埋到后方那片坟地中。”

“但不知何时，活下来的兽人忽然发现那些死去的兽人竟然又活了，它们从坟地里爬出来，袭击所有看到的活物。这些活尸还很难杀死，身体也奇怪的不会腐烂。一开始，兽人们只能使用火攻，把那些活尸全都烧成灰。”

“但不久，兽人们就发现那些活尸竟然拥有各种神血能力，基本上生前拥有什么能力的尸体，变成活尸后它也能拥有什么能力，就算没有特别能力，也可以刀枪不入。逐渐的，火焰不再能彻底克制活尸，那些活尸越来越灵活，还把一切活物当成食物。”

村长长长吐出一口气，“幸好我们没有活在那个年代，传说毒雾纪是最艰难困苦的时代没有之一。”

“那些活尸后来解决了吗？”商非凡问。

村长点头，骄傲地说：“要没有人解决，也不会有天残谷出现。当时出现一位天残大祭司，她的能力非常厉害，也是非常伟大的一个人。她用献祭自身的方式，把所有活尸都送回墓地，让它们再也不能从地底爬出。那座神殿就是她让人建造出来，用来镇压和祭祀坟地里无数死者。”

“也因为这位的奉献和牺牲，兽人们对天残略微改观，同时也是为了处理天残，当时的兽人们就在神殿前面的山谷里建造了最初的天残村。”

村长大致讲了一些天残村的来历和初期的不容易，没说两句就转回到活尸身上。

“那位天残大祭司献祭自己时曾留下警示，说如果活尸再现，这世界必将……”

“必将怎样？”商非凡没想到村长话说一半就不说了。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 14: The Legend of the Walking Corpses

The village chief revealed Ah-Dai's background right in front of the child.

"Ah-Dai couldn't transform into human form, and his reflexes are a bit slow. Three years ago, he was thrown outside our Heavenly Defect Valley, and someone even drugged him—probably afraid he would wake up. By the time we found him, he was nearly frozen to death."

"We brought him back to the village, but his health has always been poor, and he grows up thinner and smaller than orcs his age. Besides, we don't know whether his slowness is congenital or caused by the drugs."

Shang Feifan felt it might not be the best idea to discuss the child's origins right in front of him, but the village chief wore an expression of complete nonchalance.

"We never hide these children's true backgrounds from them. Do you expect us to let them keep harboring illusions about the people who abandoned them?"

A cold sneer appeared on the village chief's face.

"Yet he told me his father got lost hunting and his mother was eaten by a Gulu beast..."

"Ha! Those are all made up by the little kids in our village. At first, the adults in the village made them up to comfort the kids, but later those children learned to deceive themselves. Even after we tell them they were abandoned, they still fantasize, and they even invent a background story to comfort themselves. Saying their parents were eaten by monsters, got lost while hunting, or went on a trading trip and haven't returned yet are the most common ones. But they only do that when they're little; once they grow up, they stop self-deceiving."

Shang Feifan looked at Ah-Dai and noticed the little thing's expression was blank and dull, as if he didn't realize two adults were discussing his life story.

It was rather peculiar; when this little thing first spoke to him, he hadn't seemed this dull at all.

"Does that mean these abandoned orphans are being raised by the villagers collectively?"

"You can't really call it raising; it's just giving them a bite to eat. Some people who can't have children or particularly like kids will adopt them. But mostly, they are raised by the village as a whole. When they get a bit older, the village uniformly teaches them survival knowledge."

The village chief squatted down and ruffled Ah-Dai's head: "This is also a rule handed down since ancient times in Heavenly Defect Village. Although we have no way to look after every single defect, as long as they are thrown here, we will figure out a way to give them a bite to eat, let them grow into adulthood as best as they can, and then let them choose their own future."

Shang Feifan saw that although the village chief spoke with indifference, judging by how nervous the orcs in this village were about the little orc, perhaps they couldn't shower these abandoned orphans with the same meticulous care and affection as their own biological children, but they certainly kept them in their hearts.

Shang Feifan thought to himself: No wonder the players' spawn point was arranged here; this was quite literally the best "assistance" target and development base.

It was a pity that the native orcs here had somehow misunderstood the players, holding a high degree of vigilance and hostility toward them.

The players hadn't even stayed in this village to develop, choosing instead to run outside and build a player camp.

Or perhaps this development was originally part of the game's background setting?

If it was a set background, why did the game developers insist on forcing players and local natives into opposition right from the start?

Or could it be that this village held an even bigger secret waiting to be uncovered?

"What's the deal with those walking corpses you mentioned?" Shang Feifan wanted to take the opportunity to gather some intelligence.

"Even if you didn't ask, I was going to tell you. This matter requires a favor from you—please help us keep the appearance of walking corpses here a secret." The village chief simply sat down on the ground.

Eh? He had actually expected the village chief to ask him to help spread the word to the outside world so people out there could figure out a way to exterminate the walking corpses.

"Why?" Shang Feifan asked directly.

The village chief spoke frankly: "Because we don't want the people in our village to be wiped out along with them."

Most importantly, while those walking corpses gave them headaches, they hadn't actually harmed them.

Shang Feifan: This was an extremely solid reason. And the scenario the village chief described was indeed highly likely to happen.

"I promise you. In fact, the moment I appeared here, I became tied to your fate. If I go outside and announce that there are walking corpses here, someone might suspect I've also contracted the walking corpse virus and want to kill me 'just in case'."

The village chief nodded heavily: "Exactly! If those walking corpses were truly dangerous, we would naturally send people to pass the word out."

Shang Feifan made it clear once again that he didn't want to get mixed up in trouble either.

From Shang Feifan's expression, the village chief could tell he wasn't lying, which finally allowed him to relax and start shooting the breeze with Shang Feifan.

"Do you know the origin of our Heavenly Defect Valley?"

Shang Feifan naturally shook his head.

The village chief guessed he wouldn't know; he was simply using this as an opening to start the conversation: "Behind our Heavenly Defect Valley—meaning behind the temple you came out of today—used to be a graveyard. A long, long time ago, legend has it that during the War-Ruin Era or even the Great War Era, that place was already a cemetery."

Shang Feifan: The War-Ruin Era? The Great War Era? He seemed to remember there was also a Great Prosperous Era? What era was it now, then? The Restoration Era?

The background lore of this game world was quite complex.

Unaware that Shang Feifan knew nothing of their orcish world's history, the village chief continued narrating at his own pace: "And as for the area around our Heavenly Defect Valley, it's said that during the Great Prosperous Era, it was once an extremely bustling metropolis with many affiliated towns and villages nearby. But when the Great War Era arrived, the city was destroyed, and countless people died. Those people were buried right behind Heavenly Defect Valley."

"Afterward, during the War-Ruin Era, anyone who died nearby was also buried there. At that time, many people still lived here; it is said that the orcs of the War-Ruin Era survived by relying on things found in the surviving ruins, right up until the Poison Fog Era arrived."

Mentioning the Poison Fog Era, the village chief's face involuntarily revealed fear, unease, and disgust: "No one knows how those poison fogs came about. In a single night, poisonous fog erupted across the entire orc world. Because of the poison fog, the orcs who had managed to struggle through the War-Ruin Era died in droves once again."

"Some say those poison fogs came from the Zerg curse, though no one could ever prove it. The orcs who barely survived amidst the poison fog gathered all the nearby dead and buried them collectively in the graveyard behind us."

"But I don't know when it started; the surviving orcs suddenly discovered that those dead orcs had come back to life. They crawled out of the graveyard and attacked every living thing they saw. These walking corpses were extremely difficult to kill, and their bodies strangely refused to rot. At first, the orcs could only use fire attacks, burning all those walking corpses to ashes."

"Not long after, however, the orcs discovered that those walking corpses actually possessed various divine bloodline abilities. Basically, whatever abilities a corpse had possessed in life, it retained after turning into a walking corpse. Even if they had no special abilities, their bodies became impervious to weapons. Gradually, fire could no longer completely restrain the walking corpses; they became increasingly agile and treated all living creatures as food."

The village chief let out a long sigh, "Fortunately, we didn't live in that era. Legend says the Poison Fog Era was the hardest and most bitter era, without exception."

"Were those walking corpses dealt with eventually?" Shang Feifan asked.

The village chief nodded and said proudly: "If no one had dealt with them, Heavenly Defect Village wouldn't exist today. Back then, a Heavenly Defect Great Priestess appeared. Her abilities were terrifyingly formidable, and she was an exceptionally great person. By sacrificing herself, she sent all the walking corpses back to the graveyard, making it impossible for them to crawl out from underground ever again. That temple was built under her orders to suppress and offer sacrifices to the countless dead in the graveyard."

"Because of her dedication and sacrifice, orcs slightly altered their views on the defective, and simultaneously, to handle the discarded defects, the orcs of that era built the original Heavenly Defect Village in the valley in front of the temple."

The village chief roughly recounted the origins of Heavenly Defect Village and its initial hardships, but before he could finish two sentences, he steered the conversation back to the walking corpses.

"When that Heavenly Defect Great Priestess sacrificed herself, she left behind a warning, saying that if the walking corpses ever reappeared, the world would definitely..."

"Definitely what?" Shang Feifan hadn't expected the village chief to stop right in the middle of his sentence.

chunks.chineseText:
村长摆手：“我也不知道。相传那位天残大祭司话没说完人就没了。也有人说是时间太长，没把原话传下来。后来人根据她说的话编了不少预言，但我们天残谷有着初代谷主留下的记录，他记录了那位大祭司的话，他也明确说明那位大祭司没把话说完，所以我们这儿的人从来不相信那些假预言。”

村长还冲着商非凡笑：“你在外面生活，应该听过不少类似的预言吧？”

商非凡还没听到过，但他不能否认，只能含糊点头。

村长：“虽然那位大祭司没把话说完，但我们都能猜出不会是什么好话。”

“所以你们才这么忌惮从那座神殿里走出来的活尸？但你们又怎么知道那些走出来的兽人就是活尸，而不是正常兽人？”

“因为记录上说了，从那座神殿里走出来的只有活尸！”村长脱口说。

商非凡很想看看那份记录，他试探地问了。

村长毫不委婉地一口拒绝：“那份第一代谷主留下的记录只有村里的祭司和村长可以翻看。”

村长又笑：“其实那里面并没有什么保密内容，也没有牵涉到宝藏或遗迹之类。如果有，我们村也不会过得这么穷。不给外人看，只是那是第一位谷主写下的，出于尊重，我们不想给外人看。你能理解吧？”

商非凡表示理解。
