Chapter 24: The Sneaky Glass Sphere (Part 2)

He spent 4 contribution points to purchase the special item: [Shattered Glass Sphere].

This contraption was considered the most dangerous among the four body-monitoring items available. Its primary function seemed to be assisting with curses, while its secondary function was monitoring others' curses placed upon oneself. Its major drawback was that equipping this trinket ran the risk of being dragged into the dark world.

However, this item could simultaneously monitor non-cursed status buffs and conceal the user's own physical condition.

Considering its functional diversity and practicality, Shang Feifan was willing to assume the risk of being pulled into the dark world.

Besides, it was just a game—why overthink it?

Who knows, maybe the dark world would turn out to be even more fun.

With the item in hand, Shang Feifan hadn't even had a proper chance to open his palm and examine his newly purchased special merchandise.

That shattered glass sphere suddenly flew straight out of his palm and slammed directly into his right eye.

Shang Feifan let out a muffled grunt of pain and instinctively clutched his right eye.

Damn this one-hundred-percent pain realism!

It hurt like absolute hell!

Who could have guessed that this broken glass sphere would drill straight into his eye?!

……

Shang Feifan had no idea how long he had lain there; before he even had time to think about logging off, he had completely passed out.

Interestingly enough, passing out inside the game didn't automatically log him out.

This fleeting thought crossed Shang Feifan's mind, but he didn't dwell on it, assuming all other players experienced the same mechanic.

When he opened his eyes once more, he discovered that his field of vision had undergone a novel transformation.

He seemed to perceive distorted rays of light and pulsing symbols.

Yet before he could focus clearly, a stabbing pain flared through his brain.

Shortly afterward, several bizarre symbols popped into his right-eye's field of vision.

These strange symbols warped and twisted back and forth before finally resolving themselves into neatly rendered Orc-world Common Tongue.

[Warning! Mental faculty damaged. The damage was caused by forcibly observing the origin constitution of world energy. Mental Strength: 16(-14)/100. It is recommended to immediately consume medicine or food that restores and pacifies mental strength, and to immediately conduct deep meditation to recover mental energy. Natural recovery to maximum value requires 72 hours.]

[Warning! Body poisoned. The toxin source is the Stinky Fog Fruit; the fog from this fruit induces physical limpness and debility. Strength: 19(-15)/100, Agility: 11(-8)/100, Health Points: 99(-29)/100. Estimated toxin clearance time is approximately 24 hours, with 17 hours remaining. No special treatment is required; there will be no residual toxins. To detoxify prematurely, consume targeted medication or food.]

Both warning prompts were entirely normal and made Shang Feifan feel that the shattered glass sphere was well worth the purchase.

So worth it, in fact, that he could completely overlook the excruciating agony the glass sphere had just inflicted upon his eye.

However, aside from those two alerts, he noticed two additional prompts.

The text for these two prompts was remarkably tiny, radiating an inexplicable, sneaky, gossipy vibe.

[Family, are you currently filled with fury, longing to curse the scoundrels who captured and harmed you? Come on, let us loudly curse those who have wronged you, provided that you recite three times before cursing: 'Supreme and Magnificent Existence, God of Curses Konizeus, I shall offer a sacrifice; please help me curse my enemies.']

[Almost forgot to mention—the sacrifice will determine the effectiveness and scope of the curse.]

Shang Feifan: "..."

chunks.chineseText:
第25章 逃出地牢

这两段内置广告词一看就不太靠谱。

更别说看过多部恐怖片的人都知道这种诱惑小朋友念出咒语的桥段通常都是为了召唤出大boss，谁念谁傻。

商非凡忽略玻璃球的诅咒能力，花了1个贡献点买了一卷十米长的铁丝。

这是目前对他最有帮助、也最便宜的材料。

他刚才查看过游戏商城里的药物，能帮他提前解毒的药物没有一种低于3个贡献点，而他只剩下2个。

商非凡抽出一小段铁丝开始来回拗，直到拗断。

他的力量值因为毒雾果的毒性，只剩下4点，但那是对比他自己，实际上普通一级玩家的力量属性也就4、5点。

拗断两根铁丝，把其中一根拧成套圈钩状，一根折叠。

再把两根加工过的铁丝戳进锁眼，耐心摸索。

咔哒，手铐的锁打开了。

商非凡迅速去掉手铐，揉揉手腕，继续破解脚镣的锁头。

咔哒，脚镣的锁头也被他打开。

商非凡没有急着去打开牢房的门锁，而是先把剩余的铁丝缠到自己手腕上，再把手铐和脚镣虚虚套在自己的手腕和脚腕上。

他之前查看过牢房门锁。

可能就是为了防止囚犯撬锁，牢房大门是从外面锁上，锁头在外面。

而牢房栅栏之间的缝隙非常狭窄，他没办法把手伸出去开锁。

他现在的力气也不足以掰弯掰断栅栏。

按照玻璃珠给他的提醒，他想恢复巨力还需要等待十七个小时。

但商非凡不想干等十七个小时，当他做好伪装，他就走到门边，半趴半靠在牢门上，用手铐用力敲击牢房门。

虚弱地喊：“有人吗？放我出去。我在其他地方藏了一批货物，只要你们放我出去，我就告诉你们那些货物藏在哪里。”

哐哐的敲击声在地牢中不断回响，引来了一些骂声。

商非凡这才知道地牢里关的人不止他一个，但听声音也不多。

“别敲了！他们不会理睬的。不到时间，就算你死在里面，他们也不会多管。”一道真虚弱的声音从不远处响起。

商非凡：“那他们什么时候才会过来查看情况？”

“一天一次，他们会过来泼一勺泔水，确保我们不会饿死。他们上次下来的时候，就是把你送进来的时候，等他们下次来，还要大半天。”

“那些天杀的强盗！他们就是故意的，他们不想我们饿死渴死，但也不想我们舒坦。他们不会打开门，会从外面泼一勺泔水到牢房里，就是想要看我们趴在地上舔那点他们吃剩下不要的脏东西！”另一道声音大骂。

“你们都是什么人？也是被抓来的游商吗？”商非凡抱着打发时间的想法，找同处地牢的倒霉鬼们聊天。

地牢里突然安静下来，过了一会儿才有人带着一点痛苦的语调说：“我不是游商，我就是附近村子的村民，我出来打猎，想要给家里添一点肉食，稍微走远了一点，就被这些强盗给抓来了。”

“那你被关了多久？”

“不知道，可能有四五天了吧。”

另一道属于中年人的声音响起：“这个地牢里的人都待不长久，最多七八天就会被提出去。最后结果要么就是加入那些强盗，给他们做苦力。要么就是被他们当奴隶卖掉。”

“别想要逃跑，会被杀掉！”第三个声音响起：“这些强盗杀人不眨眼，他们是真的会杀人。我亲眼看到他们上次把一个试图逃跑的青壮给活活砍死了！”

“艹！老子竟然还被关着。”第四个声音突兀地加进来，但这个人说的话显然不是兽人通用语。

商非凡：玩家？

那名玩家大概也知道地牢中的兽人听不懂他说什么，就很随意地骂了一连串脏话，又咕哝：“这破游戏体感一流，但也太难玩了。老子都被关了两天，还不如自杀死回去。”

那名玩家又骂：“那些混蛋，说好来救老子，一个都没来！这个侦查任务，接的太亏了！两天时间啊，老子要是用来练级，说不定都能再升一级。”

该玩家过了一会儿又心疼自己的衣服装备武器和那本皮质笔记本，大骂游戏开发商变态，连条底裤都不给他留。

“要不是他们说这可能是一个隐藏副本，有可能触发奇遇任务，老子真的不想再待下去。”

该玩家还不知道自己的抱怨全都被人听了去，他抱怨完，就试图用蹩脚的兽人通用语和几个被关的兽人搭话。

商非凡不得不佩服这名玩家，这时候都还想领取任务，还想从被关的兽人中找出隐藏的职业大师，好拜入其门下，好比其他玩家抢得先机，修习隐藏职业，从此走上游戏世界玩家高手之列。

被关的兽人可能被饿得没力气，都不怎么想说话。

商非凡见没一会儿大家就不说话了，就决定下线。

回到现实世界，商非凡先查看监测仪器上的数据显示，没看到太大变化。

接收数据的研究所那边也没有特意跟他说什么，应该是一切都正常。

商非凡转而打开电脑上游戏论坛查看最新消息。

目前为止，这个游戏招募的内测玩家只有一千五百人，游戏论坛上活跃的绝大多数都不是真正玩家，而是听到风声跑过来嘲讽的云玩家。

这些云玩家压根不相信凭现在的技术已经能研发出百分百真实的全息游戏，叫嚣着让开发商放出更多内测账号，他们好验一验真假。

但游戏开发商似乎并不急着进行大面积公测，任凭云玩家怎么质疑，他们还是不肯放出第四批申请。

真正进入游戏的一千五百名玩家自然知道游戏是真全息，但无论他们怎么解释，云玩家和专门来找茬的人还是不相信。

偏偏这个游戏又没有内置拍照和摄像功能，真玩家们想要证实也很难。

到最后，这些真玩家也懒得跟云玩家们解释，他们玩他们的，任由云玩家和喷子们怀疑和嘲笑。

商非凡看到了一个特别火的帖子，是真玩家给游戏开发商提出的各种建议和抗议。

包括但不限于，要求人手最少一个空间背包，要求初期升级速度加快，要求职业技能能更容易学会，要求材料能无限量供应，要求游戏世界内时间加速等等。

更多玩家提出他们希望能一键学会各种技能，而不是要像真实世界一样一点点靠大脑、靠身体去掌握。

除此之外，玩家还希望能增加建筑模块、增添种田加速器，以及要求开通情缘系统，能有实际接触那种。

还有女玩家提议去性别化，把所有兽人都搞成天使身体，外表也不区分男女，同时除了玩家自己以外都不能脱下玩家内衣。

还有玩家反应现在的游戏内容比较无聊，搬砖种田建设营地居多，而他们更想打怪升级。

对此，游戏开发商新开了一个帖子回复，表示在近期会有一次大的版本更新升级，敬请玩家期待。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 25: Escaping the Dungeon (Part 1)

These two built-in promotional blurbs looked sketchy as hell at first glance.

Not to mention, anyone who had watched more than a few horror films knew that plots enticing little kids to read aloud incantations were usually just summoning some major boss. Only an idiot would actually read them.

Ignoring the glass sphere's cursed potential, Shang Feifan spent 1 Contribution Point to buy a ten-meter-long coil of iron wire.

Currently, this was the most helpful and cheapest material available to him.

He had just checked the game mall's medicine inventory, and not a single detoxifying drug that could speed up his recovery cost less than 3 Contribution Points. Yet he only had 2 left.

Shang Feifan pulled out a short section of wire and began bending it back and forth until it snapped.

Due to the toxicity of the Poison Mist Fruit, his strength stat had dropped to a mere 4 points. But that was only by his own standards; in reality, the strength attribute of an ordinary Level 1 player was only around 4 or 5.

Snapping two pieces of wire, he twisted one into a looped hook shape and folded the other in half.

Then, he poked the two modified wires into the keyhole and began patiently probing around.

*Click.* The handcuff lock popped open.

Shang Feifan quickly slipped off the handcuffs, rubbed his wrists, and moved on to pick the lock on his leg irons.

*Click.* The shackles on his ankles sprang open as well.

Instead of rushing to unlock the cell door, Shang Feifan first wound the remaining wire tightly around his wrists, then loosely slipped the handcuffs and leg irons back onto his wrists and ankles as a disguise.

He had inspected the cell door lock earlier.

Perhaps to prevent prisoners from picking the locks, the cell doors locked from the outside, with the locking mechanism positioned externally.

Furthermore, the gaps between the cell bars were extremely narrow, making it impossible for him to reach his arm outside to pick the lock.

His current strength was also nowhere near enough to bend or snap the bars.

According to the hint given by the glass bead, he would have to wait another seventeen hours for his superhuman strength to return.

However, Shang Feifan had no intention of just sitting around for seventeen hours. Once his disguise was in place, he walked over to the door, slumped half-lying and half-leaning against the cell gate, and banged loudly against it with his handcuffs.

"Hello? Anyone there? Let me out!" he cried out weakly. "I've hidden a batch of cargo elsewhere. As long as you let me out, I'll tell you where it's stashed."

The loud, clanging blows echoed endlessly through the dungeon, drawing a few curses from the shadows.

It was only then that Shang Feifan realized he wasn't the only one locked up down here, though judging by the voices, there weren't many prisoners.

"Stop banging! They won't pay you any mind. Until the time comes, they won't give a damn even if you die in here," a genuinely feeble voice sounded from not far away.

Shang Feifan asked, "Then when do they come to check on things?"

"Once a day. They come by to splash a ladle of slop to make sure we don't starve to death. The last time they came down was when they dragged you in here. It's going to be more than half a day before they show up again."

"Those goddamned bandits! They do it on purpose. They don't want us to starve or die of thirst, but they don't want us comfortable either. They won't open the door; they just fling a ladle of slop through the bars from the outside because they want to watch us crawl on the floor and lick up their leftover garbage!" another voice cursed bitterly.

"What kind of people are you? Are you also traveling merchants who got caught?" Thinking to pass the time, Shang Feifan tried striking up a conversation with his unlucky cellmates.

The dungeon suddenly fell silent. After a moment, someone spoke up with a slightly agonizing tone, "I'm no traveling merchant. I'm just a villager from a nearby settlement. I went out hunting, hoping to get some meat for my family, and wandered a bit too far before these bandits grabbed me."

"How long have you been locked up, then?"

"Who knows? Maybe four or five days."

Another voice, belonging to a middle-aged man, chimed in, "Nobody stays in this dungeon for long. Within seven or eight days at most, you get hauled out. The end result is either joining those bandits to do coolie work for them, or getting sold off as a slave."

"Don't even think about running—you'll be killed!" a third voice piped up. "These bandits blink an eye at murder; they actually kill people. I saw with my own eyes how they brutally hacked a strong young man to death the last time he tried to escape!"

"Shit! I'm still locked up?" A fourth voice abruptly joined in, but the language this person spoke was clearly not the Beastmen Common Tongue.

*A player?* Shang Feifan thought.

The player probably knew the beastmen in the dungeon couldn't understand him, so he casually let loose a string of curses before grumbling, "The sensory immersion in this crappy game is top-tier, but it's way too hard to play. I've been locked up for two days straight; I'd be better off committing suicide and respawning."

The player cursed again: "Those bastards said they were coming to rescue me, and not a single one showed up! Taking on this scouting quest was a total rip-off! Two whole days—if I'd spent that time grinding levels, I might have ranked up again by now."

After a little while, the player began mourning his lost clothes, equipment, weapons, and leather-bound notebook. He railed against the game developers for being perverts who wouldn't even leave him a pair of underwear.

"If they hadn't claimed this might be a hidden dungeon capable of triggering a serendipitous encounter quest, I really wouldn't want to stay here another minute."

Unaware that all his complaints had been overheard, the player tried to strike up a conversation with the imprisoned beastmen using broken Beastmen Common Tongue as soon as he finished venting.

Shang Feifan had to admire this player. Even under these circumstances, he was still trying to trigger quests and fish for a hidden profession master among the captive beastmen, hoping to apprentice under them so he could seize the initiative over other players, master a hidden class, and rise into the ranks of the game world's elite.

Perhaps too malnourished to muster the energy, the imprisoned beastmen showed little interest in talking.

Seeing that everyone fell quiet again shortly after, Shang Feifan decided to log off.

Back in the real world, Shang Feifan first checked the data on his monitoring equipment and saw no major fluctuations.

Neither did the research institute receiving the data reach out with any special notices, meaning everything should be normal.

Turning on his computer, Shang Feifan opened the game forum to check the latest news.

So far, only fifteen hundred closed-beta players had been recruited for this game. The vast majority of active users on the forum weren't actual players, but armchair gamers who had caught wind of it and rushed over to mock the project.

These armchair critics simply refused to believe that current technology could develop a one-hundred-percent realistic holographic game. They clamored for the developers to release more closed-beta accounts so they could verify its authenticity.

Yet the game developers seemed in no rush to launch a large-scale open beta; no matter how the skeptics questioned them, they steadfastly refused to issue a fourth wave of applications.

The fifteen hundred players who had actually entered the game naturally knew that the holographic experience was real. But no matter how they explained it, the armchair gamers and deliberate trolls refused to believe them.

Unfortunately, the game lacked a built-in screenshot and video-recording function, making it extremely difficult for the genuine players to prove their claims.

In the end, these real players couldn't be bothered to argue with the skeptics anymore. They simply played their own game, leaving the trolls and haters to doubt and ridicule as they pleased.

Shang Feifan spotted a particularly popular post containing various suggestions and protests submitted to the developers by real players.

These included, but were not limited to: demanding at least one spatial storage bag per person, requesting faster early-game leveling speeds, making professional skills easier to master, demanding unlimited supplies of crafting materials, and accelerating time within the game world.

Even more players requested a one-click learning function for all skills, rather than having to rely on their brains and bodies to master them bit by bit just like in the real world.

Additionally, players hoped to add architectural building modules, farming accelerators, and an officially supported romance system that allowed for physical intimacy.

Some female players even suggested desegregating genders by turning all beastmen into angelic physiques with gender-neutral appearances, while locking player undergarments so they could never be removed by anyone other than the player themselves.

Other players complained that the current game content was too boring—mostly consisting of carrying bricks, farming, and building campsites—whereas they were yearning to slay monsters and level up.

In response, the game developers opened a new thread announcing that a major version update would be released in the near future, urging players to stay tuned.

chunks.chineseText:
商非凡也对新版本很感兴趣，他在猜游戏开发商有没有发现游戏中-出现了第二个游戏系统这样的巨大bug，在下一次版本更新时会不会消灭掉这个bug。

农场的活很消耗时间，商非凡忙了一天，洗完澡吃完饭，跟下线的伏向军打了个招呼，让他帮忙留意阿呆和他的坐骑狰爷，就又戴上游戏头盔上线了。

商非凡卡的时间刚刚好，他上线不到十分钟，送饭的强盗就来了。

该强盗就跟其他被关兽人说的一样，特别恶劣，不但大声辱骂他们，还故意把桶里的泔水从栅栏缝里泼到牢房地面上。

当饥渴得受不了的囚徒趴在地上去舔那些泔水时，那个送饭强盗就会哈哈大笑。

商非凡一上线就查看了自己的生命值和力气值，他身体里的毒性已经被代谢得七七八八，但饥渴降低了他的生命值以及其他生理数据。

如果这是现实，商非凡会淡定地去收集地面的泔水来给自己保持体力。

但这是游戏，他没必要这么委屈自己。

哪怕一上游戏，他就感受到饥火烧肠嗓子冒烟的饥渴感。

“哐哐。”商非凡用手铐敲了敲牢房门，引起送饭强盗的注意。

“兄弟，我不求你放我出去，只要你每天给我一碗干净的水和一块正常的干饼，我就把我藏货物的地方告诉你。”

送饭强盗被吸引了，靠近牢房门：“你说什么？你藏了一批货物？”

“对。”商非凡真诚地说：“我不想死。吃这些东西，我就算不会被饿死，也会生病。我不管你们将来是想让我入伙，还是要卖掉我，我只是不想死，我会手艺，到哪里都能活下去，但有个好身体，也能让我找个好主顾。”

送饭强盗定定看了商非凡好一会儿，阴森森道：“你是不是以为我很蠢？”

商非凡摇头：“只要一碗干净的水和一块干净的麦饼，你就能知道我说的是真的还是假的。我就算欺骗你，也只能骗你一次。难道我就不怕谎言戳穿，你报复我？”

送饭强盗嘴角勾起：“不，蠢货，现在你需要用你藏起来的货物换你的生命！如果你不肯说，我会从你的手指开始，一根根掰断它、踩碎它，让你成为彻底的废物。”

商非凡靠在牢房门边上，眼中露出赤-裸裸的嘲讽：“你敢吗？我可是你们抢来的重要货物，留着我的手指，你们还能把我卖个高价。废掉我的手指，你老大同意了吗？”

“嗤！像你这样的人，老子遇到的太多了。”送饭强盗露出狞笑，放下泔水桶：“你现在只有一次机会，老实说出你藏货物的地点，否则我就进去了。”

商非凡眼中嘲讽更甚：“你以为我会害怕？有种你进来，只怕你根本不敢，还是去找你老大来见我吧。”

“你还想见我们老大？我呸！老子数到三，你再不说……你小子可别后悔！”送饭强盗解开腰间挂的钥匙，作势要打开牢房门。

商非凡一副吃定了送饭强盗的模样，似乎完全不担心送饭强盗会真的进来。

送饭强盗眼神变冷，他想他需要教训一下这个似乎有恃无恐的囚徒，让他知道这个地牢里到底是谁做主。

“小子，你完了，你有再多货物也救不了你！”送饭强盗打开了牢房门，庞大的身体走进牢房。

其他伙计跟他叮嘱过，说这个被抓的修理商力气很大，但送饭强盗自认力气也很大，何况对方还戴着沉重的手铐和脚镣，毒雾果的效用时间也还没过去，他不信这个修理商能在他手底下翻出天去。

砰！

送饭强盗甚至都没有看清楚那个修理商的动作，他就觉得眼前一花，接着就有沉重的东西击中了他的脑袋。

送饭强盗身体晃了晃。

商非凡抄起手铐，对着送饭强盗鼻梁又来了一次重击。

送饭强盗鼻血爆流，开瓢的脑袋跟着流出血液，手还没有抬起捂住鼻子，身体就轰地跪倒。

商非凡为了防止对方还能爬起来，对他后脑勺又是毫无人性的一击。

脑袋破碎的送饭强盗脸朝下趴在地上，变得无声无息。

商非凡扯下钥匙，走出牢房门。

地牢里几道声音同时响起：“发生了什么事？”

“兄弟，你还活着吗？”

商非凡走到附近一间囚牢外，用钥匙打开牢房门。

关在里面的囚徒不可置信地看向商非凡。

地牢里很暗，只有送饭强盗进来时顺手挂在墙上的一盏油肚虫灯发出光亮。

商非凡把钥匙扔给那名玩家，用兽人语说：“你去解救他们，设法带他们离开。如果不能，就自己想办法逃出去。”

该玩家只听懂一半，但他能看懂商非凡的意思啊，当即兴奋道：“好的好的，我一定会解救他们！”

虽然皮质笔记本不在，他不确定自己有没有接收到新任务，但只冲着能救人、还能从牢里逃出去这点，就老刺激了！

商非凡把救人的事丢给玩家，就不管了。

他转身向地牢外走去。

地牢里传出纷乱声，有人在喊先救救我，也有人在对商非凡喊，让他小心外面的强盗。

商非凡走上台阶，伸手握住地牢对外大门的门把手，轻轻一拉，发现是锁着的。

后面有兽人跟上来，对他低声说：“这道门锁只有外面的兽人能打开，就是为了防止这种情况发生。”
chunks.englishText:
Xiao Yan was also quite interested in the new version. He wondered if the game developers had discovered the massive bug—the appearance of a second game system within the game—and whether they would wipe out this bug during the next version update.

Farm work was extremely time-consuming. After a busy day, Xiao Yan took a shower, had dinner, and checked in with Fu Xiangjun, who had already logged off, asking him to keep an eye on A-Dai and his mount, the Ferocious Beast. Then, he put on his gaming helmet and logged back online.

Xiao Yan timed his entry perfectly. Less than ten minutes after he logged in, the food-delivering bandit arrived.

Just as the other imprisoned beastmen had described, this bandit was exceptionally vicious. Not only did he hurl loud insults at them, but he also intentionally splashed the slop from the bucket through the bars and onto the stone floor of the cell.

When the starving and thirsty prisoners crawled across the ground to lick up that slop, the food-delivering bandit would burst into loud laughter.

As soon as he logged in, Xiao Yan checked his health points and strength value. The toxicity in his body had been mostly metabolized, but hunger and thirst had severely drained his health and other physiological stats.

If this were reality, Xiao Yan would calmly collect the slop off the ground to maintain his stamina.

But this was a game; he had no need to wrong himself to that extent.

Even the moment he entered the game, he felt a burning hunger in his gut and a throat parched as if smoking.

*Clang, clang.* Xiao Yan tapped the cell door with his handcuffs to draw the food delivery bandit's attention.

"Brother, I'm not asking you to let me out. As long as you give me a bowl of clean water and a normal piece of dried flatbread every day, I'll tell you where I hid my goods."

The food delivery bandit was hooked, drawing closer to the cell door. "What did you say? You hid a batch of goods?"

"That's right," Xiao Yan said sincerely. "I don't want to die. Eating this garbage, even if I don't starve, I'll get sick. I don't care whether you want me to join your crew or sell me off in the future, I just don't want to die. I have skills and can survive anywhere, but having a good physique will also help me find a good master."

The food delivery bandit stared fixedly at Xiao Yan for a good while before saying darkly, "Do you take me for a fool?"

Xiao Yan shook his head. "Just a bowl of clean water and a clean wheat cake is all it takes for you to know whether what I'm saying is true or false. Even if I'm trying to deceive you, I can only do it once. Aren't I afraid that once the lie is exposed, you'll retaliate against me?"

The corner of the food delivery bandit's mouth curled up. "No, idiot, right now *you* are the one who needs to trade your hidden goods for your life! If you refuse to speak, I'll start with your fingers, breaking them one by one, crushing them until you're completely disabled."

Leaning against the edge of the cell door, Xiao Yan's eyes flashed with naked mockery. "Do you dare? I'm an important piece of merchandise you guys snatched. Keeping my fingers intact means you can still sell me for a high price. If you cripple my fingers, did your boss agree to it?"

"Tch! Guys like you, I've seen too many," the food delivery bandit sneered, setting down the slop bucket. "You only have one chance now. Honestly tell me where you hid the goods, or else I'm coming in."

Xiao Yan's mockery deepened. "You think I'm scared? If you've got the guts, come on in. I'm just afraid you don't dare at all—you'd better go find your boss to see me instead."

"You still want to see our boss? Bah! I'll count to three. If you still don't talk... don't you go crying and regretting it, kid!" The food delivery bandit unhooked the keys hanging from his waist, making a motion to open the cell door.

Xiao Yan wore an expression of absolute certainty, acting as if he wasn't worried in the slightest that the bandit would actually step inside.

The bandit's gaze turned cold. He felt he needed to teach this seemingly unfazed prisoner a lesson and let him know who was really in charge of this dungeon.

"Kid, you're done for. No matter how many goods you have, they won't save you now!" The food delivery bandit unlocked the cell door, his massive frame stepping inside.

His buddies had warned him that this captured repairman possessed immense strength, but the bandit considered himself quite strong as well. Moreover, the target was still wearing heavy handcuffs and foot shackles, and the duration of the Poison Mist Fruit's effect hadn't worn off yet. He refused to believe this repairman could flip the tables on him.

*Bang!*

Before the food delivery bandit could even clearly see the repairman's movements, a blur crossed his vision, followed immediately by a heavy impact striking his head.

The bandit's body swayed.

Seizing his handcuffs, Xiao Yan delivered a second heavy blow straight to the bandit's bridge of the nose.

Blood gushed violently from the bandit's nose, and blood began to seep from his split scalp. Before he could even raise a hand to shield his face, his body collapsed hard to his knees.

To prevent the guy from getting back up, Xiao Yan delivered another merciless blow to the back of his head.

The bandit, his skull fractured, collapsed face-first onto the ground and fell completely still.

Xiao Yan stripped the keys and stepped out of the cell door.

Several voices rang out simultaneously from the dungeon:
"What happened?"
"Brother, are you still alive?"

Xiao Yan walked over to a nearby cell and unlocked the door with the key.

The prisoner locked inside stared at Xiao Yan in disbelief.

The dungeon was pitch black, illuminated only by a belly-worm oil lamp that the food delivery bandit had casually hung on the wall when he entered.

Xiao Yan tossed the keys to the player and said in the beastman tongue, "Go release them and find a way to lead them out. If you can't, figure out a way to escape on your own."

The player only understood half of it, but he could clearly grasp Xiao Yan's intent. He immediately said with excitement, "Got it, got it! I'll definitely rescue them!"

Although his leather notebook was gone and he wasn't sure if he had officially received a new quest, just the prospect of saving people and escaping the dungeon was insanely thrilling!

Having dumped the task of saving people onto the player, Xiao Yan paid him no further mind.

He turned and walked toward the exit of the dungeon.

Chaotic noises erupted from the dungeon; someone was shouting to be saved first, while others were calling out to Xiao Yan, warning him to be careful of the bandits outside.

Xiao Yan walked up the steps, reached out to grip the handle of the outer dungeon door, and gave it a gentle tug, only to find it locked.

A beastman followed closely behind him and whispered, "This door lock can only be opened by the beastmen outside. It's meant to prevent situations like this."

chunks.chineseText:
第26章 讨债新方法

这道门还没有锁眼，商非凡的铁丝也派不上用场。

几个被解救的兽人都挤到了门边，一时都不知道该怎么办。

有个兽人竟然还低声说：“要么我们回去吧，如果被他们发现我们逃出来，说不定会把我们都杀了。”

“那你自己回去蹲着好了！没种的家伙！”一名中年兽人怒斥，他手上拿着脚镣当武器。

其他几个兽人也都拿着手铐或脚镣，没有一个想要回去等死。

那名胆小兽人缩了缩脖子，慢慢地挪到最后，但也没有蹲回地牢里。

玩家兽人也过来了，手里扶着一个已经没有力气的生病兽人。

那名兽人拉肚子拉了好几天，眼看人都快不行了。

商非凡回头，问他身后最近的那名中年兽人：“这扇大门是朝我们这边开，还是朝外开？”

中年兽人回忆：“应该是朝我们这边开。”

另外两名兽人也点头。

商非凡示意所有人站到门背后的方向，并嘱咐中年兽人和另一名兽人，在大门打开时，用力抵住大门，不让大门全部打开。

几个兽人虽然不太明白商非凡的作战思路，但在其他人都没有更好办法的情况下，决定就听他的。

“不过我们要怎么让外面强盗毫无防备地打开这扇门？”中年兽人低声问。

如果外面的强盗有了防备，他们想要逃出去就更难，更别说他们已经被饿了好几天，还有人病得连路都走不动。

商非凡没说他要怎么让外面打开这扇门，又问：“他们有开门暗号吗？”

中年兽人不确定地摇头：“我不记得了。”

另一名兽人小声说：“我记得送饭强盗每次出去都会敲几下大门，喊一声给爷爷开门。到底敲几下，好像每次都不同。”

商非凡点头，叮嘱几人：“门打开，我会先冲出去。你们听到我叫你们出来，你们再一起冲出。在我呼喊你们之前，不要轻举妄动。”

几个兽人一起-点头，握紧手中武器，深呼吸。

玩家兽人的神色最轻松，他不怕死亡，对他来说这场逃生就是游戏，成功最好，不成功不过是要再打一次副本。

商非凡看向玩家兽人：“你保护他们。”

玩家兽人一口答应，用半生不熟的兽人语回：“交给我！”

商非凡抓着脚镣用力敲击大门，对门外喊：“给爷爷开门！”

几名兽人震惊地睁大眼睛。

这声音不说和送饭强盗一模一样，但他们听来就是送饭强盗在喊话。

玩家兽人眼睛溜圆：哇哦，口技吗？有点酷，想学！

外面传来开门锁的声音。

商非凡比了个手势，中年兽人和另一名体力保持还不错的兽人连忙抵住大门。

大门被往内推开。

商非凡提起挂在墙上的油肚虫灯，先一步提高塞进打开的门缝中。

开门的人只看到一片灯光，下意识撇开目光。

商非凡抓起油灯往对方脸上一砸，同时拉开门缝冲了出去。

“啊啊啊！”被油灯砸中脸的强盗发出惨叫，灯里的火焰碰到流出来的灯油，腾地一下就燃烧起来。

门后的小屋子内有两名强盗值守。

一名强盗脸被烧着，正在捂脸惨叫。

商非凡不等他叫出第二声，就一锁链抽在他脸上，把他抽昏了过去。

另一名低头打盹的强盗一惊之下，猛地抬头，但还不等他抓起手边武器，一道黑影袭来。

脚镣锁链重重砸在他的脑门上。

毫无防备的值守强盗当即就被砸晕。

商非凡转头就溜到门边，打开一条门缝向外偷看。

还好，这不是什么地狱级难度的监牢，这扇门外面再无建筑，门外就是一片空旷，附近有几栋建筑，能看到有兽人在走动。

商非凡轻轻掩上门，返身迅速扒下昏迷强盗的衣服，迅速穿上，又抄起昏迷强盗放在桌边的长刃骨刀。

“可以出来了，动静小点。”

通向地牢的大门被拉开，几个兽人小心翼翼地鱼贯走出。

商非凡指了指对外的大门：“出去就是一个大院子，外面兽人不算多，但现在天还没黑，就这样逃出去很容易被发现，我建议你们在这里等到太阳落山再出去。但留在这里也有可能碰到来换班的兽人，你们自己决定。”

几个兽人心里一惊，“你不和我们一起逃吗？”

商非凡：“我对这里同样不熟悉。人多反而显眼，你们最好也分散跑，跑掉一个是一个。”

几个兽人互看，也没有强求非要让商非凡带着自己，他们心里也担心在危险时候，这个兽人会把他们推出去吸引注意力。

毕竟都是陌生兽人，完全没有信任可言。

“我也觉得等到天黑比较好。如果有换班兽人过来，我们想办法弄死他们，还能多弄到一点衣服和武器。”中年兽人开口。

玩家兽人举手。

大家一起看向他。

玩家兽人操着半生不熟的兽人语：“我们还需要药物，这里有病人。”

没有人说话。

生病的兽人气若游丝，他的眼中满是绝望，对玩家兽人虚弱地说：“不用带着我，我这样，肯定逃不出去。留下，说不定还有一条活路。”

玩家兽人咬牙：“……我会想办法给你找药，现在还不到绝望的时候。”

生病兽人摇头：“谢谢你，小兄弟。我不想连累你，我甚至不认识你。”

玩家兽人踟躇，理智上他知道这只是一个游戏NPC，就算死了也无所谓，不过一段数据。但无奈这些NPC的表现实在太像真实的人，再想到游戏策划说的这些NPC全都具有唯一性，死了就再也不会出现，这让他越发不想轻易放弃这名NPC。

其他兽人仍旧沉默，他们自身难保，也不想带着这么一个拖累，但也不至于在这时落井下石，只能沉默。

一颗小黑点突然抛向玩家兽人。

玩家兽人下意识伸手一抄。

商非凡眼神不带温度地说：“这是治疗痢疾的药物，给他吃下，能不能活下去就看他的运气。记住，你们欠我二十个银达鲁。如果这个人死了，就你来还。”

商非凡略心疼，这可是他用2个宝贵贡献点买下来的药物。叫价二十银达鲁，他都觉得亏。

算了，就当日行一善。

玩家兽人大喜，顾不得去想这名看上去就特别帅特别碉的兽人是从哪里弄来的药丸，当即就把药丸塞进生病兽人的嘴里。

其他兽人也惊讶又羡慕地看向商非凡。

但也没有人多问，都以为商非凡很可能在身上藏了什么东西，这也解开了被囚禁兽人们的疑惑——这名虎族兽人肯定是吃了解毒-药，才能恢复力气打倒那个送饭兽人，还解决了值守室内的两个兽人。

生病兽人也没想到峰回路转，自己还能有这样的运气。

不知道是不是心理作用，药丸一下肚，他顿时觉得好多了，不但肚子不再咕噜噜，他脱力的身体也恢复了一些力气。

生病兽人跟商非凡道谢，允诺脱困后一定会偿还这份恩情，还小声询问商非凡的名字和籍贯。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 26: A New Method of Debt Collection (Part 1)

This door didn't even have a keyhole, making Shang Feifan's iron wire completely useless.

The several rescued beastmen crowded around the entrance, all at a loss for what to do next.

One beastman even muttered in a low voice, "Maybe we should just go back. If they find out we broke out, they might just slaughter all of us."

"Then go crouch in your cell by yourself, you spineless coward!" a middle-aged beastman roared angrily, holding a pair of leg irons as a makeshift weapon.

The other beastmen also clutched handcuffs or shackles; not a single one intended to go back and wait for death.

The timid beastman shrank his neck, slowly retreating to the back of the group, though he didn't dare crawl back into the dungeon either.

The player-beastman hurried over as well, supporting a sick beastman who had run out of strength.

That sick beastman had been suffering from severe diarrhea for days, and he looked so frail he was on the verge of collapsing.

Turning back, Shang Feifan asked the middle-aged beastman standing closest to him, "Does this heavy door open inward toward us, or outward?"

The middle-aged beastman recalled, "It should open inward toward our side."

The two other beastmen nodded in agreement.

Shang Feifan gestured for everyone to position themselves behind the door and instructed the middle-aged beastman and another to brace their weight against the portal the moment it opened, preventing it from swinging fully open.

Though the beastmen didn't quite grasp Shang Feifan's tactical reasoning, with no better options among them, they decided to follow his lead.

"But how are we supposed to get the outside bandits to open this door without raising their guard?" the middle-aged beastman whispered.

If the bandits outside were alerted, escaping would become infinitely harder—let alone the fact that they had been starved for days, with some so sick they couldn't even walk.

Without explaining how he planned to make the outside guards open the door, Shang Feifan asked instead, "Do they have a password to open it?"

The middle-aged beastman shook his head uncertainly. "I don't remember."

Another beastman chimed in quietly, "I remember every time the food-delivery bandit goes out, he knocks on the big door a few times and shouts 'Open up for your grandpa!' But the number of knocks seems different every time."

Shang Feifan nodded and instructed the group, "When the door opens, I'll charge out first. Wait until I call for you before you rush out together. Do not act rashly until I give the word."

The beastmen nodded in unison, gripping their weapons tightly and taking deep breaths.

The player-beastman wore the most relaxed expression of all. He wasn't afraid of dying; to him, this prison break was just a game. Success was great, and failure simply meant replaying the dungeon.

Looking at the player-beastman, Shang Feifan said, "Protect them."

The player agreed without hesitation, replying in halting beastmen speak, "Leave it to me!"

Gripping the leg irons, Shang Feifan pounded heavily against the massive door and yelled toward the outside, "Open up for your grandpa!"

The beastmen stared in shock, eyes wide.

While not completely identical to the delivery bandit, to their ears, that was the exact voice of the meal-delivery guard calling out.

The player-beastman's eyes went round: *Whoa, ventriloquism? Pretty cool, I want to learn that!*

The sound of a lock turning came from the other side.

Shang Feifan flashed a hand signal, and the middle-aged beastman along with another physically stable companion immediately pressed their weight against the door.

The heavy door pushed inward.

Lifting the oil-belly worm lamp hanging on the wall, Shang Feifan shoved it through the opening crack first.

The person opening the door saw only a sudden glare of light and instinctively averted their eyes.

Hurl-smashing the oil lamp straight into the person's face, Shang Feifan yanked the door wider and surged outside.

"Ahhh!" The bandit whose face was struck by the lamp let out a miserable shriek as the flames inside the lamp contacted the spilling oil and flared up instantly.

Two bandits had been standing guard inside the small room behind the door.

One of them had his face set ablaze, clutching his head and screaming in agony.

Before the man could squeak out a second cry, Shang Feifan lashed out with a chain of handcuffs, striking him across the face and knocking him cold.

Startled awake, the second guard—who had been nodding off—abruptly jerked his head up. But before he could grab the weapon at his side, a dark shadow struck him.

The heavy iron chain of the leg irons smashed mercilessly against his forehead.

The unprepared guard was instantly knocked unconscious.

Slipping over to the door frame, Shang Feifan peeked cautiously outside.

Fortunately, this wasn't some hell-difficulty prison; there were no buildings directly outside this door. It opened onto an open courtyard with a few surrounding structures where a few beastmen could be seen wandering around.

Pulling the door closed slightly, Shang Feifan turned back, rapidly stripped the clothes off the unconscious guard to put them on himself, and scooped up the long-bladed bone knife the guard had left by the table.

"You can come out now. Keep the noise down."

The dungeon door was pulled open, and the beastmen cautiously filed out one by one.

Pointing toward the outer gate, Shang Feifan said, "Right outside is a large courtyard. There aren't many beastmen out there right now, but since the sun hasn't set yet, escaping right now makes it too easy to get spotted. I suggest you wait here until sunset before heading out. Of course, staying here also risks running into the changing shift of guards. Decide for yourselves."

The beastmen exchanged shocked glances. "You're not escaping with us?"

Shang Feifan replied, "I'm not familiar with this place either. Having too many people together only draws attention. You're better off scattering as you run—every single one who makes it out counts."

Looking at one another, the beastmen didn't press him to stay. In their hearts, they were also afraid this beastman might throw them to the wolves to buy time in a crisis.

After all, they were total strangers with zero trust between them.

"I agree that waiting until dark is better. If the changing guards show up, we can figure out a way to take them out and scavenge more clothes and weapons," the middle-aged beastman proposed.

The player-beastman raised his hand.

Everyone looked at him.

The player spoke in broken beastman speech, "We still need medicine. We have a sick person here."

Silence fell over the group.

The sick beastman was breathing as faintly as gossamer, his eyes filled with despair. He weakly told the player-beastman, "Don't bother taking me with you. In my condition, I'll never make it out. If I stay behind, maybe I'll still have a sliver of a chance."

Gritting his teeth, the player said, "...I'll find a way to get you medicine. It's not time to give up yet."

The sick beastman shook his head. "Thank you, little brother. I don't want to drag you down. I don't even know your name."

The player hesitated. Rationally, he knew this was just a game NPC, and dying didn't matter since it was just a string of data. But painfully, these NPCs behaved far too much like real people. Coupled with the game developer's warning that these NPCs were entirely unique and gone forever once they died, he felt increasingly reluctant to abandon this NPC so easily.

The other beastmen remained silent. They could barely fend for themselves and certainly didn't want to carry such dead weight, though they weren't cruel enough to kick a man while he was down either.

Suddenly, a tiny black pellet was tossed toward the player-beastman.

Instinctively, the player reached out and caught it.

With a completely expressionless gaze, Shang Feifan said, "This is medicine for dysentery. Feed it to him; whether he lives or dies depends on his own luck. Remember, you owe me twenty silver darus. If this guy kicks the bucket, you're paying it back."

Shang Feifan felt a twinge of heartache. This was a pill he had bought using 2 precious Contribution Points. Quoting a price of twenty silver darus still felt like a loss.

*Fine, consider it a good deed for the day.*

Elated, the player-beastman didn't even stop to ponder where this exceptionally handsome and badass beastman had gotten the pill. He immediately shoved it straight into the sick man's mouth.

The other beastmen looked at Shang Feifan with a mixture of shock and envy.

Yet no one dared ask too many questions, assuming Shang Feifan must have concealed some items on his person. This also solved the mystery for the captive beastmen—this tiger-kin beastman must have taken a detoxifying pill to recover his strength, knock out the food delivery guard, and deal with the two guards inside the duty room.

The sick beastman never expected such a sudden turnaround in his fortune.

Whether it was psychological or not, the moment the pill hit his stomach, he immediately felt much better. Not only did his stomach stop churning, but his drained body also regained a sliver of strength.

Expressing his heartfelt gratitude to Shang Feifan, the sick beastman swore that once he escaped, he would surely repay this kindness, and even softly asked for Shang Feifan's name and hometown.

chunks.chineseText:
商非凡说让两个人还药钱也就是随口说说，以后能不能碰上都不知道。他自然也不可能在这里说出自己的名字和来历。

但就在商非凡摇头之前，他心中忽然一动。

“不用你们特意寻找我。二十个银达鲁的代价，我自己会取回。当你们偿还完毕时，你们自然会知道。”

这话说得有点玄乎。

生病兽人收声，看商非凡的目光变得有点忌惮，忌惮中还夹杂着畏惧和崇敬。他在怀疑商非凡不止是一个普通的修理商。

其他兽人看商非凡的眼神也变得有点敬畏。

对这个世界大背景还不太了解的玩家兽人则没想那么多，只吐出心声：“……酷。”

中年兽人还主动说：“这次如果我们能逃出去，就都欠了你一份恩情。”

商非凡不客气地：“那就算你们每人二十个银达鲁。得痢疾的那个欠我四十。等你们逃出强盗窝后，我会找你们收回这份欠债。”

没有人能欠武器商的钱，不管他是否退役。

二十个银达鲁换一条命，多么？

当然不多。就算再贫穷的人，也愿意拿出区区二十银达鲁来换自己一条命。

几个兽人甚至在听到商非凡明确说出只要他们付出二十银的救命钱，都暗暗松了口气。

商非凡也没有贸然就这么打开门走出去，他一样在等天黑。

他打开了一条门缝，暗中观察这个非完全封闭的大院子内的兽人走动情况，以及四周的建筑物分布和道路。

其他兽人也没闲着，他们扒掉了另一名烧伤兽人的衣裤鞋，互相匀着分了分，又满屋子找干净的食物和水。

没有食物，但是有水。

在有商非凡震慑的情况下，没人敢抢，他们还把找到的清水先奉到商非凡面前，让他先喝。

商非凡没有拒绝，他这具身体极需要补充水分。

中年兽人提起另一把骨刀，对两个昏迷中的强盗一人捅了一刀，然后把刀转给另一名兽人。

另一名兽人也举刀就捅，再把刀转给下一个兽人……

那名胆小兽人不敢动手，被两名兽人强行握住手，硬是往两名强盗身上戳了两刀。

玩家兽人一开始还没看懂，看到后面就明白了这些兽人的意思，他也只好接过骨刀，也捅了早就死透的两名强盗各一刀。

没人敢逼迫商非凡，也不需要。

天色逐渐变暗，大院子这边的兽人也变多了。

十七个小时过去，商非凡体内毒素完全代谢干净，他的生命值和力量值都恢复了大半。

没有恢复到满值，只因为饥饿。

商非凡几个闻到了浓郁的饭菜香。

闻得几个兽人全都在拼命咽口水。

原来就在地牢左侧的那排房子竟然就是强盗窝的厨房。

最前面那排房子则是强盗们吃饭的地方。

右侧的房子似乎是停放车辆的地方。

怪不得地牢外面没有多少人巡逻看守。

这里就相当于强盗们的活动中心，每天至少有两段时间会有大量兽人集中在这里。而厨房这种地方，从早到晚都会有人待着，只要地牢这里动静大点，厨房那里的人肯定会发现。

商非凡脑子飞速转动，他们想要逃离这个强盗窝，光等到晚上没有用，得给这个强盗窝找点乱子，让他们混乱起来。

“咳！”希望那个小广告有点用。

“至高伟大的存在，诅咒之神科尼泽厄斯，我将奉上祭品——吃我药的痢疾兽人欠我的二十银达鲁，请帮我诅咒我的敌人，让这些强盗的厨房失火吧，大火，让整个强盗窝都烧起来。”

商非凡低声念了三遍。

念完，望天。

如果没用，他下次再也不会干这么傻叉的事。

不巧，有两个提着武器的兽人往这栋值守屋走来。

那架势，一看就是来换班的。

屋里的七个兽人全都紧张起来。

作者有话说：

商非凡：我真是个大聪明。
chunks.englishText:
Shang Feifan had only spoken offhand about making the two of them repay the medicine money; he had no idea if they would ever cross paths again. Naturally, he wasn't about to reveal his real name and origins here.

Just as Shang Feifan was about to shake his head, however, a thought suddenly stirred within his heart.

"You don't need to go out of your way to find me. The price of twenty silver darus—I will collect it myself. When you have finished paying it off, you will naturally know."

That statement sounded rather cryptic.

The sick beastman shut his mouth. The look he gave Shang Feifan turned somewhat wary, a wariness mixed with dread and reverence. He began to suspect that Shang Feifan was far more than just an ordinary repairman.

The other beastmen also looked at Shang Feifan with a hint of awe.

The player-beastman, who still didn't quite grasp the grand background lore of this world, didn't think too deeply about it and simply blurted out what was on his mind: "...Cool."

The middle-aged beastman even took the initiative to say, "If we manage to escape this time, we will all owe you a favor."

Shang Feifan didn't stand on ceremony. "Then let's count it as twenty silver darus per person. The one with dysentery owes me forty. After you break out of this bandit den, I will come looking to collect these debts."

No one got away with owing money to a weapon smith—regardless of whether he was retired or not.

Twenty silver darus in exchange for your life—was that a lot?

Of course it wasn't. Even the poorest person would gladly cough up a mere twenty silver darus to save their own skin.

Upon hearing Shang Feifan explicitly state that all they had to pay was twenty silver coins for their life-saving medicine, several of the beastmen even breathed secret sighs of relief.

Shang Feifan didn't rashly throw open the door and walk out just yet; he was waiting for nightfall, too.

He cracked the door open a sliver, secretly observing the movement of the beastmen within this semi-enclosed courtyard, as well as the distribution of the surrounding buildings and pathways.

The other beastmen weren't sitting idle either. They stripped the clothes, pants, and shoes off the other burned beastman, split them among themselves, and searched the entire room for clean food and water.

There was no food, but there was water.

With Shang Feifan's intimidating presence keeping them in check, no one dared to scramble for it. Instead, they respectfully brought the fresh water they found over to Shang Feifan first, letting him drink before anyone else.

Shang Feifan didn't refuse; his current body was in desperate need of fluid replenishment.

The middle-aged beastman picked up another bone knife, stabbed each of the two unconscious bandits once, and then passed the blade to another beastman.

The other beastman raised the knife and stabbed them as well, before passing it on to the next...

The timid beastman didn't dare to do it, so two beastmen forcefully grabbed his hand and practically shoved it forward, driving the blade twice into the bodies of the two bandits.

The player-beastman didn't understand what was going on at first, but once he saw the pattern, he caught on to what these beastmen were driving at. With no other choice, he took the bone knife and stabbed the already stone-dead bandits once each.

No one dared to force Shang Feifan, nor did they need to.

The sky gradually darkened, and the number of beastmen in the courtyard area increased as well.

Seventeen hours passed, and the toxins in Shang Feifan's body were completely metabolized. His health points and strength stats had largely recovered.

They hadn't returned to their maximum values, but that was purely due to hunger.

A rich, savory aroma drifted over to Shang Feifan and the others.

It smelled so good that several beastmen began frantically swallowing their saliva.

As it turned out, that row of buildings on the left side of the dungeon was actually the kitchen of the bandit den.

The front row of buildings served as the dining hall for the bandits.

The building on the right seemed to be a carriage house for parked vehicles.

No wonder there weren't many patrollers guarding the outside of the dungeon.

This place acted as the bandits' activity center; at least twice a day, a large concentration of beastmen would gather here. And a place like the kitchen would have people working in it from morning till night. The moment there was the slightest commotion here at the dungeon, the people in the kitchen would definitely notice.

Shang Feifan's mind spun at lightning speed. If they wanted to escape this bandit den, simply waiting for nightfall wasn't enough; they had to stir up some trouble in this bandit den and throw them into chaos.

"Cough!" Hopefully, that little advertisement would come in handy.

"Supreme and magnificent existence, the God of Curses Conizeus, I offer up a sacrifice—the twenty silver darus owed to me by the dysentery-afflicted beastman who took my medicine. Please help me curse my enemy, and let the kitchen of these bandits catch fire—a raging fire, burn the entire bandit den to the ground."

Shang Feifan muttered this in a low voice three times.

When he finished, he looked up at the sky.

If this didn't work, he swore he would never do something so idiotic ever again.

As ill luck would have it, two weapon-toting beastmen were walking toward this guardhouse.

By the looks of it, they were definitely here for a shift change.

All seven beastmen inside the room grew tense.

Author's Notes:

Shang Feifan: I really am a tactical genius.

chunks.chineseText:
第27章 诅咒成真

大厨房内，大厨、二厨和七八个帮手正忙得热火朝天。

五个大灶顺着两面墙壁排开，两个负责烧火的伙计在五个大灶前来回挪动，负责帮助大厨二厨以及厨工们调整火势。

大厨抓起挂在脖子上的布巾擦擦汗，另一只手抓着铁铲给铁板上的几十块煎肉翻面。

刚翻了两块煎肉，大厨忽然火大，抓着手上的长柄铁铲就抽向正在烧火的烧火工。

“你他妈会不会烧火？塞那么多木柴干什么？煎肉全他妈糊了！”

烧火工肩膀上连着挨了三下铁铲抽打，疼得他差点哀嚎。

但他不敢，他深知大厨脾气，不但不敢叫疼，还含胸缩背低着头不住道歉：“对不起对不起，我错了……”

大厨又是一脚踹过来：“错你麻痹！还不赶紧给老子把火减小！今晚煎肉要是全糊了，老子就把你烤了！”

烧火工低着头，恨得眼睛都红了，但他不敢回嘴，也顾不上肩膀疼得要死，慌慌忙忙把炉灶里的木块扯出来。

这些已经点燃的木柴拿出来必须放到专门的桶里，但烧火工太慌，不小心就掉出几块，还烧到了他赤-裸的脚。

大厨发泄了火气，也怕把煎肉烧糊了，连忙拿着铁铲给剩下的煎肉翻面。一边翻还一边骂，骂得特别难听。

烧火工赤着的脚忽然一拨，把一块还冒着火焰的木柴块给拨到了一边。

那里放着一小堆干燥的木柴，好方便烧火工随时取用。

烧火工起身时手肘碰到木柴堆顶端，不小心碰掉了几块木柴。

掉下来的木柴正好盖住了那块烧着的木柴。

他后悔他的冲动了，只希望这块烧着的木柴赶紧熄灭，不要让任何人发现。

大厨看到烧火工笨拙慌乱的样子，举起铁铲又对着他背脊抽了一下：“蠢货！干什么都干不好！”

烧火工被抽得一个踉跄。

等到大厨转身去翻煎肉时，烧火工才抬起头，目光仇恨无比地射向大厨的背。

大厨看到煎肉糊了好几块，气得动作也大，乒乒乓乓撒调料中，手背扫到了油罐。

油罐差点从灶台上掉下去。

烧火工本能地伸手，及时抱住了油罐。

大厨不但没道谢，反手竟然就又抽了烧火工一下，还骂：“不长眼睛的蠢货！你要是敢把这罐油给打了，老子就剥了你的皮拿你炼油！”

烧火工肩膀本来就疼得要命，加上身体瘦弱，被大厨这么一抽，胳膊一抖，油罐立刻自由落体。

啪！

碎裂声在忙乱的厨房中响起。

随后整个厨房都爆发出大厨的怒吼声。

打人的声音不断响起。

微弱的求饶声夹杂在大量恶毒难听的咒骂和凶狠抽打中。

没过多久，两个厨房帮工拖着一个耷拉着脑袋头破血流气息奄奄的兽人走出厨房，把他随手往墙边一丢，顺便在外面撒了泡尿、磨蹭了一点时间，这才回去厨房。

厨房内，一名帮工在忙着收集碎在地上的油罐，把里面能用的油转移到另一个罐子里。

大厨、二厨和其他帮工在厨房里走来走去，虽然已经绕着那片油迹走，但溅射出来的油还是泼洒得到处都是，再被大厨几个踩来踩去，很快厨房地面就布满了油迹。

不过这个大厨房的地面、墙壁和灶台本来就很脏很油腻，也没人在乎再增加一点。

牢房值守屋。

换班的两个兽人提着武器剔着牙齿走近。

商非凡对屋内几个兽人打了个手势，让他们全都站到与大门平齐的墙壁边，贴着墙壁站。

“我解决一个，你们扑上去解决另一个，尽量不要让他们发出声音。”商非凡压低声音命令。

几个兽人全都紧张点头，生病兽人和胆小兽人站在最后面，他们被其他兽人警告，帮不上忙可以，但如果捣乱，就先杀了他们。

胆小兽人知道这是说给他听的，拼命点头。

咚咚，换班兽人敲门，用很大的嗓门喊值班兽人的名字，让他们赶紧来开门。

屋里传来一声模糊的咒骂声，大门被拉开了一条缝。

站在最前面的换班兽人等不及大门被打开更大，骂骂咧咧地一推门，走进来。

屋内地面上躺着两个兽人，地上全都是发黑的血迹。

刚进来的兽人察觉不对，骨刀还没提起来，就被人从后面击中后脑勺。

第二个换班兽人也跟着进来。

他正好看到了他前面的换班兽人被击中后脑勺的一幕。

第二个换班兽人正要大叫。

突然一股大力推倒了他，他刚发出一个“来”的音，就被人击中后脑。

值守屋的大门又被关上。

刚进来的两个换班兽人全都脑袋破碎、脸朝下趴在地上。

“换上他们的衣服，拿上他们的武器，伪装这里的强盗。”

商非凡话刚说完，那两个换班兽人身上的衣裤鞋就快被扒光了。

不算商非凡，剩下的六个兽人平分四套衣裤鞋，肯定不够，但可以勉强遮体。

胆小兽人和生病兽人分到的东西最少，也没有分到骨刀，两人也不敢和其他四个兽人争，但好在他们还有铁铐和脚镣当做武器。

“外面情况怎样？”中年兽人和玩家凑近，一起贴着门缝往外偷瞧。

商非凡：“等。”

念完那儿戏一样的咒语已经过去十来分钟，到现在大厨房那边还没有什么特殊反应。

商非凡几乎已经不抱希望。

就在他准备亲自去制造混乱时，大厨房的后门打开，一名身体瘦小的兽人跟被拖死狗一样拖了出来。

商非凡转头，对屋内几名兽人说：“我去看看有没有什么能做的，等会儿你们看到厨房和食堂那边混乱起来，就自己找机会逃跑。”

中年兽人右拳触胸：“兄弟，小心！”

玩家想说我可以去帮忙，但商非凡就像是知道他要说什么一样，提前道：“你看起来很厉害，保护好自己，想办法逃出去。如果我们有个万一，你还能带人来救我们。”

玩家“最大杏鲍菇”感动了，以为商非凡要主动牺牲自己来吸引强盗们的注意力，承诺：“好，如果你被抓，我一定会带人来救你。”

外面突然传来惊慌喊叫。

“失火啦！”

“厨房着火啦！”

来了！商非凡精神一振，拉开门缝。

没想到那个儿戏一样的诅咒真的有用！

有兽人从厨房里跑出来，从外面的水缸里打水，又拎回厨房。

来来回回跑了三四趟。

厨房那边的一排房子冒起越来越大的浓烟，浓烟在夜晚不明显，但从厨房里跑出来的人越来越多。

“快灭火！”

“去叫人啊！叫在吃饭的伙计都来帮忙！”

厨房本来就是油烟之地，又正是五口大灶一起-点燃做饭的时候。

这火一烧起来，哪里是一两盆水就能浇灭。

在食堂吃饭的兽人们听到喊叫，跑出来十几个人。

值守屋内准备逃跑的几个兽人欣喜。

但商非凡看着失火的厨房觉得这火烧得还不够大，惊动的人还不够多。

如果动静能再大一点……
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 27: The Curse Comes True

Inside the large kitchen, the head chef, the second chef, and seven or eight assistants were bustling about in a frantic flurry of activity.

Five large stoves lined two of the walls, with two kitchenhands responsible for stoking the fires darting back and forth across the five stoves, adjusting the flame intensity at the behest of the head chef, second chef, and kitchen workers.

The head chef wiped the sweat from his brow with a cloth rag hanging around his neck, while his other hand wielded a metal spatula, flipping dozens of pieces of searing meat on the iron griddle.

Just as he finished flipping two pieces of meat, a sudden surge of fury overtook the head chef. Clutching his long-handled iron spatula, he lashed out, whipping it across the back of the nearest fire-stoker.

"Can't you fucking tend a fire properly?! Why did you stuff so much firewood in? All the fucking meat is burnt!"

The fire-stoker took three consecutive blows from the iron spatula across his shoulders, the pain nearly causing him to wail out loud.

Yet he dared not. Knowing the head chef's volatile temper all too well, not only did he bite back his cries of pain, but he also hunched his shoulders, cowered, and continuously bowed his head in apology: "I'm sorry, I'm sorry, I was wrong..."

The head chef lashed out with a kick: "Wrong your fucking mother! Why aren't you turning the fire down for me right this instant?! If all the pan-fried meat gets burnt tonight, I'll roast *you* instead!"

The fire-stoker kept his head lowered, his eyes burning red with a hatred so deep it stung, but he dared not talk back. Disregarding the excruciating agony in his shoulder, he scrambled in a panic to yank the burning blocks of wood out from the stove.

These ignited pieces of firewood had to be tossed into a designated barrel once pulled out, but the fire-stoker was in such a fluster that he accidentally dropped a few chunks, which even scorched his bare feet.

Having vented his rage—and terrified of burning the rest of the meat—the head chef hurriedly grabbed his spatula to flip the remaining slices. As he flipped them, he kept up a stream of vicious, ear-shattering abuse.

The fire-stoker suddenly flicked his bare foot, kicking a still-flaming chunk of firewood off to the side.

Right there sat a small pile of dry firewood, kept handy for the stoker to grab at a moment's notice.

As the fire-stoker stood up, his elbow brushed against the top of the firewood pile, accidentally knocking a few logs loose.

The falling logs happened to land squarely on top of that burning chunk of wood.

He instantly regretted his impulsive action, praying only that this burning piece of wood would extinguish itself immediately without anyone noticing.

Seeing the fire-stoker's clumsy and flustered display, the head chef raised his spatula and struck him across the spine once more: "You idiot! You can't do a single thing right!"

The blow sent the fire-stoker stumbling forward.

By the time the head chef turned back to flip the meat, the fire-stoker finally raised his head, fixing a gaze of unadulterated venom upon the chef's back.

Noticing that several pieces of the meat had indeed scorched, the head chef grew so furious his movements became violent. Amidst a clatter of pots and pans as he scattered seasonings, the back of his hand brushed against an oil jar.

The oil jar nearly tumbled off the stove ledge.

Instinctively, the fire-stoker reached out and caught the oil jar just in time.

Far from offering a word of thanks, the head chef whipped his hand around and struck the fire-stoker yet again, cursing, "Blind idiot! If you dare drop this jar of oil, I'll skin you alive and use you to render grease!"

The fire-stoker's shoulder was already throbbing with agonizing pain, and combined with his frail physique, the blow caused his arm to jolt violently. The oil jar instantly slipped into a freefall.

*Smash!*

The sound of shattering echoed sharply through the hectic kitchen.

An instant later, the roar of the head chef erupted across the entire kitchen.

The sound of physical violence rang out continuously.

Faint, wretched pleas for mercy mingled amidst a barrage of vicious, foul curses and ruthless beatings.

Not long after, two kitchen assistants dragged out a lethargic orc whose head was dripping with blood and hanging limply from his neck. They tossed him casually against the wall, took the opportunity to relieve themselves outside and stall for a bit of time, and only then headed back inside.

Inside the kitchen, one helper was busy gathering the shattered shards of the oil jar, transferring whatever usable oil remained into another vessel.

The head chef, second chef, and other assistants paced back and forth across the kitchen floor. Though they skirted around the slick patch of spilled oil, the splattered grease had already splashed everywhere. Trampled back and forth by the chef and the others, the kitchen floor soon became completely coated in a thick, greasy slick.

Still, the floor, walls, and stoves of this massive kitchen were already filthy and slick with grease to begin with; nobody cared to mind a little extra mess.

Back in the dungeon guardhouse.

The two relief orcs approached, carrying weapons and picking their teeth with toothpicks.

Shang Feifan gestured to the orcs inside the room, signaling them to press themselves tightly against the wall, aligning with the doorway.

"I'll take down the first one, and you guys charge forward to handle the second. Try to keep them from making any noise," Shang Feifan ordered in a low voice.

The orcs all nodded nervously. The sick orc and the timid orc stood at the very back; they had been warned by the others that while they didn't have to help, if they caused any trouble, they would be executed first.

Knowing full well those words were meant for him, the timid orc nodded frantically.

*Thump, thump.* The relief orcs knocked on the door, shouting loudly for the names of the on-duty orcs and demanding they hurry up and open the door.

A muffled curse came from inside the room, and the heavy door cracked open a sliver.

The relief orc standing at the front, too impatient for the door to open any wider, cursed angrily as he shoved the door open and stepped inside.

Two orcs lay sprawled across the floor inside, surrounded by pools of blackened blood.

The newly entered orc sensed something was amiss, but before he could even raise his bone knife, the back of his head was struck heavily from behind.

The second relief orc followed right behind him.

Just in time, he witnessed the scene of his companion taking a blow to the back of the head.

Opening his mouth to scream, the second relief orc never got the chance.

Suddenly, a massive force shoved him off balance. Before he could even emit the first syllable of an alarm, a strike landed squarely on the back of his head.

The guardhouse door swung shut once more.

Both newly arrived relief orcs lay face down on the floor, their skulls caved in.

"Put on their clothes, take their weapons, and disguise yourselves as the bandits here."

Before Shang Feifan's voice had even faded, the outer garments, trousers, and shoes were being rapidly stripped off the two relief orcs.

Excluding Shang Feifan, the remaining six orcs had to evenly split four sets of clothing and footwear—certainly not enough to go around, but enough to barely cover themselves.

The timid orc and the sick orc received the fewest items and got no bone knives, yet neither dared to dispute the other four orcs. Fortunately, they still had their iron handcuffs and leg shackles to use as makeshift weapons.

"What's the situation outside?" The middle-aged orc and the player edged closer, peering through the crack in the door together.

Shang Feifan: "Wait."

A full ten minutes had passed since he muttered that ludicrous, half-joke of a curse, and yet there was still no unusual reaction from the direction of the large kitchen.

Shang Feifan had almost completely abandoned hope.

Just as he was preparing to go out and manufacture some chaos himself, the back door of the large kitchen swung open, and a scrawny orc was dragged out just like a dead dog.

Shang Feifan turned his head and told the orcs inside the room, "I'm going to check if there's anything I can do. A moment from now, once you see the kitchen and the dining hall descend into chaos, seize the opportunity and run for your lives."

The middle-aged orc pressed his right fist against his chest: "Brother, take care!"

The player wanted to say he could go along to help, but as if anticipating his words, Shang Feifan preempted him: "You look formidable. Protect yourself and find a way to escape. If the worst happens to us, you'll still be able to bring reinforcements to rescue us."

The player, "Largest King Oyster Mushroom," was deeply moved, believing Shang Feifan intended to willingly sacrifice himself to draw the bandits' attention. He solemnly promised: "Alright! If you get captured, I swear I'll bring people back to save you."

Panic-stricken shouts suddenly rang out from outside.

"Fire!"

"The kitchen's on fire!"

It had begun! Shang Feifan's spirits lifted, and he pulled the door open a crack.

To his utter astonishment, that absurd little curse had actually worked!

Orcs came streaming out of the kitchen, drawing water from the water vats outside and lugging it back in.

They ran back and forth four or five times.

Billowing clouds of thick smoke began to billow from the row of buildings housing the kitchen. While the smoke wasn't terribly obvious in the night, the stream of people pouring out of the kitchen grew larger by the moment.

"Put it out, quickly!"

"Go get people! Tell the cooks eating in the mess hall to come help!"

The kitchen was naturally a place thick with grease and smoke, and it happened to be the peak hour when all five large stoves were fully stoked for cooking.

Once a fire like this took hold, a basin or two of water was nowhere near enough to quench it.

Hearing the commotion, over a dozen orcs rushed out from the dining hall.

The few orcs inside the guardhouse who were preparing to flee broke into smiles of delight.

Yet, watching the blazing kitchen, Shang Feifan felt the fire still wasn't big enough, and the number of people alarmed wasn't nearly sufficient.

If only the commotion could be just a bit bigger...

chunks.chineseText:
可惜厨房那边的火势虽然无法控制，但这场面也绝称不上慌乱。

二三十个兽人一起忙着打水灭火，眼看火势就要被控制住。

那怎么都不肯大起来的火势就像是在告诉商非凡：二十银的祭品也就只能做到这种程度了，这还是看在客人第一次下单的份上~

商非凡怎么肯让如此好机会就这么溜走。

他溜了出去，冒充灭火的兽人，接过也不知是谁递给他的水桶，拎着水桶往头上一浇，大喊：“老弟，老哥来救你了！”

商非凡从敞开的后门冲进厨房。

其他兽人没注意，想拉都没能拉住。

而这会儿又还乱着，跑出来的大厨等人也不知道厨房里是否还有其他人。

原本被扔到厨房外面的烧火工也不知道什么时候醒了过来，趁着混乱一点点爬离厨房。

别人只当烧火工被大火波及，还有人拉了他一把，把他拉到远离火场的地方。

商非凡跑进厨房，发现厨房里的火势还不小，而且东一簇西一簇的在燃烧。

他用最快速度找到装油的罐子，又抓了几根还在燃烧的木柴。

厨房和食堂之间有一扇门。

商非凡打开那道门，操起油罐就扔了进去，随后又把点燃的木柴也给扔了进去。

轰！火焰迅速上升。

食堂里正在吃饭的兽人大惊，狂喊：“失火了！厨房的火烧过来了！大伙快跑！”

商非凡盼望的大混乱终于出现，正在食堂吃饭的百多个兽人一起往外逃，他们争夺大门和窗户，为了能先逃出火场，大打出手。

原本那烧到食堂的火不算大，只要能及时隔离或扑灭，就不会有什么大事。

但这会儿强盗们都在忙着逃出火场，谁也想不到去救火。

何况还有强盗惊慌失措地大喊“快跑，火要烧过来了，我不想被活生生烧死！”

火焰随着油迹往食堂内部蔓延，木桌和长条木凳被点燃。

一道身影溜入食堂，抓起桌上还没有动过的食物塞进怀里，又抓了一壶清水。

商非凡混在逃跑的兽人中，一边乱喊制造恐慌，一边跟着一起跑出食堂，跑出来时他左手抓着一大块烤肉、右手抓着水壶，胸前也鼓鼓囊囊。

越来越多的兽人往大厨房这边跑来。

强盗窝的头目都被惊动了。

商非凡一边啃着烤肉喝着清水，一边往墙根溜。

出工不出力只想逃跑的兽人不止他一个，还很多。

商非凡经过地牢值守屋时，看到逃跑的兽人们忘记关紧的大门，还顺手给关紧。

“你们都在搞什么？乱哄哄的都在看热闹吗！赶紧灭火！”

“一队队长人呢？你带你们队的人去负责打水灭火！”

“二队队长给我带人去查看库房！”

“三队队长去查看牢房，再给我仔细巡逻，防止有人趁机捣乱！”

三名队长全都高声应是，立刻呼喊心腹小弟的名字，再让心腹小弟把手下全都集中起来。

商非凡啃着烤肉吊儿郎当地混入二队队伍，跟着离开火场。

他附近几个强盗都没有发现不对，还对商非凡抱怨，说他聪明，还知道带着吃的出来，他们都没吃上两口，就又要饿着肚子干活。

商非凡大方地把烤肉撕成几块分给几个强盗。这烤肉难吃得很，他吃饱就不想再咬第二口。

几个强盗就觉得这个大兄弟特别有兄弟情，把他肩膀拍得啪啪响。

不等几个强盗怀疑他的身份，商非凡借口撒尿脱队，身体隐入黑暗中。他已经看准逃跑方向，但沿着巷道刚跑了几步，脚尖就踢到了一个半硬不硬的物体。

商非凡低头，看到一个趴在地上的黑影，一股血腥味也跟着冲入鼻端。

叮咚。

【成功逃出地牢，奖励贡献点1点。】

【任务十八，救治被打伤的烧火工阿城，救活奖励3点贡献点。】

【任务十九，救烧火工阿城离开强盗窝，成功后奖励3点贡献点。】

【任务二十，把烧火工阿城送到摩罗城，交给炼药大师弟子嗡东亭，完成后奖励5点贡献点。】

商非凡挑眉，这个烧火工身份很不一般吗？竟然让系统连着给他发布了三个任务。

作者有话说：

商非凡：还是脑载系统更懂玩家，这才有玩游戏的感觉嘛，天天搬砖种田有什么意思？等我多赚点钱，把修理铺发展成兵工厂……
