CHINESE SOURCE TEXT (第27章 诅咒成真 (Part 2)):
"""
Unfortunately, although the fire near the kitchen was currently uncontrollable, the scene could hardly be called chaotic.

Twenty or thirty orcs were rushing around together, hauling water to put out the flames, and it looked as though the fire was about to be brought under control.

That stubborn, refusing-to-grow fire seemed to be telling Shang Feifan: A twenty-silver sacrifice could only accomplish this much to begin with, and that was already considering this was the customer's first order~

How could Shang Feifan let such a prime opportunity slip through his fingers?

He slipped outside, disguised himself as one of the orcs fighting the fire, snatched a bucket from someone whose identity he didn't even catch, dumped the water over his own head, and bellowed, "Brother, big bro's coming to save you!"

Shang Feifan charged straight through the open back door and into the kitchen.

The other orcs hadn't been paying attention and failed to grab him in time.

Besides, things were still in enough of a tumult that the head chef and the others, who had run out earlier, had no idea if anyone else was still trapped inside.

The fire-stoker who had previously been tossed outside the kitchen had also somehow regained consciousness, crawling away from the kitchen bit by bit amidst the confusion.

Everyone simply assumed the fire-stoker had been caught in the blaze, and someone even lent a hand, dragging him to a safe spot far away from the inferno.

Running into the kitchen, Shang Feifan discovered that the flames inside were still quite fierce, burning in sporadic patches of scattered fire here and there.

With maximum speed, he located the jars containing cooking oil and grabbed several pieces of still-burning firewood.

A door connected the kitchen and the dining hall.

Shang Feifan threw open that door, hoisted a jar of oil, and hurled it inside, immediately followed by the burning pieces of wood.

*Boom!* The flames surged upward at terrifying speed.

The orcs eating inside the dining hall were shocked out of their wits, screaming frantically, "Fire! The fire from the kitchen has spread over here! Everyone run for your lives!"

The massive chaos Shang Feifan had been hoping for finally materialized. Over a hundred orcs dining inside bolted for the exits simultaneously, fighting tooth and nail over the doorways and windows just to escape the blazing hall first.

Initially, the fire spreading into the dining hall hadn't been particularly large; prompt isolation or dousing would have prevented any major disaster.

Yet at this moment, the bandits were entirely preoccupied with fleeing the blazing death trap; not a single soul crossed their minds to fight the fire.

To make matters worse, panicked bandits screamed at the top of their lungs, "Run! The fire's spreading, I don't want to burn alive!"

Fueled by the spilled grease, the flames licked inward through the dining hall, igniting the wooden tables and long benches.

A solitary figure slipped into the dining hall, snatched up some untouched food from a table and stuffed it into his tunic, then grabbed a flask of fresh water.

Blending in with the fleeing orcs, Shang Feifan shouted wildly to sow panic while running out right alongside them. By the time he broke out of the building, his left hand was clutching a large chunk of roasted meat, his right hand gripped a water flask, and his chest bulged heavily with stolen provisions.

A growing horde of orcs swarmed toward the large kitchen area.

Even the chieftains of the bandit den were roused.

Munching on roasted meat and washing it down with fresh water, Shang Feifan drifted casually toward the base of the wall.

He wasn't the only one putting in minimal effort and looking solely for a chance to escape; there were plenty of others doing the exact same thing.

Passing by the dungeon guardhouse, Shang Feifan noticed the heavy door—left unlatched in the panic by the fleeing orcs—and casually swung it shut, locking it tight.

"What are you all doing?! Running around like headless chickens watching the spectacle?! Put out the fire, now!"

"Where's the First Squad leader? Take your men and get over here to haul water!"

"Second Squad leader, take your men to inspect the storage warehouse!"

"Third Squad leader, check the cell block and conduct a thorough patrol to make sure nobody's taking advantage of the chaos!"

All three squad leaders roared their compliance, immediately barking out the names of their trusted lackies and ordering them to muster their subordinates.

Chewing on his roasted meat with a nonchalant swagger, Shang Feifan slipped right into the ranks of the Second Squad, trailing them as they departed the fire zone.

None of the nearby bandits found anything amiss, and one even clapped Shang Feifan on the shoulder, complaining that he was smart to bring food along since the rest of them hadn't even managed two bites before having to work on empty stomachs.

Generously, Shang Feifan tore off a few chunks of roasted meat and shared them with the bandits. The roasted meat tasted atrocious anyway; once his hunger was sated, he didn't care to take a second bite.

Convinced this "brother" was a thoroughly loyal comrade, the bandits slapped him heartily on the shoulders.

Before any of them could grow suspicious of his identity, Shang Feifan excused himself to relieve himself, slipping away from the squad and melting into the darkness. He had already locked onto his escape route, but after sprinting just a few steps down an alleyway, his toe collided with a semi-rigid object.

Shang Feifan looked down, spotting a dark figure sprawled across the ground as a heavy reek of blood washed over him.

*Ding-dong.*

[Successfully escaped the dungeon. Reward: 1 Contribution Point.]

[Quest 18: Treat A-Cheng, the injured fire-stoker. Reward upon successful treatment: 3 Contribution Points.]

[Quest 19: Escort A-Cheng, the fire-stoker, out of the bandit den. Reward upon completion: 3 Contribution Points.]

[Quest 20: Deliver A-Cheng, the fire-stoker, to Moluo City and hand him over to Weng Dongting, disciple of the Grand Alchemy Master. Reward upon completion: 5 Contribution Points.]

Shang Feifan raised an eyebrow. Was this fire-stoker's identity something out of the ordinary? The system had actually chained three quests to him in a row.

Author's Note:

Shang Feifan: A brain-linked system really understands gamers best. This is what playing a game should feel like—what's the point of grinding bricks and farming all day long? Once I make a bit more money, I'm going to turn this repair shop into an arms factory...

chunks.chapterTitle: 第28章 意料外的效果 (Part 1)
chunks.chineseText:
第28章 意料外的效果

商非凡原地思考三秒，弯腰一把抄起地上昏迷的兽人，扛上肩头。

治疗？

他又没有点开治疗技能，赚到的贡献点也只有刚刚奖励给他的1点。

游戏商城里的药物就没有2点以下的便宜货！

只能先尝试把人带出去，如果途中遇到不可解的情况，该扔还是得扔。

附近传来脚步声和乱哄哄的说话声。

商非凡扛着人，无声无息地贴近墙根，把呼吸声压到最低。

“嗯？什么味道？你们有没有闻到一股血腥味。”脚步声突然停止。

“……好像是有一点，像是从那边传来。”

“走，过去看看。”

艹！商非凡拔脚就跑。

他之前还在庆幸这个强盗窝没有养狗，却忘了兽人要养什么狗！

他们自己就拥有不亚于犬类的嗅觉。

商非凡好不容易远离那几个闻到血腥味的兽人，为了跑到下风口，他不得不再次绕回强盗窝营地深处。

这时再看自己扛着的兽人，顿时满脸嫌弃。

要么还是扔了吧。带着这个家伙简直就是给自己增加逃出难度。

……这家伙可是等于11个贡献点。

商非凡沉默着打开游戏商城，他记得他在查看食物类商品时似乎看到过一个叫做臭果的东西。

果然有。而且只要1个贡献点就能买到。

看说明，这个臭果的汁液会散发出让兽类包括虫类都极为讨厌的味道，驱兽驱虫效果极佳，但因为伤敌一千自伤一千八，属于滞销商品，所以原本价值3个贡献点的臭果就打骨折价销售。

商非凡：“……”

他之前就发现了，这个游戏商城是不是有点皮？

商非凡花了刚刚到手的1个贡献点，手里多了一枚龙眼大、也很像龙眼的果实。

捏着果子嗅了嗅，只闻到隐约的臭味。

这种臭味无法形容，不像是人类的鼻子经常闻到的臭味，而是另一种陌生的、但又让人忍不住想要远离的味道。

商非凡手指微一用劲，捏开了果皮。

……商非凡死了。

挣扎着最后一口气，聪明的老商打开脑载游戏系统，毫不犹豫地把自己的嗅觉感知度一口气拉到0刻度。

他就是想要闻闻看这个臭果能有多臭，没想到这个披着龙眼皮的果子撕了那层皮后能真实不做作到这种程度！

这何止是自伤一千八！

如果不是能下调嗅觉感知度，他绝对绝对会把这枚果子立刻扔掉，然后把沾了一点汁液的右手也给剁掉。

被他扛在肩头、昏迷中的烧火工都被这股臭味刺激得身体动了动。

再也闻不到一丁点臭味的老商淡定地把臭果汁液涂抹到烧火工的头发和衣服上。

窸窸窣窣。

商非凡竖起耳朵，嗅觉失去，他的听觉似乎更灵敏。

附近好像有无数虫子在爬动。

不是好像！

他看到了大量虫子从他们周边疯狂往外逃逸。

……这些虫子平时都藏在什么地方？

商非凡都被这个虫子数量给惊到。

不远处，传来兽人的破口大骂声：“谁他妈在大家还在家的时候就用了强力驱虫药？臭死老子了！”

商非凡转身，大胆地往上风口跑去。

一路跑，他一路拿手中的臭果到处蹭擦。

很快，整个强盗窝都布满了让兽人无法忍受的古怪臭味。

强盗们的骂声越来越多。

他们想要找到臭味的源头，但根本找不到，现在整个营地都散发着强烈的臭气！

大量强盗往上风处跑。

穿着强盗同款衣服、腰间插着同款骨刀的商非凡扛着人跟着强盗们一起跑，一边跑，一边和旁边的强盗兄弟们一起骂，捏破的果实飞快擦过身边几个强盗的衣服。

“艹！你怎么这么臭？离老子远一点！”骂人的强盗完全没发现旁边这个扛人的家伙不是他们一伙的。

“这家伙怎么了？臭晕了？”

“厨房大火中受伤的，我们队长让我带他去找……恶！你们到底跑什么地方去弄来这么臭的味道？”商非凡脸上的嫌弃，比被他们臭到的兽人还要真情实感。

“不是我们！”奔跑中的兽人抬起袖子，不可置信：“艹，我身上怎么这么臭？”

“这一定是虫族诅咒！到底是谁把强力驱虫药给弄撒了！”

“巨虫坐骑控制不住了！它们都在踹笼子往外跑！”

“虫子！我天！哪来这么多虫子！”

“这就是强力驱虫药的效果。”

“用火，快用火烧！”

“蠢货！别用火！”

迟了，真有人拿火去烧跑出来的大量虫子。

受到惊吓的虫子带着火焰到处钻。

有虫子钻进了强盗们住的房屋，还有虫子钻进了……库房。

商非凡怀疑自己听到了强盗窝老大的大骂声。

强盗窝老大不愧是老大，他当时就反应过来这臭味和逃出地牢的兽人有关。

对，这时强盗窝老大已经知晓地牢中几个兽人逃出来的事。

他也很容易就联想到厨房和食堂的失火九成九和这几个出逃兽人有关。

这位强盗头子暴怒至极，但同时又能冷静无比地让嗅觉最好的几个强盗去嗅闻地牢中几个逃跑兽人的味道，并让这几个嗅觉最好的兽人带领人手去追捕那几个逃跑兽人。

这一招非常管用。

根据传来的信号，他们的人已经发现了逃跑者踪迹，且就快追上他们。

但千算万算，强盗头子怎么也没算到营地里突然散发出强力驱虫剂的强烈臭味。

就好像那些逃跑的兽人知道他会干什么一样，且抢先一步就想到了应对方法。

强盗头子眼睛气得赤红，他一定要抓住那几个出逃兽人，他已经不想收服他们，也不想卖了他们，他要把那几个虫艹的混蛋全都活烤了！

能被关在那个地下地牢里的兽人全都是有一技之长的，没杀他们，就是想要收服他们为强盗们所用。实在收服不了的，也可以卖个高价——有一技之长的奴隶总是更受欢迎。

但现在有比抓这几个出逃兽人更重要的事情！

“保护库房！所有人全都给我去保护库房！”

他们抢来的所有财产都集中在库房中，还有最珍贵的粮食。

什么都可以失去，唯独库房绝对不能有失！

商非凡扛着烧火工跟着其他强盗们一起经过了库房。

库房被点燃了，好多兽人在灭火。

商非凡听说那一大排房子就是强盗们的库房，眼含可惜地望了一眼。

如果他身上有游戏玩家必备的空间背包就好了，他一定会假借帮忙灭火进去捞一把。

但现在他不但没有空间背包，肩上还扛着一个拖累。

而且大量强盗都在往这边集中，想要捞一把还不被发现的可能性很小。

商非凡通过那个强盗头子的几次命令就察觉这个强盗头子并不是一个莽撞的人，黑吃黑虽然美妙，但也要考虑现实情况。

在这种情况下，他还是赶紧跑路的好。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 28: Unexpected Effects

Shang Feifan stood frozen in place for three seconds, then bent down, scooped up the unconscious orc from the ground, and heaved him over his shoulder.

Treat him?

He hadn't unlocked any healing skills, and the only Contribution Point he had earned was the 1 point just awarded to him.

The game mall didn't have any medicinal items as cheap as under 2 points!

His only option was to try and get the person out first. If they encountered an impossible situation along the way, he would just have to drop him.

Footnotes and noisy chatter echoed from nearby.

Carrying the body, Shang Feifan silently hugged the base of the wall, pressing his breathing down to the absolute minimum.

"Huh? What's that smell? Did any of you smell blood?" The footsteps suddenly stopped.

"...Seems like there is a bit, coming from over there."

"Let's go, take a look."

Damn it! Shang Feifan turned and bolted.

He had been congratulating himself earlier that this bandit den didn't keep dogs, forgetting what kind of "dogs" orcs actually kept!

They possessed a sense of smell that was in no way inferior to a canine's.

After finally putting some distance between himself and those orcs who had caught the scent of blood, Shang Feifan had to loop back deep into the bandit camp in order to reach the downwind side.

Looking at the orc slung over his shoulder now, disgust washed over his face.

Maybe he should just drop him. Lugging this guy around was simply increasing the difficulty of his escape.

...Yet this guy was worth a cool 11 Contribution Points.

Shang Feifan silently opened the game mall. He remembered seeing an item called a "Stinky Fruit" while browsing through the food category.

Sure enough, it was there. And it cost a mere 1 Contribution Point.

According to the description, the juice of this Stinky Fruit emitted an odor that beasts and insects alike loathed to the extreme. Its repellent effect against beasts and bugs was top-notch, but because it possessed the self-destructive flaw of "hurting the enemy a thousand while crippling yourself a thousand," it was a sluggishly moving product. Originally valued at 3 Contribution Points, it was currently being heavily discounted like a broken-leg sale.

Shang Feifan: "..."

He'd noticed it before: did this game mall have a mischievous streak?

Shang Feifan forked over the 1 Contribution Point he had just acquired, and a fruit the size of a longan—and looking remarkably like one—appeared in his hand.

He pinched the fruit and gave it a sniff, catching only a faint, subtle stench.

This smell was indescribable; it wasn't the kind of stench human noses frequently encountered, but rather an entirely alien odor that nonetheless made one instinctively want to flee.

Shang Feifan applied a tiny bit of force with his fingers and cracked the rind.

...Shang Feifan died.

Gasping his last dying breath, the clever Lao Shang opened his brain-link gaming system and unhesitatingly dragged his olfactory perception slider all the way down to zero.

He had just wanted to see how smelly this Stinky Fruit could possibly be. Little did he expect that once that longan-like rind was torn away, it would be this genuinely, unpretentiously horrific!

This was far beyond "hurting yourself a thousand"!

If he hadn't been able to lower his sense of smell, he absolutely, 100% would have hurled this fruit away instantly and then chopped off his right hand for having touched a drop of its juice.

The unconscious stoke-worker slung over his shoulder even twitched instinctively at the assault of this stench.

No longer smelling a single trace of the odor, Lao Shang calmly smeared the juices of the Stinky Fruit onto the stoke-worker's hair and clothes.

Rustle, rustle.

Shang Feifan perked up his ears. With his sense of smell gone, his hearing seemed noticeably sharper.

It sounded like countless bugs were crawling around nearby.

It wasn't just sounding like it!

He saw a massive swarm of insects frantically fleeing outward from their surroundings.

...Where on earth did these bugs usually hide?

Shang Feifan was genuinely startled by the sheer quantity of insects.

Not far away, an orc's angry curse rang out: "Who the fuck used heavy-duty bug spray while everyone's still at home?! It's choking the life out of me!"

Shang Feifan turned and boldly bolted toward the upwind side.

As he ran, he smeared the Stinky Fruit in his hand everywhere, brushing it against surfaces.

Before long, the entire bandit den was saturated with a bizarre, unbearable stench that drove the orcs to distraction.

The bandits' curses grew louder and more numerous.

They wanted to find the source of the stink, but it was utterly untraceable; the entire camp was now reeking with a suffocating miasma!

Swarms of bandits fled toward the upwind areas.

Dressed in standard bandit garb with an identical bone knife tucked into his belt, Shang Feifan carried his burden and ran right alongside the bandits. As he ran, he cursed right along with his "bandit brothers," swiftly brushing the crushed fruit against the clothes of several nearby thugs.

"Damn it! Why do you smell so foul? Get away from me!" The cursing bandit completely failed to notice that this guy carrying a body wasn't one of their crew.

"What's wrong with this guy? Did he pass out from the stink?"

"Got hurt in the kitchen fire; our captain told me to take him to... Ugh! Where on earth did you guys go to track down such a foul stench?" Shang Feifan's expression of disgust was far more genuine and heartfelt than that of the orcs suffering from the stink.

"It wasn't us!" A running orc lifted his sleeve in disbelief. "Damn it, why do I smell so foul too?!"

"This has got to be a bug curse! Who the hell spilled the heavy-duty insecticide?!"

"The giant bug mounts are losing it! They're kicking their cages and trying to break out!"

"Bugs! Good god! Where did all these bugs come from?!"

"This is the work of heavy-duty bug spray!"

"Use fire! Quick, burn 'em!"

"Idiots! Don't use fire!"

It was too late. Someone had indeed used fire to deal with the massive swarm of bugs pouring out.

The terrified insects scurried everywhere, trailing flames behind them.

Some bugs burrowed into the dwellings of the bandits, and some even burrowed into... the armory.

Shang Feifan suspected he heard the roar of the bandit boss's furious cursing.

The bandit boss was no fool; he instantly deduced that this stench was connected to the orcs who had escaped the dungeon.

Right, by this time, the bandit boss was already aware that several orcs had broken out of the hold.

It was also very easy for him to connect the fires in the kitchen and cafeteria nine times out of ten to these escaped orcs.

The bandit leader was blazing with rage, yet he was calm enough to order his orcs with the keenest sense of smell to sniff out the lingering traces of the escaped prisoners, dispatching them to hunt the fugitives down.

This tactic was extremely effective.

According to incoming signals, their men had already picked up the trail of the escapees and were closing in fast.

Yet, for all his scheming, the bandit leader never anticipated the overpowering stench of the heavy-duty bug repellent suddenly flooding the camp.

It was as if those escaped orcs had known precisely what he was going to do and had thought of a countermeasure ahead of time.

The bandit leader's eyes turned bloodshot. He had to capture those escaped orcs; he no longer wanted to subjugate them, nor did he want to sell them—he was going to roast those bug-fucking bastards alive!

The orcs locked in that underground dungeon all possessed specialized skills. They hadn't been killed because the bandits wanted to subjugate them for their own use. Those who truly couldn't be broken could still fetch a high price—skilled slaves were always in demand.

Yet right now, there was something far more important than catching a few runaways!

"Protect the armory! Every single one of you, get over to the armory and protect it!"

All the loot they had plundered was concentrated in the armory, along with their most precious food supplies.

They could lose anything else, but the armory could not be compromised under any circumstances!

Carrying the stoke-worker, Shang Feifan passed right by the armory alongside the other bandits.

The storehouse had been ignited, and numerous orcs were frantically fighting the fire.

Hearing that that massive row of buildings served as the bandits' treasury, Shang Feifan cast a regretful glance their way.

If he only possessed a spatial storage pouch, a gamer's staple, he would have gladly used the excuse of helping put out the fire to slip inside and loot a fortune.

Alas, not only did he lack a spatial pouch, but he was also hauling dead weight on his shoulder.

Furthermore, with hordes of bandits congregating in the area, the odds of looting something without being discovered were practically zero.

From the bandit leader's series of commands, Shang Feifan could tell the man wasn't a reckless brute. Playing dog-eat-dog was wonderful, but one had to factor in reality.

Under these circumstances, making a break for it was the wisest choice.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第28章 意料外的效果 (Part 2)
chunks.chineseText:
原本他购买臭果只是想要遮掩烧火工身上的血腥味，没想到这枚臭果的杀伤力会这么大，比他花了二十银的厨房大火要有效果得多，真搞得强盗窝大乱。

如果不是强盗头子强行命令所有强盗都来救库房守库房，恐怕所有强盗都会逃出臭味弥漫的营地。

商非凡把手中捏着的已经挤不出汁液的臭果悄悄往强盗们的脚底下一抛，脚步拐弯，混杂在人群中，三钻两钻就不见了人影。

另一头，玩家兽人和中年兽人几个分开了，他们原本以为逃出去的希望不大，等后面有人追来时，更有人脚软想要跪地求饶。

谁想！强盗窝突然就乱了，真正的大乱。

好些强盗就这么捂着鼻子跑过他们身边，都没有发现他们。

玩家兽人和中年兽人几个感觉到生机再现，顾不上极臭，胆子大的就混入强盗中一起往外跑，胆子小的就躲躲藏藏，一点点往外挪。

也有倒霉催的不知道出口在哪里，乱跑一通，反而跑回强盗窝中心，之后又稀里糊涂地跟着躲避臭味的强盗往外跑。

商非凡扛着烧火工跟着几十个受不了臭味的强盗跑出了一道用石头堆砌的围墙大门。

守门的强盗们都阻止不了这些兽人擅自打开大门的行为，而且守门强盗们也只想远离营地和这些身上沾染了臭味的好兄弟们。

跑到外面后，那几十个强盗全都往一个方向跑。

商非凡听到他们说话，知道了那些强盗在往水源地跑。

商非凡放慢脚步，和他们分开。

天色黑暗，那几十个强盗谁也没发现他们中间少了两个人，他们现在都急着赶紧去洗澡，把身上沾染到的臭味给洗掉。

商非凡扛着烧火工越跑越远。

他听到了任务十九完成的提示，3点贡献点到账。

跑了一段路，商非凡没有发现地缝，也就是说他现在跑的不是回头路。

商非凡在一处背风的小山坡停下，放下扛着的烧火工，先试探他的鼻息。

还好，还有气。

再仔细检查对方的伤势，发现他的脑袋被打破、身上外伤一堆，胸腹和背部都有大量血痕和青肿，暂时无法判断烧火工有无内伤，也无法确定他是否伤到骨头。

要怎么救活他？

商非凡不得不再次打开游戏商城。

但他没有立刻选择治伤药物，而是自言自语：“这个连环任务太亏了，我冒了这么大危险，结果赚到的贡献点全都花在了这个烧火工身上。如果我不救他，我现在至少还有2点贡献点的纯利润。

救他的话，他这么重的伤势，至少要花2到3个贡献点才能买到有效药物。也就是说我最后的纯利润很可能还是2个贡献点，最多3个，那我何苦费这么多事？”

“算了，就这么放生他吧。”

商非凡真的停止选择药物，转身就要离开烧火工。

叮咚。

【任务二十一，帮助地牢中的被囚禁兽人逃出强盗窝，成功逃出一人即奖励1点贡献点。现六人全部逃出，共奖励6点贡献点。】

商非凡：……行吧，他已经感受到脑载系统最后的倔强。

同时也说明这个烧火工可能真的很重要，也许关系到游戏新地图的推进，或者是故事主线的展开？

商非凡还有一个小小猜想。

他猜，如果他没有提前来到这个强盗窝，这个烧火工的故事线应该是在天残谷主率领玩家们推强盗窝的时候才会跳出来。

说不定推翻这个强盗窝和救出烧火工，还会成为这个全息游戏的一次重大剧情资料片。

但现在他提前来了，脑载系统就搞了个先下手为强，截胡了这条故事线。

虽然不知道这对脑载系统有什么好处，但……

管它呢。反正这样做对他又没有什么害处，他还赚到了贡献点。

天残谷主是谁？

和他不熟。

商非凡特别残酷特别冷漠地无视了人家游戏很可能会因为这次截胡出现巨大bug的凄凄未来。

哦，对了，他的皮质笔记本还被强盗给搜走了。

想要补回来还得花二十银。

他没钱，只能暂时放生笔记本系统。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 28: Unexpected Results (Part 2)

Originally, he had only purchased the Stinky Fruit to mask the bloody scent on the furnace hand, never expecting its destructive force to be this astronomical. It proved far more effective than the twenty-silver kitchen fire he had bought, truly plunging the bandit den into utter chaos.

If not for the bandit leader's ironclad order commanding every single bandit to rescue and defend the armory,恐怕 all the bandits would have bolted straight out of the stinking encampment.

Quietly tossing the squeezed-dry fruit skin at the feet of passing bandits, Shang Feifan took a sudden turn, merged into the milling crowd, and vanished from sight in a few swift weaves.

On the other side, the player-orcs and the middle-aged orc had split up. Initially, they thought their chances of escaping were slim, and when they heard footsteps pursuing them from behind, some even went weak at the knees, wanting to drop to the ground and beg for mercy.

To their absolute shock! The bandit den suddenly erupted into chaos—true, unadulterated chaos.

Several bandits sprinted right past them, clamping their noses, completely failing to notice their presence.

Sensing a revival of hope, the player-orcs and the middle-aged orc pushed the overpowering stench to the back of their minds. The bolder ones mingled with the running bandits to bolt outward, while the timid ones ducked and dodged, inching their way forward step by step.

There were also a few unlucky souls who didn't know where the exit was and ran around aimlessly, only to wind up back in the heart of the bandit den before blindly tagging along with bandits fleeing the stench.

Shouldering the furnace hand, Shang Feifan followed dozens of orcs who couldn't stomach the foulness and charged out through a stone-piled gatehouse.

The gate guards were utterly powerless to stop these orcs from taking it upon themselves to burst the gates open. Besides, the guards themselves were desperate to put distance between the camp and these "good brothers" drenched in the obnoxious odor.

Once outside, the dozens of bandits all bolted in a single direction.

Catching snippets of their conversation, Shang Feifan realized those bandits were making a dash for the water source.

Slowing his pace, Shang Feifan peeled off from their group.

Under the dark shroud of night, none of the fleeing bandits noticed that two members were missing from their ranks. They were all consumed by the desperate urge to scrub themselves clean and wash away the stench clinging to their bodies.

Carrying the furnace hand, Shang Feifan ran further and further away.

He heard the prompt indicating the completion of Quest Nineteen, and 3 contribution points were credited to his account.

Running for a stretch, Shang Feifan spotted no subterranean fissure, meaning he wasn't retracing his steps.

He halted on a wind-sheltered little hill, set down the furnace hand, and first tested his breathing.

Fortunately, there was still air.

He then carefully inspected the fellow's injuries, discovering a cracked skull, a litany of external wounds, and heavy bruises and bloodstains across his chest, abdomen, and back. For the moment, it was impossible to tell whether the furnace hand had sustained internal injuries, let alone fractured bones.

How was he supposed to save him?

Shang Feifan was forced to open the game store once more.

Instead of immediately buying healing medicine, he muttered to himself: "This chain quest is a total ripoff. I took such massive risks, only to blow every single contribution point I earned right here on this furnace hand. If I don't save him, I'd at least have a net profit of 2 contribution points right now.

If I save him, given injuries this severe, it'll cost at least 2 to 3 contribution points just to buy effective medicine. Meaning my final net profit will probably still be 2 points—maybe 3 at most. Why on earth should I put myself through all this trouble?"

"Forget it. I might as well just set him free here."

Shang Feifan actually stopped browsing for medicine and turned as if to walk away from the furnace hand.

Ding-dong.

[Quest Twenty-One: Help the imprisoned orcs in the dungeon escape the bandit den. Successfully escaping with one grants 1 contribution point. All six have now escaped, granting a total of 6 contribution points.]

Shang Feifan: ...Fine. He could truly feel the final, stubborn pride of his neural-loaded system.

At the same time, this implied that the furnace hand might genuinely be important, perhaps tied to the advancement of a new game map or the rollout of the main storyline?

Shang Feifan harbored one tiny conjecture.

He guessed that had he not arrived at this bandit den early, this furnace hand's storyline would likely only have triggered when the Master of Sky-Remnant Valley led players to raid the bandit den.

Perhaps uprooting this bandit den and rescuing the furnace hand would even serve as a major plot expansion pack for this holographic game.

Yet now that he had arrived ahead of schedule, the neural system had preemptively seized the initiative, hijacking this storyline.

Though he didn't know what good this did for the neural system, but...

Whatever. It didn't hurt him in the least, and he even pocketed contribution points out of it.

Who was the Master of Sky-Remnant Valley?

He didn't know him.

With utter coldness and cruelty, Shang Feifan completely ignored the wretched future where the game might encounter massive bugs purely due to this hijacked sequence.

Oh, right—his leather-bound notebook had also been confiscated by the bandits.

Replacing it would cost another twenty silver.

He had no cash, so he had no choice but to temporarily "release" the notebook system into the wild.

第29章 会合

商非凡在游戏商城的药物栏里挑挑拣拣，花了2个贡献点买了一瓶“初级修复液”。

根据说明，这玩意可以修复致死和致残以下的轻伤，对于内伤也有一定效果。中度伤害以上可以缓解。

商非凡捏开烧火工的嘴，把药液倒进其口中。

接下来就是等待。

商非凡把玩着瓶身，瓶身看起来像玻璃，但他刚学会的铁匠技能之一辨识矿物，让他直觉这瓶子的材料不是玻璃，很可能是和他买的那盏油肚虫灯的罩子材质一样。

瓶身也不大，只有手指粗细。

商非凡随手把瓶身塞进怀里。

烧火工眼皮抖动。

叮咚，商非凡收到系统提示，他完成了任务十八，得到了3个贡献点。

扣除所有用掉的贡献点，他现在一共剩余10个贡献点。

烧火工刚一醒来就开始疯狂呕吐。

太臭了！

这气味对于伤者实在太过刺激。

“别浪费我的药剂。你知道这附近哪里有水源吗？”

商非凡轻轻踢了踢趴在地上的烧火工。

烧火工想要捂鼻，却闻到自己的手也有臭味。想撕下衣服堵住鼻孔都不行，因为衣服更臭。

臭味刺激也让烧火工大脑清醒过来。

他没有立刻回答商非凡的问题，而是偷偷观察四周。

天色黑暗，看不清远方，但根据附近地形可以判断出，他现在似乎并不在强盗窝营地，这是野外？

最重要的是，他原本疼痛到让他昏厥的伤势似乎不再让他那么痛苦，身体还暖洋洋的，就像是春天在家睡了一个懒觉，被阳光暖醒的感觉。

烧火工挪动身体，发现他的伤势貌似愈合了大半，再抬手摸头，头顶被大厨用锅铲硬抽出来的裂痕变成了一块硬疤。

包括手背、手臂……他能看到的伤口部位，都是愈合状态。

“你……救了我？”烧火工表情扭曲，要和这股臭气相抗衡，太难了！

“显而易见的事。水源在哪里？”商非凡再次问道。

烧火工也受不了了，站起来略微判断，迅速抬手指向十点方向：“那边，我跟他们去打过水，那里有一条河。”

“河水流淌方向？”

烧火工不明其意，但还是比划了一下回答：“就是从上面往下流。”

商非凡根据烧火工比划的方向看出河水是从西往东流，之前奔赴水源而去的几十个强盗是往东边跑，那么他们就只能去往西边，还得把距离拉得越长越好，务必不能让那些强盗发现他们。

“走。先把身上的臭味洗掉。”

烧火工赶紧爬起来，跟上商非凡。

他还有点搞不清楚状况，跟在后面喏喏地问：“您是谁？为什么要救我？您带来我出来，那些强盗知道吗？”

“你觉得他们可能知道吗？”商非凡似笑非笑：“你叫阿城？”

“……对。”烧火工满是惊讶。就连那些强盗都不知道他叫阿城，这是他的小名。在强盗窝，大家都叫他瘦鼠。

“认识摩罗城炼药大师弟子嗡东亭吗？”

阿城目光微微一闪，“您是……呕！”

商非凡加快脚步：“先把身上的臭味洗掉，再说其他。”

阿城也不说话了，为了跟上商非凡的速度，也为了更看清周围环境，他身体一缩，竟然变成了一只圆头长尾的紫黑色小貂。

就是营养不太好，让他原本光润的皮毛都枯涩了。

商非凡还是第一次亲眼看到有兽人从人形变成兽形。

但他很好地掩饰住自己的表情，把快走变成奔跑。

紫黑色小貂从衣服里钻出来，不想再要那沾满了血和臭味还破破烂烂的衣服鞋袜，飞快跟上商非凡。

阿城还奇怪这位救命恩人为什么不变身成兽身，这样可以让他们速度更快，也能让他们在晚上看得更清楚。

商非凡压根就没想到还能变身的事，就算想到，他也不会变！

两人一路狂奔，距离强盗窝越来越远。

臭果虽然臭，但对逃跑也有好处，一路上的虫兽凶禽等刚闻到味儿就全都远远逃开，没有一个来找两人麻烦。

商非凡听到了水流声。

两人接近了河边。

小貂超过商非凡，一头冲进河水里。

这种臭果的臭气可以凝聚两三天不散，但只要用水冲洗就能除味。

因为效果绝佳，一般都是当做强力驱虫剂来使用。用的时候，人都会离开除虫地点，直到气味散尽后才会回来。

商非凡听到了轰隆的落水声。

顺着落水声往前走，他看到了一道巨大的瀑布。

瀑布落入裂开的地缝中。

这边的地缝两边相距更远，中间有将近四五十米的裂口。

商非凡看到这条地缝，反而露出笑容。

不过现在不是召唤狰爷的时候，就算狰爷听到他的召唤，闻到他的臭味，也不会过来。

商非凡靠近河边，观察周围和河水里有没有危险。

他见那小貂在近岸的河水里沉沉浮浮，周围似乎没有水类生物攻击他。

也许臭果的气味连水类生物都不愿意靠近？

商非凡特意等小貂洗干净爬上岸，他这才走进河水里。

小貂果然发出人声催促他：“不要太深入河水，里面有可怕的生物，会把我们拖进去。那些强盗除非打水，平时都不敢靠近河岸，等臭味洗没了就赶紧出来！”

商非凡听劝，穿着衣裤鞋连带骨刀和脚镣锁链把自己涮了几遍，就迅速上岸。

再调整自己的嗅觉到满值。

很好，臭味已经变得很淡。

“我们不能在河岸边待太久，河里的巨鳄会爬出来袭击兽人。”小貂再次提醒。

两人就往远离河岸的方向走。

小貂看商非凡顺着地缝往前走，焦急：“那边是回去强盗窝的路，我们得顺着河道往上游走。”

“我在等我的伙伴。”商非凡找了两块石头，互相击打，发出特定的召唤声。

野外空旷，敲击声传出很远。

商非凡也不能确保狰爷能听见，他打算一路走一路敲。

小貂却不肯再往前走，就怕碰到巡逻的强盗。

这里还在强盗窝的巡逻范围内，太不安全。

商非凡看他过于紧张，就让他在原地等待自己。

小貂又不肯了，他怕商非凡把他丢下。

“您、您为什么救我？我该怎么称呼您？”

“我接到任务，要把你带到摩罗城，交给嗡东亭。”商非凡直接道。

阿城眼中闪过狂喜。他就说他失踪后，他家人肯定会向佣兵公会发布任务，他能在强盗窝熬到现在，就是有这么一股坚信他家人一定会找到他的信念在支持着他。

现在，希望果然出现了。

“但我有自己的事情，有自己要去的地方。如果摩罗城顺路，我就带你过去。如果不顺路，你就自己过去。”商非凡真是这么想的。

一听商非凡这么说，烧火工焦急起来，“您要去什么地方？”

商非凡没有回答，反问：“你知道摩罗城在哪里吗？”
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 29: Rendezvous (Part 1)

Poking around the medicine tab of the game store, Shang Feifan spent 2 contribution points to purchase a bottle of "Junior Repair Fluid."

According to the description, this concoction could mend minor injuries short of fatal or disabling wounds, and possessed a certain efficacy against internal injuries. For moderate wounds and above, it could provide relief.

Prying open the furnace hand's jaws, Shang Feifan poured the fluid down his throat.

Next came the wait.

Twirling the vial in his hand, Shang Feifan noted it looked like glass; however, his newly acquired blacksmithing skill, Mineral Identification, gave him an intuitive sense that the material was not glass at all. It was likely the exact same substance as the lampshade of the Oil-Belly Bug Lantern he had purchased.

The bottle was diminutive, merely the thickness of a finger.

Casually, Shang Feifan tucked the vial into his bosom.

The furnace hand's eyelids fluttered.

Ding-dong! Shang Feifan received a system prompt: he had completed Quest Eighteen and obtained 3 contribution points.

Deducting all spent contribution points, his current balance stood at a total of 10 contribution points.

The moment he regained consciousness, the furnace hand began to retch violently.

Too stinky!

This stench was altogether too assaulting for someone in his battered state.

"Don't waste my potion. Do you know where there's a water source nearby?"

Shang Feifan gave the prone furnace hand a gentle kick.

The furnace hand tried to cover his nose, only to find that his own hands reeked just as badly. Ripping off a strip of clothing to stuff his nostrils was out of the question, as his garments smelled infinitely worse.

The stimulation of the stench also cleared the furnace hand's groggy head.

Instead of answering Shang Feifan's question immediately, he cast furtive glances around him.

The night was dark, obscuring the distance, but judging from the surrounding terrain, he didn't seem to be in the bandit camp anymore—was this the wilderness?

Most importantly, the pain that had previously brought him to the verge of fainting seemed to have largely subsided. His body felt warm, reminiscent of taking a lazy nap at home in spring and being gently baked awake by the sunshine.

Shifting his body, the furnace hand realized his injuries had seemingly healed by more than half. Raising a hand to touch his head, he found that the fissure smashed into his scalp by the head chef's spatula had crusted over into a hard scar.

From the back of his hands to his arms... every wound in his field of view was in a state of mending.

"You... saved me?" The furnace hand's expression twisted; fighting off this wave of stench was simply too arduous!

"An obvious conclusion. Where is the water source?" Shang Feifan asked again.

Unable to bear it any longer either, the furnace hand struggled to his feet, made a brief mental calculation, and hastily pointed toward the ten-o'clock direction: "Over there. I've been sent to fetch water with them before; there's a river."

"Which direction does the river flow?"

Failing to grasp the intent behind the question, the furnace hand nonetheless gestured and replied: "It flows from high up down."

Judging by the direction indicated, Shang Feifan deduced that the river flowed from west to east. Since the dozens of bandits who had bolted for water earlier ran eastward, they themselves had no choice but to head west, extending the distance as far as possible to ensure those bandits never discovered them.

"Let's move. Wash that stench off first."

Scrambling up in haste, the furnace hand fell in step behind Shang Feifan.

Still somewhat bewildered by the situation, he asked timidly from behind: "Who are you? Why did you save me? And did those bandits know you brought me out?"

"Do you think it's possible they knew?" Shang Feifan gave a half-smile. "Your name is A-Cheng?"

"...Right." The furnace hand's eyes widened in shock. Even those bandits didn't know his name was A-Cheng; that was his childhood pet name. Back in the bandit den, everyone called him Skinny Rat.

"Do you know Weng Dongting, the disciple of the Grandmaster Alchemist of Molo City?"

A-Cheng's gaze flickered slightly. "You are... Ugh!"

Shang Feifan quickened his pace: "Wash the stench off your body first, then we'll talk."

Ceasing his questions, A-Cheng shrank his body down to keep pace with Shang Feifan's speed and peer more clearly through the surrounding gloom, abruptly transforming into a purple-black marten with a round head and a long tail.

He was simply poorly nourished, leaving his once-lustrous fur dull and coarse.

It was the first time Shang Feifan had witnessed an orc shift from human form to beast form with his own eyes.

Yet, masking his expression admirably, he transitioned his brisk walk into a full run.

Emerging from his clothes, the purple-black marten abandoned his blood-stained, reeking, tattered garments, shoes, and socks, sprinting rapidly to keep up with Shang Feifan.

A-Cheng couldn't help wondering why his savior hadn't transformed into his beast form; doing so would have granted them greater speed and sharper night vision.

Shang Feifan hadn't even considered the possibility of transforming, and even if he had, he wouldn't have done it!

The two ran wildly all the way, putting greater and greater distance between themselves and the bandit den.

Though noxious, the Stinky Fruit had its perks; beasts, monsters, and fierce birds along the path fled far away the moment they caught a whiff of the odor, leaving not a single one behind to hassle the pair.

The sound of rushing water reached Shang Feifan's ears.

They were nearing the riverbank.

Overtaking Shang Feifan, the little marten plunged headfirst into the river water.

The reek of the Stinky Fruit could linger for two to three days, but it could be neutralized instantly by a thorough water rinse.

Because of its stellar efficacy, it was normally deployed strictly as a heavy-duty insect repellent. When applied, people would evacuate the treated zone until the scent dissipated entirely before returning.

Shang Feifan heard the roaring sound of falling water.

Following the sound forward, he beheld a massive waterfall plunging into a fractured subterranean fissure.

The chasm here was wider on both sides, spanning a gap of nearly forty to fifty meters across the middle.

Catching sight of this fissure, Shang Feifan broke into a smile instead.

Of course, this wasn't the time to summon Master Zheng. Even if Master Zheng heard his call, he wouldn't come near after catching a whiff of his stench.

Approaching the riverbank, Shang Feifan scanned the perimeter and the river current for potential threats.

Seeing the little marten bobbing up and down in the shore-side shallows without any aquatic creatures attacking him, he deduced that perhaps even water-dwellers preferred to steer clear of the Stinky Fruit's stench.

Waiting specifically until the marten had washed clean and crawled ashore, Shang Feifan stepped into the river himself.

True to form, the marten piped up in a human voice to urge him: "Don't venture too far into the current; there are terrifying beasts in there that will drag us under. Normally, even those bandits never dare approach the riverbank unless they're fetching water. Get out the moment the smell washes off!"

Heeding the advice, Shang Feifan dunked his clothes, shoes, bone shackles, and iron chains in the water several times before scrambling swiftly back to dry land.

Dialing his sense of smell back up to maximum:

Splendid. The stench had faded to a negligible trace.

"We can't linger by the riverbank; giant river-crocs crawl out to ambush orcs," the marten warned once more.

The two began moving in a direction away from the riverbank.

Noticing Shang Feifan tracing the edge of the chasm forward, the marten grew anxious: "That leads back toward the bandit den! We need to follow the river channel upstream."

"I'm waiting for my companions." Selecting two stones, Shang Feifan struck them together to produce a distinctive summoning signal.

In the empty wilderness, the ringing impact carried far into the distance.

Shang Feifan couldn't guarantee that Master Zheng would hear it, but his plan was to strike the stones all the way as they walked.

Yet the marten dug his heels in, terrified of running into patrolling bandits.

They were still well within the patrol perimeter of the bandit den; it was far too unsafe.

Seeing how high-strung the creature was, Shang Feifan told him to wait in place while he checked ahead.

The marten refused outright, terrified that Shang Feifan would abandon him.

"Wh—Why did you save me? What should I call you?"

"I accepted a quest to bring you to Molo City and hand you over to Weng Dongting," Shang Feifan stated flatly.

A surge of wild ecstasy flashed in A-Cheng's eyes. He had known it! After his disappearance, his family would undoubtedly issue a quest through the Mercenary Guild. The unwavering faith that his family would track him down was the sole conviction that had sustained him through the horrors of the bandit den.

Now, hope had indeed materialized.

"But I have my own matters to attend to, and my own destination. If Molo City happens to be on the way, I'll take you there. If not, you'll have to make your own way." That was precisely what Shang Feifan intended.

Hearing this, the furnace hand panicked: "Where are you going?"

Without answering, Shang Feifan countered with a question: "Do you even know where Molo City is?"

chunks.chineseText:
小貂飞快点头：“摩罗城距离这里不算太远，顺着河道往上，越过一道悬崖，悬崖后面就是大平原，按照我们现在的脚程计算，只要走大约二十多天就能到达。”

当然，旅途危险，如果加上各种特殊情况，那就远远不止二十多天。小貂怕时间说长了，这名兽人更不愿带他去摩罗城。

优秀的方向感让商非凡脑中自然形成一副大致地图：“先往北，再往东，摩罗城在强盗窝的东北边？”

黑森林城却在强盗窝的东边，不算太顺路，但应该可以同行一段路。

方向感不是特别好的小貂：“应该是……吧。”

“黑森林城距离摩罗城多远？”商非凡是个谨慎人，他不会让没有获得他信任的人知道他真正的目的地。

小貂一听商非凡的目的地有可能是黑森林城，大喜过望：“我没去过黑森林城，但摩罗城有前往黑森林城的专车和空乘，两城来往很多。”

小貂怕商非凡不肯绕路，又飞速补充：“您是不是没有去过摩罗城？摩罗城是虎国最著名的药城，这座城里有很多炼药大师，虎国最大的药师协会总会也在摩罗城。摩罗城有通往各大城市包括王都在内的专车和空乘，听说还有传送阵。”

“传送阵？”商非凡没想到他还能听到这么奇幻的交通方式。

这个世界似乎越来越向神秘侧靠拢。

“就是传说，我也没有见过。”小貂吹牛吹过头，连忙弥补：“您救了我，我一定会报答您。如果您能把我安全送到摩罗城，我家人一定会支付让您满意的报酬。”

“你落到强盗手上时，为什么不告诉那些强盗，你有亲人是炼药大师的弟子？就算让你家人出赎金，也总好过被困在强盗窝里被他们虐待的好吧？”商非凡盯着小貂的眼睛。

天色虽然黑暗，但商非凡觉得他看得还算清楚，到现在都没有觉得有什么不方便。

小貂看到商非凡冷不丁发出幽绿色光芒的眼眸，吓了一跳。

野兽的眼眸在晚上变成绿色很常见，但没有变身的兽人很少会这样。

但很快，商非凡的眼眸就没有那么亮了，虽然还是绿莹莹的。

“我……不想拖累他们。这些强盗贪得无厌，一旦让他们知道我和摩罗城的炼药大师有关系，他们不但不会只收一笔赎金就放过我，还会就此控制住我，借我来从我的亲人身上掠取更多好处。”小貂期期艾艾地说。

最重要的是他不想让摩罗城的任何人知道他落到了强盗手中，当初是他主动离开摩罗城，还是灰头土脸的离开，如果让人知道他落下狠话离开从小长大的城市，最后不但没有做出一番事业，反而成了强盗的奴隶……他宁可死在外面！

人生经验丰富的商非凡哪能看不出这只小貂隐瞒了部分事实，但无所谓，他对打探任务对象的心事没兴趣，更不想当知心哥哥。

小貂不断朝强盗窝的方向看，又开始催促商非凡：“那些强盗晚上也会出来巡逻，如果他们发现我们……我们就两个人，肯定跑不掉。”

商非凡不急，笃定地说：“今天晚上不会有强盗出来巡逻，现在也不适合往东边走。我们需要洗掉身上的臭味，他们同样。”

小貂张张嘴，他还以为身上沾到臭味的只有他们两个。

商非凡不但没有往东边走，他还顺着地缝继续往强盗窝的方向走。

小貂心惊胆战，但想到地缝这边没有水源，又比较危险，强盗就算巡逻也不会太靠近地缝。而和地缝相接的大瀑布距离强盗窝的直线距离要比他们往东边河道跑的距离远得多，应该也不会有强盗特意绕这么远的路来洗澡，尤其身上味道那么臭的时候。

哒哒哒，哒哒哒的敲击声不断响起。

但混合在夜晚的虫鸣中并不突兀，这就是模仿巨蟹虫召唤伙伴的声音。

两人边走边停，大约过了一个多小时，小貂困乏得都要睡着了。

地缝里突然冒出一只巨大的身影。

商非凡露出笑容，嘴唇模仿振翅声。

狰爷跳出地缝，欢快地跑到商非凡面前，还抬起一根长腿碰了碰商非凡。

狰爷宽阔的背部探出一颗方方的小脑袋。

阿呆呆呆地看着站在那里的商非凡好一会儿，哇地一声哭出来，还从狰爷的背上直接跳了下来。

商非凡手臂一伸，接住了嚎啕大哭的小家伙。

“哭什么？鼻涕脏死了。”商非凡嫌弃。

“呜呜哇，爸爸，你好臭啊……呜呜！”阿呆一边哭一边用小爪子扒拉老商的皮甲。

小貂被惊醒，抬头就看到这么一副父子分离八百年终于见面的温情（？）场面。

Little Mink nodded rapidly. "Molo City isn't too far from here. If we follow the river upstream, cross a cliff, and head onto the vast plain right behind it... at our current pace, it should take us roughly twenty-odd days to get there."

Of course, the journey was full of danger. Factoring in various unforeseen circumstances, it would take far longer than twenty days. Little Mink was simply afraid that if he quoted too long a timeframe, this beastman wouldn't be willing to take him along.

Shang Feifan’s exceptional sense of direction naturally formed a rough mental map in his head. "First north, then east... Molo City lies northeast of the bandit den?"

Black Forest City was due east of the bandit den, which wasn't entirely on the way, but they could likely travel together for a stretch of the journey.

Little Mink, whose sense of direction wasn't particularly stellar, stammered, "I... think so."

"How far is Black Forest City from Molo City?" Shang Feifan was a cautious man; he would never reveal his true destination to someone who hadn't earned his trust.

Hearing that Shang Feifan’s destination might be Black Forest City, Little Mink was overjoyed. "I’ve never been to Black Forest City myself, but Molo City has dedicated carriages and aerial transport heading there. There's constant traffic between the two cities!"

Fearing that Shang Feifan might refuse to make a detour, Little Mink hastily added, "Have you never been to Molo City before, sir? Molo City is the most famous city of medicine in the Tiger Kingdom. Countless grandmaster alchemists reside there, and the main headquarters of the Tiger Kingdom's Alchemists' Association is located there as well. They have dedicated ground transports and aerial transports leading to every major city, including the royal capital—I’ve even heard they have teleportation formations!"

"Teleportation formations?" Shang Feifan hadn't expected to hear about such a fantastical mode of transportation.

This world truly seemed to be leaning closer and closer to the realm of the mystical.

"Well, that's just a legend. I haven't seen one myself either," Little Mink quickly backtracked, realizing he had exaggerated a bit too much. He scrambled to make amends: "You saved my life, sir, and I will definitely repay you! If you can safely escort me to Molo City, my family will pay you a reward that will surely satisfy you."

"When you fell into the hands of those bandits, why didn't you tell them that your relative was the disciple of a grandmaster alchemist?" Shang Feifan stared into Little Mink's eyes. "Even if your family had to pay a ransom, wouldn't that be better than being trapped in a bandit den and abused?"

Though the night was dark, Shang Feifan felt he could see quite clearly and hadn't experienced any inconvenience up to this point.

Little Mink flinched when Shang Feifan’s eyes suddenly gleamed with an eerie green light.

It was common for wild beasts' eyes to glow green in the dark, but it was rare for a beastman who hadn't shifted forms to do so.

Soon, however, the glow in Shang Feifan’s eyes dimmed slightly, though they remained faintly iridescent green.

"I... didn't want to drag them down," Little Mink faltered, looking down. "Those bandits are insatiably greedy. Once they found out I was connected to a grandmaster alchemist in Molo City, they wouldn't just take a single ransom and let me go. They would use me to control my family and extort even more benefits out of them."

Most importantly, he didn't want anyone in Molo City to know he had been captured by bandits. He had left Molo City on his own initiative back then, leaving in total disgrace. If people found out that after making grand promises and walking away from the city where he grew up, he ended up accomplishing nothing and instead became a slave to bandits... he would rather die out in the wilderness!

With his rich life experience, how could Shang Feifan fail to see that the little mink was hiding part of the truth? But it didn't matter. He had no interest in prying into his mission target's private secrets, nor did he want to play the role of a comforting big brother.

Little Mink kept glancing toward the direction of the bandit den, anxiously urging Shang Feifan again, "Those bandits send out patrols at night too. If they spot us... there are only two of us, we definitely won't be able to run away."

Shang Feifan was in no rush, stating with absolute certainty, "No bandits will be patrolling tonight, and right now isn't a good time to head east anyway. We need to wash the stench off ourselves, and so do they."

Little Mink opened his mouth in surprise. He had assumed they were the only two covered in the foul odor.

Instead of heading east, Shang Feifan actually led the way further along the earth fissure, heading back toward the bandit den.

Little Mink’s heart beat wildly in terror. But thinking about it, there was no water source near the fissure, and it was quite dangerous, so bandits wouldn't venture too close during patrols. Furthermore, the massive waterfall connected to the fissure was much further in straight-line distance than heading east along the river. No bandit would travel so far out of their way just to take a bath—especially when they reeked so terribly.

*Tap-tap-tap, tap-tap-tap...*

A rhythm of soft tapping sounds echoed continuously, blending seamlessly into the night's insect chirps without sounding out of place. It was an imitation of the signal giant crab insects used to call their companions.

The two walked and paused repeatedly. After about an hour, Little Mink was so exhausted he was practically falling asleep on his feet.

Suddenly, a massive silhouette emerged from the earth fissure.

A smile touched Shang Feifan’s lips, and his mouth mimicked the sound of buzzing wings.

Lord Zheng leaped out of the fissure, scuttling merrily up to Shang Feifan and using one of its long legs to gently nudge him.

From behind Lord Zheng’s broad back, a tiny, square head poked out.

Ah Dai stared blankly at Shang Feifan standing there for a long moment before bursting into a loud, blubbering cry. He dropped straight down from Lord Zheng’s back.

Shang Feifan stretched out an arm and caught the wailing little guy.

"What are you crying for? Look at all those gross snot bubbles," Shang Feifan said with mock disgust.

"Waaah! Dad, you smell so bad... boohoo!" Ah Dai wept, using his little paws to scratch at the old man's leather armor.

Awakened from his daze, Little Mink looked up, only to be met by this touching (?) scene of a father and son reuniting after a long separation.

chunks.chineseText:
第30章 倒霉的老商

“我们先离开这里。”

商非凡招呼小貂，抱着阿呆跳上狰爷的背。

小貂在狰爷脚边徘徊几秒，见它并不反对自己上去，就顺着狰爷的长脚一路爬上去。

狰爷身体动了动，它貌似也嫌弃商非凡和小貂身上的臭味，但还在能忍受的范围内。

商非凡把阿呆和小貂一起塞进网兜里，双手抓住直立骨刺，脚尖轻点：“狰爷，走了！”

狰爷按照商非凡的指示，向河道飞速奔跑。

晚上才是它们最活跃的时候，深黑的夜色对它们没有任何障碍。

阿呆歪头看小貂。

小貂抬爪子，向这只皮毛斑秃不太好看的方头小家伙打招呼。

这个一看就是幼崽，和他天生体型小不一样。

阿呆往角落缩了缩，似乎认生，也可能是被臭到，不太想要接近这个陌生人。

小貂虽然有意和这只幼崽打好关系，但见对方有点排斥他，也没有硬贴上去找不愉快。

有巨虫坐骑就是不一样，小貂身体终于放松下来——如果真遇到强盗，他们打不过还可以跑。只要强盗不使用臭雾果……

小貂连忙提醒商非凡，表示强盗窝有一种能致使人和巨虫昏迷的果实，比较珍贵，他们只有遇到大肥羊才会使用，但也难保不会用在他们身上。

商非凡就是着了臭雾果的道，怎么可能不提防这点。

所以他询问狰爷，能不能从瀑布这边直接过河。

狰爷凝视河道和瀑布，往后退了两步。

商非凡明白了：狰爷没有把握可以横渡这条河。这条河里一定有让狰爷忌惮的生物。

“那我们就往上游走。”

商非凡计算了他们寻找和等待狰爷的时间，盘算那些去河道洗澡的强盗应该都已经洗完回到强盗窝附近。

但也有可能碰到后面分批次去洗澡的强盗。

但他们也不能一直在这里等待，等到强盗们把库房和强盗窝全都收拾好，一定会下大力去寻找逃出的兽人。

任何人吃了这么一个大亏，在不知道是谁动手的情况下，只会想要报复任何一个能报复的人。

狰爷顺着河道奔跑起来。

商非凡始终警戒着，两只眼睛发出绿幽幽的荧光。

商非凡也发现他能在夜晚看出去很远，还能看得很清楚，视觉只比白天差一点。

他也没多想，以为这就是兽人本身拥有的特长之一。

河道边比他想象得要安静，可能夜晚出来喝水捕食的动物全都被臭跑。

这对他们显然很有利。

远处隐约有说话声传来。

商非凡让狰爷放慢脚步，看能不能躲过这批强盗。

狰爷很灵活地找到一处可以遮挡它巨大身体的凹陷，趴了下去。

河道边长满灌木和野草。

有水源滋润，这些植物长得十分茂盛，野草都有一米多高。

商非凡示意阿呆和小貂都不要发出声音，他也跟着趴下。

说话声变得清晰。

十几个强盗结伴而行，大多变身成了兽体，少数几个人形大咧咧地光着身体，手里提着湿叽叽的衣服鞋。

他们在骂人，说狠话。

商非凡侧耳细听，似乎强盗头子已经告诉强盗们，是逃出地牢的肉羊在强盗营地放火、涂抹臭果汁液，造成强盗窝大乱。

强盗头子在分批次同意强盗们去河边洗澡的同时，也命令这些兽人沿着河道寻找逃出的肉羊。

但强盗头子也担心这是调虎离山之计——他想不通那些逃出的肉羊是从哪里弄来的臭果，又是如何溜进厨房放火，以为是有外人支援，就留了大半的强盗在营地守护库房重地、加强整个强盗窝的防守。

到河边洗澡顺便找人的强盗们对于头领命令的执行力度不太高。

这些强盗始终对河中生物怀有忌惮，并不想在河道边多待。

而且他们晚饭都还没怎么吃，一个个都饿着肚子，现在是又饿又困，只想回去弄点吃的赶紧睡觉。如果不是没有多少寻找肉羊的心情，他们也不至于一路走一路骂骂咧咧，一点都不担心被逃跑的肉羊们听到。

商非凡看到那十几个兽人往他们这边越走越近，神色不见半丝慌乱，只是他的手握紧了骨刀，随时准备杀出去。

小貂的视线被野草挡住，但他也听到了强盗的说话声，重新变得紧张起来。

商非凡忽然感觉到狰爷似乎有一些不安，它发育不完全的翅膀动了动，紧紧贴住身体两侧。

没一会儿，狰爷忽然变得无声无息，就好像死掉了一样。

商非凡先以为狰爷在警惕那些靠近的强盗，但……

有什么不对劲！

在战区待了多年的商非凡对危险感知非常敏锐。

他发现周围的虫鸣声全都消失了，虽然有大量虫鸟动物被臭走，但跑得并不远，他在路上还是能听到野外独有的各种声音。

可这会儿，河道边乃至附近一大片全都变得安静至极。

河水流淌的声音在此时变得特别突出明显。

那十来个无心寻找逃跑肉羊的强盗们也莫名其妙止住了说话声，他们要么握紧了武器，要么警惕地看向周围。

阿呆紧紧缩成一团，他不知道外面发生了什么，他只是本能地感到恐惧。

小貂同样如此，跟阿呆一样缩紧了自己。

商非凡猛地抬头。

天空中-出现了重叠排列的月亮，这还是他第一次在游戏世界看到月亮。

游戏世界的太阳和地球差别不大，没想到晚上的月亮竟然有七个，还是重叠排列的状态。

七个月亮从远到近，远处的最小，近处的最大，仔细看，它们之间的排列距离还十分均等。

这个游戏世界的潮汐影响一定很大，也一定会因此发生更多诡异的事情。商非凡脑中突然掠过这么一个想法。

之前七个重叠月亮一直躲在云朵背后，这会儿全都跑了出来。

大地被照耀得明亮许多。

如果月亮们没有转变成红色就更好了。

血月很美，但也不可否认那会让看到的人类不安，更别说这是七个血月重叠。

商非凡亲眼看到原本亮白色的月亮们从近到远一点点转变成红色。

妖异，美丽，又有说不出的诡秘……

咚咚，咚咚……心跳声逐渐变大，他不但听到了自己的心跳声，还听到了自己血液在血管中流动的声音。

太-安静了，安静到所有声音寂灭的程度。

这是怎么回事？

难道有什么极为可怕的捕猎者出现了？

还是有什么异常天象即将发生？

商非凡目光投向那十几个强盗。

他们似乎也不知道发生了什么事，但本能让他们停下所有动作，他们甚至不敢说话。

就在这时，一名面向河道的强盗脸上露出极度恐惧的神情，他的眼睛睁得极大，嘴巴也张开了，却没有发出半点喊声。

“快、快跑！”这是另一名强盗，他的身体在颤抖，但他也是所有强盗中反应最快的一个。

该强盗发出微弱的提醒后，自己第一个向强盗窝方向狂奔。

其他强盗被他带动，跟着疯狂奔跑起来。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 30: Unlucky Old Shang

"Let's get out of here first."

Shang Feifan motioned to Little Sable and scooped A-Dai up as he leaped onto Zheng Ye's back.

Little Sable lingered by Zheng Ye's feet for a few seconds, and seeing that the beast didn't object to him climbing aboard, he scrambled all the way up using Zheng Ye's long legs.

Zheng Ye shifted its body. It seemed to despise the foul stench clinging to Shang Feifan and Little Sable as well, but it was still within tolerable limits.

Shang Feifan stuffed A-Dai and Little Sable together into a net pouch, grabbed the upright bone spikes with both hands, and lightly tapped his toes. "Zheng Ye, let's go!"

Complying with Shang Feifan's directions, Zheng Ye sprinted swiftly toward the river.

Nighttime was when they were most active, and the pitch-black darkness posed no obstacle to them whatsoever.

A-Dai tilted his head to look at Little Sable.

Little Sable raised a paw, waving a greeting to this patchy-furred, rather homely, square-headed little fellow.

This one was clearly a cub, unlike himself who was naturally small-statured.

A-Dai shrank back into the corner, seemingly suffering from shyness around strangers, or perhaps overwhelmed by the stench, unwilling to get close to this unfamiliar face.

Although Little Sable intended to get on the good graces of this cub, seeing that the little one was somewhat repulsed by him, he didn't press forward and make himself unwelcome.

Having a giant insect mount made all the difference; Little Sable's body finally relaxed. If they truly ran into bandits, they could fight or run. As long as the bandits didn't use Foul-Fog Fruit...

Little Sable hurriedly reminded Shang Feifan, explaining that the bandit den possessed a precious fruit capable of causing humans and giant insects to lose consciousness. They only used it when encountering extremely wealthy targets, but there was no guarantee they wouldn't use it on them.

Shang Feifan had fallen victim to the Foul-Fog Fruit himself; how could he possibly fail to guard against it?

Thus, he asked Zheng Ye whether it was possible to cross the river directly from the waterfall side.

Zheng Ye gazed at the river and the waterfall, then took two steps back.

Shang Feifan understood: Zheng Ye was not confident it could cross this river safely. There must be creatures in the river that made Zheng Ye wary.

"Then we'll head upstream."

Shang Feifan calculated the time they had spent searching for and waiting to reunite with Zheng Ye, reckoning that the bandits who had gone to the river to bathe should have finished and returned to the vicinity of the bandit den by now.

However, there was also a chance they might run into bandits going to bathe in later batches.

Still, they couldn't just wait here indefinitely. Once the bandits finished tidying up their storehouse and camp, they would definitely mobilize heavily to hunt down the escaped Orcs.

Anyone who suffered such a massive loss, without knowing who was behind it, would only want to exact vengeance on any target within reach.

Zheng Ye broke into a run along the riverbank.

Shang Feifan remained on high alert at all times, his two eyes emitting a faint, eerie green glow.

He had also discovered that he could see a great distance in the night with remarkable clarity, his vision only slightly inferior to daylight.

He didn't dwell on it too much, assuming this was simply one of the innate traits possessed by Orcs.

The riverbank was much quieter than he had expected. Perhaps the animals that usually came out at night to drink and hunt had all been driven away by the stench.

This was clearly advantageous to them.

Faint voices drifted from afar.

Shang Feifan had Zheng Ye slow its pace to see if they could bypass this group of bandits.

Zheng Ye nimbly found a depression capable of concealing its massive body and dropped flat to the ground.

The riverbank was overgrown with bushes and wild grass.

Nourished by the water source, these plants grew with extraordinary vigor, with the wild grass standing over a meter tall.

Shang Feifan signaled A-Dai and Little Sable to remain completely silent, and he dropped flat alongside them.

The voices grew clearer.

A dozen or so bandits were walking together. Most of them had transformed into their beastly forms, while a small handful remained in human form, swaggeringly stark naked as they carried damp clothes and shoes in their hands.

They were cursing and spouting vicious threats.

Shang Feifan cocked his ear to listen closely. It seemed the bandit leader had already informed his men that the livestock who escaped the dungeon had set fire to the camp and smeared foul fruit juice everywhere, throwing the bandit den into chaos.

While permitting the bandits to visit the river in batches to wash up, the bandit leader had also ordered these Orcs to search the riverbank for the escaped livestock.

However, the bandit leader was also worried this might be a trick to lure the tiger away from its mountain—he couldn't figure out where the escaped livestock had gotten hold of the foul fruit or how they had sneaked into the kitchen to start a fire, suspecting outside assistance. Consequently, he had kept the majority of the bandits at the camp to guard the vital storehouse and reinforce the camp's overall defenses.

The bandits going to the river to wash up while searching on the side showed very little enthusiasm for executing their leader's orders.

These bandits harbored a lingering dread of the river's creatures and had no desire to linger by the riverbank.

Moreover, they hadn't even properly eaten dinner yet; their stomachs were rumbling, and they were starving and exhausted. All they wanted was to head back, rustle up some food, and crash into sleep. If they hadn't been completely devoid of any mood to hunt down escaped livestock, they wouldn't have cursed all the way along, completely unconcerned about being overheard by the runaways.

Shang Feifan watched as the dozen-odd Orcs drew closer and closer to their hiding spot, his expression devoid of the slightest panic. His hand merely tightened around his bone blade, ready to strike at a moment's notice.

Little Sable's line of sight was blocked by the tall grass, but he too heard the bandits' voices, and tension gripped him once more.

Suddenly, Shang Feifan sensed that Zheng Ye was growing restless. Its underdeveloped wings twitched, pressing tightly against the sides of its body.

A moment later, Zheng Ye abruptly fell completely silent, as if it had died.

Shang Feifan initially thought Zheng Ye was on guard against the approaching bandits, but...

Something was wrong!

Having spent years in war zones, Shang Feifan possessed an extremely acute perception of danger.

He noticed that all the insect chirping around them had vanished. Although a vast number of insects, birds, and animals had been driven off by the stench, they hadn't run far, and he could still hear various unique sounds of the wild along the way.

Yet at this moment, the riverbank and the surrounding vast area had grown utterly, deathly still.

The sound of the flowing river water suddenly became exceptionally prominent and distinct.

Those dozen-odd bandits, who had had no heart to search for escaped livestock, inexplicably choked off their conversation. They either tightened their grips on their weapons or cast wary, searching gazes around them.

A-Dai huddled tightly into a ball. He didn't know what was happening outside; he only felt a primal, instinctive terror.

Little Sable was the same, curling up tightly just like A-Dai.

Shang Feifan jerked his head up.

Overlapping layers of moons had appeared in the sky—this was the first time he had ever seen moons in this gaming world.

The sun in the gaming world differed very little from Earth's, but he hadn't expected there to be seven moons in the night sky, and arranged in an overlapping formation at that.

The seven moons ranged from distant to near; the furthest was the smallest, and the closest was the largest. Looking closely, the spacing between their arrangements was remarkably uniform.

*The tidal effects in this game world must be immense, and it's bound to trigger even more bizarre events because of it.* Such a thought flashed through Shang Feifan's mind.

Previously, the seven overlapping moons had been hiding behind the clouds, but now they had all emerged.

The earth was illuminated with a much harsher brightness.

It would have been even better if those moons hadn't turned red.

A blood moon was beautiful, but one could not deny that it would unnerve any human who beheld it, let alone when seven blood moons overlapped.

Shang Feifan watched with his own eyes as the originally bright white moons gradually shifted to red, one by one, from closest to furthest.

Eerie, beautiful, and filled with an indescribable, unfathomable secrecy...

*Thump-thump, thump-thump...* The sound of his heartbeat grew louder and louder. Not only could he hear his own heartbeat, but he could even hear the sound of his blood rushing through his veins.

It was *too* quiet—quiet to the point where all sound was extinguished.

What on earth was going on?

Could some terrifying predator have appeared?

Or was some abnormal celestial phenomenon about to take place?

Shang Feifan cast his gaze toward the dozen or so bandits.

They seemed equally clueless as to what was happening, but instinct halted all their movements; they didn't even dare to speak.

At that very moment, the face of the bandit turned toward the river twisted into an expression of extreme terror. His eyes bulged to their absolute limit, and his mouth hung open wide, yet not a single sound of a scream escaped his lips.

"Run... run!" That was another bandit. His body was trembling violently, but he was also the fastest to react among all the bandits.

After issuing that faint warning, he took off running like a madman toward the bandit den.

Spurred by him, the other bandits broke into a frantic, panicked dash.

chunks.chineseText:
他们不知道为什么这么恐惧，但此刻，他们只想赶紧逃离河岸！

那名面向河道的强盗身体却似被冻住一般，整个人都凝固了。

“呜——”

商非凡听到了一声像是大风刮过的呜鸣声。

他也在看河道，但他什么也没有看到。

不，他虽然没有看到，但他感觉到有什么庞然大物从河道里出来了。

丝丝缕缕的雾气从河面升起，逐渐向四周蔓延。

雾气弥漫的速度极快。

商非凡的视线被遮挡。

他听到了惨叫声。

倏地转头。

他看到了明明已经跑出很远的十几个强盗在一瞬间全都爆成了血花。

血花还没有落到地面就消失了。

雾气似乎被血花染红，又像是被血月染红，变得血气弥漫。

血红色的雾气在向强盗窝的方向延伸，同样笼罩住了他们。

……

天亮了。

阿呆啪地睁开眼睛，一骨碌爬起来。

他爸爸呢？

他刚找回来的爸爸去哪里了？

狰爷还在，他们的行李还在。

但他的爸爸不见了！

同样不见的还有那只小貂。

阿呆焦急地团团转。

狰爷撑起身体。

“带我去找我爸爸。”阿呆跟老商学了一点基本操纵巨蟹虫的方法。

但可能他说的话太复杂，狰爷半天没动。

等到狰爷终于理解（？）他的意思，狰爷从草丛里跳出来，背对河道，一路跑向强盗窝。

那里有好吃的东西。

它在过地缝的时候就闻到了，可惜碰到了讨厌的臭雾果，还发现了好多对它不怀好意的讨厌兽人。

现在，它能感觉到让它讨厌的兽人和东西都消失了。

它终于可以去寻找那好吃的东西了。

它的兽人伙伴？

大概已经死了吧。

它要怎么告诉那个寄居在它身上的兽人幼崽，它爸爸已经被怪物吃掉了呢。

也就是他们好运，怪物放过了他们。

阿呆什么也不知道，他跟着狰爷一路跑进了强盗营地。

强盗营地一片空荡荡。

建筑物都还在，南北两边的围墙大门也都紧紧关闭着。

但围墙和哨塔上不见一个强盗。

狰爷不用大门，顺着墙壁一路往上爬，很顺利地就爬进强盗营地中。

一路都极为安静。

没有人声，也没有豢养牲畜和坐骑的声音。

狰爷一路跑到库房门口。

用爪子扒拉紧锁的大门。

好吃的就在里面。

就是要费点工夫挖开它的外壳。

“爸爸——！”

阿呆大声呼唤起来。

“爸爸，你在哪里？”

阿呆看狰爷一心一意只想要扒开那扇紧闭的大门不肯离开，就从狰爷的背脊上爬下来，一边跑一变喊。

烧掉大半的大厨房和食堂还冒着黑烟，除了焦糊味，还有肉类和谷类被烤熟的香味。

阿呆在强盗营地中跑来跑去，没有找到半个活物。

偌大的营地，似乎只有他和狰爷。

商非凡现在在哪里？

老商自己也不知道。

他最后记得的景象就是血雾笼罩了他们。

然后……他的记忆就断片了。

等他意识再次清醒，他已经成为串烧大军中的一员。

一连串的兽人，不管是兽体还是人体，全都被绑缚串联起来，被人用鞭子抽打着往前走。

从他前后兽人身上的穿着看，这些被抓的兽人有不少都是强盗窝中的强盗。

阿呆呢？

狰爷呢？

还有那个烧火工阿城呢？

商非凡不知道这条漫长的串烧队伍中有没有他要找的人，他刚探出身体往前后看，就被飞过来的鞭子抽打了一鞭。

手持鞭子的兽人脸色狰狞，两只巨大的牙齿露在嘴唇外面。

兄弟，要不要考虑一下牙齿整形？你这样会不会很不方便吃饭？商非凡竟然还对抽打他的兽人笑了一下。

兽人发出沉闷咆哮：“不要东看西看！走！”

商非凡神态很碉地对巨齿兽人点点头，从容地跟上前面兽人的步伐，不再试图脱队。

巨齿兽人用力瞪商非凡。

他还是第一次看到这么奇怪的兽人。

只看这兽人的神态，不知情的还以为他是被邀请来出席宴会的大佬，而不是被绳子拴着手脚脖颈只能被迫等待命运降临的可怜虫。

更奇怪的是，其他兽人都还没有恢复神智，只能木愣愣地跟着队伍走，可这个兽人竟然这么快就恢复了清醒。

巨齿兽人记住了这个奇怪兽人，并盯住了他。

商非凡无视自己在一条失魂队伍中有多么异常，他抬头看天空，再看周围环境。

这里绝对不是强盗窝。

天空灰蒙蒙的，透着一点暗红。

他们正走在荒野中，但脚下的土路很清晰，这是一条被经常踩踏形成的野道。

不远处，他看到了一座巨大城池的身影。

叮咚。

【打开新地图点，奖励贡献点10点。】

商非凡震惊，他还是第一次获得这么多贡献点，还这么轻易。

这里是哪里？竟然让吝啬的脑载系统一下奖励给他这么多贡献点。

脑载系统似乎也在犹豫要不要提醒他，过了好一会儿，才磨磨蹭蹭地发布出一个新任务。

【任务二十二，检测到新地图环境十分危险，请倒霉的你努力活过三个小时。成功后奖励3点贡献点。】

商非凡：“……”

系统这是有多么不看好他？

而且什么叫倒霉的你？！
chunks.englishText:
They didn't know why they were so terrified, but in this moment, all they wanted was to flee from the riverbank as fast as possible!

Yet the bandit facing the river seemed frozen in place, his entire body stiffened solid.

"Wooow—"

Shang Feifan heard a low, wailing groan, like a gust of fierce wind blowing past.

He was looking toward the river as well, but he saw nothing.

No... though he couldn't see it, he could feel some colossal entity emerging from the river channel.

Strands of dense mist rose from the surface of the water, rapidly spreading in all directions.

The mist expanded at a terrifying speed.

Shang Feifan’s vision was completely obscured.

Then came the screams.

He snapped his head around.

He saw the dozen bandits—who had clearly run a long distance away—burst into bursts of bloody mist in a single instant.

The blood sprays vanished before they could even hit the ground.

The mist seemed to be dyed crimson by the blood, or perhaps by the blood moons, becoming heavy with the reek of gore.

The blood-red mist surged toward the direction of the bandit camp, engulfing them as well in its wake.

...

Day broke.

Ah Dai snapped his eyes open and scrambled up in a hurry.

Where was his dad?

Where did the dad he had just found go?

Lord Zheng was still here, and their luggage was still here.

But his dad was gone!

Also missing was that little mink.

Ah Dai spun around in anxious circles.

Lord Zheng pushed its body up.

"Take me to find my dad," Ah Dai said, having learned a few basic command methods for controlling the giant crab insect from old Shang.

However, perhaps the sentence was too complex for it, as Lord Zheng remained motionless for a long time.

When Lord Zheng finally seemed to understand (?) his meaning, it hopped out of the grass, turned its back to the river, and sprinted all the way toward the bandit camp.

There was delicious food over there.

It had smelled it back when they crossed the earth fissure. Unfortunately, it had run into that detestable Stink Mist Fruit back then, along with a bunch of annoying beastmen who harbored ill intentions toward it.

Now, it could sense that those annoying beastmen and terrible odors had all vanished.

It could finally go search for that delicious food.

As for its beastman partner?

He was probably dead already.

How was it supposed to tell the beastman cub piggybacking on its shell that his father had already been eaten by a monster?

They were simply lucky that the monster had spared them.

Ah Dai knew nothing of this. He rode Lord Zheng all the way into the bandit camp.

The bandit camp was completely deserted.

The structures were all intact, and the main gates on both the north and south palisades were tightly shut.

Yet not a single bandit could be seen on the walls or watchtowers.

Lord Zheng didn't need the gates. Scaling the walls with ease, it climbed right into the camp.

It was dead silent the whole way.

There were no human voices, nor any sounds of livestock or mounts.

Lord Zheng ran straight to the storehouse door.

It used its claws to scratch at the locked doors.

The delicious food was inside.

It just needed to put in a little effort to pry open its outer shell.

"Dad—!"

Ah Dai called out at the top of his lungs.

"Dad, where are you?"

Seeing that Lord Zheng was single-mindedly intent on tearing open the locked door and refused to leave, Ah Dai climbed down from Lord Zheng’s back, running through the camp while shouting as he went.

The mostly burned kitchen and mess hall were still emitting black smoke. Aside from the burnt odor, there was the fragrance of roasted meat and grains.

Ah Dai ran back and forth across the bandit camp, but he couldn't find a single living creature.

In this vast camp, it seemed only he and Lord Zheng remained.

Where was Shang Feifan right now?

Old Shang didn't know himself.

The last memory he had was of the blood-red mist enveloping them.

And then... his memory had gone blank.

By the time his consciousness returned, he had already become a member of a chained marching line.

A long line of beastmen—whether in beast or human form—were all bound and chained together, being driven forward by guards cracking whips.

Judging from the attire of the beastmen in front of and behind him, quite a few of these captives were actually bandits from the camp.

Where was Ah Dai?

Where was Lord Zheng?

And what about Ah Cheng, the kitchen hand?

Shang Feifan didn't know if the people he was looking for were in this long, chained column. Just as he leaned his body out to look forward and backward, a whip slashed through the air and struck him squarely.

The beastman holding the whip had a fierce, brutal face, with two massive tusks protruding outside his lips.

*Brother, have you considered getting dental braces? Doesn't that make it super inconvenient to eat?* Shang Feifan actually flashed a faint smile at the beastman who had whipped him.

The beastman let out a muffled roar: "Don't look around! Keep moving!"

Shang Feifan gave the big-tusked beastman an impossibly cool nod, calmly keeping pace with the beastman ahead of him, no longer attempting to break rank.

The big-tusked beastman glared hard at Shang Feifan.

This was his first time seeing such a bizarre beastman.

Judging purely by this guy's posture and composure, anyone unaware would think he was a high-status boss invited to attend a grand banquet, rather than a miserable wretch with his hands, feet, and neck bound by ropes, helplessly awaiting his grim fate.

Even stranger was that the other beastmen hadn't even regained their senses yet, numbly following the queue like mindless puppets. Yet this beastman had actually regained full clarity so quickly.

The big-tusked beastman etched this strange beastman into his memory and kept his eyes locked on him.

 Shang Feifan ignored how anomalous he looked among a line of soul-drained captives. He raised his head to look at the sky, then surveyed the surrounding environment.

This was definitely not the bandit camp.

The sky was a hazy gray, tinged with a faint shade of dark red.

They were walking through a wasteland, but the dirt path beneath their feet was clearly defined—a wild trail forged from frequent trampling.

Not far in the distance, he caught sight of the looming silhouette of a massive city.

*Ding!*

【New map point discovered. Rewarded 10 Contribution Points.】

Shang Feifan was stunned. This was the first time he had earned so many Contribution Points at once, and so effortlessly at that.

Where was this place? It had actually caused the stingy brain-hosted system to suddenly hand out so many Contribution Points!

The brain-hosted system seemed to hesitate over whether to remind him. Only after a good long while did it reluctantly issue a new task.

【Task 22: Detected that the new map environment is extremely dangerous. Please try your best to survive for three hours as the unlucky person you are. Upon successful completion, 3 Contribution Points will be awarded.】

Shang Feifan: "..."

Just how little faith did this system have in him?

And what on earth did it mean by "the unlucky person you are"?!

chunks.chapterTitle: 第31章 学徒级诅咒祭司 (Part 1)
chunks.chineseText:
第31章 学徒级诅咒祭司

队伍还在缓慢前进。

商非凡正在翻看游戏商城，寻找合适的工具，打算逃跑。

盯着他们的只有几个丑陋的巨齿兽人，每个巨齿兽人负责一段距离。

他旁边那个一直在盯着他，他不用看都能感觉到对方凶狠的目光。

拘束他手脚、缠绕住他脖子的是绳子，没有锁头。

绳子不知道是什么材质，摸上去绝不是金属，但也不像是麻绳。

商非凡试着弹出指甲，他的食指指甲竟然真的变长变尖，微微弯曲，宛如虎爪。

他的手腕和脖颈并排绑在一起，这个姿势对于想要逃跑的人非常不友好，但他手掌张开也正好可以遮掩另一只手的动作。

锋利的虎爪在绳子上来回摩擦，绳子竟然只起了一点毛，按照这个磨损程度，至少得磨半个小时才能磨得断。

而那座看着就充满不祥的巨大城池已经近在眼前。

商非凡最终决定了要购买的商品，这花掉了他3个贡献点。

一只瓶子出现在商非凡手掌心。

悄悄使力拔-出瓶塞，把瓶子里的液体倾倒在绳子上。

他的手很稳，瓶子里的液体准确落在绳索上，半点没有碰到皮肉。

“滋——”

一股白烟冒起。

“你在干什么！”

鞭子伴随怒吼声，同时朝商非凡的头脸落下。

商非凡上半身往后一仰，躲过骨鞭，手指灵活又稳定地塞上瓶塞，两腕用力挣开已经断裂的绳索，伸手一把薅住巨齿兽人的头毛，压低，另一只握住瓶子的手猛击他的面部鼻梁。

一连串动作快到眨眼之间全部完成。

“嗷！”巨齿兽人痛呼出声，鼻血和眼泪狂涌而出。

还没等他剧烈挣扎，两只拳头重重击中他两边太阳穴。

巨齿兽人眼皮一翻，昏死过去。

商非凡丢掉巨齿兽人，迅速弯身，拔掉瓶塞，把里面那危险至极的腐蚀药水倒在脚腕附近的绳索上。

“滋——”，白烟冒起，他的脚腕也自由了。

他前后的兽人受到他动作影响，脚步磕绊，导致这一小片都停顿混乱了一下。

前面监督的巨齿兽人转头看到后方混乱，看到自己的伙伴倒在地上，立刻大叫起来。

商非凡大脑飞速计算，电光石火间就做出决定，他不等巨齿兽人围杀过来，就先一步对着最近的巨齿兽人冲刺过去。

他刚刚放倒一个巨齿兽人，发现这些巨齿兽人身躯高大面目凶狠力气也很大，但动作迟缓，只要自己反应比他们快、力气也比他们大，想要干倒这几个巨齿兽人并不难。

最重要的是，他前后左右都看了，负责押送这支队伍的巨齿兽人加起来就五个人。

发出大喊的巨齿兽人万万没想到那个逃离队伍的兽人不但没有逃跑，反而还冲他杀了过来。

砰砰砰！

商非凡出手，招招都是杀招，每一拳都是冲着对方要害而去。

巨齿兽人举着长鞭想要回击，但商非凡的速度太快，他还没有扬起鞭子，对方的拳头已经砸到他的脸上。

鼻梁！脾脏！脖颈！

巨齿兽人身体瘫倒在地。

商非凡一把抄起巨齿兽人掉落的骨鞭，再次冲向第三个巨齿兽人。

前面三个巨齿兽人已经反应过来，全都暴怒喊叫着什么，一起向商非凡这边哐哐哐地冲杀过来。

一对三！

巨齿兽人的身体全都超过两米，比将近两米的商非凡高出半个头。

三个大高个一起冲过来的架势非常怕人。

商非凡跳了起来，骨鞭狠狠抽向最左边的巨齿兽人，同时他左手一扬，已经拔掉瓶塞的腐蚀液体泼到中间巨齿兽人的脸上，

惨叫和怒嚎同时响起。

商非凡跳起的身体踩踏左边巨齿兽人的肩膀，骨鞭用力抽打在最右边兽人的耳朵上。

左右两边巨齿兽人被重鞭击打得头骨裂开，中间的巨齿兽人捂着脸不断惨叫，他们还想反击商非凡。

商非凡半空拧身落地，一双长腿一个回旋飞踢。

砰！

右边的巨齿兽人被踢得飞出三米多远。

商非凡再次挥动骨鞭，他的力气要比巨齿兽人大得多，一鞭子下去就能把巨齿兽人的骨头给抽断。

三名巨齿兽人失去先机，又都受了重伤，根本组织不起来有效反攻。

不到半分钟，三名冲杀过来的巨齿兽人全都重伤倒地。

商非凡嫌那名头脸被腐蚀的巨齿兽人叫得太难听，把对方也给抽昏了过去。

头脸被腐蚀的巨齿兽人双手从脸上滑下来。

商非凡不小心瞄了一眼，当即倒抽一口凉气。

这腐蚀药剂真他妈厉害！

竟然连骨头都腐蚀烂了。

幸好他使用的时候足够小心，没有沾到自己。

就是可惜刚才泼洒时无法控制多少力道，瓶子里的腐蚀液体已经见底。

商非凡捡起被他顺手扔到地上的瓶子，用专用的塞子把瓶口塞紧，把用过的小瓶子塞进怀里。

他有个收集各种小瓶子的爱好~

缓行的队伍并没有因为这场打斗停止，那些失去神智的兽人还在往前走。

最前面的兽人已经快要接近城门。

城门口似乎有骚动，像是已经发现这边出现变故。

商非凡沿着队伍快速奔跑。

找到了！

倒霉的烧火工阿城还是小貂的样子，他被绑在一只驴形兽人的背脊上。

商非凡掏出装有腐蚀药剂的瓶子，倒转瓶口，试图把里面最后一滴液体给倒到绳子上。

一秒，两秒……

城池门口的守卫在往这边跑。

吧嗒，最后一滴腐蚀药液滴在绳索上。

商非凡收起瓶子，两手握住绳索两段，使出八成力气，用力一扯！

啪！绳索被扯断。

商非凡迅速解开剩下的绳索，把小貂从绳索里掏出来。

一手提着小貂，一手提着骨鞭，飞速撤离。

守卫追来了。

商非凡跑得飞快，眼看距离那座不祥的巨大城池越来越远。

后面追赶的守卫突然停下脚步，不再追赶。

一座一望无际的城市废墟突然出现在商非凡眼前。

就那么冷不丁地冒出来。

商非凡来不及刹住脚步，又往前冲刺了几步。

一种怪异的感觉让商非凡下意识回头。

见鬼！

追他的守卫不见了。

那支被串烧在一起的失魂队伍也不见了。

包括那座巨大的不祥城池也同样消失无踪。

系统没有任何提醒。

第一次，商非凡不知道自己该停下脚步，还是继续往前走。

这个地方真的太诡异了！

前方的城市废墟让商非凡越看越觉得古怪。

他以为这个世界的文明发展大约与地球的中世纪类似，结果他现在看到了什么？

他竟然看到了一座满是高楼大厦的现代化都市。

虽然这座都市已经被摧毁，高楼大厦全都变成了断壁残桓。

他甚至看到一座架设在半空中的环形高架轨道，轨道也大多残破断裂。

他还看到了一座也许以前是地标建筑的巨大雕像。

那座雕像的头颅被削掉了一半，手臂也断了一根，身体中间满是裂痕。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 31: Apprentice-grade Cursing Priest (Part 1)

The procession continued to move at a slow pace.

Shang Feifan was flipping through the game mall, searching for suitable tools with the intention of escaping.

The only things keeping a watchful eye on them were a few ugly Toothed Orcs, each responsible for a designated stretch of the road.

The one right beside him kept staring at him; he didn't even need to look to feel the vicious glare burning into him.

He was bound hand and foot, with a rope wrapped around his neck, though there were no locks.

The material of the rope was unknown; touching it, it was definitely not metal, nor did it feel like hemp rope.

Shang Feifan tried flexing his fingernails, and his index fingernails actually grew longer and sharper, curving slightly like a tiger's claws.

His wrists and neck were bound together in a parallel fashion—a posture extremely unfriendly to anyone planning to escape—but by spreading his palm wide, he could just manage to conceal the movements of his other hand.

The sharp tiger claws rubbed back and forth against the rope, yet it only managed to fray the surface slightly. At this rate of wear and tear, it would take at least half an hour to saw through it.

And that huge city, which looked ominous just by the sheer sight of it, was already looming close ahead.

Shang Feifan finally decided on the item he wanted to purchase, which cost him 3 Contribution Points.

A small bottle appeared in the palm of Shang Feifan's hand.

Quietly exerting strength, he pulled out the cork and poured the liquid from the bottle onto the rope.

His hand was remarkably steady; the liquid dropped precisely onto the bindings without touching a single inch of his flesh or skin.

"Hisss—"

A puff of white smoke rose into the air.

"What are you doing?!"

A whip lash accompanied an angry roar as it descended straight toward Shang Feifan's head and face.

Shang Feifan leaned his upper body backward, dodging the bone whip. With fingers that were both nimble and steady, he jammed the cork back into the bottle, used all his strength in both wrists to snap the already weakened bindings, reached out to grab a handful of the Toothed Orc's hair, forced his head down, and struck the brute's nasal bridge violently with the hand still holding the bottle.

The entire sequence of movements was completed in the blink of an eye.

"Aargh!" the Toothed Orc let out a cry of agony as a torrent of nosebleed and tears gushed forth.

Before the beast could thrash about wildly, two heavy fists slammed mercilessly into both of his temples.

The Toothed Orc's eyes rolled back, and he passed out cold.

Shang Feifan discarded the unconscious brute, quickly bent down, pulled the cork, and poured the lethally dangerous corrosive potion onto the ropes around his ankles.

"Hisss—" White smoke rose, and his ankles were freed as well.

The orcs immediately in front of and behind him were disrupted by his movements, their footsteps stumbling, causing this small section of the line to halt in a moment of confusion.

The supervising Toothed Orc further up the front turned his head to look at the commotion in the rear and spotted his comrade lying motionless on the ground. He immediately let out a loud screech.

Shang Feifan's brain calculated at lightning speed, making a decision in a fraction of a second. Instead of waiting for the Toothed Orcs to swarm him, he took the initiative and charged directly at the nearest beast.

Having just knocked down one Toothed Orc, he realized that although these creatures were towering in stature, fierce-looking, and possessed immense brute strength, their movements were sluggish. As long as his reflexes were quicker and his strength greater, taking down a few of these brutes wouldn't be too difficult.

Most importantly, after scanning front, back, left, and right, he confirmed that the total number of Toothed Orcs escorting this procession was only five.

The screaming Toothed Orc never expected that the captive who had broken free not only failed to run away, but actually countercharged straight at him.

Bang, bang, bang!

Shang Feifan struck, every single blow aimed to kill, every punch targeted at vital anatomical weak points.

The Toothed Orc raised his long whip to counterattack, but Shang Feifan was far too fast. Before the whip could even be raised high, the opponent's fist had already smashed into his face.

The bridge of the nose! The spleen! The neck!

The Toothed Orc's body collapsed limply to the ground.

Shang Feifan snatched up the bone whip dropped by the fallen orc and lunged toward the third Toothed Orc.

The remaining three Toothed Orcs had now reacted, roaring in absolute fury as they all charged fiercely toward Shang Feifan with heavy, booming footfalls.

One against three!

Every single one of the Toothed Orcs stood over two meters tall, making them half a head taller than Shang Feifan, who was himself nearly two meters.

The momentum of three towering giants charging together was terrifying.

Shang Feifan leapt into the air, the bone whip lashing out viciously at the Toothed Orc on the far left. Simultaneously, his left hand flicked upward, splashing the uncorked corrosive liquid directly into the face of the middle Toothed Orc.

Shrieks of agony and enraged howls erupted in unison.

Mid-air, Shang Feifan's leaping body kicked off the shoulder of the left-hand Toothed Orc, while the bone whip cracked forcefully against the ear of the right-hand beast.

The orcs on the left and right had their skulls cracked open by the heavy whipping, while the middle orc clutched his face, shrieking incessantly as they still attempted to counterattack.

Twisting in mid-air, Shang Feifan landed gracefully and unleashed a sweeping roundhouse kick with his long legs.

Bang!

The orc on the right was sent flying over three meters away.

Shang Feifan swung the bone whip once more. His physical strength far exceeded that of the Toothed Orcs; a single lash of his whip was enough to snap their bones.

Having lost the initiative and sustained heavy injuries, the three Toothed Orcs were completely incapable of mounting an effective counter-offensive.

In less than half a minute, all three charging Toothed Orcs crashed heavily to the ground, critically wounded.

Finding the screeching of the orc whose face had been corroded too grating on the ears, Shang Feifan lashed out with the whip and knocked him unconscious as well.

The face-corroded Toothed Orc's hands slipped down from his visage.

Shang Feifan accidentally caught a glimpse and immediately sucked in a sharp breath of cold air.

This corrosive potion was truly fucking terrifying!

It had actually dissolved the bones right down to the flesh.

Fortunately, he had been exceedingly careful during application and hadn't let a single drop touch himself.

It was just a pity that, due to the inability to control the flow rate during the splash, the corrosive liquid in the bottle was now completely exhausted.

Shang Feifan picked up the bottle he had casually tossed aside, sealed the opening tightly with its specialized stopper, and tucked the small, used vial into his bosom.

He had a little hobby of collecting various kinds of tiny glass bottles~

The slowly shuffling procession hadn't paused because of this brief scuffle; those mind-numbed beasts kept trudging forward.

The orcs at the very front were already nearing the city gates.

A commotion seemed to be stirring at the entrance, as if the turmoil here had already been detected.

Shang Feifan sprinted rapidly along the side of the procession.

Found him!

The hapless stoker A-Cheng was still in his form as a small sable, bound securely to the back of a donkey-shaped beast.

Shang Feifan pulled out the vial containing the corrosive potion, inverted it, and attempted to coax the very last drop of liquid onto the rope.

One second, two seconds...

The guards at the city gates were beginning to run over in this direction.

*Drip*, the final drop of corrosive liquid fell onto the bindings.

Shang Feifan stowed the bottle away, gripped both ends of the rope with his hands, mustered eighty percent of his strength, and gave a fierce yank!

Crack! The rope snapped apart.

Shang Feifan swiftly unwound the remaining bindings and scooped the little sable out of the restraints.

Holding the little sable in one hand and the bone whip in the other, he bolted away at top speed.

The guards were in hot pursuit.

Shang Feifan ran at a blistering pace, watching the distance grow rapidly between himself and that ominous, gigantic city.

The guards chasing from behind suddenly halted their footsteps and gave up the chase.

A boundless expanse of city ruins suddenly materialized before Shang Feifan's eyes.

It popped up just like that, out of nowhere.

Shang Feifan was unable to check his momentum in time and stumbled forward a few more steps.

A strange sensation prompted Shang Feifan to look back instinctively.

What the hell?!

The guards chasing him were gone.

The soul-deprived procession strung together like skewered meat had also vanished.

Including that massive, ominous city—it, too, had disappeared without a trace.

The system gave no warning whatsoever.

For the first time, Shang Feifan didn't know whether he should stop in his tracks or keep pushing forward.

This place was entirely too bizarre!

The ruined city ahead made Shang Feifan feel more and more strange the longer he looked at it.
