Shang Feifan had won the goodwill of all the beast-folk in this caravan using his skill at making flatbreads, and he had even helped them repair a cart axle that was on the verge of breaking. That was the trickiest part to fix; once it broke, if there were no spare parts, they would simply have to abandon the cart.

Moreover, Shang Feifan was traveling with a little toddler, and his other beast-folk companion was also thin and small, plus they had their own mount. No matter how you looked at it, they posed zero threat and didn't require any special care. Without much hesitation, the caravan agreed to his request to travel together.

Seeing that everyone's spirits were high and the conversation was lively, Shang Feifan brought it up casually: "I passed through Sky-Shatter Valley, walking for about two days, and ran into a massive fissure in the ground where neither side was visible. The widest gap was easily a hundred meters across. If my mount hadn't found an underground stone bridge, I wouldn't have known how to cross that chasm."

"Ah, I know the fissure you're talking about; that's the famous Abyss Crevice. That place always has all sorts of bizarre things happening, and people frequently go missing there. If you keep walking south along the fissure, you'll see a stone bridge built by nearby beast-folk. Caravans usually cross through there," a young beast-folk livelily chimed in.

chunks.chineseText:
“我听说那边还有一个强盗窝，那边的兽人村落很讨厌，会跟强盗通风报信，吃过亏的商队都会绕着那边走。不过那些强盗也不敢往石桥那边跑，那边有一个大镇子，当地组成了一支兽人民兵队，石桥那儿都有民兵镇守。”另一名兽人也跟着说。

商非凡心想怪不得他一路走来都没有遇到多少兽人，原来是大家都知道那里有一个强盗窝，都绕着那边走。

“我对这边不太熟悉，我也是第一次走这条道。”商非凡咬了一口大饼夹肉咀嚼，等吞下嘴里的食物才说：“在我越过地缝后，我看到了一条大河，就沿着河道走。路上我遇到了几个神色仓惶的兽人，他们像是从哪里逃出来一般。他们原本还想要抢劫我，被我揍了，他们哭得很可怜。我给了他们一些食物，他们跟我说了一件事。”

十几个兽人都来了兴趣，全都看向他。

商队一共有上百名兽人同行，除了商队原本的人，也有不少像商非凡一样主动跟上来的小商人和远行客。

休息地点燃了七八个火堆。

商非凡很容易就混入了商队主人的队伍。

“他们跟我说他们是被强盗抓起来的倒霉鬼，就在他们以为以后要沦为奴隶或强盗时，发生了一件让他们恐惧无比的事情……”

商非凡更换了主角，把“最大杏鲍菇”在论坛里描绘的被吞吃经过，稍微修改后，述说了出来。

篝火边顿时一片沉默。

几名年轻兽人总觉得这事听起来更像是某种异闻传说。

可那名老年兽人，也是商队的副手，忽然面色严峻的开口：“这不是那几个兽人在编故事。商队为什么要避开那一带行走，可不仅仅是因为那里有个强盗窝。实际上，”

老人停顿了一下：“那边一直都有着恐怖传说，你们听过亡灵谷、活尸城吗？”

好几个兽人同时摇头。

“唔，那是过去的传说了，你们好多年轻人都不知道。天残谷，你们总知道吧？”

这次大家都点头了。

阿呆窝在商非凡怀里，跟老商一样的动作，两只小爪子抱着大饼用力啃。

阿城坐在旁边，他这会儿是人形，身上伤势已经痊愈，就是看起来特别瘦。

老人抹抹嘴唇：“天残谷就是原先的亡灵谷，活尸城也就在那一带。在大繁华纪的时候，那一带可是极为繁华的大城市。因为战争，那里死了太多人。毒雾纪时期，那里掩埋的尸体突然就活了……”

商非凡从老人口中听到了和天残村村长跟他说的内容差不多的天残谷历史。

老人继续说：“当时的兽人根本无法抵抗这些根本就不怕伤害、也很难杀死的活尸，于是当时那一带最厉害的祭司就献祭了自己的小儿子和九百九十九个天残兽人，请求神灵帮他们消灭那些活尸。”

商非凡停住咀嚼大饼。这可是天残村村长没有跟他说过的内容！

老人：“神灵给予了回应。那祭司的小儿子变成了不可直视、极为可怕的怪物，当场吞噬了那九百九十九个天残兽人。没多久，所有活尸都消失了。人们都传说，是那怪物带走了那些活尸。”

好些兽人在摩擦自己的手臂，明明很普通的叙述，却让他们打从心底生出一股寒意。

“后来只要那个祭司想要消灭敌人，就会呼唤小儿子的名字，他那变成怪物的小儿子就会出现，先吞噬祭品，然后就会带走祭司的敌人。”

“但是怪物并不是可以被控制的，尤其那怪物还是神灵的奴仆。传说那怪物第二次出现时就吞噬了自己的父亲，自此以后就只有神灵可以命令它，再也没有谁能控制它。”

“但也有人说只要知道那个怪物的名字，呼唤它，就能让它再次出现。”

有年轻兽人忍不住问：“那个怪物叫什么名字？”

老人摇头：“不知道。人们恐惧它，没有人敢真的呼唤它的名字，久而久之就没有人知道它的名字。”

“那大家都怎么称呼……这个不可直视的怪物？”商非凡问。

老人叹息：“大家都称呼它为恐惧之神的奴仆，因为它每次出现都会给人们带来极致的恐惧。你不需要看到它，也不需要听到它，只要它出现，你就知道它来了。因为你的恐惧会告诉你。”

商非凡好奇：“恐惧之神？那是怎样的神灵？”

老人再次摇头：“正神中没有恐惧之神，这只是人们为了方便称呼那可怕的存在，才起了这样一个名字。”

“那当时那名祭司又是向哪位神灵乞求，才换来他小儿子变身成怪物？”商非凡又问。

老人看向商非凡：“不知道。各种说法都有，有人说是战神、有人说是黑暗之神、甚至有人说是知识之神。但神灵的说法在神血族裔没落后，就变成了传说。早在大繁华纪之前，就有神灵早已全部陨落的说法。所以那位祭司乞求的神灵一定不是真正的正位古神。”

“会是大战纪以后诞生的邪神吗？”有年轻兽人小声问。

“谁知道呢。”老人眼睛有些浑浊，“有人说神灵也好、邪神也好都只是迷信传说。但也有人坚信那些超越凡人的存在真的存在，否则神血族裔又是哪里来的呢？”

最后老人说道：“总之，传说中那个恐惧之神的奴仆总是徘徊在活尸之城附近，还有人说它就住在那条深渊裂缝中，当它饥饿时、心情不好时，它就会出来捕猎。每次这位出现都会吞吃一部分祭品，再带走一部分兽人。”

商非凡：“为什么要带走一部分兽人？那一部分被带走的兽人又去了哪里？”

老人笑：“这我就不知道啦。也许是带给神灵了吧。”

商非凡沉默。未知区域会是神之领域吗？感觉还是有点不太像。

老人说古结束，忽然像是临时想起来一样，补充：“有传说说那位特别喜欢臭果的味道，如果有人使用臭果，就有一定可能把那位召唤出来。这也是臭果为什么那么不受欢迎的原因这一，就算使用，炼药师们也会改善臭果的味道。当然，知道这点的兽人很少，这是活尸城附近才有的说法。”

商非凡：“……”

阿城唰地看向商非凡。

阿呆则呆呆地抬起脑袋。

商非凡按住阿呆的方脑袋，什么都不想说。
chunks.englishText:
"I heard there’s a bandit's den over that way. The beastman village nearby is awful—they leak info to the bandits. Any merchant caravan that’s suffered at their hands makes sure to bypass the area entirely. But those bandits don't dare venture toward the stone bridge either. There's a major town over there with a locally organized beastman militia, and they keep the bridge well-guarded," another beastman chimed in.

*No wonder I barely ran into any beastmen along the way,* Shang Feifan thought. *Everyone knows about that bandit nest and gives it a wide berth.*

"I’m not very familiar with this region; it's my first time taking this route as well," Shang Feifan said, taking a bite of his flatbread wrapped around savory meat. After chewing and swallowing, he continued, "After I crossed the ravine, I came across a grand river and just followed the riverbed downstream. On the way, I ran into a few panic-stricken beastmen who looked as though they were fleeing for their lives. At first, they tried to mug me, but after I gave them a thorough thrashing, they wept pitifully. I gave them a bit of food, and in return, they shared a story with me."

A dozen or so beastmen suddenly perked up with interest, all turning their gazes toward him.

The merchant caravan had over a hundred beastmen traveling together. Aside from the original members of the caravan, there were quite a few small traders and long-distance travelers like Shang Feifan who had joined up for safety in numbers.

Around the campsite, seven or eight campfires had been lit. 

Shang Feifan had easily mingled into the group surrounding the leader of the caravan.

"They told me they were unfortunates captured by the bandits. Just as they thought they were doomed to spend the rest of their lives as slaves or bandits, something terrifying beyond belief took place..."

Shang Feifan swapped out the protagonist, recounting the experience of being swallowed—which "Largest King Oyster Mushroom" had described on the forum—with just a few minor modifications.

A sudden silence fell over the campfire.

A few younger beastmen felt the tale sounded more like some wild urban legend or myth.

However, the elderly beastman—who was also the deputy leader of the caravan—suddenly spoke up with a grave expression. "Those beastmen weren't making up stories. The reason caravans avoid that region isn't merely because of a bandit nest. In fact..."

The old man paused for effect before continuing, "That place has always had a terrifying legend attached to it. Have any of you heard of the Valley of Undead Spirits or the City of Living Corpses?"

Several beastmen shook their heads in unison.

"Ah, those are legends from the past. It’s no surprise you young folk don't know. But you must know about Heaven-Handicapped Valley, don't you?"

This time, everyone nodded in agreement.

A'Dai was curled up in Shang Feifan’s arms, mimicking Old Shang's exact posture as he clutched a piece of flatbread with both small paws and nibbled eagerly.

A'Cheng sat beside them in his human form. His injuries had fully healed, though he still looked remarkably thin.

The old beastman wiped his lips. "Heaven-Handicapped Valley was originally the Valley of Undead Spirits, and the City of Living Corpses was right in that general vicinity. Back during the Era of Great Prosperity, that area was a bustling, magnificent metropolis. But because of the war, countless people perished there. During the Era of Toxic Mist, the corpses buried under that land suddenly came back to life..."

From the old man's mouth, Shang Feifan heard a history of Heaven-Handicapped Valley that closely mirrored what the village chief of Heaven-Handicapped Village had told him.

The old man continued, "Back then, the beastmen had no way to resist these living corpses, which feared no pain and were nearly impossible to kill. Thus, the most powerful priest of the region sacrificed his youngest son and nine hundred and ninety-nine handicapped beastmen, begging the gods to help them eradicate the walking dead."

Shang Feifan stopped chewing his flatbread. *This was a detail the village chief never mentioned!*

The old man said, "The gods answered his prayer. The priest's youngest son transformed into an unspeakable, horrifying monster, devouring those nine hundred and ninety-nine handicapped beastmen on the spot. Shortly after, all the living corpses vanished. Legend has it that the monster took the corpses away."

Several beastmen began rubbing their arms. Though it was told in an ordinary narrative tone, a chill rose from the depths of their hearts.

"From then on, whenever the priest wanted to destroy an enemy, he would call out his youngest son's name. His son, turned monster, would manifest, devour the offerings first, and then drag the priest's enemies away."

"However, monsters are not creatures that can be controlled—especially when that monster is a servant of the gods. Legend says that the second time the monster appeared, it devoured its own father. Since then, only the gods can command it; no mortal can control it."

"Yet, some say that as long as you know the monster's name and summon it, it can be made to appear once more."

A young beastman couldn't help but ask, "What was the monster's name?"

The old man shook his head. "No one knows. People feared it so much that no one dared speak its true name. Over time, the name was forgotten."

"Then what did people call... this unspeakable monster?" Shang Feifan inquired.

The old man let out a long sigh. "Everyone referred to it as the Servant of the God of Fear, because every time it appeared, it brought absolute horror to the world. You didn't need to see it, nor did you need to hear it—the moment it arrived, you would know. Because your terror would tell you."

Shang Feifan felt a surge of curiosity. "The God of Fear? What kind of deity is that?"

The old man shook his head again. "There is no God of Fear among the Righteous Gods. It’s merely a title people made up for convenience to address that terrifying entity."

"Then which god did the priest pray to in order to transform his youngest son into a monster?" Shang Feifan probed further.

The old man looked at Shang Feifan. "Who knows? There are all sorts of claims—some say the God of War, some say the God of Darkness, and some even say the God of Knowledge. But after the decline of the Divine-Blooded Lineages, talk of deities faded into mere myth. Even before the Era of Great Prosperity, there were rumors that all the gods had already fallen. So, whichever god that priest prayed to, it certainly wasn't one of the ancient Righteous Gods."

"Could it have been an Evil God born after the Era of Great Warfare?" a young beastman asked in a low voice.

"Who can say for sure?" The old man's eyes looked somewhat cloudy. "Some say gods and evil deities are nothing more than superstitious fables. But others firmly believe that entities transcending mortals truly exist—otherwise, where did the Divine-Blooded Lineages come from in the first place?"

Finally, the old man concluded, "In short, according to legend, that Servant of the God of Fear always wanders around the City of Living Corpses. Some even claim it dwells right within that abyssal rift. Whenever it grows hungry or finds itself in a foul mood, it emerges to hunt. Every time this entity appears, it devours a portion of the offerings and drags away a portion of the beastmen."

Shang Feifan asked, "Why does it drag away a portion of the beastmen? Where do those captured beastmen go?"

The old man chuckled. "That, I do not know. Perhaps they are brought to the gods."

Shang Feifan fell silent. *Could the Unknown Region be a realm of the gods? It doesn't quite feel like it.*

Finishing his story, the old man suddenly added as if just remembering, "There's also a rumor that this entity is exceptionally fond of the scent of Stink Fruit. If someone uses Stink Fruit, there is a chance it might summon that being forth. That's one of the reasons why Stink Fruit is so reviled. Even when alchemists use it, they refine it to alter its odor. Of course, very few beastmen know this—it’s a tale exclusive to the vicinity of the City of Living Corpses."

Shang Feifan: "..."

A'Cheng snapped his head around to stare directly at Shang Feifan.

A'Dai blankly raised its square head as well.

Shang Feifan pressed his hand down onto A'Dai's square head, utterly speechless.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第36章 现实身体的反应 (Part 1)
chunks.chineseText:
第36章 现实身体的反应

幸好没有人知道是他弄出了臭果。

就算阿城有所怀疑，也没有证据。

商非凡老神在在，假装他也是无辜受害者之一。

阿呆会那样望老商，只是觉得老商的运气太糟糕了。

不过他们现在都没事，这运气是不是又算好呢？

这个问题太复杂，阿呆想着想着就变得更呆。

就着这个传说，大家就开始聊他们知道的一些奇闻怪谈。

商非凡突然感觉到来自口袋里的颤动，掏出来一看是他失而复得的笔记本系统。

这玩意落在非玩家手里就是一本普通的皮质笔记本，还是非常常见的款式。

商非凡就看到商队领头和副手口袋里都装着这么一本笔记本，还有一支笔。只不过副手用来早晚清点货物做记录，年轻的商队领头则是用来记录各种见闻。

【更新提示！请诸位玩家注意，为给玩家们带来更好的游戏体验，本游戏将于现实世界时间XX年10月20日凌晨1：00开始进行全服务器维护与系统更新。注：不同时间区域的玩家将显示不同的下线维护时间，请诸位玩家以各自系统收到的个人时间为准。更新完成时间预计为6:00。请诸位玩家注意好时间，做好下线准备，以防装备等物品遗失。尤其是正在野外的玩家，请一定找好安全的地方下线，以防身体有失。】

商非凡挑眉。他很想知道自己如果在笔记本系统要求的时间点不下线的话，会对自己产生什么影响。

不过……到了笔记本系统约定玩家全部下线的时间，商非凡还是下线了。

冒险也分必要和不必要，现在就是不必要。

摘掉头盔，就看伏向军已经先一步醒来。

商非凡忍不住跟伏向军吐槽。

他怎么知道伤敌一千自伤一千八是这种伤法？

而且按照老兽人的说法，臭果会吸引恐惧之神的奴仆，也只是有可能而已。

谁知道到了他这里就成了百分百！

伏向军听了哈哈大笑。

笑完了自己老大的衰运，伏向军问：“会不会跟你买的那个玻璃球也有关系？”

“兴许。”商非凡摸了摸自己的右眼，想到这玩意儿对黑暗的吸引力，他的吐槽也跟着变得无力。debuff太多，也怪不得一定几率变成百分百。

伏向军还嘲笑他，说他还没有看过他在游戏中的果体，结果就先被别人看光了。

商非凡走过去一掌盖在伏向军的脸上，黑着脸：“那家伙就是为了找话题度，我从地牢单间里出来时，身上就已经穿着强盗的衣服，那家伙压根什么都没看见！”

伏向军毫不给面子的继续哈哈哈。

商非凡照例先查看所有监控仪器的检测数据。

网络通讯铃声响起。

商非凡按下通话键。

对面传来研究所张博士的声音：“我们发现了一点小小的异常。或许也不该说是异常，这种变化非常微小，直到连续数天下来，我们才发现这种变化呈现一种缓慢的上升趋势。”

商非凡：“什么变化？”

伏向军也担心地看过来。

张博士：“数据已经传输过去。我们通过你的脑电波活动和血氧水平变化，发现你的精神力在缓慢增长。这种说法比较游戏。详细请看你的大脑神经末梢的转移酶菌群落，那里有一种类似量子结构的微管，我们人类大脑的所有活动，都是由这些数量庞大的微管率先运动，并在确定某种状态，就像是得到明确指令以后再释放脑信号。

这是不是很像是自然形成的量子计算机？实际上我们人类的大脑就是一台比人工制造出来的量子计算机还要发达和精密的超级量子计算机，或者说是生物量子计算机。

而我们目前对这台超级生物量子计算机的开发和应用还不到百分之八……”

商非凡耐心地听张博士跟他科普，这位一说起自己的专业就滔滔不绝。

说了半天，张博士觉得对面应该听懂了，这才说回正事：“我们就是通过这些信号的一系列变化，综合模拟出一条游戏系统中提到的精神力值。然后我们发现，这条精神力值变成了一条缓慢上升的线，这说明你的精神力在一点点提高。如果我们的数据记录和分析都没有出错的话。”

商非凡明白了，这是张博士在跟他验证他在游戏中的个人数据。

想要更好地监控自己的身体，商非凡自然不会隐瞒自己的身体数据，直接就把脑载系统显示出来的个人数据默写下来，输入到计算机中，发给张博士。

张博士在那边看过后，声音变得兴奋：“数据变化还是吻合的，这说明我们的分析没有走错方向。”

“张博士！”对面有女性的提醒声出现。

张博士：“哦。重点不是这个。重点是……你知道我们监测的不是你游戏中那具兽人身体的数据，而是你现实身体的数据，对吧？”

商非凡耐着性子：“嗯。”

张博士声音更加兴奋：“我们发现的精神力变化就是你现实身体中的精神力变化！你明白我的意思吗？人的精神力是一直在变动的，这种精神能量会形成一种不规则的波段。但我们分析出来的精神力值变化曲线是根据微管信号运动分析出来，它在增长！

就像是普通人需要耗费0.1的能量启动自己的思维，但只要超过1这个界限，普通人就会感到精神疲劳，从而让大脑皮丘发出不想工作，想要休息的信号。

但是你的精神能量启动值低到了0.01，而你的精神能量界限值却超过了3。

你知道这代表了什么吗？这代表你可以在别人近乎昏迷的状态仍能有效控制自己的思维甚至是部分-身体，同时你比别人拥有更多的能量去进行思维。别人大脑工作一天就会超负荷，你大脑工作三天仍旧能保持思维清晰。

这是多么惊人的发现！没想到只是一个全息游戏，竟然能对大脑造成这样的影响。

当然，我们现在不知道这种影响是完全良性还是怎样，也不知道这是你的个人现象还是普遍现象，这需要持续观察。”

张博士越说越兴奋，还想问商非凡一些问题。

商非凡打断他：“老伏现实身体的精神力数值有变化吗？”

张博士：“没有。伏先生的精神力数值不但没有良性变化，我们发现他每次从游戏中醒来，都会产生一定疲惫，这种疲惫达不到工作一天的程度，但跟做了很多梦以后的精神力疲劳类似。”

伏向军皱眉，插话：“这代表好还是坏？”

张博士清清嗓子：“不好也不坏。我说了，你每次摘下游戏头盔醒来就跟睡了一个多梦觉一样，你的身体和大脑依然能提供你在现实世界活动一天的能量。另外，你会产生肌肉僵硬，跟头盔的舒适度以及你的坐姿有很大关系。如果该游戏商能把头盔升级为可躺入式的游戏仓，并提供一定的肌肉按摩功能，你醒来后就不会产生肌肉僵硬感。”
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 36: Reactions of the Real-World Body (Part 1)

Fortunately, no one knew that he was the one who had created the Stink Fruit.

Even if A'Cheng harbored suspicions, he lacked any concrete proof.

Shang Feifan remained calm and composed, pretending to be just another innocent victim in all of this.

As for A'Dai, the little guy had looked at Old Shang simply because it felt Old Shang's luck was terribly awful.

Yet, considering they were currently safe and sound, didn't that mean his luck was actually quite good?

The logic was far too complex for A'Dai, who grew increasingly dazed the more he pondered it.

Building upon that legend, the surrounding beastmen began exchanging various strange tales and bizarre rumors they had heard throughout their lives.

Suddenly, Shang Feifan felt a vibration coming from his pocket. He pulled out the source of the commotion, revealing his lost-and-found Notebook System.

In the hands of non-players, this item appeared to be nothing more than an ordinary leather notebook—a fairly common design, at that.

Shang Feifan had even noticed that both the caravan leader and his deputy carried a similar notebook and pen in their pockets. The deputy used his to keep inventory logs every morning and evening, while the young caravan leader used his to jot down various anecdotes and travel notes.

[UPDATE NOTICE! Attention all players: To provide a better gaming experience, the game will undergo a server-wide maintenance and system update starting at 1:00 AM on October 20th, XX Year (Real-World Time). Note: Players in different time zones will display different offline maintenance times; please refer to the personal time received by your individual system. The update is expected to take six hours, concluding at 6:00 AM. Please keep track of the time and prepare to log off to prevent the loss of equipment and items. Players currently out in the wilderness must find a safe location to log off to ensure their bodies remain unharmed.]

Shang Feifan raised an eyebrow. He was genuinely curious to know what would happen to him if he refused to log off at the time dictated by the Notebook System.

However... when the designated log-off time arrived, Shang Feifan chose to log off anyway.

Risks were divided into necessary ones and unnecessary ones; right now, taking a risk was entirely unnecessary.

Removing his VR helmet, he saw that Fu Xiangjun had already woken up ahead of him.

Shang Feifan couldn't help but complain to Fu Xiangjun about his ordeal.

How could he have known that "injuring the enemy by a thousand at the cost of eighteen hundred to oneself" would manifest in such a absurd manner?

Besides, according to the old beastman, the Stink Fruit attracting the Servant of the God of Fear was only a *possibility*.

Who could have predicted that in his case, the probability would spike straight to a hundred percent?!

Fu Xiangjun burst into hearty laughter upon hearing the story.

After getting his fill of laughing at his boss's miserable luck, Fu Xiangjun asked, "Could it have something to do with that glass orb you bought?"

"Perhaps." Shang Feifan rubbed his right eye. Thinking about that object's innate attraction toward darkness, his urge to complain evaporated into sheer helplessness. With so many debuffs stacked on him, it was no wonder a random chance turned into a guaranteed trigger.

Fu Xiangjun even mocked him, teasing that he hadn't even seen Shang Feifan naked in the game yet, only for his boss to be seen stark naked by someone else first.

Shang Feifan walked over, slapped his palm straight onto Fu Xiangjun's face, and gritted his teeth. "That guy was just trying to generate clout! When I stepped out of the solitary cell in the dungeon, I was already wearing bandit clothes. He didn't see a damn thing!"

Fu Xiangjun showed zero restraint and continued to roar with laughter.

As per his routine, Shang Feifan checked the monitoring equipment's telemetry data first.

Suddenly, the network communication chime rang out.

Shang Feifan pressed the answer button.

From the other end came the voice of Dr. Zhang from the research institute: "We've discovered a minor anomaly. Or perhaps 'anomaly' isn't the right word—the change was extremely minute, to the point that it was only after several consecutive days of observation that we noticed a slow, upward trend."

Shang Feifan asked, "What kind of change?"

Fu Xiangjun looked over with concern as well.

Dr. Zhang explained, "I've transmitted the data to your terminal. By analyzing your brainwave activity and changes in blood oxygen levels, we discovered that your Mental Power is slowly increasing. Using 'Mental Power' is a bit game-centric, but to be specific: if you look at the transferase clusters at your brain's nerve endings, there exists a microtubule network resembling a quantum structure. All human brain activity originates from these vast arrays of microtubules moving first, establishing a state, and releasing brain signals once a clear command is formed.

Doesn't that sound remarkably like a naturally formed quantum computer? In reality, the human brain is a super-quantum computer—a biological quantum computer—far more advanced and intricate than any artificial creation.

Yet, our current development and application of this super biological quantum computer stands at less than eight percent..."

Shang Feifan listened patiently to Dr. Zhang's lecture. Whenever the doctor got onto the topic of his field of expertise, he would talk endlessly.

After a lengthy explanation, Dr. Zhang assumed the listener understood and finally returned to the main topic: "It is through this series of signal variations that we comprehensively simulated a Mental Power value corresponding to the one mentioned in the game system. Then, we discovered that this Mental Power value has transformed into a steadily rising curve, indicating that your real-world Mental Power is incrementally increasing—assuming our data recording and analysis are correct."

Shang Feifan understood. Dr. Zhang was cross-referencing his in-game personal data with real-world metrics.

To better monitor his own physical condition, Shang Feifan naturally had no reason to hide his status. He directly transcribed the personal data displayed by his neural-link system, typed it into the computer, and sent it over to Dr. Zhang.

After reviewing the file on his end, Dr. Zhang's voice grew noticeably excited: "The data trends match perfectly! This proves our analytical direction isn't wrong."

"Dr. Zhang!" A female voice came from the background, offering a quiet reminder.

Dr. Zhang cleared his throat. "Ah, right. That's not the main point. The main point is... you realize that what we are monitoring isn't the data of your beastman body in the game, but your real-world physical body, right?"

Shang Feifan maintained his patience. "Yes."

Dr. Zhang's voice grew even more ecstatic: "The shift in Mental Power we detected is occurring right inside your real-world body! Do you grasp what this implies? Human mental energy is constantly fluctuating, generating an irregular band of energy waves. But the Mental Power growth curve we calculated based on microtubule signal movement shows actual, sustained growth!

Think of it this way: an ordinary person requires 0.1 units of energy to initiate a thought process. However, the moment they cross the limit threshold of 1, they experience mental fatigue, prompting the cerebral cortex to send signals indicating it wants to stop working and rest.

In your case, your mental energy initiation threshold has dropped to an astonishing 0.01, while your upper limit threshold has broken past 3!

Do you realize what this signifies? It means that even in a state where a normal person would be near-unconscious, you can still effectively control your thoughts and even parts of your physical body! At the same time, you possess vastly more energy to process thoughts than others do. Where another person's brain would overload after a single day of high-intensity work, your brain can function for three straight days while maintaining pristine clarity!

What a monumental discovery! Who could have imagined a mere holographic game could exert such a profound physical impact on the human brain?

Of course, we cannot yet determine whether this influence is entirely benign, nor do we know if it's a unique phenomenon isolated to you or a universal effect. This requires long-term, continuous observation."

The more Dr. Zhang spoke, the more thrilled he became, clearly eager to barrage Shang Feifan with a battery of questions.

Shang Feifan cut him off cold: "Has Old Fu's real-world body shown any changes in his Mental Power metrics?"

Dr. Zhang paused. "No. Mr. Fu's Mental Power metrics haven't shown any positive growth. On the contrary, we've noticed that every time he wakes up from the game, he suffers a certain degree of fatigue. It's not severe enough to equal a full day's manual labor, but it closely mirrors the mental exhaustion one feels after experiencing a night filled with restless dreams."

Fu Xiangjun frowned and cut in, "Does that mean it's good or bad?"

Dr. Zhang cleared his throat. "Neither good nor bad. As I said, every time you remove the game helmet and wake up, it's virtually identical to waking up from a dream-filled sleep. Your body and brain still supply more than enough energy for your daily activities in the real world. As for the muscle stiffness you experience, that has more to do with the helmet's comfort level and your sitting posture. If the game developer could upgrade the helmet to a full-immersion gaming pod equipped with built-in muscle massage features, you wouldn't feel any stiffness upon waking."

chunks.chapterTitle: 第36章 现实身体的反应 (Part 2)
chunks.chineseText:
张博士说着又把话题扯远，一副想要给游戏商做指点，好让对方快点搞出游戏仓的架势。

那道女性声音再次提醒张博士，大概是他的助手。

张博士又把话题拉回来：“说到你们的肌肉变化，其实也有一定区别。伏先生的就是普通人在躺椅上睡了一觉，还做了很多梦以后，起来时的身体状态。对伏先生目前还说不上太大危害，只要能注意每天醒来都进行热身活动，以及玩游戏时调整自己的坐姿和睡姿，让自己的身体肌肉可以更为放松……”

“张博士，重点！”商非凡声音清冷。

张博士干咳：“但你就没有这样的调整必要。明明你的坐姿和伏先生差不多，按理你的肌肉疲劳程度也应该跟他数据类似，但是我们发现……你的大脑一直在输送某种微电信号，不断刺激你的肌肉，甚至是骨骼筋膜等。这个还需要我们进一步分析，也需要更加精密的仪器。仪器我们会想法让人送过去……”

“张博士！”

这次是几个人同时喊出。

张博士无奈：“好了好了，我知道你们嫌弃我废话多。但是我不说清楚，你们又会不断问我为什么。外行就是难侍候。”

商非凡和伏向军：“……”看在对方是专门研究人体奥秘学的大佬还对他们有帮助的份上，忍了。

张博士：“总之商先生目前的身体变化暂时可以定为良性。就好像这个全息游戏的游戏系统在你们两人身上产生了不同反应，也许该游戏的开发商就想搞出一个能让人们利用睡眠时间，还能健身健脑的游戏，只不过他们应该也还在摸索中，所以才会出现相同的游戏系统和游戏头盔，却对你们产生不同影响的结果。

当然，想要知道你们为何会出现如此不同的影响结果，最好还是能让我们详细检测你们的游戏头盔。因为是对你们的现实身体产生物理影响，所以头盔的可能性最高。也许你们俩的游戏头盔的材质，或者是里面内置的一些功能有所不同。”

伏向军看向商非凡。

商非凡拥有两个游戏系统的事只有他们两个人知道。

伏向军是商非凡的死忠，只要商非凡不开口，谁也别想从他口中知道这个秘密。

商非凡思考片刻，对张博士说：“如果要详细检测我们的游戏头盔，恐怕得麻烦您和您的团队过来一趟。你们那边能找到理由过来吗？我们俩现在还不方便回国。”

张博士没有立刻回答，对面响起低语声，似乎张博士在询问他助理某些事情。

过了一会儿，出现了一个新的成年男性声音：“您好，商先生。我们会以研究学习的名义跟这边的大学协商，最短一周、最长两周，等我们通知。”

“好，我知道了，辛苦。”商非凡没有听出这个人的声音是谁，他也没问。

就像对方只会叫他商先生一样。

等那边挂上通讯，伏向军才跟商非凡说：“那边换负责人了？”

商非凡不在意地道：“有成果，自然就开始重视。”

伏向军一边活动身体一边说：“希望不是来抢功的讨厌家伙。”

“应该不会。如果真是那种烦人鬼，就让他摔断腿。”商非凡随口说。

伏向军吐气：“我不想再换一重身份，我还挺喜欢这个农场。”

商非凡推开大门：“你以为他们知道我们在哪儿？”

伏向军一愣：“他们不知道……等等，他们以为？”

伏向军反应过来：“他们具体要到哪个大学？”

商非凡微微一笑：“到时候我们提前带上游戏头盔，到隔壁洲转转，DZ大学的运动医疗学科很有名，我在那所大学所在的城市有一套房子，当时我让他们送仪器就是送到那里，之后又通过别人转送了几次，才送到这里。研究所那边分析出来的最后IP地址应该也是那边。听说那城市周边的肯恩农场培育出了一种专长肌肉的牛，我正好想去看看，如果口感好的话，看看能不能引进几只。”

伏向军对他老大竖起大拇指，要论狡猾还是得看他老大。人家是狡兔三窟，他十三窟都不止，还疑似巢穴搞了一个又一个。

不过也正是他老大的这份谨慎和对同行包括同仁的高度警惕，才能让他们安然无恙到现在。

这人始终给自己和自家兄弟留着至少一条的退路。
chunks.englishText:
As Dr. Zhang spoke, he digressed once again, sounding as if he intended to lecture the game developers directly so they would hurry up and manufacture gaming pods.

The female voice chimed in once more to remind Dr. Zhang, likely acting as his assistant.

Dr. Zhang reined the topic back in. "Speaking of your muscle variations, there is indeed a distinct difference between you two. Mr. Fu's condition is equivalent to an ordinary person who took a nap on a recliner and had a flurry of dreams before waking up. At present, it poses no significant harm to Mr. Fu, provided he takes care to perform warm-up exercises every time he wakes up and adjusts his sitting or sleeping posture while playing to keep his muscles as relaxed as possible..."

"Dr. Zhang, get to the point!" Shang Feifan's voice turned cool and sharp.

Dr. Zhang coughed dryly. "Right, right. But in your case, Mr. Shang, such adjustments aren't even necessary. Even though your sitting posture is nearly identical to Mr. Fu's, and logic dictates your muscle fatigue metrics should mirror his, our readings show that... your brain has been continuously emitting a specific micro-electric signal. This signal is constantly stimulating your muscles, fascia, and even your skeletal structure. This phenomenon requires deeper analysis on our end, as well as far more precise instrumentation. We will find a way to have the necessary equipment delivered to you..."

"Dr. Zhang!"

This time, several voices called out his name simultaneously.

Dr. Zhang sighed helplessly. "Alright, alright! I get it, you think I ramble too much. But if I don't explain things clearly, you'll just keep asking me why. Laymen are truly difficult to serve."

Shang Feifan and Fu Xiangjun: "..." 

Considering the man was a top-tier expert in human physiological science who was actively assisting them, they decided to endure it.

Dr. Zhang continued, "In summary, Mr. Shang's current physical transformation can tentatively be classified as benign. It appears as though this holographic game's system produces differing reactions across different individuals. Perhaps the game's developer set out to create a system that allows people to exercise their bodies and minds during sleep, but because they are still in the experimental phase, the same game system and helmet yield entirely different outcomes on different subjects.

Of course, if we wish to pinpoint why such vastly different results occurred between the two of you, the best approach would be for us to conduct a thorough analysis of your gaming helmets. Since physical effects are being exerted onto your real-world bodies, the helmets are the most probable variable. Perhaps there are discrepancies in the materials used or the internal features built into your respective units."

Fu Xiangjun shot a glance at Shang Feifan.

The fact that Shang Feifan possessed two game systems was a secret known only to the two of them.

Fu Xiangjun was fiercely loyal to Shang Feifan; as long as Shang Feifan didn't give the word, no one would ever pry that secret out of his mouth.

Shang Feifan pondered for a moment before addressing Dr. Zhang. "If you need to thoroughly inspect our gaming helmets, I'm afraid we'll have to trouble you and your team to make a trip over here in person. Can your side arrange a valid pretext to travel abroad? It remains inconvenient for the two of us to return to the country right now."

Dr. Zhang didn't answer immediately. Muffled murmurs sounded from his end, suggesting he was consulting his assistant.

After a short pause, a new, mature male voice joined the line: "Hello, Mr. Shang. We will coordinate with the local university under the guise of an academic research exchange. It will take a week at the shortest, two weeks at the longest. Please await our notification."

"Understood. Thank you for your hard work." Shang Feifan didn't recognize the speaker's voice, nor did he bother to ask his identity.

Just as the other party refrained from addressing him as anything other than "Mr. Shang."

Once the communication ended, Fu Xiangjun turned to Shang Feifan. "Did they switch out the person in charge over there?"

Shang Feifan said indifferently, "Now that results are showing, people naturally start paying closer attention."

Fu Xiangjun stretched his limbs as he spoke. "I just hope they don't send over some annoying prick trying to steal credit."

"Unlikely. If it really is some insufferable pest, we'll just make sure he breaks a leg," Shang Feifan remarked casually.

Fu Xiangjun let out a breath. "I really don't want to change identities again. I've actually grown quite fond of this ranch."

Shang Feifan pushed open the front door. "Do you honestly think they know where we are?"

Fu Xiangjun froze. "They don't know... wait, they *think* they know?"

Realizing the play, Fu Xiangjun asked, "Which university are they planning to go to?"

Shang Feifan smiled faintly. "When the time comes, we'll pack up our gaming helmets in advance and head over to the neighboring state for a visit. DZ University's Sports Medicine department is quite famous. I happen to own a property in the city where that university is located. Back when I had them ship the equipment, that was the address I provided. It went through several secondary drop points before finally reaching us here. The final IP address their research team traced should point right to that city.

"I heard a farm near that city, the Kane Ranch, bred a special breed of cattle known for packing on dense muscle mass. I happen to want to check it out. If the beef tastes good, we can see about importing a few heads."

Fu Xiangjun flashed his boss a big thumb-up. When it came to cunning, no one could hold a candle to his boss. Where others had three burrows like a crafty rabbit, his boss had well over thirteen—and even went out of his way to set up fake nests one after another.

Yet, it was precisely his boss's extreme caution and relentless vigilance toward both enemies and associates alike that had allowed them to remain safe and sound to this day.

The man always kept at least one escape route open for himself and his brothers.

chunks.chineseText:
第37章 意外之喜

忙活了一天下来，游戏早已更新完毕。

伏向军因为和别人约好，早在更新刚结束的时候就已经戴上游戏头盔。

商非凡不紧不慢，算着那边早上起来的时间……他感觉游戏世界似乎有人在叫他。

这一定是错觉！

商非凡刚进入游戏，就听到阿呆在喊他。

“爸爸？爸爸！”

“醒了，我不是跟你说过我睡觉比较沉。”商非凡坐起身，揉揉小东西的脑袋。

这小家伙跟他东奔西跑了好些天，途中也少不了各种担惊受怕，但他们粮食充足，路上不愁食物，小家伙貌似被他养得脸上稍微有了一点肉。

阿城也在另一边坐了起来。

他们三人睡的是商非凡在玩家营地找玩家制作的普通帐篷。

等三人从帐篷里出来，外面已经有不少兽人在忙活。

有人在煮早饭，有人在收拾帐篷，有人在喂坐骑……

天边太阳露出大半张脸，朝霞鲜红。

“朝霞不出门，晚霞行千里。”商非凡低喃。

阿呆仰头看他，似乎在问他“爸爸你在说什么”。

商非凡：“我是说今天有可能会下雨，我们等会儿要在狰爷的背上支一个雨棚。”

支雨棚之前，他们三人得先弄早饭。

大家吃饭都是分开弄，除非给商队交钱。

商非凡从行李里找出他自己炼制的铁锅和铁勺，又从行李里假装掏出一袋面粉。

这面粉就是他在强盗库房里发现的灰色粉末。

他一开始不知道这是什么，加上有点腥味，就没动它。

碰到商队后，他以交换为名义，拿出灰色粉末，才知道这粉末竟然是虫粉。

别听虫粉这个名字很可怕，但在兽人世界，这竟然是比小麦面粉还要常见的主流粮食之一。

虫粉的原材料来自于各种可食用虫，经过晾晒、碾压成粉，再掺和一种植物果实粉末，就形成了营养成分不错、还量大便宜的虫粉。

甚至很多种族比较特殊的兽人可以不吃小麦面粉，虫粉却是必须吃的主食。

除了虫粉以外，还有一种骨粉，也是兽人常见粮食之一。

商非凡就用虫粉跟商队的人换了一些香料和佐料。

有了丰富的香料和做饭常用佐料，商非凡烙的虫粉饼特别受欢迎，吃起来口感不算特别细腻，里面还有颗粒感，但咸中带甜，带着一些鲜虾的鲜味，倒是比普通虫粉饼更有嚼头。

不但阿呆和阿城喜欢吃，商队里的人闻到香味也会拿着自己的食物过来跟老商交换。

阿城为了不让老商父子俩嫌弃自己白吃白喝，所有洗洗刷刷收拾整理打下手的活他都包了。他在强盗厨房待了有两年，这些简单活计做得又快又好。

商非凡在大家都在吃早饭的时候，光明正大地拿出皮质笔记本翻开。

这次更新内容还挺多，比如增加地图扫描功能，可以直接在地图上的一定范围内显示代表玩家的绿点和代表仇家的红点。

另外地图上还增加了草药、矿物、以及其他自然材料的搜索和辨识功能。

就是想要打开这个功能，玩家必须先激活相关职业技能。

除此之外，还增加了语言包，这次玩家们不用再辛苦学习当地兽人语言，而是只要达到十级就能购买语言包，一键学会听说读写当地通用语。

就是语言包的价格比较贵，高达五十银。不过想要买的玩家肯定还是会有很多，毕竟没有多少人有那耐心花时间花精力去学习一门外语，还是在现实世界用不上的游戏世界语言。

而这次的最大更新应该就是笔记本外形可以变形这点，因为大量玩家反应随身携带笔记本太不方便，强烈要求更换成腕表或其他方便的形式。

于是这次更新，笔记本就有了第二和第三形态。

第二形态就是玩家最想要的皮质手镯样式。

第三形态则是隐形模式。这个模式不免费，要交纳一百银才能开通。

不少玩家为此宁可花费一个宝贵的铜达铢也要在世界频道骂狗开发商赚黑心钱。

还有玩家在世界频道询问空间背包和游戏商城什么时候能上线。

游戏策划只表示他们开发组正在努力工作，将来会为游戏增添更多丰富内容，请玩家们耐心期待。

商非凡还查看了笔记本系统上自己的个人数据。

两个系统的个人数据已经有了明显差别。

商非凡还注意到，笔记本系统中竟然没有精神力值，只有精力值。也没有隐藏的幸运值。

而两个系统都没有游戏最常见的好感度值。

商非凡肯定是不会花一百银给笔记本系统购买隐形模式，他是在强盗营地搜刮到一些钱币，但也不多。那些强盗肯定有另外藏钱的地方，比如他们的老巢。

那就只有戴手腕上了。

叮咚。

【系统为你解忧。是否选择游戏系统融合？注：如果选择融合，笔记本系统会就此消失。】

商非凡：脑载系统兄你是越来越不掩饰你对笔记本系统的不待见了是吧。说是融合，其实就是吞噬吧？

“那边会察觉吗？”商非凡问得很含糊。

脑载系统保持了绝不回答玩家提问的高冷范。

商非凡推测脑载系统应该十分有信心，因为如果它吞噬笔记本系统的行为会让开发商那边察觉，它也不会提出这么一条建议。

再想到脑载系统必要时可以模拟笔记本系统，商非凡最终：“同意游戏系统融合。”

【感谢你的信任。游戏系统融合开始，融合过程中游戏商城和地图功能暂时无法使用，其他功能正常使用。】

商非凡的右眼视界中-出现了一个新的进度条，进度看起来比较缓慢。

商非凡隐藏了这个进度条，顺便打开寻宝罗盘看了看。

寻宝罗盘功能没有受到任何影响。

一个红色的箭头坚定地指向东北方向。

在强盗窝时，这个红色箭头还转来转去，像是在寻找，又像是受到了某种影响。

直到他们离开地缝范围，红色箭头才给出了明确的方向指示。

好在东北方向正好是他们要去的摩罗城方向。

如果寻宝罗盘指出的方向和他要去的地方不同，他也不打算更换目的地。

对他来说，寻找雕像缺失部位只是顺带，哪怕这是主线任务。

吃过早饭，商非凡就开始在狰爷背部搭建简单雨棚。

经验老到的商队也在忙着用雨布盖上不好被淋湿的货物。

其他不会看天气的兽人看到商队在忙活防雨，有那余力的也在货物和身上披上防雨的东西。

阿城把锅碗瓢盆洗刷收拾好，就过来帮忙。

他发现商非凡拿出的一些材料似乎不像是他们原本行李中就有的，比如几根长直棍。

但他什么都没说，就当什么都不知道。

阿城不比普通兽人，他从小在繁华富裕的摩罗城长大，自然知道这世上有一种神奇的储物工具，能以小小的身体装入很多很多物品。

不过空间储物工具非常昂贵，就连他身为炼药学徒的父亲也只能望之兴叹。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 37: An Unexpected Bonanza

After a busy day, the game had long since completed its update.

Because Fu Xiangjun had made plans with others, he had already put on his gaming helmet the moment the update ended.

Shang Feifan remained unhurried. Calculating the morning hour over there... he felt as though someone in the game world was calling him.

That had to be an illusion!

As soon as Shang Feifan entered the game, he heard Ah Dai shouting for him.

"Daddy? Daddy!"

"I'm awake. Didn't I tell you I sleep heavily?" Shang Feifan sat up and ruffled the little thing's head.

The little fellow had been running around with him through thick and thin for days. Along the way, there had been no shortage of scares and frights, but their provisions were plentiful, and they lacked nothing to eat. Under his care, the little fellow seemed to have grown slightly fleshier on his face.

Ah Cheng also sat up on the other side.

The three of them slept in an ordinary tent that Shang Feifan had paid a player to make at the player camp.

By the time the three emerged from the tent, quite a few Orcs were already bustling about outside.

Some were cooking breakfast, some were packing up tents, and others were feeding their mounts...

More than half of the sun's face peeked over the horizon, casting a brilliant red glow of morning clouds.

"Morning clouds portend rain; evening clouds portend a thousand-mile journey," Shang Feifan murmured.

Ah Dai looked up at him, seemingly asking, "Daddy, what are you talking about?"

Shang Feifan replied, "I'm saying it might rain today. Later, we need to rig a rain canopy on Master Zheng's back."

Before putting up the canopy, the three of them had to make breakfast.

Everyone prepared their meals separately unless they were paying a fee to a caravan.

Shang Feifan retrieved an iron pot and spoon he had forged himself from his luggage, then feigned pulling a bag of flour from his pack.

This flour was actually the gray powder he had discovered in the bandits' storeroom.

At first, he hadn't known what it was, and coupled with a slight fishy odor, he had left it untouched.

After encountering the caravan, he took out the gray powder under the guise of trading, only to discover that it was actually insect powder.

Don't let the name "insect powder" sound terrifying; in the Orc world, it was actually one of the most common and mainstream staple foods, far more prevalent than wheat flour.

The raw material for insect powder came from various edible insects, which were dried, ground into powder, and then mixed with a certain plant fruit powder. This created an insect powder that was rich in nutrients, bulky, and cheap.

In fact, Orcs of many special races could go without wheat flour, but insect powder was an absolute dietary staple.

Aside from insect powder, there was also bone powder, which was another common foodstuff among the Orcs.

Shang Feifan used the insect powder to trade with members of the caravan for some spices and seasonings.

With an abundance of spices and cooking seasonings, Shang Feifan's pan-fried insect powder cakes were exceptionally popular. While the texture wasn't particularly refined and still had a grainy feel, they were salty yet sweet, carrying a savory shrimp-like umami that made them much more chewable than ordinary insect powder cakes.

Not only did Ah Dai and Ah Cheng love eating them, but people from the caravan who smelled the aroma would also bring their own food to trade with Old Shang.

To avoid being resented by Shang Feifan and his son as a freeloaders, Ah Cheng took charge of all the washing, scrubbing, tidying, and menial chores. Having spent nearly two years in the bandits' kitchen, he performed these simple tasks quickly and efficiently.

While everyone else was eating breakfast, Shang Feifan openly pulled out his leather-bound notebook and flipped it open.

This update contained quite a lot of content, such as the addition of a map-scanning function, which could directly display green dots representing players and red dots representing enemies within a certain range on the map.

Additionally, the map now included search and identification functions for herbs, minerals, and other natural materials.

However, to unlock this feature, players first had to activate the relevant professional skills.

On top of that, a language pack had been added. This time, players no longer needed to painstakingly study the local Orc language; as long as they reached level ten, they could purchase the language pack and instantly master listening, speaking, reading, and writing in the local common tongue.

The only catch was that the language pack was quite expensive, costing a hefty fifty silver coins. Even so, many players would undoubtedly still buy it, seeing as few people had the patience and stamina to spend time and energy learning a foreign language—especially a game world language useless in the real world.

As for the biggest update this time, it was probably the fact that the notebook's appearance could now be transformed. Because a massive number of players had complained that carrying a notebook around was inconvenient, strongly demanding it be changed to a wristwatch or another convenient form.

Consequently, with this update, the notebook gained a second and third form.

The second form was the leather bracelet style most desired by players.

The third form was an invisibility mode. This mode wasn't free; it required paying one hundred silver coins to activate.

For this reason, quite a few players preferred to waste a precious copper Dhu coin just to curse the damn developers in the world channel for making a killing off heartless money.

Other players were asking in the world channel when the spatial backpack and game store would go online.

The game planners only stated that their development team was working hard and would add more rich content to the game in the future, asking players to wait patiently.

Shang Feifan also checked his personal data on the notebook system.

There was already a clear distinction between the personal data of the two systems.

Shang Feifan also noticed that the notebook system surprisingly lacked a mental strength value, having only a stamina value. Nor was there any hidden luck value.

Furthermore, neither system had the game's most common favorability value.

Shang Feifan certainly wasn't going to spend one hundred silver coins to purchase the invisibility mode for the notebook system. He had looted some coins from the bandit camp, but not that much. Those bandits surely had other hidden stashes of money, such as their lair.

In that case, wearing it on his wrist was the only option.

Ding-dong.

[The system solves your worries. Do you choose to fuse the game systems? Note: If fusion is selected, the notebook system will cease to exist.]

Shang Feifan: Brain-borne system brother, you're becoming less and less covert about your disdain for the notebook system, aren't you? You call it a fusion, but it's actually devouring, right?

"Will they notice over there?" Shang Feifan asked rather vaguely.

The brain-borne system maintained its aloof attitude of never answering player inquiries.

Shang Feifan deduced that the brain-borne system must be extremely confident; otherwise, if its act of devouring the notebook system would alert the developers, it wouldn't have proposed such a suggestion.

Thinking further that the brain-borne system could simulate the notebook system when necessary, Shang Feifan ultimately decided: "I agree to the game system fusion."

[Thank you for your trust. Game system fusion initiated. During the fusion process, the game store and map functions will be temporarily unavailable; other functions will operate normally.]

A new progress bar appeared in Shang Feifan's right eye's field of vision, its progress looking rather sluggish.

Shang Feifan hid this progress bar and incidentally opened the treasure-hunting compass to take a look.

The treasure-hunting compass function remained completely unaffected.

A red arrow pointed steadfastly toward the northeast.

Back at the bandit lair, this red arrow had spun around in circles as if searching or being subjected to some kind of interference.

It wasn't until they left the range of the abyss fissure that the red arrow gave a clear directional indication.

Fortunately, the northeast happened to be the direction of Molo City, where they were headed.

Even if the treasure-hunting compass had pointed in a different direction from where he wanted to go, he had no intention of changing his destination.

To him, finding the missing parts of the statue was merely secondary, even if it was the main quest.

After finishing breakfast, Shang Feifan began constructing a simple rain canopy on Master Zheng's back.

The experienced caravan was also busy using tarpaulins to cover goods that were susceptible to water damage.

Other Orcs who didn't know how to read the weather saw the caravan bustling with rain-prevention measures and, having some spare capacity, threw waterproof coverings over their goods and themselves.

After washing and packing away the pots and pans, Ah Cheng came over to help.

He noticed that some of the materials Shang Feifan took out didn't seem to be things originally in their luggage, such as a few long, straight sticks.

Yet he said nothing, acting as though he knew nothing.

Ah Cheng was different from ordinary Orcs; having grown up in the prosperous and affluent Molo City since childhood, he naturally knew that there existed miraculous storage tools in this world capable of holding massive amounts of items within a tiny frame.

However, spatial storage tools were exorbitantly expensive, to the extent that even his father, an alchemy apprentice, could only sigh in despair.

chunks.chineseText:
这让阿城对商非凡的身份有诸多猜测，也让他对商非凡更加敬畏。

老商手脚麻利，不到半小时就在狰爷背上搭建出一个燕子型的小雨棚。

这个雨棚不算重，对狰爷算不上负担，就是固定时有一点麻烦。狰爷不喜欢固定物出现在自己的肢体上，商非凡就一边询问它的意见，一边找对狰爷没有影响又比较坚硬的部位，拴上固定用的绳索。

阿呆很喜欢这个雨棚，这让他待在狰爷背脊上时也能充满安全感。如果粑粑肯抱着他，而不是把他塞在网兜床里就更好啦。

商队的护卫头领发出一声嘹亮的哨声，商队再次出发。

果然，太阳出来没多久就被云层掩盖。临近中午的时候，天空就出现比较厚的灰色云层。

中午没有人停下做饭，只是简单休息了下腿脚，吃了一些干粮。

下午雨水落下。

除了天气不太美好，一路算得上平安无事，接近傍晚的时候，商队来到一座小村庄，晚上大家将在这里休息一晚。

这也是他们赶路至今歇脚的第一个村落。

商非凡跟商队副首领的老兽人关系比较好，从他口中得知，之前的路途附近不是没有兽人聚集地，但他们曾经吃过一些亏，对那些村落的兽人感观很差，就绕开了那些村落。

商非凡把这些信息全部记下。

当晚，商非凡下线前。

【系统融合完成。今后笔记本系统更新，本系统也会进行同步更新和融合，你不会错失任何一个新增功能。】

商非凡莞尔。他怎么有种脑载系统在薅笔记本系统羊毛的感觉？

两个系统融合，看起来没有什么特别变化。

只他的右眼视界和地图功能结合，竟然能打开矿物搜索功能。

而能打开矿物搜索功能，则和他之前开启的铁匠职业有关。

这个功能显然非常实用，如果能找到一个无主矿藏，他占领下来就能当一个家中有矿的矿场主。

但……商队老兽人告诉他，这些土地都是有主的。

第一个主人就是虎国的国王。

理论上，只要是虎国国境范围内的土地和土地上下所有矿藏资源等，全都属于虎国国王。

第二个主人则是土地的实际拥有者。

虎王是名义上的国王没错，但虎国实行的是分封制，也就是说虎国境内有很多领主，这些领主对自己的领地具有实际拥有权，他们只要交税给国王。

还有第三主人。

领主也有强弱之分，有些领主比较弱，就会出现领地被非领主人士占领的事。

这些实际占有者虽然没有正当的名义，但想要从他们口中夺食，跟和拥有正当名义的领主开战没有任何区别。

像是深渊地缝到天残谷那一带，那么大一片土地怎么可能没有领主？

但因为那带诡异传说太多，当地领主不肯住到那里，就变成了领主遥领这片土地，只在固定时间派军队和税务官过来收税，导致这片土地上的兽人们大多自由野蛮生长，占下一片地就敢说自己是主人。

但那是被占土地没有发现高价值物品的前提情况下。

如果发现矿藏，就算那片土地再诡异再危险，真正的领主也会派兵过来捞一票，顺便把占领矿藏的小偷干掉。

还是有很大便宜可占的。商非凡心想。这大概也是玩家大本营建在那一片的重要原因。

一日复一日，旅途危险但也无聊，疲累是主流。

就算是风景党，在没有网络和其他事件刺激下，就这么走啊走，也得走崩溃。

商非凡好几次询问系统有没有挂机功能，他真的不想这么一天天走下去。

无聊的商非凡干脆在狰爷背部立了一面旗子，打出了修理商的广告。

没想到商队里真有人来找他修理物品。

经过的村镇也让他做成了不少笔生意。

更让他意想不到也哭笑不得的是，他遇到了一个专门种植草药的村落，这个村落里的兽人对种植和炮炙药草非常有一手，但他们不善于任何机械方面的活计。

因为距离大城镇比较遥远，他们用坏的东西堆了不少，就等着遇到商队可以重新购买，或找商队里的修理工帮忙修理。

这次遇到挂着修理商旗帜的商非凡，该村落的兽人一窝蜂地过来询问。

当他们得知这个修理商不仅可以修理机械类物品，甚至能帮他们重新打制铁制品，该村的兽人们都高兴坏了。

因为要修理的东西太多，该村兽人又太热情，商非凡不得不和商队分开，在这个村落里多待了一段时间。

好吧，他其实是看中了另一个隐藏好处。

因为他几次不收钱，免费给一些孤寡老弱兽人修理工具，这些兽人心里感激他，也不想欠他人情，就一个劲送他草药，还跟他介绍这些药草的用途。

就在一个老妇人跟他絮絮叨叨介绍家里的药草园，还有她正在晾晒的草药时，系统突然通知他，他达成了开启草药师职业的基本条件。

于是，当他离开那个村子时，他头上就多了一个草药师学徒的头衔。同时他的地图功能也多了一个草药搜索功能。

这完完全全就是一个意外之喜。

商非凡可从来没想过自己会在草药学、医师、治疗方面有所发展。

但能多一个技能，显然也不是什么坏事。

就这么一路走走停停，将近两个月后，商非凡一行三人终于看到了摩罗城的身影。
chunks.englishText:
This led Ah Cheng to harbor numerous speculations regarding Shang Feifan's identity, filling him with even greater awe and reverence toward Shang Feifan.

Old Shang was quick-handed and nimble; in less than half an hour, he had built a swallow-shaped small rain canopy on Lord Zheng's back.

This rain canopy wasn't heavy and didn't count as a burden for Lord Zheng, though securing it was slightly troublesome. Lord Zheng disliked fixed objects appearing on its limbs, so Shang Feifan asked for its opinion while searching for parts of its body that wouldn't be affected yet were sturdy enough, tying down the ropes used for securing it.

Ah Dai loved this rain canopy very much, as it gave him a full sense of security while staying on Lord Zheng's spine. It would have been even better if Papa had been willing to hold him instead of stuffing him into the mesh net bed.

The caravan's guard leader let out a shrill whistle, and the caravan set off once more.

Sure enough, not long after the sun came out, it was masked by a layer of clouds. As noon approached, thick gray clouds appeared in the sky.

No one stopped to cook at noon; they merely rested their legs briefly and ate some dry rations.

Rain fell in the afternoon.

Aside from the rather unpleasant weather, the journey could be described as safe and sound. As evening approached, the caravan arrived at a small village where everyone would rest for the night.

This was also the very first settlement they had stopped at since the journey began.

Shang Feifan had a fairly good relationship with the old Orc who served as the caravan's deputy leader. From him, he learned that it wasn't as if there weren't Orc settlements near their previous route, but the caravan had suffered losses there before, leaving them with a very poor impression of the Orcs in those villages, so they had deliberately bypassed them.

Shang Feifan noted down all of this information.

That night, before Shang Feifan went offline:

[System merge complete. From now on, whenever the notebook system updates, this system will also undergo simultaneous updates and integration, ensuring you never miss a single newly added feature.]

Shang Feifan chuckled softly. Why did he have this strange feeling that the brain-loaded system was shearing wool off the notebook system?

The merger of the two systems didn't seem to bring any particular changes.

Except that his right-eye field of view was now combined with the map function, unexpectedly unlocking the mineral search function.

And the ability to unlock the mineral search function was tied to the blacksmith profession he had previously unlocked.

This function was clearly extremely practical. If he could find an unclaimed mineral deposit, occupying it would allow him to become a mine owner sitting on top of wealth.

But... the old Orc from the caravan told him that these lands all had owners.

The first owner was the King of the Tiger Kingdom.

Theoretically, any land within the borders of the Tiger Kingdom and all mineral resources above and below that land belonged entirely to the Tiger King.

The second owner was the actual holder of the land.

The Tiger King was indeed the nominal monarch, but the Tiger Kingdom practiced a feudal system. This meant there were numerous lords within the Tiger Kingdom who held actual ownership over their respective territories, only needing to pay taxes to the king.

Then there was a third owner.

Lords also varied in strength; some weaker lords might find their territories occupied by non-lord individuals.

Although these actual occupiers lacked legitimate standing, trying to seize food from their mouths was no different from waging war against the lord who held legitimate rights.

Take the stretch from the Abyss Fissure to the Valley of the Sky-Shattered, for instance. How could a piece of land that vast possibly have no lord?

However, because there were far too many bizarre legends surrounding that region, the local lords refused to live there, turning the area into land ruled from afar by absentee lords who only sent troops and tax collectors at fixed times to collect taxes. As a result, the Orcs on this land mostly grew wild and unconstrained, daring to claim they were the masters the moment they seized a patch of ground.

That was only under the premise that the occupied land hadn't yielded any high-value items, though.

If mineral deposits were discovered, no matter how bizarre or dangerous the land might be, the true lord would dispatch troops to make a killing, conveniently wiping out the thieves who had occupied the deposit.

Still, there were plenty of easy bargains to be picked up, Shang Feifan thought to himself. This was likely a major reason why the player base camp was built in that very area.

Day after day, the journey was as perilous as it was monotonous, with fatigue being the prevailing theme.

Even scenery enthusiasts, without the stimulation of the internet and other events, would simply walk like this until they felt like breaking down.

Shang Feifan asked the system several times if there was an idle-play function; he really didn't want to keep walking day after day like this.

Out of sheer boredom, Shang Feifan simply erected a banner on Lord Zheng's back, advertising himself as a repairman.

To his surprise, someone in the caravan actually came to him to have items repaired.

The villages and towns they passed through also netted him quite a few business transactions.

What was even more unexpected—and left him unsure whether to laugh or cry—was that he encountered a village specializing in growing medicinal herbs. The Orcs in this village were exceptionally skilled at planting and processing herbs, but they were completely inept at any mechanical work.

Because they were far away from major towns, they had piled up quite a number of broken items, just waiting to encounter a caravan to make new purchases or ask a caravan repairman to help fix them.

Upon meeting Shang Feifan, who was flying a repairman's banner, the Orcs of this village swarmed over to make inquiries.

When they learned that this repairman could not only fix mechanical goods but could even help them re-forge iron products, the village's Orcs were overjoyed.

Since there were too many things to repair, and the village's Orcs were too enthusiastic, Shang Feifan had no choice but to part ways with the caravan and stay in the village for a while longer.

Well, truth be told, he had actually set his sights on another hidden benefit.

Because he repeatedly refused payment, fixing tools for free for some lonely, elderly, and frail Orcs, these locals felt deeply grateful to him and didn't want to owe him favors. They kept sending him herbs and explaining the uses of these various plants.

Just as an old woman was chattering away, introducing the herb garden at her home and the herbs she was currently drying, the system suddenly notified him that he had met the basic conditions to unlock the herbalist profession.

Thus, when he left that village, he had gained the title of Herbalist Apprentice above his head. At the same time, his map function gained an additional herb-searching feature.

This was an absolute, unexpected windfall.

Shang Feifan had never imagined he would develop along the lines of herbalism, medicine, or healing.

Yet, gaining an extra skill was clearly not a bad thing.

Stopping and going all the way, nearly two months later, Shang Feifan and his group of three finally caught sight of Moluo City.
"""

chunks.chineseText:
第38章 摩罗城偶遇

阿城激动起来，一会儿坐一会儿站，总想找点事做。从两天前开始他就是这个样子。

商非凡正在查看游戏商城。这两个月他零零碎碎接了不少小任务，从任务二十四做到了任务五十。

他能感觉到脑载系统的努力，为了让他的旅途不那么无聊，为了不让他弃游，兢兢业业地给他发任务。

他也得承认，就是有这些小任务和贡献点奖励勾着他，才能让他日日不落地进入游戏。

当然，游戏本身给他带来的好处也不小，而且日渐明显。这才是真正让他愿意跟打卡上班一样上游戏的最重要原因。

现在负责研究和分析他身体数据的研究员还是那位张博士，但项目组又多了几位大拿。

国家层面已经越来越重视这个游戏，除了他以外，上面又找到几个愿意参与研究的国内玩家，也在争取拿到第五批玩家的申请名额。

这两个月，玩家在游戏中的发展也有了长足进步，玩家营地已经从一号建到了五号。

第一批玩家等级已经普遍达到十级。

激活神血天赋和开启职业技能的玩家越来越多。

购买语言包的玩家……虽然昂贵，但几乎每一个玩家只要手头有五十银就都购买了语言包，因为他们与当地兽人的接触也越来越多。

天残谷附近一带已经有了天残军的传言。

这个传言还没有传到那位真正的领主耳朵中，但想必这个时间也不会太久。

商非凡虽然没有和玩家们怎么实际接触，但他有伏向军随时跟他交流消息，玩家那边发生了什么大小事，他基本都清楚。

游戏商在上个月开通了第四次游戏账号申请，那批放出的游戏账号也比较多，有足足三千个。

据说这个月月底将要放出第五次游戏账号申请，而且放出的游戏账号多达八千个。

这个游戏世界要热闹起来了。商非凡心想。

玩家营地那边的发展暂时还影响不到他，商非凡就跟个风景党一样，两个月独行千里路。

笔记本系统似乎没有察觉有这么一个单独玩家已经远离玩家营地这么远，也许是脑载系统的掩护？

话说回头，脑载系统发布的这些小任务的奖励都不多，但这段时间他没有要特别购买的东西，就把贡献点给积累下来了。

加上拓展地图赚到的贡献点，如今他已经有了足足53个贡献点盈余。

原先商非凡想要攒贡献点买个空间储物工具，但现在他有了雕像广场，就改换了目标。他想开启炼金职业，初级炼金师只要一百点。

当然，如果能碰到一位炼金大师愿意收他为学徒，那最好。这笔贡献点就可以省下来。

可他也得做好两手准备，如果他一直碰不到愿意收他为徒的炼金师怎么办？

实际上，他到现在都没有遇到一位真正的炼金师。

而现在他已经品尝到开启职业技能的好处，如果他已经拥有一百贡献点，他绝对会毫不犹豫地就去开启炼金师职业。

“霍希尔先生，我们今天、今天就进城吗？要不要先在附近村落休息一天？”阿城期期艾艾地说。

商非凡看向他，摇摇头：“都已经到门口了，自然是进城找地方休息，而且你不想早点回家？”

他可是很想把这个包袱赶紧交接出去，然后拿到奖励。

阿城尴尬地笑。

商非凡懂，这就是近乡情怯，尤其还不是衣锦还乡。

如果阿城这时对他说“不要进入摩罗城，我们去其他地方”这种话，他都不会觉得奇怪。

但在强盗窝近两年的奴隶生涯让阿城变得胆小许多，他已经没有了当初离开家乡时的勇气和对摩罗城以外世界的无限向往。

他既感到就这么回家很丢脸，又为马上就能迎来真正平静安全且富足的生活而感到安心。

在阿城第N次偷看他时，商非凡开口：“跟你家人可以说实话，但对外人就没必要。就说你这两年在外面游学，在各个商队流浪打工，期间得到一位商队厨师的青睐，跟着学了一点手艺。现在想家了，更想念自己的家人，想要回来照顾父母，就决定回来开一家小餐馆平稳度日。”

阿城感动得眼睛都红了，他在强盗窝的厨房里虽然学会了打杂，但真正的厨艺并没有偷学到多少。反倒是跟着商非凡这两个月，学到不少美味食物的做法。

他是偷偷打算回家后想办法开一家小餐馆，他不想回来继续啃父母，可他本人对炼药学也确实七窍只通了六窍。

但偷学总是不好，何况商非凡还是他的救命恩人。没想到这位救命恩人竟然主动建议他开餐馆，还给他失踪两年找好了理由。

商非凡看到阿城哆嗦着嘴唇，一副要扑上来抱住他大哭的模样，立刻抬手指向摩罗城：“我们马上就要进城，你把之前买的衣服和装备换上。”

人靠衣装马靠鞍。两年没回来，回来像个乞丐，流言蜚语就能冲垮这个年轻人。

商非凡经验足，早早准备好三套行头，就连狰爷身上都打扮一新。

精心梳洗打扮后变得光鲜亮丽的阿城看起来果然比刚才要镇定不少。他也不再在口头上对商非凡道谢，而是打算回家后让父母好好报答这位连他的面子都愿意挽救的救命恩人，另外……

阿城按了按自己的肚子，决定忠于自己的心意。

阿呆也换上了新行头。阿呆不能变身成人形，兽人们也不习惯在兽形体上穿衣服，但可以增加一些防护和攻击装备。

商非凡在草药村时请村里皮匠帮忙给三人制作了三套防身皮甲，之后他又给自己和阿呆的皮甲上增加了一些小零件。

阿呆对这套小号皮甲喜欢极了，穿上后就觉得自己威风至极，站在包裹的最顶端，昂头挺胸地傲视周围。

途中一些兽人看到这个方头方脑的小家伙，都对他报以微笑，这孩子丑萌丑萌的，一脸呆样，却被家人打扮得很精神，还长得圆滚滚毛茸茸，一看就很受家人疼爱。

对，阿呆胖了一大圈，小肚子都鼓出来了，毛发也长好了，现在真正有了小幼崽的奶胖和毛绒感。

到了摩罗城附近，来来往往的行人和车辆如湍流的河水。

摩罗城城门大开，虽有守卫，却没有设置障碍，任由行人和商队进出。

商非凡看到这一点，顿觉这座城的城主很聪明。

城门税那点收入，哪能比得上如此多的客流量带来的连带效应？

当然，人多也会给安保带来极大压力。

收城门税除了给城主增收，另一个重要功能就是让城卫观察和找出不太-安定的份子，要么不让其进城，要么就标注为重点注意对象。

那么这座城的城主要怎么解决城内安全问题？

坐在狰爷背上，就这么进入城门的商非凡很快就发现了答案。

首先，那些在城门边身姿挺拔的城卫们并不是样子货，他们的眼神十分锐利，嗅觉恐怕也十分敏锐，他们警惕地盯着进出城门的每一个人。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 38: An Accidental Encounter in Moluo City

Ah Cheng grew excited, alternately sitting and standing, always trying to find something to do. He had been like this since two days ago.

Shang Feifan was browsing the game mall. Over the past two months, he had taken on quite a few minor quests here and there, progressing from quest twenty-four all the way to quest fifty.

He could feel the brain-loaded system's hard work; in order to make his journey less boring and prevent him from quitting the game, it conscientiously kept issuing quests to him.

He had to admit that it was precisely these small quests and contribution point rewards dangling before him that kept him logging into the game day after day without fail.

Of course, the benefits the game itself brought him were far from small, and they were becoming increasingly obvious day by day. This was the most important reason why he was truly willing to log into the game like clockwork, treating it like punching in for work.

The researcher responsible for studying and analyzing his physical data was still Dr. Zhang, but a few heavyweight experts had been added to the project team.

At the national level, the game was receiving more and more attention. Aside from him, the authorities had found several other domestic players willing to participate in the research and were also striving to secure application slots for the fifth batch of players.

Over these past two months, the players' development within the game had also made substantial progress, with player camps having been built from number one all the way to number five.

The first batch of players had generally reached level ten.

More and more players were activating Divine Blood talents and unlocking professional skills.

Players purchasing the language pack... Although expensive, almost every player bought the language pack as long as they had fifty silver on hand, because their interactions with the local Orcs were steadily increasing.

Rumors of the Sky-Shattered Army had already begun circulating around the vicinity of the Valley of the Sky-Shattered.

These rumors had not yet reached the ears of that true lord, but presumably, that day wouldn't be far off.

Although Shang Feifan hadn't had much actual contact with the players, he had Fu Xiangjun communicating news with him at any time, so he was basically clear on whatever major or minor events happened on the player side.

Last month, the game merchants opened the fourth round of game account applications, and the batch of game accounts released was quite large, reaching a full three thousand.

It was said that at the end of this month, the fifth round of game account applications would be released, featuring as many as eight thousand game accounts.

This game world was about to get lively. Shang Feifan thought to himself.

The development over at the player camp couldn't affect him for the time being, so Shang Feifan acted just like a scenery enthusiast, traveling a thousand miles alone over two months.

The notebook system seemed completely unaware that a solitary player had wandered so far away from the player camp—perhaps thanks to the brain-loaded system's cover?

Speaking of which, the rewards for these minor quests issued by the brain-loaded system weren't large, but during this period he hadn't needed to buy anything specific, so he had managed to accumulate his contribution points.

Coupled with the contribution points earned from expanding the map, he now had a surplus of a full 53 contribution points.

Originally, Shang Feifan had wanted to save up contribution points to buy a spatial storage tool, but now that he possessed the Statue Square, he changed his goal. He wanted to unlock the alchemy profession; a primary alchemist only cost one hundred points.

Of course, if he could run into an alchemy master willing to take him on as an apprentice, that would be even better, as these contribution points could then be saved.

Yet he also had to prepare for both contingencies—what should he do if he kept failing to meet an alchemist willing to take him as an apprentice?

In truth, he still hadn't encountered a single true alchemist up to this point.

And now that he had tasted the benefits of unlocking professional skills, the moment he possessed one hundred contribution points, he would undoubtedly go and unlock the alchemy profession without a second's hesitation.

"Mr. Hosier, are we going to... are we going to enter the city today? Should we rest in a nearby village for a day first?" Ah Cheng asked hesitantly.

Shang Feifan looked at him and shook his head. "We've already reached the gates; naturally, we're going into the city to find a place to rest. Besides, don't you want to go home sooner?"

He was quite eager to hand over this burden and collect his reward as quickly as possible.

Ah Cheng smiled awkwardly.

Shang Feifan understood. This was the timidity one felt when nearing home, especially when one wasn't returning covered in glory.

If Ah Cheng were to say to him right now, "Let's not enter Moluo City, let's go somewhere else," he wouldn't even find it strange.

However, nearly two years of slave life in the bandit den had made Ah Cheng far more timid; he no longer possessed the courage he had when first leaving his hometown nor the infinite yearning for the world outside Moluo City.

He felt both deeply ashamed to return like this and reassured that he could immediately welcome a truly peaceful, safe, and affluent life.

When Ah Cheng stole a glance at him for the N-th time, Shang Feifan spoke up: "You can tell the truth to your family, but there's no need to do so with outsiders. Just say that these past two years you've been traveling and studying abroad, wandering and doing odd jobs with various caravans, during which you won the favor of a caravan chef and learned a bit of culinary skill. Now that you miss home and yearn for your family even more, wanting to return to take care of your parents, you decided to come back and open a small restaurant to live out your days in peace."

Ah Cheng was so moved that his eyes turned red. Although he had learned how to handle odd chores in the bandit camp's kitchen, he hadn't managed to steal away much genuine culinary technique. On the contrary, following Shang Feifan over these past two months, he had learned the preparation methods for quite a few delicious foods.

He had secretly planned to figure out a way to open a small restaurant after returning home; he didn't want to come back and continue bleeding his parents dry, yet he truly lacked the aptitude for pharmacy.

Still, stealing knowledge without permission was never a good thing, let alone the fact that Shang Feifan was his savior. He hadn't expected this savior to proactively suggest he open a restaurant and even fabricate a ready-made excuse for his two-year disappearance.

Seeing Ah Cheng's lips tremble, looking as though he might throw himself forward to hug him and cry his eyes out, Shang Feifan immediately raised a hand and pointed toward Moluo City: "We are about to enter the city. Hurry up and change into the clothes and gear you bought earlier."

Clothes make the man. Having spent two years away only to return looking like a beggar, the gossip and rumors alone could crush this young man.

Shang Feifan had plenty of experience and had prepared three sets of outfits early on, even giving Lord Zheng a brand-new makeover.

After careful grooming and dressing up, the radiant Ah Cheng indeed looked much steadier than before. He no longer offered verbal thanks to Shang Feifan, instead planning to have his parents properly repay this savior—who had even been willing to salvage his pride—upon returning home. Besides...

Ah Cheng pressed his stomach and decided to remain true to his heart's desires.

Ah Dai had also changed into a new outfit. Ah Dai couldn't transform into human form, and Orcs weren't accustomed to putting clothes on beastly bodies, but they could add some protective and offensive gear.

When they were at the herb village, Shang Feifan had asked the local leatherworker to craft three sets of defensive leather armor for the three of them, and later he added a few small accessories to his own and Ah Dai's leather armor.

Ah Dai liked this set of small-sized leather armor immensely. Once he put it on, he felt utterly majestic, standing atop the very peak of the baggage pile, chest puffed out and head held high as he looked down disdainfully at his surroundings.

Along the way, some Orcs caught sight of this blocky little fellow and smiled warmly at him. The child was ugly-cute, carrying a dazed expression, yet he was dressed up quite spiritedly, growing round, chubby, and furry—at first glance, he was clearly deeply cherished by his family.

Indeed, Ah Dai had fattened up by a wide margin, his little belly bulging out, and his fur had grown in nicely. Now he truly possessed the chubby, fluffy cuteness of a baby cub.

Upon reaching the vicinity of Moluo City, the pedestrians and carriages coming and going flowed like a torrential river.

The gates of Moluo City were wide open. Although there were guards, no barriers were set up, allowing pedestrians and caravans to enter and exit freely.

Seeing this, Shang Feifan immediately felt that the city lord of this place was extremely clever.

How could the meager income from city gate taxes ever compare to the chain reaction brought by such massive customer traffic?

Naturally, large crowds also placed immense pressure on security.

Aside from increasing revenue for the city lord, another important function of collecting city gate taxes was allowing the city guards to observe and spot unstable elements—either barring them from entering or marking them as high-priority targets of surveillance.

So how did the city lord of this place resolve the safety issues within the city?

Sitting atop Lord Zheng's back, Shang Feifan, who had just passed through the city gates, quickly discovered the answer.

First of all, those city guards standing with upright postures near the city gates were not just for show; their gazes were exceptionally sharp, and their sense of smell was likely terrifyingly acute as they vigilantly stared at every single person entering and leaving the gates.

chunks.chineseText:
其次，城门口有着告示板，上面张贴着各种告示和通缉犯的图像。

商非凡还看到一些虫子在城门口盘旋，他一开始还奇怪城门口怎么这么多虫子，还没有被拍死，还好他及时观察到这些虫子就像蜜蜂一样，在城门口拥有自己的木箱房屋。

而且这些身形也很像蜜蜂，只是比蜜蜂要更小一号的虫子最喜欢跟着紧闭的车厢和被盖上的货车飞舞。而那些车厢和货车主人看到这些虫子钻入他们的车厢和货车中，也跟没看到一样。

商非凡猜测那些虫子大概也肩负和城卫一样的职责。

阿城的介绍也验证了这一点。这些虫子还有一个名字，叫“警卫虫”，对血腥味和某些特殊物品的味道异常敏感，是摩罗城治安队和警卫厅专门豢养的好帮手。

进城后，城内有巡逻队几乎不间断地在城内大小街道上巡逻，比较繁华的街道边角则都有治安岗亭。

这些负责治安的兽人也不是做做样子。他们刚进城就看到一队治安兵一边奔跑一边吹哨，让行人让开道路。

路上行人和车辆似乎早已习以为常，还有人冲着某处吹口哨。

商非凡抬头就看到一个兽人正飞快爬向一座楼的阳台，想要翻进去。而街道两头已经各自跑来一队治安兵，这些治安兵身手矫健，攀爬跑跳得比他们正在追踪的兽人更快更灵活。

两个治安兵飞快冲进小楼，很快就把那兽人制伏，用绳子捆绑住四肢，把人押解了出来。

喝彩声和掌声响起。

治安兵面无表情地把被抓兽人塞进囚车，快跑离开。

“我家人住在第五街。一直往前走，经过药剂市场，拐向东边，那里有大量的住宅区，很多炼药学徒都住在那边。”

阿城看着熟悉又陌生的街道，神色复杂。

“炼药师之间很讲究资历，只要能从学徒升级到真正的炼药师，都会搬离第五街，搬到炼药师们喜欢住的第三街。但第三街也只是普通炼药师居所，真正的大师只会住在第一街。城主和城里的一些大贵族反而只能住在第二街。”

“第四街住的是普通贵族和一些大商人。第六街就是药剂市场。第七街是商业区，也是摩罗城最繁华的街区。第八街是工坊区，手艺人大多都住在这里。第九街和第十街住的都是普通城民。还有第十一街，那里也被称为贫民区……”

商非凡耳中听着阿城对摩罗城的介绍，一边观察这座城。

经过药剂市场时，商非凡突然让狰爷停下。

阿城一惊。怎么了，发生了什么事？

阿呆也抬头看老商。

商非凡盯着药剂市场的一栋楼，他刚刚好像看到了虎不帅？

虎不帅怎么会在这里？

他是来采购药物的吗？

商非凡没想到会这么巧，他以为要等他离开摩罗城，再走上十天半个月赶到莫约山谷镇才能再见到这个让他有点惦记的年轻兽人。

商非凡不想和虎不帅错过，他直接让狰爷进入了药剂市场。

疑似虎不帅的年轻兽人进入的那栋小楼外面挂着牌子，这是一家药剂店。

“日安，先生，想要购买药剂吗？我们店有一批皮翰药师刚刚炼制的外伤药剂，疗效上佳，价格也比其他地方更合理公道。先生要进来看看吗？”药行伙计跑出来热情揽客。

商非凡听到药剂师的名字有点耳熟，听到伙计提到外伤药剂，立刻想起来，他在强盗窝库房里收集到的药物的药瓶上有一半就署着这位中级炼药学徒的名字。

这还真是有缘。

商非凡抱着阿呆从狰爷背脊上跳下来，阿城也跟着跃下。

狰爷不用管，它自己会顾好自己，这个药剂市场有专门给巨虫坐骑使用的休息区，里面放着免费的巨虫食物和清水。摩罗城里的巨虫坐骑很多，这些巨虫也都已经习惯和兽人们的共同生活。

阿城以为商非凡要购买药剂，正想跟他说，这些药剂不用买，他可以让他父亲免费送。如果他父亲没有的，他也可以请他父亲帮忙拿到最便宜的进货价。

但商非凡已经抱着阿呆走入药剂店。阿城只好跟了进去。

店铺内，一道熟悉的背影站在货柜前，正跟一个貌似药行掌柜的人说话。

真的是他！

“嗨。”商非凡谨慎地没有叫出虎不帅的名字，而是走到他身边，轻轻打了个招呼。

虎不帅转头，脸上顿时出现惊讶神情：“是你？你……”

你真的还活着？

当时发生了什么事？

为什么你现在看起来已经没事？

还有你为什么会出现在这里？

虎不帅想问的问题太多，但这里显然不是说话的地方。

商非凡脸上笑容变大，他发现他对这个NPC是真的很喜欢，前面两个月没见到也没怎么想，但真见到人，那股从心底泛起的欢喜，让他甚至想要抱抱这个年轻兽人。

商非凡忍住冲动，对虎不帅眨眨眼，正要开口，门外突然传来喧哗声。

大量兽人在往同一个方向跑动，还有人在大喊：“巨虫休息区出事了，好几个巨虫被毒死了！”
chunks.englishText:
Secondly, there were notice boards at the city gates, plastered with various public notices and portraits of wanted criminals.

Shang Feifan also noticed a few insects hovering around the city gates. At first, he found it strange that there were so many bugs at the gate without being swatted to death, but fortunately, he observed in time that these insects were like honeybees, having their own wooden box-like hives right at the gates.

Moreover, their body shapes were very much like bees, just a size smaller. These insects were most fond of flying closely alongside closed carriages and covered cargo carts. Yet, the owners of those carriages and carts acted as though they saw nothing when these bugs drilled into their vehicles.

Shang Feifan guessed that those insects probably shouldered the same duties as the city guards.

A-Cheng’s introduction verified this thought. These insects had another name: "Guard Bugs." They were exceptionally sensitive to the scent of blood and the smell of certain special items, making them fine assistants specially raised by the Mo Luo City security squad and guard precinct.

After entering the city, patrol squads could be seen patrolling the large and small streets almost uninterruptedly. Near the corners of the more prosperous streets, there were security sentry posts.

These beastmen responsible for public security weren't just putting on a show. Just after entering the city, they saw a squad of security guards running while blowing whistles, urging pedestrians to clear the way.

Pedestrians and vehicles on the road seemed long accustomed to this, and someone even whistled toward a certain spot.

Shang Feifan looked up and saw a beastman rapidly climbing toward the balcony of a building, attempting to vault inside. Meanwhile, security guard squads had already run over from both ends of the street. These security guards were agile, climbing, running, and leaping even faster and more fluidly than the beastman they were tracking.

Two security guards swiftly charged into the small building, and before long, they subdued the beastman, bound his limbs with rope, and escorted him out.

Cheers and applause rang out.

With expressionless faces, the security guards shoved the captured beastman into a prisoner wagon and hurried away.

"My family lives on Fifth Street. Just keep going straight, pass through the apothecary market, and turn east. There are a large residential area over there, and many apothecary apprentices live on that side."

Looking at the streets that were both familiar and unfamiliar, A-Cheng wore a complex expression.

"Apothecaries are very particular about seniority. As long as someone is promoted from an apprentice to a true apothecary, they will move out of Fifth Street and move to Third Street, which apothecaries prefer to live in. But Third Street is only a residence for ordinary apothecaries; true masters only live on First Street. Interestingly, the City Lord and some of the city's grand nobles can only live on Second Street."

"Fourth Street is where ordinary nobles and major merchants live. Sixth Street is the apothecary market. Seventh Street is the commercial district and also the most prosperous neighborhood in Mo Luo City. Eighth Street is the workshop district, where most artisans live. Ninth and Tenth Streets are where ordinary citizens live. Then there's Eleventh Street, which is also known as the slums..."

Listening to A-Cheng's introduction of Mo Luo City, Shang Feifan observed the city at the same time.

Passing through the apothecary market, Shang Feifan suddenly had Zhen Ye stop.

A-Cheng was startled. *What's wrong? What happened?*

A-Dai also looked up at Old Shang.

Shang Feifan stared at a building in the apothecary market; he thought he had just caught a glimpse of Hu Bushuai?

Why would Hu Bushuai be here?

Did he come to procure medicine?

Shang Feifan hadn't expected such a coincidence. He thought he would have to wait until he left Mo Luo City and traveled another ten days to half a month to reach Moyao Valley Town before he could see this young beastman who had lingered a bit in his thoughts.

Not wanting to miss Hu Bushuai, Shang Feifan directly had Zhen Ye enter the apothecary market.

The small building that the suspected Hu Bushuai had entered had a plaque hanging outside; it was an apothecary shop.

"Good day, sir. Are you looking to purchase potions? Our shop has a batch of trauma potions just brewed by Apothecary Pihan. Their therapeutic efficacy is top-notch, and the price is much more reasonable and fair than elsewhere. Would sir like to come inside and take a look?" A shop assistant ran out, enthusiastically soliciting customers.

Hearing the apothecary's name, Shang Feifan found it somewhat familiar. Hearing the assistant mention trauma potions, he immediately recalled that half of the medicine bottles he had collected in the bandits' stronghold warehouse were inscribed with the name of this intermediate apothecary apprentice.

This really was quite the affinity.

Clutching A-Dai, Shang Feifan jumped down from Zhen Ye’s back, and A-Cheng leaped down as well.

Zhen Ye didn't need to be managed; it would look after itself. This apothecary market had a designated rest area specifically for giant insect mounts, equipped with free giant insect feed and fresh water. There were many giant insect mounts in Mo Luo City, and these giant insects had already grown accustomed to living alongside beastmen.

Thinking that Shang Feifan wanted to purchase potions, A-Cheng wanted to tell him that these potions didn't need to be bought—he could have his father send them for free. If his father didn't have them, he could also ask his father to help acquire them at the cheapest wholesale price.

However, Shang Feifan had already walked into the apothecary shop holding A-Dai. A-Cheng had no choice but to follow inside.

Inside the shop, a familiar back stood before the counter, speaking with someone who looked like the shopkeeper.

It really was him!

"Hi." Cautiously refraining from calling out Hu Bushuai's name, Shang Feifan walked up beside him and offered a gentle greeting.

Hu Bushuai turned his head, an expression of astonishment instantly surfacing on his face: "It's you? You..."

*You're actually still alive?*
*What happened back then?*
*Why do you look completely fine now?*
*And why are you appearing here?*

Hu Bushuai had too many questions he wanted to ask, but this was clearly not the place to talk.

The smile on Shang Feifan's face grew wider. He realized he genuinely liked this NPC. During the past two months of not seeing him, he hadn't thought about him much, but upon actually seeing him, the joy welling up from the bottom of his heart made him want to even give this young beastman a hug.

Suppressing the impulse, Shang Feifan blinked at Hu Bushuai and was just about to speak when a commotion suddenly broke out from outside the door.

A large crowd of beastmen was running in the same direction, and someone was shouting at the top of their lungs: "Something's happened at the giant insect rest area! Several giant insects have been poisoned to death!"

chunks.chapterTitle: 第39章 我和拉斐尔有特殊关系 (Part 1)
chunks.chineseText:
第39章 我和拉斐尔有特殊关系

两个人脸色一变，顾不上叙旧，一起冲往店铺外面。

包括店内其他客户也一样。

对兽人们来说，巨虫坐骑跟兽人伙伴没什么区别，想要得到一只巨虫坐骑，不是花钱购买就行。巨虫愿不愿意跟随你，讲的是一个投缘，如果巨虫看你不顺眼，管你使出十八般花样，它也不会理你。

同一时间，系统发布新任务。

【任务五十一，摩罗城药剂市场发生紧急情况，坐骑休息区有数只巨虫坐骑被毒杀。请你调查这次投毒事件，找到凶手。成功找到凶手，奖励5点贡献点。】

药剂市场的兽人们好多都在往巨虫休息区跑。

情况太乱，商非凡把阿呆塞给阿城，让他们在店里老实待着，哪里都不要去。

阿城立刻抱紧阿呆，停住脚步。

两个月的旅程，阿呆早就习惯这种“出事爸爸冲前面，他和阿城待后面”的待遇，乖乖窝在阿城臂弯里。

虎不帅目光扫过阿城和阿呆，就感到身边一阵风刮过，商非凡已经冲到了最前面。

坐骑休息区一片混乱。

“是谁！是谁下的毒？你给我出来！我要你偿命！”

“啊啊啊，我的巨虫坐骑死了，这可是能飞的巨虫！你们知道想要得到这么一只能飞的巨虫坐骑有多难吗？你们市场必须赔我！”

“今天的食物和水是谁提供的？把人带过来！”

“你们市场必须负责！谁也逃不掉！”

“你们摩罗城在搞什么，我们来你们这里买药剂，你们竟然让人毒死我们的巨虫伙伴？我跟你们说，这事没完！”

“大家好好说，不要吵也不要打！我们会负责调查清楚这件事，治安队马上就过来，法医也会过来，我们一定会给大家一个交代！”

休息区的负责人在拿着喇叭喊话，到处都是乱哄哄一片。

“狰爷！”商非凡发出召唤声。

一只比其他巨虫体型都要大上一圈的巨蟹断翅虫从休息区哒哒走出来，长腿轻轻戳了戳商非凡的胳膊。

商非凡吐出一口气，两个月的旅程让他一遍又一遍认识到狰爷的重要性。如果没有狰爷，他还不知道哪个猴年马月才能走到摩罗城，还是带着一个幼崽和一个没有多少武力的貂兽人。

“你没事吧？”商非凡摩擦嘴唇询问。

“哒哒哒。”狰爷碉碉地表示它也是刚到，还没来得及喝这里的水、吃这里的食物，就闻到有巨虫死了。

商非凡拍拍狰爷，提醒它暂时别食用这里的食物和水。

狰爷脚尖敲击出哒哒两声。

商非凡知道狰爷的警觉性极好，它还能和其他巨虫交流，只要它知道死掉的几只巨虫和这里的食水有关，就算那些食水再合它口味，它也绝对不会碰。

虎不帅也赶过来了，正在查看自己的巨虫坐骑。

其他兽人同样。

商非凡带着狰爷走到虎不帅身边。

虎不帅脸色极为难看，单膝跪到巨虫跟前。

他的巨虫坐骑死了。

随着赶来的兽人越多，周围的情况越发混乱。

被毒死的巨虫不止一只两只，市场麻烦大了。

药剂市场负责休息区的兽人满头满身的汗，拼命和失去巨虫坐骑的兽人们解释，但悲痛的兽人们根本不听，只一心要药剂市场付出代价，要他们交出投毒的人。

治安巡逻队赶到，隔开了兽人，并喝令无关兽人立刻离开。

商非凡没想到虎不帅竟然是中招的倒霉蛋之一。

这种情况，不管怎么安慰都不适合。

“你可能只是被卷进了某个报复事件。我会帮你找出投毒者，给你的巨虫报仇。”商非凡拍拍虎不帅。

虎不帅没说话，他在怀疑投毒者根本就是冲着他来的。

这让虎不帅快要难以抑制心中升腾的怒火。

他已经避之又避，甚至主动离开莫约山谷镇，就是为了不和那些来找他的人接触，想通过他的避让行为来让某些人放心。

可……也许他姨父说得没错，只要他活着，某些人就不会真正安心。

还有些人不敢真的弄死他，却能想出各种方法来恶心他、骚扰他，抱着一种只要你不愉快我就愉快的变态心理。

虎不帅垂下眼眸，缓慢吸气，平息自己的怒火。

他要查清楚这件事，弄明白他遇到的到底是无妄之灾，还是他才是源头。

商非凡看着情绪内敛的虎不帅，在心中叹息。

有时候怒火和悲伤还是发泄出来的好，内耗可不是什么好事。

只要想想面前死的巨虫是狰爷，他就能感受到虎不帅这时有多么难过和愤怒。

商非凡想要拍抚对方肩膀。

虎不帅躲过，自己站了起来。

药剂市场治安官正在统计一共死了多少只巨虫。

食槽和水槽那边已经有人在取样验毒。

这里是药城，对于投毒事件的反应比其他案件都快。

巡逻队又增加一支，看热闹的兽人被驱散，只剩下巨虫受害者的主人和其他关系者。

“这只死去的巨虫是你的？”一名治安官手里拿着皮质笔记本和笔，走过来询问。

“是。”虎不帅回答。

“你是商人？从哪里过来？”治安官先询问虎不帅的姓名来历，接着就是要查验他的身份骨牌。

“我不是商人，只是跟家人过来这边采买药剂。”虎不帅掏出一枚骨牌递给治安官。

“金麦城下属的莫约山谷镇？那里离我们这里可不近。”治安官抬头看虎不帅。

虎不帅眼神平静：“往年有商队会带药物到我们镇，但今年这支商队一直没来。偏偏我们镇附近一个兽人聚集区爆发了疫病，我们只能自己出来买药。”

“疫病？”治安官看虎不帅的眼神变了。

虎不帅：“还没有传到我们镇子上，我们镇子已经封锁了那个聚集地通往我们镇子的路。我们镇长只是为了以防万一，才让我们过来购买针对疫病的药剂和伤药等。”

虎不帅顿了顿，又道：“如果我们感染疫病，早在来的路上就发作了。同样，如果我们感染疫病，我也不会主动告诉你疫病的事。”

治安官心想也是，再估量金麦城到这里的距离，安心了不少。

“这种疫病对巨虫有影响吗？”治安官又问。

商非凡冷不丁插话：“这些死去的巨虫难道不都是被毒死的吗？就说这些巨虫的主人来自各个地方，就算一只巨虫感染疫病，总不能刚接触就把其他巨虫都给传染死了吧？”

治安官看向商非凡，“你是？”

“诺曼霍希尔，来自黑森林城。”商非凡刚刚就已经想好要利用真诺曼的身份，摸出代表身份的骨牌，递到治安官面前。

治安官看到身份牌上显示的信息，面色微变。

商非凡压低声音：“请对我的身份保密。”

治安官皱紧眉头，左右看看，也压低声音：“您是来我们这里调查什么的吗？这个投毒事件是否……”
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 39: I Have a Special Relationship with Raphael (Part 1)

The expressions of the two men shifted abruptly. Setting aside reminiscing, they rushed out of the shop together.

The same went for the other customers inside the store.

To beastmen, giant insect mounts were no different from beastman companions. To acquire a giant insect mount wasn't simply a matter of spending money to buy one. Whether a giant insect was willing to follow you came down to a mutual affinity; if a giant insect didn't take a fancy to you, it wouldn't pay you any mind no matter what eighteen martial arts tricks or fancy methods you pulled out.

At the same time, the system issued a new quest.

[Quest Fifty-One: An emergency has occurred at the Mo Luo City apothecary market; several giant insect mounts in the mount rest area have been poisoned to death. Please investigate this poisoning incident and find the culprit. Successfully finding the culprit rewards 5 contribution points.]

Many of the beastmen in the apothecary market were running toward the giant insect rest area.

The situation was too chaotic. Shang Feifan shoved A-Dai into A-Cheng’s arms, telling them to stay put in the shop obediently and go nowhere.

A-Cheng immediately hugged A-Dai tightly and stopped in his tracks.

During their two-month journey, A-Dai had long since grown accustomed to this kind of treatment—"Dad rushes to the front when trouble happens, while he and A-Cheng stay in the back." He obediently curled up in the crook of A-Cheng's arm.
