chunks.chapterTitle: 第45章 赔偿金的用法 (Part 1)
chunks.chineseText:
第45章 赔偿金的用法

有火焰天赋者帮忙，焚烧巨虫坐骑的速度很快，虎不帅的坐骑还被排在了第一个。

连同骨灰，赔偿金也被送到他手中。

虎不帅不想让自己异于他人，就接过了这份赔偿金。但他转手就把这份赔偿金送给了在药剂市场乞讨的两个小孩子。

他观察了一会儿，才选择了这两个孩子。

小小兽人抱着这么一笔对她来说异常庞大的财产，摇晃着尾巴，惊讶地睁大眼睛。

“你们身后有人控制你们吗？”虎不帅轻声问。

“你想干嘛？”另一个更大一点的小兽人警惕地看着虎不帅，把妹妹拉到身后。

“没有。”小小兽人清脆地说。

虎不帅眼睛扫过小小兽人，温和地笑笑，这是个把自己打扮成男孩的小女孩。

“那就好。那你们有父母或其他对你们好的家人吗？”

“你想干嘛？”做哥哥的小兽人凶巴巴地再次喝问。

虎不帅温和道：“我知道摩罗城有一所专门培养小兽人的学校，可以一直培养到成年。他们是寄宿制，除了教导普通知识，还会根据个人特长和喜好进行职业培训，确保将来离开学校也能找到一门工作养活自己。校长和教导主任都是非常好的人，他们对学校的小兽人们严厉，但也非常关心。小兽人们住在那座学校，至少可以保证吃穿不愁且能安全长大。”

“你说的是育成少年职业综合学校吗？”小兽人哥哥问。

虎不帅：“你知道这所学校？”

小兽人哥哥神色不再那么警惕：“知道。这所学校很有名，收费也不贵，而且愿意收贫民区的孩子。我打算再存一点钱就和我弟弟一起去参加考试，听说如果天赋好，还能免学杂费。”

虎不帅很想揉揉小兽人的脑袋，但他并没有伸手：“我认识那里的校长，你们俩可以今天就过去，就说是我介绍你们去的。这笔钱就是你们俩的学费和住宿费，应该够交五年的。五年后也不用担心，学校有对贫困生的学费减免、对优秀学生的奖励金，还能当勤杂工勤工俭学。记住，这笔钱不要交给任何大人，包括你们的父母。”

小兽人哥哥打开妹妹怀里的袋子看了看，吃惊地看向虎不帅。

小兽人妹妹还小，不懂得隐瞒，很诚实地说：“我们不上学，我们要给妈妈治病，妈妈生病了，爸爸没有钱给妈妈治病。爸爸偷偷哭了。”

虎不帅蹲下来，让自己的视线可以和小兽人平齐：“你们是好孩子，但给你妈妈治病是你爸爸的事，不是你们现在的责任。而且想要真正帮到你妈妈，必须改变你们现在的现状。

如果你们把钱拿去给你们妈妈治病，也许她能恢复健康，但也有可能遇到其他事情，导致你们人财两失。

而你们错过这个改变人生的机会，以后你们家再有人生病，你们同样没有办法筹集到足够钱财给他们治病，只会陷入恶性循环。”

“可是……”小兽人哥哥握住妹妹的手，迟疑。他们心里第一重要的就是爸爸妈妈，然后才会想到自己。

虎不帅耐心说：“去育成学校，把钱交给学校。你们成为学校的学生，以后吃住都不用你们父母操心，那你们父亲也能省下大笔开支给你们母亲治病。而你们父母知道你们将来有保证，他们心里轻松又高兴，说不定对你们母亲的身体恢复就大有帮助。”

小兽人哥哥灵机一动：“那我们能先交一两年的费用给学校，剩下来的钱给我母亲治病吗？”

虎不帅笑了，这真的是两个很好的孩子：“你可以在交学费的时候，把你们家的情况跟学校老师说明清楚。我想，他们学校的老师会很愿意帮助你们，告诉你们怎么做最好。”

小兽人哥哥的眼睛亮了。这个好心的大哥哥没有否决他的想法，也就是说他能这么操作？

这让小兽人也对虎不帅产生了一点信任，这让他把自己的担心也说了出来：“您给我们这么多钱，很多人看到了。我害怕……您能跟我们一起去育成学校吗？”

虎不帅当即点头，他一开始就想送小兽人去育成学校，只是怕小家伙误会，才没有主动开口。

两个小家伙互看，眼中都是兴奋和雀跃。

小兽人哥哥抬头，忍不住问：“为什么？您为什么要帮助我们？”

虎不帅只是笑笑，说：“算是缘分吧。”

因为这笔赔偿金来自只是倒霉被牵连的药剂市场，而不是真正应该赔偿的凶手。也因为他希望通过这种方式来告慰他的巨虫坐骑的亡灵。

相信他的巨虫坐骑也更希望自己的死亡赔偿金能换来两个可爱小兽人的光明未来，而不是被随便花掉。

另外，虎不帅注意到药剂市场有很多乞讨者，其中不少都是幼年小兽人。

这么多小兽人中，只有这两个小兽人衣着破旧，却很干净，身上脸上也比较干净，身上也不见多少伤口，瘦但还算健康。

这说明他们家人把两个小家伙照顾得还行，也说明他们应该只是遇到了一时难以解决的大困难。

如果能在这时候伸手捞他们一把，两个小家伙也许不会就此陷入黑暗人生。

最重要的是，在其他小兽人一个劲纠缠看起来好说话的兽人进行强行乞讨时，这两个小兽人却只是很有礼貌地询问，被拒绝不会纠缠，得到施舍则衷心感谢。

他们更没有和其他小兽人联合，转移被乞讨兽人的注意力，去搞偷窃。

其他小兽人也很可怜，但虎不帅不想等两个小家伙完全沉沦后再伸手。他希望能在这两个小家伙感受到什么是真正的黑暗、学会做坏事和伤心绝望前，就把他们拉上岸。

他做不到拯救全世界的可怜人，也不想当圣人，就是随手一帮，全凭眼缘。

而且他只会付钱，绝不想和这些被帮者有过多牵扯。

商非凡就在他们身后，在虎不帅把钱袋送给那个小兽人时，他就拎着一大包食物过来了。

阿呆抱着一大块麦饼夹肉，用力啃啊啃。

“我们先送这两个孩子去育成学校。”虎不帅转头跟商非凡打招呼。

商非凡问都没问缘由，直接点头：“好。”

两个小兽人看到又有一个成年兽人过来，有点害怕。

但他们看到商非凡怀里抱着一个比他们还小的小幼崽，又只是跟在他们身后，就稍微放了点心。

小兽人哥哥还跟自己妹妹咬耳朵，让她随时注意他的暗号，做好随时逃跑的准备。

虎不帅在后面听得清清楚楚，就笑。

商非凡撞了撞他的肩膀，从袋子里掏出一个香喷喷的麦饼夹肉递给他：“日行一善？”

虎不帅接过道谢，又摇头：“只是给这笔赔偿金找个更适合的去处。”

商非凡也发现虎不帅完全没有做了好事的自觉，那神情特别平淡，就好像这种事对他来说特别平常。

一个……有点随心所欲的人？

商非凡感觉自己发现了虎不帅的另一面。

“你和那个育成学校很熟？”
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 45: The Usage of Compensation Money

With the help of a fire-element user, the cremation of the giant insect mount proceeded very quickly, and Hu Bushuai's mount happened to be placed first in line.

Along with the ashes, the compensation money was handed over to him.

Not wanting to stand out from the others, Hu Bushuai accepted the compensation money. However, he turned around and handed the entire sum over to two young children who were begging in the potion market.

He had observed for a while before selecting these two children.

The little beastman child cradled a sum of wealth that was exceptionally massive to her, her tail swaying as she opened her eyes wide in astonishment.

"Is someone behind you controlling you?" Hu Bushuai asked softly.

"What do you want?" Another slightly older little beastman looked at Hu Bushuai with vigilance, pulling his younger sister behind him.

"No one," the little beastman girl said crisply.

Hu Bushuai's gaze swept over the little beastman girl and he smiled gently. This was a little girl who had disguised herself as a boy.

"That's good. Then do you have parents or other family members who treat you well?"

"What do you want?" The older little beastman brother demanded fiercely once more.

Hu Bushuai said mildly, "I know there is a school in Molo City dedicated to training young beastmen, which can educate them all the way to adulthood. It's a boarding school. Aside from teaching general knowledge, they also provide vocational training based on personal traits and hobbies, ensuring that when the students leave the school in the future, they can find a job to support themselves. The principal and the headmaster are exceptionally good people; they are strict with the young beastmen in the school, but they care for them deeply as well. If young beastmen live in that school, they can at least be guaranteed to never go hungry or cold and grow up safely."

"Are you talking about the Youth Vocational Comprehensive School?" asked the older little beastman brother.

Hu Bushuai: "You know about this school?"

The older little beastman brother's expression was no longer so guarded: "I know. This school is very famous, the tuition isn't expensive, and they are willing to take in children from the slums. I was planning to save a bit more money and go take the entrance exams with my younger brother—I heard that if your talent is good, miscellaneous fees can even be waived."

Hu Bushuai desperately wanted to rub the little beastman's head, but he didn't reach out: "I know the principal there. The two of you can go over today and just say I introduced you. This money should be enough to cover the tuition and boarding fees for both of you for five years. After five years, you won't need to worry either; the school has tuition reductions for impoverished students, scholarships for outstanding students, and you can also do odd jobs through work-study programs. Remember, do not hand this money over to any adults, including your parents."

The older little beastman brother opened the bag in his younger sister's arms to take a look, then looked at Hu Bushuai in astonishment.

The younger beastman sister was still too young to understand how to hide things, and said quite honestly, "We aren't going to school. We need to buy medicine for Mom. Mom is sick, and Dad doesn't have money to buy medicine for her. Dad cried in secret."

Hu Bushuai squatted down so that his line of sight was level with the little beastmen: "You are good children, but buying medicine for your mom is your dad's job, not your responsibility right now. Moreover, if you want to truly help your mom, you must change your current situation.

If you take this money to buy medicine for your mom, perhaps she can recover her health, but there is also a chance you will run into other troubles, leaving you with neither the money nor the person.

And once you miss this chance to change your lives, the next time someone in your family falls ill, you still won't have a way to gather enough money to cure them, and you'll just fall into a vicious cycle."

"But…" The older little beastman brother held his sister's hand, hesitating. In their hearts, their mother and father came first, and only after that did they think of themselves.

Hu Bushuai said patiently, "Go to the Youth School and hand the money over to the school. Once you become students of the school, your parents won't have to worry about your food and lodging anymore, which means your father can save a large sum of expenses to buy medicine for your mother. And when your parents know that your future is guaranteed, they will feel relieved and happy, which might even be of great help to your mother's physical recovery."

A flash of inspiration struck the older little beastman brother: "Then can we pay the school for just one or two years of fees first, and use the remaining money to cure our mother?"

Hu Bushuai smiled; these truly were two very good children: "When you pay your tuition, you can explain your family's situation to the school teachers. I believe the teachers at that school will be very willing to help you and tell you what is best to do."

The older little beastman brother's eyes lit up. This kind-hearted older brother hadn't shot down his idea, which meant he could actually operate this way?

This caused the little beastman to develop a bit of trust in Hu Bushuai, prompting him to voice his lingering worry: "You gave us so much money, and many people saw it. I'm scared… Can you go with us to the Youth School?"

Hu Bushuai nodded immediately. He had wanted to escort the little beastmen to the Youth School from the very beginning, but he hadn't proactively spoken up for fear that the little fellows would misunderstand his intentions.

The two little fellows looked at each other, their eyes filled with excitement and eager anticipation.

The older little beastman brother raised his head and couldn't help asking: "Why? Why are you helping us?"

Hu Bushuai merely smiled and said, "Consider it fate."

Because this compensation money came from the potion market, which had merely suffered bad luck and been implicated, rather than from the true culprit who deserved to pay. And also because he hoped to use this method to comfort the departed spirit of his giant insect mount.

He believed his giant insect mount would likewise prefer its death compensation to be exchanged for a bright future for two adorable little beastmen, rather than being squandered casually.

In addition, Hu Bushuai had noticed that there were many beggars in the potion market, among whom quite a few were young beastman children.

Out of so many young beastmen, only these two had clothing that was tattered yet clean; their bodies and faces were also relatively clean, with few visible wounds, and though thin, they were still fairly healthy.

This showed that their family members took decent care of the two little fellows, and also indicated that they were likely just encountering a major difficulty that was temporarily hard to resolve.

If he could reach out and pull them up at this moment, perhaps these two little fellows wouldn't plunge into a dark life from here on out.

Most importantly, while other young beastmen persistently pestered beastmen who looked easy-going to carry out forced begging, these two little beastmen merely made polite inquiries; when rejected they didn't pester, and when given alms they expressed heartfelt gratitude.

Nor did they join forces with other young beastmen to distract the targeted beastman and engage in petty theft.

The other young beastmen were also pitiful, but Hu Bushuai didn't want to wait until the two little fellows had completely sunk into the abyss before reaching out. He hoped to pull them ashore before these two little fellows experienced what true darkness was, before they learned to do bad things, and before they felt heartbreak and despair.

He couldn't save all the pitiful people in the world, nor did he want to play the saint; this was just a random act of assistance, driven entirely by a meeting of eyes.

Moreover, he would only pay the money and had no desire to get overly entangled with those he helped.

Shang Feifan was right behind them. The moment Hu Bushuai handed the money bag to that little beastman, he had already sauntered over carrying a large package of food.

Ah Dai was cradling a large piece of meat-stuffed wheat pancake, biting into it with great effort.

"Let's escort these two kids to the Youth School first." Hu Bushuai turned his head to greet Shang Feifan.

Without asking for the reason, Shang Feifan nodded directly: "Alright."

Seeing another adult beastman approach, the two little beastmen felt a slight flutter of fear.

However, when they saw that Shang Feifan was cradling a young cub even smaller than themselves and merely following behind them, their hearts settled down a bit.

The older little beastman brother even whispered into his younger sister's ear, telling her to pay attention to his signal at any time and get ready to run if necessary.

Hearing this crystal-clearly from behind, Hu Bushuai chuckled.

Shang Feifan bumped his shoulder against Hu Bushuai's, pulled a fragrant meat-stuffed wheat pancake out of the bag, and handed it to him: "Doing a good deed every day?"

Hu Bushuai took it, muttered his thanks, and shook his head: "Just finding a more suitable destination for this compensation money."

Shang Feifan also noticed that Hu Bushuai had completely zero self-awareness of having done a good deed; his expression was remarkably casual, as though this sort of thing was completely ordinary to him.

An… somewhat capricious person?

Shang Feifan felt as though he had discovered another side to Hu Bushuai.

"Are you very familiar with that Youth School?"

chunks.chapterTitle: 第45章 赔偿金的用法 (Part 2)
chunks.chineseText:
“谈不上熟悉，只是认识几个人。”虎不帅含糊道。

“你有想过做国王吗？”商非凡也拿出一个麦饼夹肉，牙齿用力撕扯下一块，咀嚼。

“什么？”虎不帅扭头，惊讶。

商非凡咀嚼着麦饼，看着他的眼睛说：“你做了国王就能按照你的想法改变这个世界。”

虎不帅失笑：“不，我对当国王一点兴趣都没有。我也没有这个能力。我承认，我确实对现在的虎国有很多不满，希望她能变得更宜居更能让国民幸福。但管理一个国家，并不是有希望她好的心就能做好，如果能力不够，反而只会把她拖入更可怕的深渊。只会打开国库和开粮仓，把东西分给穷人的国王可不是什么好国王。”

“所以这笔赔偿金你只是帮助了两个你认为最值得帮助的小孩，而不是平分给所有乞讨者。”商非凡看虎不帅的眼神变了：“你很理智。”

理智得完全不像是才二十左右的年轻兽人。

这跟性格和学习无关，虎不帅更像是从经验中得到的总结。

纸上谈兵和有实际领兵经验的将领，给人的感觉完全不同。商非凡现在看虎不帅，觉得他就像是后者。

商非凡还想跟虎不帅说：不要妄自菲薄，你已经有了当个好国王的资质。

虎不帅也看向商非凡，很想跟他摊牌：“你想从我这里得到什么？”

商非凡一脸我不懂你在说什么：“我以为……我们已经是朋友？”

“朋友？”虎不帅似乎对这个词不是很感冒，直接啃咬起手中麦饼。

商非凡看虎不帅脸颊用力一鼓一鼓，就觉得特别可爱。

可惜啊，这就是个纸片人，是一段程序编写出来的数据，如果现实世界有这么一个人，他可能就直接把人按在墙上这样那样了。

两个大人加阿呆一路啃咬着麦饼夹肉，把两个小兽人送到位于第八街区和第七街区交界处的育成少年职业综合学校。

两个小兽人看他们吃得喷香，一路吞咽着口水，但两个小兽人很懂事地都没有开口讨要。

偏偏两个在他们看来很善心的大哥哥就像是没有注意到他们咕咕叫的小肚子，一点麦饼都没有分给他们。

吃完了整整一个大麦饼的阿呆有点得意，爸爸还是最喜欢他！

他又偷偷看虎不帅，他也有一点点喜欢这个哥哥啦。

虎不帅没有走入学校大门，只是在门口目送两个小兽人走到里面。

两个小兽人回头看，却发现那两大一小已经走远。

两个小兽人满脸迷茫，要不是他们怀中的钱袋还在，他们还以为自己做了一场特别棒的美梦。

没多久，收到消息的两个小兽人的父亲飞快赶来学校。

这名在外面干苦力活的兽人听完长子陈述，一脸被幸运砸晕的不可置信。同时也很生气，他压根不知道两个孩子背着他跑出去乞讨，还持续了好几天，他以为两个孩子只是出门玩耍或者做了一些他们力所能及的小零工。

不过这时也不是斥责两个孩子的时候，这位父亲抱着两个孩子感动得眼泪汪汪。

当两个孩子说要把其中大半钱财拿去给母亲治病时，这位父亲一个劲摇头：“不用，这是恩人给你们上学和学技能的。你们妈妈的病，是我的责任，我一定会找人看好她！”

就如虎不帅所说，没有养育两个孩子的负担，做父亲的不但大大减轻了实际压力，更对未来充满希望和期待。他相信，就凭有好心人资助他两个孩子进入育成学校读书这点，他就能跟原来借不到钱的亲戚和朋友，甚至是跟老板借到足够给孩子母亲看病的钱。

反倒是学校职工对这位父亲说：“我觉得两个孩子的想法也很好。他们愿意在学校勤工俭学，这笔钱就可以拿出一半来给他们母亲治病，这也是他们对你们的心意。等你们两口子全都能健康做活，也能更多地照顾两个孩子，说不定将来还能筹出足够的学费。”

最后一家人商量妥当，一半钱用来给两个孩子当这两年的学费和寄宿费用，一半钱拿去给孩子母亲治病。

孩子父亲和两个孩子很想知道恩人的名字。

那名一直接待他们的学校职工笑了笑，说：“他是拉斐尔郎沐。”

虎不帅走得非常干脆。这件事对他来说连个人生小插曲都算不上，他甚至都没有记住两个小兽人的容貌特征，更没有问他们的名字。

商非凡又轻轻撞了撞虎不帅的肩膀，“这样就行了？你不进去交代两句？”

虎不帅：“为什么要交代？”

“你就不怕他们被人骗，或者他们做出其他选择？”

“那是他们的选择。我只是把一笔我不想要的钱给了我认为可以给的人，至于他们会怎么做，那是他们的事情。我不负责他们的未来。至于被骗，”

虎不帅睨商非凡：“你明明看到那学校来接孩子的职工看到我，对我点头微笑。在对方认识我的基础上，你觉得他们会骗那两个孩子的钱财吗？”

商非凡：“你不介意让我知道你来过摩罗城，还认识育才学校的人？”

“为什么要介意？难道你想跟谁出卖我？”虎不帅像是在开玩笑。

商非凡认真脸：“我觉得你在试探我。”

虎不帅眼里毫无波澜，他甚至没有露出半点笑意：“那你呢？调查官先生，你的真实目的又是什么。就算你失忆，这么长时间不回黑森林城，你就不怕被革职？”

“革职就革职。我失去了大部分记忆，尤其是调查局的工作。我甚至连自己的真实身份都忘了，如果不是有那枚骨牌，我甚至不知道自己来自黑森林城。如果我在这种情况下回去，就算不会被革职，也会被停职。既然如此，还不如不回去。”商非凡九假一真地混说。

虎不帅一边怀疑商非凡是否真的失忆，一边猜测他没有认出他就是拉斐尔郎沐是否就和他的失忆有关。

说不定这家伙不但失忆，还有些记忆混乱，否则他怎么会说出他和拉斐尔有特殊关系？

虎不帅完全没想到他被调戏的可能，前两世的人生经验包括这辈子的这张脸，都让他坚定认为自己是个没有多少魅力的人。

就算别人对他口花花，他也只以为别人在开玩笑。

“你不是正在调查药剂市场投毒和两起被自杀案件吗？你这也算是有在做工作，等回去黑森林城，你可以写一份调查报告，证明你不是在外面闲晃荡。”

“这是个好主意。”就是他压根就不是诺曼霍希尔，回去述职就不可能，不回黑森林城还能继续冒充这个身份。

“所以，你现在掌握了什么线索？”虎不帅停下脚步。

商非凡也跟着停下：“线索就是我知道强迫弗兰克自杀的凶手在哪里，现在我们正在往那个方向去。一起？”

虎不帅舔了舔略微干燥的嘴唇：“好。”

商非凡忽然也感到有点渴，迅速从腰带上解下水壶，递过去。

虎不帅表示自己也有。

商非凡知道他有，他就是想和虎不帅共用一个水壶，可惜被拒了。
chunks.englishText:
"Not familiar, I just know a few people," Hu Bushuai said vaguely.

"Have you ever thought about being a king?" Shang Feifan also pulled out a wheat-flour pancake stuffed with meat, tore off a piece with his teeth, and chewed.

"What?" Hu Bushuai turned his head, surprised.

Chewing his meat pancake, Shang Feifan looked into his eyes and said, "If you become king, you can change this world according to your own ideas."

Hu Bushuai gave a dry laugh: "No, I have zero interest in being a king. Nor do I have that kind of ability. I admit, I really have a lot of dissatisfaction with the current Tiger Kingdom, and I hope it can become more livable and bring more happiness to its citizens. But managing a country isn't something you can do just by having a good heart; if your ability falls short, you'll only drag it into a more terrifying abyss. A king who only knows how to open the national treasury and granaries to hand out goods to the poor is not a good king."

"So that's why you only used this compensation money to help the two kids you thought were most deserving, instead of dividing it equally among all the beggars." Shang Feifan's look at Hu Bushuai changed: "You're very rational."

Rational to the point that he didn't look like a young beastkin in his early twenties at all.

This had nothing to do with personality or book smarts; Hu Bushuai seemed more like someone who had summarized things through hard-earned experience.

Generals who only talked battle on paper versus those with actual frontline command experience gave off completely different vibes. Looking at Hu Bushuai now, Shang Feifan felt he was definitely the latter.

Shang Feifan really wanted to tell Hu Bushuai: Don't belittle yourself; you already possess the qualifications to be a good king.

Hu Bushuai also looked back at Shang Feifan, itching to lay his cards on the table: "What do you want to get out of me?"

Shang Feifan put on a face of absolute incomprehension: "I thought... we were already friends?"

"Friends?" Hu Bushuai didn't seem particularly fond of the word, simply taking another bite out of the meat pancake in his hand.

Watching Hu Bushuai's cheeks swell and contract rhythmically as he chewed, Shang Feifan thought it was exceptionally cute.

What a pity, though—this guy was just a 2D cutout, a chunk of data compiled by some program. If someone like this existed in the real world, he might have just pinned him against a wall and done all sorts of things.

The two adults, along with Dadai, gnawed on meat-flour pancakes all the way as they escorted the two young beastkins to the Vocational Comprehensive School for Youths, located at the intersection of the Eighth and Seventh Districts.

Seeing the two older ones eating with such relish, the young beastkins swallowed mouthfuls of saliva along the way, but being very sensible, neither of them dared to ask for any.

Yet these two big brothers, who seemed so kind in their eyes, acted as though they hadn't noticed their rumbling little bellies at all, not sharing even a crumb of the pancake with them.

Having finished an entire large wheat pancake, Dadai felt a little smug—Daddy loved him best after all!

He sneaked another glance at Hu Bushuai; he actually liked this older brother just a tiny bit now, too.

Hu Bushuai didn't walk through the school gates, simply standing at the entrance to watch the two young beastkins walk inside.

The two little ones looked back, only to discover that the two big ones and the little one had already walked far away.

Their faces were filled with bewilderment; if not for the money pouches still clutched tightly to their chests, they would have thought they had just experienced a magnificent dream.

Not long after, upon receiving the news, the young beastkins' father rushed to the school at top speed.

Hearing his eldest son's account, the beastkin—who earned his living doing hard labor outdoors—wore a look of incredulous disbelief, as if struck by a massive bolt of good fortune. At the same time, he was furious; he had no idea the two kids had been sneaking out behind his back to beg, and for days on end at that. He had thought they were just going out to play or doing some minor odd jobs within their capabilities.

However, this was no time to scold the children. The father pulled both kids into his arms, tears streaming down his face in deep gratitude.

When the two children declared that they wanted to use the greater portion of the money to cure their mother's illness, the father shook his head vigorously: "No, this is for you two to go to school and learn skills, given to you by our benefactor. Your mother's illness is my responsibility—I will definitely find a way to get her cured!"

Just as Hu Bushuai had said, relieved of the burden of raising the two children, the father not only felt his practical pressure immensely lightened, but his heart also filled with hope and expectation for the future. He believed that, backed by the kindness of a benefactor sponsoring his two children to study at the vocational school, he could borrow enough money from relatives and friends who had previously turned him down—or even from his boss—to pay for his wife's medical treatment.

On the contrary, a school staff member said to the father: "I think the two children's idea is actually quite good. Since they're willing to do a work-study program here at the school, half of this money can be taken out to treat their mother. This is also their filial heart toward you. Once both of you are healthy and able to work, you'll be able to take better care of the kids, and perhaps scrape together enough tuition for the future."

In the end, the family discussed and settled on a plan: half of the money would be used for the two children's tuition and boarding fees for the next two years, while the other half would go toward their mother's medical treatment.

The father and the two kids desperately wanted to know their benefactor's name.

The school staff member who had been dealing with them all along smiled and said, "His name is Raphael Langmu."

Hu Bushuai left with absolute decisiveness. To him, this matter didn't even count as a minor interlude in his life; he hadn't even remembered the facial features of the two young beastkins, let alone asked for their names.

Shang Feifan nudged Hu Bushuai's shoulder lightly. "Just like that? Aren't you going to go in and say a few parting words?"

Hu Bushuai: "Why would I?"

"Aren't you afraid they'll get scammed, or make some other choices?"

"That's their choice. I just gave money I didn't want to people I thought worthy of it. As for what they do with it, that's their business. I am not responsible for their future. As for getting scammed,"

Hu Bushuai slanted a glance at Shang Feifan: "You clearly saw the school staff member who came to receive the kids look at me and nod with a smile. Given that they recognize me, do you think they'd dare swindle those two kids out of their money?"

Shang Feifan: "You don't mind letting me know that you've been to Moro City and even know people at the Vocational School?"

"Why should I mind? Could it be you want to sell me out to someone?" Hu Bushuai asked, as if joking.

Shang Feifan wore a serious face: "I feel like you're probing me."

There was not a ripple of emotion in Hu Bushuai's eyes; he didn't even crack the faintest smile: "And what about you, Mr. Investigator? What is your true purpose? Even if you've lost your memory, staying away from Black Forest City for so long—aren't you afraid of being dismissed from your post?"

"Dismissed is dismissed. I lost most of my memories, especially concerning my work at the Investigation Bureau. I've even forgotten my own true identity; if it weren't for that bone tablet, I wouldn't even know I came from Black Forest City. If I went back under these circumstances, even if I weren't dismissed, I'd be suspended. Since that's the case, I might as well not go back." Shang Feifan bluffed, mixing nine parts falsehood with one part truth.

While harboring suspicions as to whether Shang Feifan had truly lost his memory, Hu Bushuai also guessed that his failure to recognize him as Raphael Langmu might be related to that amnesia.

Maybe this guy not only lost his memory, but his recollection was also a bit scrambled; otherwise, how could he utter such nonsense about him having a special relationship with Raphael?

Hu Bushuai completely failed to consider the possibility that he was being hit on; his life experiences from his past two lives, combined with the face he wore in this one, had firmly convinced him that he was a man of very little personal charm.

Even when others flirted with him verbally, he simply assumed they were joking around.

"Aren't you currently investigating the poisoning of the potion market and the two forced-suicide cases? Doing this counts as doing your job. When you return to Black Forest City, you can write an investigative report proving you weren't just wandering around outside."

"That's a good idea." Except that he wasn't Norman Hochel at all, making a return to report on his duties impossible. But as long as he didn't return to Black Forest City, he could continue masquerading under this identity.

"So, what clues have you managed to grasp by now?" Hu Bushuai stopped in his tracks.

Shang Feifan stopped alongside him: "The clue is that I know where the culprit who forced Frank to commit suicide is, and right now, we're heading in that direction. Coming along?"

Hu Bushuai licked his slightly dry lips: "Alright."

Suddenly feeling a bit thirsty himself, Shang Feifan unhooked his water flask from his belt and handed it over.

Hu Bushuai indicated that he had his own.

Shang Feifan knew he had one; he just wanted to share a flask with Hu Bushuai, but unfortunately, he was rejected.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第45章 赔偿金的用法 (Part 3)
chunks.chineseText:
不知在哪儿溜达一圈的狰爷哒哒哒地自己跑过来。这位就是自由虫，想来就来，想走就走，听不听老商召唤、什么时候响应召唤全看它狰大爷的心情。

商非凡邀请虎不帅共骑，这次虎不帅没有拒绝。

狰爷体型比一般巨虫要大一圈，负重也更厉害。再多一个虎不帅，对它的灵活度也没有多少影响。

商非凡追着诅咒之线，指挥狰爷跑了大半个城市，来到了第二街区。

虎不帅微皱眉：“这里是摩罗城贵族住的街区，你确定你要找的线索在这里？”

商非凡已经清楚看到诅咒之线伸入一栋大宅子中。

“你知道那栋宅子里住的是谁吗？”商非凡伸手一指。

虎不帅眼色微沉：“那是彘庞男爵的男爵府。”

嗐，这么快就要和boss对上了吗？商非凡同时想到，虎不帅对这里果然很熟悉。

“男爵权力很大吗？”商非凡以为男爵就是一个低级爵位。

虎不帅解释：“男爵这个爵位不高，彘庞男爵甚至只是一个二等男爵，连一等都不是。但他在摩罗城的地位很特殊，摩罗城的地皮属于他们家，他祖父曾是上一代虎王亲封的当地领主，爵位伯爵。

但彘庞祖父的爵位属于不世爵，连降等袭爵都不是，他祖父一死，他们家就没有了爵位。按理这里的封地也会被收回。可彘庞男爵的父亲是一名很厉害的炼药师，他还从某个遗迹中找到了一本炼药配方书，当代虎王为了留住这位有可能会成为大师的炼药师，就没有收回封地。

后来彘庞男爵的父亲成为了高级炼药师，虎王就给他封了子爵的爵位，一样是不世爵。但彘庞男爵的父亲拒绝了这个封赏，恳请虎王把爵位封给他的长子。虎王同意。

可谁也没想到就在封赏下来的当天，那位长子就突然得了急病去世。最后是那位高级炼药师的小儿子，也就是彘庞承袭了爵位，只不过子爵变成了男爵。”

商非凡挑眉：“听起来那位长子的死似乎另有隐情？”

“谁知道呢。作为父亲的高级炼药师没有深究这件事，其妻族也没有出头。也许跟这对兄弟娶了一对姐妹花有关。”虎不帅神色淡然。

商非凡调侃：“懂。兄长没了，还有弟弟有爵位，总能捞着一头。彘庞男爵的嫂子还活着吗？”

虎不帅：“……死了，据说在其丈夫死后半年，她就因为思念丈夫成疾，病死了。死时，她肚里的孩子都已经有七个半月。”

商非凡感叹：“王位面前无兄弟，这个彘庞男爵也是个狠人。”

虎不帅没有回应这句话，只说：“因为彘庞男爵的父亲对炼药师的庇护，以及彘庞男爵的操作，让摩罗城成了近百年来最有名的药城。而摩罗城虽然有名，占地也大，可在这里，男爵就是最高等的贵族。外地来的更高等贵族在彘庞男爵面前也不敢托大。同样，王城派下来的一些高级行政管理人员也得看彘庞男爵的脸色。”

“彘庞男爵的爵位也是不世爵？”商非凡问。

“对，所以他的长子一直在王城活动，想要让虎王给他封爵。最重要的是，希望能持续继承他们家的领地，也就是摩罗城。

去年，彘庞的长子彘圭似乎得到了某个明确承诺，就转回了摩罗城。

彘庞的小儿子彘献也不甘于将来只能做个普通富人，就也跑到了王城活动。目前，彘献似乎搭上了三王子的路。彘圭则和大王子走得很近……”

虎不帅把自己知道的关于彘庞男爵家的一些事情告诉了商非凡。

商非凡在心中嘀咕：虎不帅的身份绝对不简单，一个普通的贵族私生子可不会知道这么多事情。

“男爵府的守卫看起来很严。”商非凡就像是路过一样，不紧不慢地绕着男爵府走了大半圈。

男爵府的护卫盯了他们好几眼。

“你不会想就这么闯进去吧？那是找死。”虎不帅说得特别直白。

商非凡捏捏阿呆：“是得做些准备。”

“你发现的线索就在这里？”虎不帅低声问。

商非凡：“是啊，而且是位于后宅方位。”

虎不帅也不知道商非凡是哪里来的情报，竟然能把目标锁定到男爵府邸的后宅。

这个人奇奇怪怪的，也不知道拥有什么样的天赋能力。

“如果那几个案件都和男爵府有关，这事就得从长计议。”虎不帅首先得搞清楚，彘庞男爵牵扯进这几个案件中是否和他有关。

商非凡此时也在想，他被人诅咒，诅咒的人还跑到了男爵府邸中，会不会是彘庞男爵已经得到消息，知道是他拿走了内莉母亲传给她的神秘物品，才会特意让人教训他？

Lord Zheng, having completed a leisurely stroll somewhere nearby, came trotting back on its own. This creature was a true embodiment of free spirit—coming and going as it pleased, obeying or ignoring Old Shang’s summons entirely based on its mood.

Shang Feifan invited Hu Bushuai to ride together, and this time, Hu Bushuai didn’t refuse.

Lord Zheng’s frame was a notch larger than that of ordinary giant mounts, and its carrying capacity was far superior. Carrying one more person like Hu Bushuai had virtually no impact on its agility.

Following the trail of the curse line, Shang Feifan guided Lord Zheng across half the city, eventually arriving at the Second District.

Hu Bushuai creased his brows slightly. “This is the noble quarter of Moluo City. Are you certain the clue you’re looking for is here?”

Shang Feifan could clearly see the curse line extending directly into a grand, sprawling estate.

“Do you know who lives in that manor?” Shang Feifan asked, pointing a finger.

Hu Bushuai’s gaze darkened slightly. “That is the residence of Baron Zhipang.”

*Heh, are we confronting a boss this quickly?* Shang Feifan noted internally, realizing once more that Hu Bushuai was indeed remarkably familiar with this place.

“Does a baron hold substantial power here?” Shang Feifan had assumed a baron was merely a low-tier noble title.

Hu Bushuai explained, “The title of baron itself isn’t particularly high—Baron Zhipang is merely a second-class baron, not even a first-class one. However, his status in Moluo City is exceptionally unique. The very land of Moluo City belongs to his family. His grandfather was once the local lord granted fealty by the previous Tiger King, bearing the rank of Earl.

“However, his grandfather’s title was a non-hereditary one, not even eligible for reduced-rank inheritance. Thus, upon his grandfather’s death, the family lost their noble title, and by right, this fiefdom should have been reclaimed by the crown. But Baron Zhipang’s father happened to be a remarkably gifted apothecary who uncovered an ancient book of potion recipes from a ruined domain. To retain an apothecary who held the potential to become a grandmaster, the reigning Tiger King refrained from reclaiming the land.

“Later, when Baron Zhipang’s father successfully became a high-grade apothecary, the Tiger King bestowed upon him the title of Viscount—likewise non-hereditary. However, the father declined the honor for himself, begging the Tiger King to grant the title to his eldest son instead. The Tiger King agreed.

“Yet, no one anticipated that on the very day the decree arrived, that eldest son suddenly succumbed to a sudden, fatal illness. In the end, it was the high-grade apothecary’s younger son—Zhipang—who inherited the title, though the rank was downgraded from Viscount to Baron.”

Shang Feifan raised an eyebrow. “Sounds like there’s more to the eldest son’s death than meets the eye.”

“Who knows?” Hu Bushuai’s expression remained placid. “The father, despite being a high-grade apothecary, did not investigate the matter deeply, nor did his wife’s family press the issue. Perhaps it had something to do with the fact that both brothers had married a pair of sisters.”

Shang Feifan teased lightly, “Ah, I get it. The elder brother dies, but the younger brother retains the title—either way, the family keeps its grip on power. Is the elder brother’s widow still alive?”

Hu Bushuai: “...Dead. Supposedly, six months after her husband’s passing, she succumbed to a fatal illness born of grief over her loss. At the time of her death, she was seven and a half months pregnant.”

Shang Feifan sighed with genuine appreciation for the drama. “No brotherhood before the throne. This Baron Zhipang is quite a ruthless piece of work.”

Hu Bushuai didn’t comment on the statement, merely adding, “Thanks to the protection provided to apothecaries by Baron Zhipang’s father, coupled with Baron Zhipang’s own shrewd maneuvers, Moluo City has become the most famous potion hub in the region over the past century. Although Moluo City is renowned and covers a vast territory, the baron remains the highest-ranking noble residing here. Even higher-ranking nobles visiting from outside wouldn’t dare act arrogantly in front of Baron Zhipang. Likewise, high-level administrative officials dispatched from the Royal Capital must tread lightly around him.”

“Is Baron Zhipang’s title also non-hereditary?” Shang Feifan inquired.

“Correct. That is why his eldest son, Zhigui, has been actively networking in the Royal Capital, seeking to have the Tiger King confer a title upon him. Most importantly, he hopes to secure the continued inheritance of their family’s fiefdom—Moluo City itself.

“Last year, Zhigui seemed to secure a firm promise from someone influential, whereupon he returned to Moluo City.

“Meanwhile, Baron Zhipang’s younger son, Zhixian, refused to accept a future as a mere wealthy commoner, so he too headed to the Royal Capital to pull strings. Currently, Zhixian appears to have aligned himself with the Third Prince, whereas Zhigui maintains close ties with the First Prince...”

Hu Bushuai shared the details he possessed regarding Baron Zhipang’s household with Shang Feifan.

Shang Feifan mused internally: *Hu Bushuai’s background is definitely anything but simple. A mere ordinary noble illegitimate child wouldn’t know this much intimate detail.*

“The manor’s security looks remarkably tight,” Shang Feifan remarked casually, steering his mount as if merely passing by, making a leisurely half-circle around the estate.

The guards posted outside the baron’s residence shot sharp, vigilant glances toward them multiple times.

“You’re not thinking of barging straight in, are you? That would be suicide,” Hu Bushuai noted with blunt honesty.

Shang Feifan gave A'Dai a gentle squeeze. “Indeed, some preparation is in order.”

“The clue you discovered is right inside?” Hu Bushuai asked in a low voice.

Shang Feifan replied, “Yeah, and it’s located toward the inner residential quarters at the back.”

Hu Bushuai had no idea where Shang Feifan had gathered his intelligence, to the point of pinpointing the target down to the rear quarters of a baron’s estate.

This man was utterly enigmatic, leaving one to wonder what kind of innate talent or ability he actually possessed.

“If those cases are indeed tied to the baron’s estate, this matter requires careful, long-term planning,” Hu Bushuai noted. He first needed to figure out whether Baron Zhipang’s involvement in these cases had anything to do with himself.

Meanwhile, Shang Feifan was reflecting on his own situation: he had been targeted by a curse, and the practitioner had fled directly into the baron’s manor. Could it be that Baron Zhipang had already received word that he had taken the mysterious item Nelly’s mother passed down to her, and thus deliberately dispatched someone to teach him a lesson?

chunks.chineseText:
第46章 快递包裹

如何进入男爵府是个问题。

“如果彘庞男爵主动把凶手给赶出来就好了。”商非凡看着防守严密的男爵府喃喃。

“别想这种不可能的事情。就算男爵把凶手赶出来，也一定是扔出尸体，而不是扔出一个活人。”虎不帅现实地道。

商非凡也知道这个理，他就是随口说说……也不完全是随口，因为他推测那个凶手很可能遭到了反噬，虽然他不知道被反噬会是什么样子，但说不定男爵府的人会恐惧那人染上什么奇怪的病或者担心其他事情，而把人赶出府邸也不是不可能。

而没有万全把握，恐怕也没有人敢随意杀死一名咒术师。

商非凡心头忽然冒出一个新主意。

“走吧，我们继续待在这附近就要引起注意了。”

虎不帅表示他要和同伴交代之前发生的一系列事情，同时还需要继续购买所需药剂，总之就是要和商非凡分开行动。

商非凡：“你这么一说，我刚认识一个炼药师，他说可以帮忙从炼药师手上直接购药。我和他约好明天见面，如果你有需要……”

虎不帅迟疑：“会不会太麻烦？”

“不会。”商非凡豪爽地一摆手：“他欠我人情，巴不得能帮我做些事情。我想他会很高兴我这么快就让他把这份人情还了。”

“可是……”

“或者你能找到其他炼药师，拿到更好更便宜的药物？”商非凡突然逼近虎不帅。

虎不帅下意识身体后退，商非凡一把抓住他的手。

“小心！”

狰爷的背部也就那么大，虎不帅差点一脚踏空。

虎不帅重新站稳，“……谢谢。”

商非凡松开手，脸上带着笑容，语气却完全不容拒绝：“那就这么说定了，明天上午九点，我们在第五街南入口见面。”

虎不帅再次感受到商非凡强势的一面，这个人似乎总是有办法达成自己的目的，而不管别人是否愿意。

但这种强势，又不会让人心生反感，只会让人有点无可奈何的头疼。

虎不帅盘算了一下自己要做的事情和时间安排，再加上他也好奇商非凡到底是真失忆还是假失忆，想看看他接近自己到底有什么目的，最终还是同意第二天早上见面。

商非凡本来想把虎不帅一路送到他在第九街的住处，但虎不帅表示他还有一点私人事情要去办，离开第二街后就和商非凡告辞。

商非凡目送虎不帅背影消失在街道拐角，忽然说：“为什么没有与他相关的任务？”

脑载系统保持沉默。

窝在网兜里的阿呆抬头，用眼神问：爸爸你在说什么？

商非凡的直觉告诉他，虎不帅很可能是游戏中一个很重要的NPC。但古怪的是系统似乎一直没有发布与虎不帅直接相关的任务。

商非凡按下心中疑惑，在本城最热闹的第七街找了一家可以与巨虫坐骑同住的旅馆，定了一间客房，让阿呆和狰爷先待在客房里休息。

客房很大，房梁很高，狰爷走进来让房间一下变得狭窄不少，但它往房顶一挂，下方空间就空出来了。

商非凡伸手从雕像广场把他需要的东西掏出来，坐在桌子前开始对自己的脸进行新的塑造。

阿呆好奇地蹲在桌子上观看。

狰爷挂在房顶打瞌睡。

没多久，一个身材高大、戴着遮阳草帽的兽人从这家旅馆大门走出。

等拐过街道，高大的兽人摘下帽子换掉外衣混入人群，顿时就变成街道中讨生活的当地苦力兽人中的一员。

高大兽人蹲在一群等活干的苦力当中，一边跟他们聊天，一边把特意买来的麦饼分享了出去。没多会儿就和这些苦力混得像亲兄弟一样。

再过半个小时，高大兽人就经人介绍认识了当地专门做某些特殊手艺活的地头蛇，然后花了十银得到了一枚新的真身份骨牌。

该骨牌应该来源于某个没有登记死亡信息的流浪汉，但谁在乎这点呢，只要这枚骨牌能用就好。

“请问你们这里在招快递员吗？我看到你们门口有招聘的告示。”

“招招招！”正在忙碌的邮递员一看有人来应聘，还身材高大，看着特别结实有力，立刻眼睛发亮。

该邮递员像是怕人跑了一样，拉着高大兽人的手臂就往后面办公室领：“我们这儿日常缺人手，但活计简单，只要你手脚完好会认路，马上就能上手工作。你是想做长工，还是打短工？”

“先打短工，如果我能适应，报酬也还行，我就做长工。”高大兽人意外地腼腆老实。

“短工也没问题。对了，你有担保人吗？”

高大兽人摇头。

邮递员快速说：“没有也没事，登记下-身份信息，交保证金也可以。你懂的，因为我们不清楚你的底细，而你要送那么多快递。所以你需要先付一定的保证金。但你放心，只要你的快递件没问题，当你离职时，所有保证金全额退还。你什么时候可以开始工作？”

“呃，马上？”

“太好了！”

可能邮递局真的极为缺人手，高大兽人交了两银的保证金，就穿上快递员的制服，开始上岗工作。

邮递局还问他的兽形是什么，是否善于奔跑以及是否能负重。如果不能的话，他们会提供带拉车兽的车辆。

就是邮递局额外提供拉车兽，需要快递员另付租金。车辆免费。

“不需要拉车兽，我力气很大，只要有一辆车子，我可以拖着跑。”高大兽人展示了一下自己的力气。

于是，邮递局就很爽快地给新来的打工人配了一辆可以让兽人拖着跑的三轮车。

高大兽人先把邮局贴在墙上的全城地图扫描了一遍。

叮咚。

【摩罗城全地图更新成功，奖励1点贡献点。】

有了游戏的地图功能帮忙，把这些快递件送往指定地址就不再是什么难事，只是要花时间跑腿而已。

高大兽人还算敬业地先把车上快递件都送完，这才弄了几个新的包裹放在三轮车上，向男爵府奔去。

快速奔跑在石砖路上，高大兽人心想赚钱的门当来了，他也许可以在摩罗城推出自行车和脚踩三轮车。

到了男爵府正门口，被呵斥。

高大兽人这才知道人男爵府正门不收快递，更不会让他们这些苦力进入，他们得走后门。

后门同样有人把守。

但高大兽人没打算进去，他只是把车上的包裹放到后门口，告知守卫：“这是贵府的包裹，收件人名字都写在包裹上了。东西送到，麻烦你们签个名。”

“等等！这个包裹上写的什么？咒术师？哪个咒术师？”守卫看到包裹上的名字，立刻叫住快递员。

高大兽人一脸迷茫：“我不知道啊，我只负责送快递。”

两名守卫互看。

男爵府有规定，不明的邮件不能收，他们得先检查。

但是这邮件包裹上偏偏写着咒术师亲启的字样，这让他们……有点怂。

守卫们也不知道府邸里有没有咒术师，只能把事情先禀报上去。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 46: The Express Package

How to gain entry into the baron’s manor remained a thorny problem.

“It would be great if Baron Zhipang just kicked the killer out on his own initiative,” Shang Feifan muttered under his breath, staring at the heavily guarded estate.

“Stop dreaming about impossible scenarios. Even if the baron drove the culprit out, it would certainly be a corpse thrown out, not a living person,” Hu Bushuai countered realistically.

Shang Feifan knew the logic held sound. He had merely spoken off the cuff... though not entirely without reason. He deduced that the killer was likely suffering from a magical backlash. While he didn't know what that backlash looked like, it wasn't impossible that the baron's household might fear contracting some strange affliction or worry about complications, prompting them to expel the person from the estate.

Furthermore, without absolute certainty, hardly anyone would dare recklessly kill a curse master.

A novel idea suddenly sprouted in Shang Feifan’s mind.

“Let’s move along. Lingering around here much longer will draw unwanted attention.”

Hu Bushuai indicated that he needed to touch base with his companions regarding the recent chain of events, and that he still needed to purchase the required potions—in short, he intended to part ways with Shang Feifan for the time being.

Shang Feifan chimed in, “Speaking of which, I recently met an apothecary who mentioned he could help purchase potions directly from potion-makers. I made an appointment to meet him tomorrow morning. If you need anything...”

Hu Bushuai hesitated. “Wouldn’t that be too much trouble?”

“Not at all,” Shang Feifan waved a hand generously. “He owes me a favor and is practically begging for a chance to make it up to me. I’m sure he’ll be thrilled to clear that debt so quickly.”

“Still...”

“Or can you find another apothecary who can secure better and cheaper medicine?” Shang Feifan suddenly leaned in close to Hu Bushuai.

Startled, Hu Bushuai instinctively leaned backward, and Shang Feifan reached out to catch his hand.

“Careful!”

The back of Lord Zheng was only so wide, and Hu Bushuai had almost stepped off into midair.

Steadying himself, Hu Bushuai cleared his throat. “...Thank you.”

Releasing his grip, Shang Feifan flashed a warm smile, though his tone left zero room for refusal. “Then it’s a deal. Tomorrow morning at nine, we meet at the south entrance of the Fifth District.”

Once again, Hu Bushuai experienced Shang Feifan’s assertive side. This man always seemed to have a way of achieving his goals regardless of whether others agreed.

Yet, this overbearing manner didn't invite resentment; it merely left one feeling somewhat helpless and plagued by a mild headache.

Hu Bushuai mentally calculated his upcoming tasks and schedule. Coupled with his curiosity about whether Shang Feifan’s amnesia was genuine or feigned—and a desire to discern his true motives for approaching him—he ultimately agreed to the meeting the following morning.

Shang Feifan originally intended to escort Hu Bushuai all the way to his lodgings in the Ninth District, but Hu Bushuai mentioned he had a few personal errands to run, parting ways with him after leaving the Second District.

Watching Hu Bushuai’s silhouette disappear around the street corner, Shang Feifan suddenly asked out loud, “Why are there no system quests associated with him?”

The brain-hosted system maintained absolute silence.

A'Dai, snuggled inside the mesh carrier, raised his head and looked up with inquisitive eyes, silently asking: *Daddy, what are you talking about?*

Shang Feifan’s instincts told him that Hu Bushuai was very likely a major NPC within the game. Yet peculiarly, the system had failed to issue a single quest directly tied to him.

Suppressing the doubts in his heart, Shang Feifan headed to the bustling Seventh District—the liveliest quarter in town—and located an inn that permitted giant insect mounts to board alongside guests. He booked a room and instructed A'Dai and Lord Zheng to rest inside.

The room was vast, featuring exceptionally high ceiling beams. The moment Lord Zheng walked in, the space felt noticeably cramped, but once it hoisted itself up and suspended itself from the ceiling, the floor space opened right back up.

Reaching into his inventory to retrieve the items he had retrieved from the Sculpture Plaza, Shang Feifan sat before the desk and began crafting a new disguise for his face.

A'Dai crouched curiously on the tabletop, watching intently.

Lord Zheng dangled from the ceiling, dozing off.

Before long, a tall, burly beastman wearing a sun-shading straw hat stepped out through the inn’s main entrance.

Once he turned a couple of street corners, the tall beastman removed his hat, swapped his outer garments, and seamlessly blended into the crowd, instantly becoming indistinguishable from the local beastman laborers struggling for a living on the streets.

Squatting among a group of laborers waiting for work, the tall beastman chatted with them while sharing flatbreads he had specially purchased. Within moments, he was getting along with them like long-lost brothers.

Half an hour later, through a worker's introduction, the tall beastman met a local fixer specializing in "specialized craftsmanship." For the price of ten silver coins, he obtained a brand-new, valid identity bone token.

The bone token likely belonged to some vagrant whose death had gone unregistered, but who cared about such minor details? As long as the token functioned, it served its purpose.

***

“Excuse me, are you hiring couriers here? I noticed the recruitment notice posted at your door.”

“Yes, yes, we are!” A busy postal worker looked up to see an applicant who was tall, well-built, and exceptionally sturdy. His eyes immediately lit up.

Fearing the man might slip away, the postal worker grabbed the tall beastman’s arm and led him straight to the back office. “We’re constantly short-handed here, but the work is straightforward. As long as your limbs are intact and you can read street signs, you can start immediately. Are you looking for long-term employment or short-term gig work?”

“Short-term for now. If I adapt well and the pay is decent, I’ll stay on long-term,” the tall beastman replied with an unexpectedly bashful and honest demeanor.

“Short-term is totally fine! By the way, do you have a guarantor?”

The tall beastman shook his head.

The postal worker quickly added, “It’s fine if you don’t. Just register your identity information and pay a security deposit. You understand, since we don’t know your background and you’ll be handling so many express packages, you need to put down a small deposit first. But rest assured, as long as none of your deliveries go missing or get damaged, the deposit will be fully refunded when you resign. When can you start?”

“Uh... right now?”

“Wonderful!”

Perhaps the post office was truly desperate for help. After paying a security deposit of two silver coins, the tall beastman donned a courier's uniform and immediately began his shift.

The postal staff asked about his beast form, specifically whether he was good at running and capable of hauling heavy loads. If not, they could provide a cart equipped with a draft beast.

However, using an agency-provided draft beast required the courier to pay an extra rental fee, though the cart itself was free.

“No need for a draft beast. I’ve got plenty of strength—just give me a cart and I can pull it myself,” the tall beastman demonstrated his physical prowess.

Thus, the post office readily provided the new hire with a sturdy tricycle designed to be pulled by a beastman.

The tall beastman first scanned the full city map posted on the post office wall.

*Ding!*

【Moluo City Complete Map successfully updated. Reward: 1 Contribution Point.】

With the assistance of the game’s map interface, delivering packages to specific addresses was no longer a difficult task—it merely required time and legwork.

The tall beastman dutifully delivered all the parcels loaded onto his cart before placing several new packages onto his tricycle and making a beeline toward the baron’s manor.

Sprinting swiftly across the stone-paved streets, the tall beastman mused to himself that a business opportunity had presented itself—perhaps he could introduce bicycles and foot-pedaled tricycles to Moluo City.

Upon arriving at the front gate of the baron’s residence, he was promptly barked at by the guards.

Only then did the tall beastman learn that the main entrance of the baron’s estate did not accept deliveries, nor were laborers like him allowed inside. They were required to use the back gate.

The back gate was similarly guarded.

However, the tall beastman had no intention of going inside. He simply unloaded the parcels onto the ground by the back entrance and informed the guards, “These are packages for your esteemed estate. The recipient’s name is clearly written on the labels. Now that the goods are delivered, please sign for them.”

“Hold on! What’s written on this package? 'Curse Master'? Which Curse Master?!” Seeing the name written on the label, a guard instantly called out to stop the courier.

The tall beastman put on a look of utter cluelessness. “I have no idea. I’m just responsible for delivering the mail.”

The two guards exchanged glances.

Regulations within the baron’s manor stipulated that unidentified mail could not be accepted without prior inspection.

Yet this particular package explicitly bore the words *To Be Opened Personally by the Curse Master*, which made them... somewhat terrified.

Unsure whether a curse master actually resided within the manor, the guards had no choice but to report the matter to their superiors first.

chunks.chineseText:
守卫们还叫住快递员，不让他走。

高大兽人小声骂骂咧咧，但最后还是一副畏于权势的模样，在男爵府后门口蹲下等待。

一名像是管事的兽人走出来。

他没有打开包裹，而是先质问快递员：“这个包裹是谁让你送来的？”

高大兽人一脸呆样：“就是邮局让我送的。”

“我是问这个包裹上为什么没有送件人的姓名和地址？”管事耐着性子又问。

高大兽人抓头：“这我哪知道。你得问我们邮局的办事人员。”

管事噎住，瞪高大兽人。

高大兽人还咕哝说：“我能走了吗？我还有几件没送完呢。如果今天送不完，我就拿不到工资了。”

管事：“……你给我老实等着！不让你走，你就不准走。”

管事拿起那个包裹，脚步匆匆地走入府邸内部。

那个包裹经过几个人的手，最后还是完好地放在了大管家面前。

大管家眉头紧皱，他是男爵的心腹，自然知道男爵府里都藏着什么人。

不过咒术师绝不会堂而皇之地告诉别人他是咒术师，雇佣咒术师的人也绝不会把这点告诉别人。

所以大管家只能猜测。

他心中很快就想到了一个最可能的人选，打算把这个包裹送去给那个人。

他总不能为了一个莫名其妙的包裹跑去问男爵——我们府有一个咒术师吗？他是谁？

脸色苍白的兽人看着被送到他面前的包裹，眼神阴沉地没有说话。

大管家暗中吞咽了一口口水，他昨天还见过这个人，那时这位虽然也很阴冷，但不至于像现在这么……不过一天没见，这个人看起来已经瘦脱形，面容跟骷髅一样，连头发都变得稀疏。

这人肯定是咒术师，只有咒术师才会这么诡异又可怕，还丑陋！

“日安，阁下。您觉得这个包裹是送给您的吗？”大管家有些小心翼翼地问。

卢希恩抬起头，阴沉沉地：“送这个包裹的人在哪里？”

他的身份在这座府邸里应该没人知道才对。

唯一知道他真实身份的就是彘庞男爵，可他绝不会给自己寄送这么一个包裹。

管家……也只是有所猜测，同样不会干这样的蠢事。

那么会给他寄送包裹，还敢在包裹上大咧咧地写着咒术师亲启字样的人……

想到他受到的反噬，卢希恩再看这个包裹，眼睛都要滴血。

大管家：“他只是一名普通的邮递人员，就在府邸后门口。”

卢希恩喝令：“带他来见我。”

大管家心中不快，这人虽然是男爵大人交代要好好敬着的贵客，但对他用这种命令口吻，是否有点自恃过高？

可一想到包裹上写着的“咒术师”，大管家决定还是不要惹这位贵客不愉快为好。

蹲在门口等待的高大兽人听管事说要他进入府邸回话，特别不情愿。

管事瞪，用力瞪：“快点跟我过来！别磨蹭。”

高大兽人只好跟着管事进入府邸，进去前还再三请后门口的守卫帮他看好他的车子和车上的包裹。

守卫们：“……”哪里来的夯货！

进入府邸后，高大兽人好奇地东瞅西看。

管事不高兴：“不要乱看！给我老实点！”

高大兽人长长的哦了一声，仍旧转着脖子看个不停。

管事气死，走得特别快。

绕过一个又一个院子，管事在一个看起来很精致的小院门口停下。

“你自己进去。进去后不要乱看，也不要乱说话。”管事懒得跟这个没有见识又傻大胆的夯货说话，直接伸手就把人推进了小院大门。

大管家不在，里面只有一名脸色苍白、形容像骷髅的兽人。

高大兽人傻愣愣地看着坐在院子中的兽人，还对他抬手打了个招呼：“日安，先生。就是你找我吗？”

卢希恩打量这个高大兽人，怎么看都像一个底层苦力，还一脸蠢相。

“这个包裹是谁让你送来的？”阴沉沉的嗓音。

高大兽人翻了个白眼：“你们怎么老是问我同样的问题。我不是已经说了，这就是邮局让我送的。”

“所以你也不知道寄件人是谁。”

“不知道。”高大兽人硬邦邦地说，转而又问：“我可以走了吗？我还有活没……”

“你过来。”卢希恩喝令：“过来拆开这个包裹。”

高大兽人不高兴：“这又不是我的包裹，邮局要求我们不能拆开客人的包裹，否则会扣除我的工资和保证金。”

“我身体不好，不方便动手。你过来把包裹拆开，我会给你酬劳。”卢希恩并不想拆开一个有可能是能让他反噬的人寄来的包裹。

高大兽人眼睛一亮：“你给我报酬？给我多少？”

卢希恩手一扬，说是不方便动手的他，却抛出了一枚银达鲁。

高大兽人毫不嫌弃地弯腰捡起那枚银达鲁，吹了吹，看清面额：“才一银？”

卢希恩神情厌厌：“你想要多少。”

高大兽人脸上露出贪婪神情：“最少十个、不，一百个银达鲁，我就帮你拆。”

卢希恩怀疑自己的耳朵，一百银对他是不多，但只是拆一个包裹就要他一百银？这个苦力干一个月能不能拿到十银都是问题。

高大兽人一脸殷切地看着卢希恩。

为了见这么一面，他花了多少成本？不赚回来怎么行！

卢希恩现在看这个高大兽人就跟看死人一样，他已经决定，等这个蠢货拆开包裹，不管他有什么变化，他都不会让对方活着走出这个院子。

正好他现在极为需要补充生命能量。

而这个蠢货看起来就是一个上佳祭品。

卢希恩等了一会儿，见高大兽人没动，忍不住喝：“还不过来把包裹拆开。”

高大兽人伸出手，掂了掂。

卢希恩甩手就扔出一个钱袋，差点砸到高大兽人的脸上。

高大兽人一把接住，喜滋滋地打开，还把袋子里面的钱币数了一遍，发现只多不少，当即笑开花。

“这位尊贵的先生，我这就给您把包裹拆开。”

高大兽人欢喜地搓着手上前，一把抓住卢希恩的脖子，用力掐紧。

卢希恩眼睛瞪直，不可置信，当即就施展咒术反击。

别以为他说不出话就不能反击，身为一名咒术师怎么可能被人制住就没有反抗的能力？

见鬼！为什么这个兽人还不倒下？为什么他的咒术没有用！

高大兽人单手把他举了起来。

卢希恩想要喊人，但他什么都喊不出来。

因为他职业特殊，他身边也没有安排侍候的人，门口更没有人敢随便停留。

卢希恩挣扎。

突然，大量的黑点从他鼻孔、耳孔和其他孔窍里冒出。
chunks.englishText:
The guards even stopped the deliveryman and refused to let him leave.

The tall beastman muttered and cursed under his breath, but eventually put on a subservient look of being intimidated by power, crouching down by the back gate of the baron’s estate to wait.

An orc who looked like a steward walked out.

Instead of opening the parcel, he first interrogated the deliveryman, "Who made you deliver this package?"

The tall beastman wore a blank look. "The post office just told me to deliver it."

"I'm asking you why there is no sender's name and address on this parcel?" the steward asked, trying his best to keep his patience.

The tall beastman scratched his head. "How would I know that? You'll have to ask our post office staff."

The steward choked, glaring at the tall beastman.

The tall beastman continued to mumble, "Can I leave now? I still have a few deliveries left. If I can't finish them today, I won't get my pay."

The steward: "...You just honestly stay right here! You are not allowed to leave until I say so."

The steward picked up the parcel and strode hurriedly into the interior of the estate.

After passing through several hands, the package finally landed intact before the head steward.

The head steward furrowed his brows. As the baron's confidant, he naturally knew what kind of people were hiding within the baron's estate.

However, a spellcaster would never openly and blatantly tell others that they were a spellcaster, and someone who hired a spellcaster would never reveal that fact to others either.

Therefore, the head steward could only guess.

A most likely candidate quickly came to mind, and he intended to have this package delivered to that person.

He couldn't possibly run up to the baron over some inexplicable parcel and ask—*Do we have a spellcaster in our estate? Who are they?*

The pale-faced beastman looked at the parcel delivered to him, his gaze gloomy and silent.

The head steward secretly swallowed a mouthful of saliva. He had seen this person just yesterday; back then, although this individual was also chillingly cold, he wasn't quite as... Yet after just a single day, this person looked sunken to the bone, his face resembling a skeleton, and even his hair had grown sparse.

This man was definitely a spellcaster. Only a spellcaster could be so bizarre, terrifying, and ugly!

"Good day, Your Excellency. Do you think this parcel was sent to you?" the head steward asked with cautious care.

Lucian raised his head, his voice gloomy. "Where is the person who delivered this package?"

His identity within this estate should be known to no one.

The only one who knew his true identity was Baron Zhipang, but he would never send him a package like this.

The steward... had only made a guess, and similarly would not do such a foolish thing.

So, who could possibly send him a package, and dare to brazenly write *'To be opened by the spellcaster in person'* right on it?

Thinking of the backlash he had suffered, Lucian felt his eyes drip with blood as he looked at the package again.

The head steward: "He is just an ordinary deliveryman, right outside the back gate of the estate."

Lucian ordered, "Bring him to see me."

Displeasure stirred in the head steward's heart. Although this man was an honored guest whom Lord Baron had instructed them to treat with utmost respect, wasn't he being a bit too self-important by using such a commanding tone with him?

Yet, at the thought of the word "spellcaster" written on the parcel, the head steward decided it was better not to displease this esteemed guest.

The tall beastman, crouching by the gate waiting, was extremely reluctant when the steward told him to enter the estate and answer some questions.

The steward glared, staring hard at him. "Come with me right now! Don't drag your feet."

The tall beastman had no choice but to follow the steward into the estate, though before entering, he repeatedly asked the guards at the back gate to watch his cart and the packages on it for him.

The guards: "..." Where did this blockhead come from!

Upon entering the estate, the tall beastman looked around curiously, casting glances left and right.

The steward was displeased. "Stop looking around! Behave yourself!"

The tall beastman let out a long "Oh," but still kept turning his neck to stare endlessly.

Furious, the steward walked at a brisk pace.

Bypassing courtyard after courtyard, the steward stopped before the entrance of a seemingly exquisite little courtyard.

"Go in by yourself. Once inside, don't look around blindly, and don't speak nonsense." Too lazy to converse with this ignorant and foolishly bold blockhead, the steward directly reached out and pushed the man through the courtyard gates.

The head steward was absent; inside was only a pale-faced beastman whose appearance resembled a skeleton.

The tall beastman looked in a daze at the beastman sitting in the courtyard, and even raised a hand to greet him, "Good day, mister. Were you the one looking for me?"

Lucian sized up this tall beastman. No matter how he looked, he seemed like a bottom-tier laborer, and a foolish-looking one at that.

"Who made you deliver this package?" A gloomy voice rasped.

The tall beastman rolled his eyes. "Why do you guys keep asking me the same question? Didn't I already say, the post office told me to deliver it."

"So you don't know who the sender is either."

"I don't," the tall beastman said stiffly, then asked in turn, "Can I go now? I still have work..."

"Come here," Lucian ordered. "Come over here and open this package."

The tall beastman was displeased. "This isn't my parcel. The post office requires that we aren't allowed to open customers' packages, otherwise they'll dock my pay and deposit."

"I am in poor health and it is inconvenient for me to move. Come over here and unpack the parcel, and I will reward you." Lucian had no desire to unwrap a package that might have been sent by someone capable of backlash.

The tall beastman's eyes lit up. "You'll pay me? How much?"

Lucian flicked his hand, and despite claiming it was inconvenient to move, he tossed out a silver daru.

Without a shred of disdain, the tall beastman bent down to pick up the silver daru, blew on it, and checked its denomination. "Only one silver coin?"

Lucian's expression was weary. "How much do you want?"

A greedy look appeared on the tall beastman's face. "At least ten—no, one hundred silver darus, and I'll open it for you."

Lucian doubted his own ears. One hundred silver wasn't much to him, but he wanted a hundred silver just to open a package? It was a question whether this laborer could even make ten silver in a full month.

The tall beastman looked at Lucian with eager anticipation.

How much did it cost him just to get this meeting? If he didn't make a profit, how would that do?

Lucian now looked at this tall beastman as if looking at a dead man. He had already decided that once this fool opened the parcel, regardless of any changes that might occur, he would not let this fellow leave the courtyard alive.

It just so happened that he currently had an extreme need to replenish his life energy.

And this fool looked like a prime sacrifice.

After waiting for a moment and seeing that the tall beastman hadn't moved, Lucian couldn't help but snap, "Still not coming over to unpack the parcel?"

The tall beastman reached out his hand and weighed it in his palm.

With a flick of his wrist, Lucian threw out a purse of coins, which nearly smacked the tall beastman right in the face.

The tall beastman grabbed it, opened it cheerfully, and even counted the coins inside, finding that there were only more than expected, which immediately made him beam with delight.

"Respected sir, I'll unpack the parcel for you right away."

Joyfully rubbing his hands together, the tall beastman stepped forward, grabbed Lucian by the neck, and squeezed tight with all his might.

Lucian's eyes bulged in disbelief, and he immediately cast a spell to counterattack.

Just because he couldn't speak didn't mean he couldn't fight back; as a spellcaster, how could he possibly lose the ability to resist just because he was restrained?

*What the hell?! Why hasn't this beastman collapsed yet? Why isn't his spell working?!*

The tall beastman lifted him up with a single hand.

Lucian wanted to shout for help, but not a single sound came out.

Because of his peculiar profession, he had no attendants arranged around him, and no one dared to linger casually near his door.

Lucian struggled.

Suddenly, a massive swarm of black dots emerged from his nostrils, ear canals, and other facial orifices.

chunks.chineseText:
第47章 拿到口供

这些黑点疯狂往高大兽人爬去，想要钻入他的身体。

但它们似乎受到了某种阻碍，无法钻进去。

咒术师遇到了诅咒祭司，现在就看谁的咒力更强。

高大兽人一脸嫌弃：“草，这些是什么鬼东西？虫子？”

右眼突然跳出提示：【遇到虫咒，消灭还是吞噬？吞噬有一定可能遭到操纵者的反噬，但如果能完全吞噬吸收，你的咒术将会得到提升。】

“消灭要怎么消灭？”

【请信徒自己解决。】右眼表示它只负责提示。

高大兽人迅速翻阅脑中刚学到没多久的诅咒知识，根据关键词找到虫咒。

虫咒简单说就是捕捉一大堆虫子，对它们进行惨无虫道地折磨，同时给它们提供能量，让它们死都没办法死，提升它们的怨念和疯狂，打磨它们的神智，最后利用秘术操纵这些虫子攻击被诅咒者。

虫咒非常难以解除，因为它们是一群，不是一只。

同样，当它们以实体出现时也难以消灭，因为它们的状态既不是生也不是死。

高大兽人脑子飞速转动。

受到折磨死不了也活不了是吧？

想要报复控制你们的人也报复不了只能发泄在他人身上是吧？

那么如果我能吸收你们身上的所有怨气，放你们自由，让你们可以反噬操控你们的人，觉得如何？

高大兽人一边掐紧卢希恩的脖子，让他双眼充血呼吸不畅挣扎越来越小，一边主动吸收那些虫子和卢希恩身上聚集的怨气。

能够转移身上的怨气，这对普通兽人来说是一件好事。

但对咒术师来说就相反了，他们需要怨气来施展咒术，更需要怨气来保护自己。

高大兽人看到怨气离开卢希恩后，卢希恩的反应，若有所思。他似乎知道他的身体为什么会主动吸收怨气了。

但高大兽人现在还不知道，并不是所有黑暗类施法者都能主动吸收怨气，他是特殊情况。

失去怨气，卢希恩就像是失去了一层强大的防护罩，原本他还能在高大兽人手下微微挣扎，可现在高大兽人都要担心会不会一个用劲掐断他的脖子。

高大兽人忽然把卢希恩丢到地上。

卢希恩翻身想跑。

高大兽人一脚踹在他的后脑勺上。

卢希恩眼睛一翻，昏死过去。

高大兽人弹出锋利的爪尖，划破卢希恩的手腕，取其鲜血在地上绘制咒术阵。

绘制好阵法，直接就把卢希恩丢到献祭位。

“至高伟大的存在，诅咒之神科尼泽厄斯，您的信徒正在向您献上祭品，他的咒术来源于您，现在也将归还于您……”

昏迷中的卢希恩突然发出了凄厉的惨叫声，硬是被疼醒了过来。

附近听到惨叫的人身体下意识抖了抖，有人想要过来查看，但转而就想到了大管家刚才让人下达的命令。

据说某位贵客正在办事，不管听到什么动静，都不得靠近那位贵客的院子。

这也是那位贵客的叮嘱。

卢希恩哪里想到自己的命令竟然成了阻拦自己得救的最大障碍。

他也完全没想到送包裹的兽人会这么大胆，竟然在男爵府邸内就直接对他动手。

最主要的是他就没想到有人敢当面对付一名咒术师，就算那人是他的同行。

卢希恩身上冒出来的黑点不再向高大兽人身上攀爬，而是全都反向爬回他的身体、钻入他的身体内部。

高大兽人随手从卢希恩身上撕下一块布料塞住他的嘴。

卢希恩在地上疯狂翻滚挣扎，他操控的无数虫子在噬咬他！

他的咒术失灵了，这些虫子都不再听他的操控。

这种反噬比他咒术失败的反噬要可怕得多，他会死……

高大兽人一脚踩住卢希恩的脖子，弯下腰：“我知道你能听见。回答我的问题，我可以让你死得痛快一点。”

卢希恩拒绝回答任何问题，他恨死了这个高大兽人。

可被千万虫子啃食的痛苦让他逐渐失去理智。

实在太痛苦了！

是人都无法忍受！

“第一个问题，为什么要逼迫治安员弗兰克饮毒自杀？”高大兽人扯出卢希恩嘴里的布巾。

“杀……了……我……啊……唔！”嘴巴再次被堵住。

“我的耐心很好。而你看起来短时间内也不会立刻死亡，你这里恐怕也没有什么人过来，对吗？那就让我们看看你能熬多久。”高大兽人早就做好有人来查看的准备。

如果有人来查看，能混过去最好，不能，他就彻底解决这个咒术师，再在男爵府邸内放把火，搞出混乱后想法离开。

虽然这样做会得不到口供，但至少能让他出口气。

两个小时后，天色已经黑透，男爵府各处都点亮了油肚虫灯。

只有卢希恩住的小院仍旧一片黑暗。

过了一会儿，有人拉开紧闭的大门从小院出来，刚打开门就看到之前的管事被惊动地往后急退的样子。

这位管事刚刚正贴在门上听院子里的动静，没想到有人会突然开门。

看到高大兽人完好无损地出来，管事提着灯，眼睛睁大：“你、你……”还活着？

他以为他需要过来处理尸体。

高大兽人憨憨的，脸也红红的，似乎很不好意思，避开管事的眼睛，说：“是我。里面那位高贵的先生他累了，让人不要打扰他。”

管事：累了？什么意思？

管事忍不住问：“这么长时间，你待在里面干什么了？”

高大兽人越发不好意思，声音也变小，还有点扭扭捏捏：“你、你别问了，这种事不好说。不过以后如果那位高贵的先生还有需要，再叫我过来就是。我、我不要钱也可以的。”

管事眼睛瞪得溜圆：草！不会是我想的那样吧？

高大兽人的大手羞涩地提了提裤腰带，还特意拢了拢身上的工作服，似乎就怕被人看出来他刚才干了什么。

管事重新打量面前的兽人，不得不承认这人身材是真不错，有料！虽然黑了点，五官长得也还行。

“……走吧，我送你出去。”

高大兽人一路被送到男爵府后门口，发现自己的三轮车和车上包裹还在，他很高兴地对门口守卫挥手道谢，拖着车子高高兴兴地离开了。

管事回去把事情禀告给大管家。

大管家听到管事的猜测，神色淡定，脸上不见半点惊讶。

贵族有多荒淫-糜烂，他是知道的。那位咒术师大人也许只是需要补充一点能量，嗯，就是那种能量，这也是有可能的。

也就那个送包裹的苦力还以为自己占到了莫大便宜，说不定过几天就会突然变得皮包骨头，甚至直接死于非命。

大管家现在反倒感谢那位咒术师大人没有在男爵府里搜刮，而是找了一个外面的兽人。

直到第二天，负责给卢希恩送饭的仆役打开虚掩的院门，发现院子的主人不在，他试着大声询问，也没有听到院子主人的回应。

仆役不敢进入内屋查看，就出来把事情告诉管事。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 47: Securing the Confession

These black dots crawled frantically toward the tall beastman, attempting to burrow into his body.

However, they seemed to encounter some sort of barrier, unable to pierce through.

A warlock had run into a curse priest; now it all came down to whose curse power was stronger.

The tall beastman wore a look of utter disgust. "Damn it, what are these creepy-crawlies? Bugs?"

A prompt suddenly flashed in his right eye: [Insect Curse detected. Exterminate or devour? Devouring carries a certain risk of a backlash from the controller, but if completely devoured and absorbed, your spellcraft will be enhanced.]

"How do I exterminate them?"

[Please resolve this yourself, believer.] The right eye indicated it was only responsible for prompts.

The tall beastman rapidly flipped through the cursing knowledge he had learned not long ago, locating the entry for "Insect Curse" via keywords.

Simply put, an Insect Curse involved capturing a massive horde of bugs, subjecting them to unimaginably cruel torture while providing them with a trickle of energy so they couldn't even die. This magnified their resentment and madness, honed their consciousness, and finally utilized esoteric arts to manipulate these insects to attack the cursed target.

Insect Curses were notoriously difficult to dispel because they came as a swarm, not a single entity.

Likewise, when they manifested physically, they were exceedingly hard to eradicate because their state hovered somewhere between life and death.

The tall beastman's brain spun at lightning speed.

*Tortured to the point where they can neither live nor die, right?*

*Burning with a desire for revenge against the one controlling you, yet unable to exact it, leaving you no choice but to vent it on others, right?*

*Then how about this—if I absorb all the resentment from your bodies, set you free, and let you backlash against the one who manipulated you, how does that sound?*

While tightening his grip on Lucian's throat—causing the man's eyes to bloodshot, his breath to fail, and his struggles to grow increasingly weak—the tall beastman actively absorbed the bugs and the gathered resentment clinging to Lucian.

Being able to purge resentment from one's body was a blessing for an ordinary beastman.

For a warlock, however, the opposite was true; they required resentment to cast spellcraft, and even more so to protect themselves.

Seeing Lucian's reaction after the resentment drained away, the tall beastman grew thoughtful. He finally seemed to understand why his body had been actively absorbing resentment in the first place.

Yet the tall beastman did not yet know that not all dark-path spellcasters could actively absorb resentment; his case was a special anomaly.

Losing his resentment was like losing a powerful protective shield. Previously, Lucian could still manage a feeble struggle under the tall beastman's grip, but now the tall beastman actually had to worry about accidentally snapping his neck with too much force.

Abruptly, the tall beastman tossed Lucian onto the ground.

Lucian rolled over, attempting to flee.

With a swift kick, the tall beastman planted his boot squarely on the back of Lucian's head.

Lucian's eyes rolled back, and he passed out cold.

Extending his sharp, razor-like claws, the tall beastman slit Lucian's wrist and used his fresh blood to draw a curse array directly on the ground.

Once the formation was drawn, he dumped Lucian right into the sacrificial position.

"Supreme and magnificent existence, God of Curses Coconizeus, your believer is offering a sacrifice. His spellcraft originated from you, and now it shall be returned to you..."

The unconscious Lucian suddenly let out a piercing, miserable scream, jolted ruthlessly awake by the agony.

Nearby residents who heard the shriek involuntarily shuddered. A few wanted to come over and investigate, but they immediately recalled the stern orders the head butler had relayed earlier.

It was said that a certain esteemed guest was busy attending to matters; regardless of what sounds were heard, no one was permitted to approach that guest's courtyard.

This had also been the honored guest's explicit instruction.

Little did Lucian imagine that his own order would become the greatest obstacle preventing his rescue.

Nor did he ever expect that the delivery beastman would be so audacious as to make a direct move on him right inside the baron's estate.

Above all, he had never dreamed anyone would dare confront a warlock face-to-face, even if that person was a peer in the craft.

The black dots emerging from Lucian's body no longer swarmed toward the tall beastman; instead, they reversed course, crawling frantically back and burrowing deep inside his flesh.

Casually tearing off a piece of fabric from Lucian's clothes, the tall beastman stuffed it into his mouth to gag him.

Lucian rolled and thrashed wildly on the floor—the countless bugs he once controlled were now devouring him alive!

His spellcraft had failed; these insects no longer heeded his commands.

This backlash was far more terrifying than the backlash of a failed curse; he was going to die...

Stepping on Lucian's neck with one foot, the tall beastman bent down. "I know you can hear me. Answer my questions, and I'll give you a quick death."

Lucian refused to answer anything, hating this tall beastman with every fiber of his being.

Yet the torment of being chewed upon by ten thousand insects gradually eroded his sanity.

The agony was simply too intense!

No human could possibly endure it!

"First question, why did you force Constable Frank to drink poison and commit suicide?" The tall beastman pulled the cloth gag out of Lucian's mouth.

"Kill... me... ah... mmph!" His mouth was stuffed right back up.

"I have immense patience. And you don't look like you're going to die immediately. Besides, nobody really comes around this place of yours, do they? Let's just see how long you can hold out." The tall beastman had prepared himself for someone coming to investigate.

If someone came to check, bluffing his way through would be best; if not, he would thoroughly deal with this warlock, set fire to the baron's estate to create chaos, and figure out a way to slip away.

Though doing so meant forfeiting the confession, at least it would let him vent his anger.

Two hours later, night had completely fallen, and oil-belly worm lamps had been lit across every corner of the baron's estate.

Only the small courtyard where Lucian resided remained pitch black.

After a while, someone slid open the tightly shut courtyard doors and stepped outside, only to find the previous steward recoiling in shock as he was startled.

The steward had just been pressing his ear against the door to listen to the commotion inside, never expecting someone to suddenly push it open.

Seeing the tall beastman emerge unscathed, the steward held his lantern aloft, his eyes widening. "Y-You..." *Still alive?*

He had assumed he would need to come over to dispose of a corpse.

The tall beastman put on a naive, blushing expression, looking thoroughly embarrassed as he avoided the steward's gaze. "It's just me. The esteemed gentleman inside got tired and asked not to be disturbed."

The steward: *Tired? What's that supposed to mean?*

Unable to contain his curiosity, the steward asked, "You spent all this time in there—what were you doing?"

The tall beastman grew even more bashful, his voice dropping lower with a coy, twisting posture. "D-Don't ask about that, it's not the sort of thing you talk about. But if that esteemed gentleman has any more need for me in the future, just call me over again. I—I don't even need money."

The steward's eyes bulged into perfect circles: *Damn it! It couldn't be what I'm thinking, could it?!*

The tall beastman's large hand shyly hitched up his waistband, deliberately smoothing down his work uniform as if terrified someone might guess what he had just been up to.

Reassessing the beastman before him, the steward had to admit the fellow's physique was genuinely impressive—he was well-built! Even if a bit dark-skinned, his facial features weren't half bad either.

"...Let's go, I'll see you out."

Escorted all the way to the back gate of the baron's estate, the tall beastman was delighted to find his tricycle and the packages still sitting there. He waved cheerfully at the guards in gratitude, hauling his cart away in high spirits.

Returning to headquarters, the steward reported the matter to the head butler.

Hearing the steward's speculations, the head butler remained calm, not a trace of surprise crossing his face.

He knew all too well how dissolute and decadent nobles could be. Perhaps that warlock lord simply needed to replenish a bit of energy—yes, *that* kind of energy—which was entirely plausible.

As for that delivery laborer, he probably thought he had struck gold, oblivious to the fact that within a few days he might suddenly turn into a bag of bones or even drop dead of unnatural causes.

Instead, the head butler was now grateful that the warlock lord hadn't gone on a rampage pillaging within the estate, choosing instead to pick some outsider beastman.

It wasn't until the following day that the servant responsible for delivering Lucian's meals pushed open the ajar courtyard gate, discovering that the master of the house was nowhere to be seen. He tried calling out loudly, yet received no response from within.

Not daring to step inside the inner chambers to investigate, the servant hurried out to report the matter to the steward.

chunks.chineseText:
管事猜测那位贵客会不会只是悄悄出门办事，就没有立刻去查看。

等到晚上，仆役再次去送饭，发现自己早上和中午送去的饭食还好好地放在桌子上。

管事得知消息，想到昨天那个快递兽人，心里总觉得有哪里不得劲，终于带人过去查看情况。

贵客卢希恩并不在他住的小院内，哪里都找不到他的人影。

等到次日，这位也没有露面。

管事只好把事情报给大管家知道。

大管家再次带人去查看，发现那位贵客的换洗衣服等基本都还在，但一些贵重物品似乎都消失了，包括钱袋。

贵客到底是自己离开，还是遇到了什么事情？

大管家没有在小院内发现任何痕迹，只好把事情禀报给男爵府的主人。

彘庞男爵挑眉。卢希恩离开，不可能不告诉他。

“他已经消失多久？”

“两天两夜。”大管家低着头回答。

“消失前，他见了谁？”

“一个送快递的兽人。”

“快递？”

“事情是这样的，两天前的下午，一名快递人员送了一个包裹，包裹上写着‘咒术师亲启’的字样……”

彘庞男爵听完，思索片刻：“去查那个快递员，找到他，把他带回来。”

“是。”

时间倒回到两天前。

高大兽人回到邮局，找到值班的工作人员，把三轮车和工作服都还给了邮局。

“你就干了半天就不干啦？”值班人员很惊讶，也有点无奈和生气。

高大兽人兴奋地说：“我今天运气好，送包裹的时候遇到一位贵人，他让我以后跟着他，一个月给我一百银！”

“哇！你运气真好。”值班兽人妒忌了。一百银啊，他们局长一个月都拿不到这么多。

高大兽人太高兴了，值班兽人让他五天后来找负责的管事拿抵押的保证金——只要这五天内没有人投诉，他也只是挥挥手就跑了。

高大兽人离开邮局，七转八转，等他从一条巷子里走出来，身上的衣服鞋袜都换了，样貌也变了。

商非凡回到旅馆，阿呆都等睡着了，听到动静一骨碌爬起来。

“吃过了吗？”商非凡揉揉小幼崽的脑袋。

阿呆指了指桌子上的干粮和水。

商非凡：“今天委屈你了，明天带你吃好的。”

“爸爸，你去干什么了？你看起来有点高兴，也有点不高兴。”阿呆仰着头问。

商非凡往浴室走：“去解了一些疑惑，搞明白了一些事情。另外还得了一些意外之财。”

阿呆一口道破：“爸爸，你黑吃黑了吗？”

他们在旅途中的两个月可是遇到好几次打劫，打不过的，他们就想法跑掉。打得过的，老商就反过头来把打劫者打劫一遍，那手法那利落劲比职业打劫者还要职业。

“投资比较大，只能想办法回本再加一点利息。再说被动挨揍可不是咱兽人的美德。”商非凡施施然地带上浴室门。

阿呆歪头。

狰爷也就是不会说兽语，否则它一定要说：完了，这孩子被教歪了。

晚上，商非凡躺到旅馆床上，安然入睡。

阿呆就窝在他身边。

两秒后，商非凡在现实世界醒来。

习惯性地活动活动身体，商非凡感觉自己的身体越来越灵活。

这两个月，他自感自己的力气都比以前大了一些。

研究所那边派人过来仔细研究了他和伏向军的游戏头盔，但什么都没有查出来。

制作游戏头盔的材质不算特别，最特别的就是密密麻麻的芯片层。

但那些感触芯片被焊接在头盔内侧，还被弄成了一个整体，对于该技术，研究人员束手无策，推断只要拆解一个芯片就会毁坏整个芯片层。

因为游戏资格太难申请到，别看至今为止已经放出五批账号，但所有账号加起来只有一万五千个。

这还不是针对一个地区释放出的账号，而是全球。

一万五对七十亿，这概率得多低？

而且游戏商已经在论坛放出话，一旦游戏头盔被人为损毁，就不会再做补充。也就是说和那个游戏头盔绑定的游戏账号会跟着废掉。

商非凡和伏向军两人都不愿意牺牲自己的账号，上面综合考虑后，也觉得先保留账号更好。想要拆解头盔，只能等他们申请到更多游戏账号。

商非凡在农场里忙活了半个上午，身上带着牲畜的臭味回到主屋。他现在看起来就是一个特别英俊的农场主。

伏向军拿着手机探出头：“两个消息。”

“说。”商非凡换掉长筒胶靴，脱掉外衣挂在门口走廊上。

“第一个消息，上面有人让我问你，有没有兴趣接手一家兵工厂，不在国内，在……”伏向军说了一个地点代号，“该工厂手续齐全，因为老板经营不善准备转手。”

“经营不善？”商非凡露出嘲讽的笑。

伏向军耸肩：“是被人瞄上了，那家伙仇家太多，自己又没能耐，在当地的靠山被人暗杀，他不跑就只能等死。”

“上面为什么要找我？他们自己没有人接手？”商非凡再次重申：“我退役了。”

伏向军：“知道你退役，你不退役，上面还不会找你。上面要求就是希望看起来和国内没有任何关系，并在国外已经拥有自己人脉网络和一定势力，但又身家清白，不会让国际刑警注意的商业成功人士，你正好符合所有条件。你还和那边上上下下的关系都很好，还持有那边的合法护照。”

伏向军看出商非凡兴趣不大，补充：“条件是国内出钱出技术包括材料，只要你能帮助出货和维持当地关系。不过你从此在明面上就再也不能回国，一旦出事，你也得自己兜底。好处就是这是无本买卖。”

“所以这个兵工厂就是一个加工厂和代销点，我们差不多就是一个代销商？”商非凡懒懒地。

“没错。”伏向军打了个响指。

商非凡瞥向老伙计：“你看起来很有兴趣？”

伏向军承认：“这事能赚钱，能赚大钱。我不知道你手上具体有多少资金，但如果能再多赚一些，为什么不赚？我们还年轻，就算再做个十年再退休也还是年轻人。”

“你只看到赚钱，没看到风险吗？”

“做什么事没有风险？我们办农场一样有很大的风险，辛苦还赚不到什么钱。”

商非凡没说话，他搞个农场就是用来养老休闲，就没想过赚钱。他前面十来年赚的钱已经足够这个农场就算年年赔本也能让他舒舒服服地过两辈子。

伏向军蹲到走廊上，也不知道在跟谁发消息，两个拇指动的飞快。

“上面会找我跟你递话，也是看中你的能力。毕竟至今为止，上面派出去的人能在十几年内就给自己赚出一个大农场还能在各国拥有房子，且银行存款未知，更能完成上面派下的全部任务的人，也只有你了。哦，你还完好活到现在，并没有暴露身份。”
chunks.englishText:
The manager guessed whether that distinguished guest might have just gone out on a quiet errand, so he didn't immediately go to check.

By evening, when a servant went to deliver meals again, he found that the food sent in the morning and at noon was still sitting untouched on the table.

When the manager received the report, he thought of the courier beastman from yesterday and felt a lingering sense of unease in his heart. Finally, he brought some people over to inspect the situation.

The distinguished guest, Lucien, was not in the small courtyard where he stayed; his figure was nowhere to be found.

By the next day, this person still hadn't shown up.

The manager had no choice but to report the matter to the head steward.

The head steward brought people to check once more and discovered that the distinguished guest's clothes for washing and other basic belongings were still there, but some of his valuables seemed to have vanished, including his money pouch.

Had the distinguished guest left on his own, or had something happened to him?

Finding no clues left behind in the small courtyard, the head steward had no choice but to report the matter to the master of the baron's estate.

Baron Zhipang raised an eyebrow. It was impossible for Lucien to leave without telling him.

"How long has he been missing?"

"Two days and two nights," the head steward replied with lowered head.

"Before he disappeared, who did he see?"

"A courier beastman."

"A courier?"

"The thing is, on the afternoon two days ago, a courier delivered a package with the words 'To be opened personally by the sorcerer' written on it..."

After listening to the account, Baron Zhipang pondered for a moment: "Go investigate that courier. Find him and bring him back."

"Yes."

Time rewound to two days ago.

The tall beastman returned to the post office, found the staff member on duty, and returned the tricycle and uniform.

"You're quitting after working just half a day?" The staff member was astonished, as well as a bit exasperated and annoyed.

The tall beastman said excitedly, "I had great luck today. While delivering a package, I met a noble benefactor who told me to follow him from now on, and he'll pay me a hundred silver coins a month!"

"Whoa! You're so lucky." The on-duty beastman grew envious. One hundred silver coins! Even their bureau director didn't make that much in a month.

The tall beastman was too overjoyed. The on-duty beastman told him to come back in five days to collect his deposit from the manager in charge—provided no one complained within those five days. With a wave of his hand, he dashed off.

The tall beastman left the post office, turned and twisted through several alleys, and by the time he emerged from one of them, his clothes, shoes, and socks had all been replaced, and his appearance had changed completely.

When Shang Feifan returned to the inn, Adai had already fallen asleep waiting, but bolted upright at the slightest sound.

"Have you eaten?" Shang Feifan ruffled the little cub's head.

Adai pointed to the dry rations and water on the table.

Shang Feifan: "I've wronged you today; I'll take you out for something good tomorrow."

"Dad, what did you go do? You look a little happy, but also a little unhappy," Adai asked, tilting his head up.

Shang Feifan walked toward the bathroom: "Went to clear up some doubts and figure out a few things. Plus, I made some unexpected wealth."

Adai hit the nail on the head: "Dad, did you rob the robbers?"

During the two months of their journey, they had encountered robbers several times. When they couldn't beat them, they figured out a way to run. When they could beat them, Old Shang would turn the tables and rob the robbers right back, with a smoothness and efficiency that made him more professional than professional robbers.

"The investment was a bit large, so I just had to find a way to break even and add a little interest. Besides, passively taking beatings is not our beastman virtue." Shang Feifan leisurely pulled the bathroom door shut.

Adai tilted his head in confusion.

As for Lord Zhen—if only he could speak the beastman language, otherwise he definitely would have said: *It's over, this child has been taught all wrong.*

That night, Shang Feifan lay down on the inn bed and fell peacefully asleep.

Adai curled up right beside him.

Two seconds later, Shang Feifan woke up in the real world.

Out of habit, he stretched and moved his limbs, feeling that his body was becoming more and more agile and flexible.

Over the past two months, he could sense that his physical strength had grown even greater than before.

The research institute had sent people over to carefully examine both his and Fu Xiangjun's gaming helmets, but nothing unusual was discovered.

The material used to make the gaming helmets was not particularly special; what stood out the most were the dense layers of microchips.

However, those sensory chips were welded to the inside of the helmet and fused into a single integrated unit. The researchers were completely helpless against this technology, deducing that trying to dismantle even a single chip would destroy the entire chip layer.

Because gaming qualifications were so difficult to apply for, even though five batches of accounts had been released so far, all accounts combined totaled only fifteen thousand.

This wasn't just for a single region either, but globally.

Fifteen thousand against seven billion—just how low was that probability?

Moreover, the game developers had already released a statement on the forum that once a gaming helmet was artificially damaged, no replacements would be issued. In other words, the gaming account bound to that helmet would be permanently scrapped.

Neither Shang Feifan nor Fu Xiangjun was willing to sacrifice their accounts. After comprehensive consideration from the higher-ups, it was also deemed better to preserve the accounts first. If they wanted to dismantle a helmet, they would just have to wait until they could secure more gaming accounts.

Shang Feifan had been busy around the farm all morning, returning to the main house reeking of livestock. Right now, he looked precisely like an exceptionally handsome rancher.

Fu Xiangjun poked his head out while holding his phone: "Two pieces of news."

"Speak." Shang Feifan changed out of his tall rubber boots, took off his outer garment, and hung it on the hallway wall by the entrance.

"First piece of news: someone from the higher-ups had me ask you if you'd be interested in taking over an arms factory. It's not in the country, it's located in..." Fu Xiangjun stated a location code name. "The factory has complete paperwork, but the owner is transferring it due to poor management."

"Poor management?" Shang Feifan let out a mocking laugh.

Fu Xiangjun shrugged: "He was targeted. The guy has too many enemies, and since he lacks ability himself, his local backer was assassinated. If he doesn't run, all he can do is wait for death."

"Why are the higher-ups looking for me? Don't they have their own people to take it over?" Shang Feifan reiterated once more: "I've retired."

Fu Xiangjun: "They know you've retired. If you hadn't retired, the higher-ups wouldn't even be looking for you. What they want is a successful businessman who looks completely unrelated to the domestic side, already possesses his own networking and a certain sphere of influence abroad, yet has a clean background that won't attract the attention of Interpol. You fit every single condition perfectly. You also have great relations with everyone up and down the chain over there, and you hold a valid local passport."

Seeing that Shang Feifan wasn't very interested, Fu Xiangjun added: "The condition is that the domestic side provides the funding, technology, and materials, as long as you can help with shipping and maintaining local relations. However, from then on, you can never return to the country openly, and if something goes wrong, you'll have to handle the fallout yourself. The benefit is that this is a zero-capital venture."

"So this arms factory is just a processing plant and distribution outlet, and we're basically acting as sales agents?" Shang Feifan asked lazily.

"Spot on." Fu Xiangjun snapped his fingers.

Shang Feifan cast a glance at his old partner: "You look awfully interested?"
