第52章 打架和解决

院子里吵吵囔囔，帮工的兽人们敢怒不敢言，他们只是来打零工，还不至于为老板拼命，而来闹事的人一看就是职业混子，就是专门来找麻烦的，当地人一般都不敢招惹他们。

闹事的混子嘴里骂着难听的脏话，鼻子里闻着诱人的香气，伸手就去抓货架上的小面包。

艹！真他么好吃。怪不得一份食谱能卖二十银。

想到那些排队买食谱的兽人数量，混子们馋得眼睛发红，如果他们能拥有这张配方，如果他们能拥有更多配方……！

砰！

“嗷——！”

一只正在抓小面包的爪子被击中。

混子兽人发出惨叫。

“来捣乱的就是你们？”商非凡手持擀面杖点了点闯进院子的混混们。

高大的身材一夫当关，杀气腾腾。

尤其对方那架势那神情，感觉比真流氓还要流氓。

“泥马X！你竟然敢打人？”被打的兽人眼睛赤红地要冲过来，被同伙拉住。

“我们是来检查你们有没有行商资格！你们开店得到允许了吗？税钱和保护费交了吗？”一名混混大声喊。

虎不帅负责食谱订购的事，这时候也过来了。

“我已经通知治安官，巡逻队一会儿就能赶到。”虎不帅放声说。

“切！”混混们不屑，好几个人脸上都露出讥笑。

虎不帅心下一沉，看来这些混混并不是自作主张来打秋风，他们很可能得了某些人授意。

虎不帅怀疑是不是自己的身份给商非凡惹来麻烦。

商非凡手一伸，把虎不帅扯到自己身后，同时示意所有帮工兽人后退。

“跟这些混子没什么好说的。对付这种人，就是要把他们打趴下，打到怕，打到他们以后再也不敢来。”

混混们恼恨，纷纷破口大骂，当头目的手一挥：“给我砸！砸完了再说话。”

虎不帅眉眼变冷，伸手按住腰间。

但他还没来得及动手，商非凡已经先一步冲了过去。

他打架不喜欢废话。

噼里啪啦，兵兵乓乓！

院子里一片混乱，混子们被打得吱哇乱叫，有人想要变身抵抗也被捶得断腿断爪。

商非凡的擀面杖落到谁身上，地上就得躺一个。

这个兽人的速度怎么能这么快？

他的力气怎么能这么大？

他打人真的好疼！

砰！

“嗷呜！”正要变身的混混头目捂住自己的头脸，他的鼻梁被打断了，鲜血狂流。

又是一棍，落到他的大腿上，生生把他的大腿打断。

混混头目倒在地上一手捂脸一手捂腿大声惨叫。

虎不帅愣住，放在腰间的手缓缓放下，这才多一会儿，来捣乱的混混就全都躺下了？

原来商非凡的武力值这么高的吗？

虽然他第一次看到商非凡就知道这人不好惹，但真的看到他出手，还是充满了震撼感。

来帮工的兽人们更是看直了眼，随后他们就用火热的目光看向商非凡。

兽人们最为慕强，哪怕是大繁华纪时期，兽人世界施行的仍旧是强者为尊，只不过那时候有法律束缚，强者不会随便对他人动手。

商非凡提起一个混混，伸手就把他身上的钱袋摸出来，扔向虎不帅。

虎不帅迅速接住，脸上打出问号。

“赔偿。他们把院子弄得这么乱，还吃了我们不少小面包，更打坏不少东西，怎么能不赔偿？”

商非凡把这个搜刮完的混混丢出院子，走向第二个混混。

虎不帅：“……”怎么感觉这个人做得特别顺手？

阿呆突然蹿出来，跳到那些倒地的混混身上，用小爪子挨个搜索这些混混，发现钱袋就拖出来交给老商，没有钱袋就用其他值钱的东西抵偿，比如武器和配饰之类。

商非凡拍拍他的方脑袋，夸奖。

阿呆喜滋滋。

虎不帅：“……”

外面排队等着买小面包和食谱的兽人看到混混们闯进院子，听到院子里传来叫嚣和谩骂声，也听到里面貌似打架的声音。

但还不等兽人众同情这位倒霉的厨艺世家传人，就看到敞开的院门里扔出来一个又一个兽人。

嘭！啪！

这些被扔出来的混混趴在地上，爬都爬不起来，一个个不是满脸血，就是捂住肢体惨嚎，看起来特别惨。

商非凡提着擀面杖从院子里走出来，他也没说话，只是冲看热闹的人群笑了笑。

然后走到那些被扔出来的兽人面前，放下擀面杖，提起这些兽人的脸，挥起拳头把他们挨个揍得鼻青脸肿妈都不识。

这、这么凶残的吗？

打断腿还要再揍一遍？

混混们被揍得不断惨叫，还开始求饶，一个劲说自己错了，以后再也不敢来了。

人群先是一片安静，随后一片叫好声。

摩罗城的人谁不恨这些不事生产专门找普通居民麻烦，对老人小孩都能敲诈勒索的混子！

但这些混子背后有人罩着，他们面对巡逻城卫和治安官都能嬉皮笑脸，只要不闹出人命，他们顶多被带进治安拘留室关上几天，过几天又能大摇大摆地出来，还会变本加厉地报复那些报案的人。

摩罗城的居民们简直恨透了他们。

偏偏这些混子找他们麻烦没什么事，他们如果对这些混混下狠手，就会被这些混混反告伤人。闹到最后，受害者不但精疲力尽，还得摊上官司，不但有坐牢的危险，还得赔钱给那些混混。真的是要有多憋屈就有多憋屈！

现在看到那商厨把那些混混打得屁滚尿流，一个比一个惨，心里都要高兴疯了，全都在心里喊打得好。

有那脾气暴躁性子直的，直接就喊出声来。

比较忠厚和爱操心的兽人则对商非凡喊道：“兄弟，这些人背后都有人，你们要小心。等会儿治安官和巡逻队来了，他们说不定反而会抓你们。你们看你们有没有认识什么大人物，最好请他打个招呼。”

商非凡丢下最后一个求饶的混混，随便撕了混混的衣服擦擦手上血迹，捡起放在地上的擀面杖，对吱声的兽人道谢。

“我知道了，谢谢。”

商非凡随即就表示生意继续，想买的可以继续买，他们不会关门。

不少怕事的兽人离开了。

胆大的兽人不少，胆小的兽人更多，这跟他们的种族天性有莫大关系。

鸟类兽人停驻在附近的围墙和屋顶上，把这一幕幕全都看在眼里，好几只鸟兽人拍翅离开，他们就是天生的斥候和信息传递者。

也是因为有这些鸟兽人，商非凡的生意才会在一天之内就传遍全城。

治安官和巡逻队来了。

他们一来就要驱散排队买小面包和食谱的兽人。

兽人们不敢得罪他们，只能骂骂咧咧地散开，但有些胆大的人并没有走远，留在附近探头看这件事的后续。

混混头目趴在地上，爬向治安官，哭喊着让治安官为他们做主，说他们只是来帮忙检查这一户的行商资格，就被这户不明来历的外来商人给打了。
chunks.englishText:
CHINESE SOURCE TEXT (第52章 打架和解决 (Part 1)):
"""
第52章 打架和解决

The courtyard was noisy and chaotic. The beastmen helping out were full of anger but dared not speak out; they were only here for odd jobs and weren't about to risk their lives for the boss. Moreover, the troublemakers looked like professional thugs who came looking for trouble on purpose—locals generally didn't dare provoke them.

Spitting foul curses, the troublemakers caught a whiff of the alluring aroma and reached out to grab the little bread off the shelves.

*Damn it! It really tastes fucking good. No wonder a single recipe can sell for twenty silvers.*

Thinking of the number of beastmen queuing up to buy the recipe, the thugs' eyes turned red with greed. If they could own this recipe, if they could own even more recipes...!

Bang!

"Aah—!"

A claw that was in the midst of snatching a little bread was struck squarely.

The beastman thug let out a miserable shriek.

"So you're the ones here to stir up trouble?" Shang Feifan wielded his rolling pin, pointing it at the thugs who had barged into the courtyard.

His tall figure blocked the path entirely, exuding a murderous aura.

Especially given his posture and expression, he felt even more like a ruffian than the actual ruffians.

"What the fuck! You actually dare hit people?" The beaten beastman's eyes turned bloodshot as he tried to charge forward, only to be grabbed by his accomplices.

"We're here to check if you have your trading qualifications! Did you get permission to open a shop? Have you paid your taxes and protection money?" one of the thugs shouted loudly.

Hu Bushu was in charge of recipe orders, and at this moment, he also walked over.

"I've already notified the magistrate; the patrol squad will be here in a moment," Hu Bushu said aloud.

"Hmph!" The thugs sneered with disdain, several of them wearing mocking grins on their faces.

Hu Bushu's heart sank. It seemed these thugs weren't just acting on their own impulse to shake people down; they had likely been instigated by someone.

Hu Bushu couldn't help but wonder if his own identity had brought trouble to Shang Feifan.

Shang Feifan reached out, pulled Hu Bushu behind him, and signaled all the beastman helpers to step back.

"There's nothing to say to these thugs. Dealing with trash like this means beating them flat, beating them until they're terrified, beating them until they never dare to come back again."

Infuriated, the thugs burst into frantic curses as their leader waved a hand: "Smash the place! Smash everything first, then we'll talk."

Hu Bushu's eyes turned cold as he reached for his waist.

Before he could make a move, however, Shang Feifan had already charged out ahead of him.

He didn't like wasting words when fighting.

*Crack, snap, bang, crash!*

The courtyard descended into utter chaos. The thugs were beaten into shrieking wails; those who tried to transform and resist had their limbs and paws snapped right off.

Whichever thug Shang Feifan's rolling pin landed on, another body hit the ground.

*How can this beastman move so fast?*

*How can his strength be so monstrous?*

*His beatings really hurt!*

Bang!

"Awoo!" The thug leader, who was about to transform, clutched his head and face. His nasal bone was shattered, and fresh blood poured profusely.

Another strike fell squarely on his thigh, cleanly snapping the bone.

The thug leader collapsed to the ground, clutching his face with one hand and his thigh with the other, wailing miserably.

Hu Bushu froze. He slowly lowered the hand resting on his waist. *In just this short span of time, the troublemaking thugs have all been laid out flat?*

*Was Shang Feifan's combat power actually this high?*

Even though he knew this guy wasn't someone to be trifled with the moment they met, actually seeing him strike in person was still full of shock.

The beastman helpers stared with wide-open eyes, their gazes instantly turning burning hot as they looked at Shang Feifan.

Beastmen worshipped the strong above all else. Even in the Great Prosperous Era, the beastman world still operated on the law of the jungle—the strong were supreme; it was just that back then, laws restrained them, so the strong wouldn't arbitrarily attack others.

Shang Feifan hoisted up a thug, fished the money pouch right off his body, and tossed it to Hu Bushu.

Hu Bushu reflexively caught it, a question mark plastered across his face.

"Compensation. They messed up the courtyard, ate quite a bit of our little bread, and smashed a bunch of things to boot. How could they not pay compensation?"

Shang Feifan tossed the thoroughly plundered thug out of the courtyard and walked toward the second one.

Hu Bushu: "..." *Why does it feel like this guy does this with practiced ease?*

Ah-Dai suddenly darted out, pouncing onto the fallen thugs. With his tiny paws, he searched each thug one by one, dragging out money pouches and handing them to Lao Shang. If a thug didn't have a money pouch, Ah-Dai would accept other valuables as compensation, such as weapons and accessories.

Shang Feifan patted the little fellow's square head in praise.

Ah-Dai was overjoyed.

Hu Bushu: "..."

The beastmen lined up outside waiting to buy little bread and recipes had heard the arrogant shouting and cursing from inside the courtyard, followed by the sounds of what seemed to be a brawl.

However, before they could even pity this down-on-his-luck descendant of a culinary family, one beastman after another was tossed flying right out of the open courtyard gates.

*Thud! Slap!*

These tossed-out thugs sprawled on the ground, unable to even crawl up. Every single one of them was either covered in blood or clutching their limbs in agonizing shrieks, looking utterly wretched.

Shang Feifan walked out of the courtyard holding his rolling pin. He didn't speak; he simply smiled at the crowd of onlookers.

Then, he walked over to the discarded beastmen, dropped his rolling pin, grabbed their faces, and threw punch after punch, beating every single one of them until their faces were so bruised and swollen not even their own mothers could recognize them.

*S-So vicious?*

*He breaks their legs and then beats them all over again?!*

The thugs wailed incessantly under the beating, eventually resorting to frantic pleas for mercy, crying out that they were wrong and would never dare come back again.

The crowd fell silent for a moment before bursting into roaring cheers.

Who in Molo City didn't despise these parasites who produced nothing, specialized in harassing ordinary residents, and extorted old folks and children!

Yet these thugs had backing. Whenever they faced city guards and magistrates, they could flash cheeky smiles; as long as no lives were lost, they would at most be dragged into a detention cell for a few days, only to swagger right back out and exact even worse revenge on those who reported them.

The residents of Molo City utterly detested them to the bone.

Yet these thugs could harass citizens with impunity, whereas if the citizens retaliated with heavy hands, the thugs would turn around and sue them for assault. In the end, the victims would be physically and mentally exhausted while also slapped with a lawsuit, facing not only the risk of prison time but also the requirement to pay compensation to the thugs. It was the most suffocating feeling imaginable!

Now, seeing this Chef Shang beat those thugs until they fled in disarray, each one looking more miserable than the last, their hearts were thrilled to the point of bursting, and they were all shouting *serves them right* in their heads.

Those with short tempers and direct personalities simply shouted it out loud.

The more honest and meddlesome beastmen called out to Shang Feifan, "Brother, these guys have people backing them up. You need to be careful. When the magistrate and patrol squad get here later, they might turn things around and arrest you instead. See if you know any big shots—it's best to have someone make a call."

Shang Feifan dropped the last begging thug, casually tore a piece of the thug's clothes to wipe the blood off his hands, picked up the rolling pin on the ground, and nodded his thanks to the warning beastmen.

"I know. Thank you."

Shang Feifan immediately announced that business would continue—those who wanted to buy could continue lining up, and they wouldn't be closing their doors.

Quite a few timid beastmen took off.

While there were plenty of bold beastmen, there were even more cowardly ones, which had a great deal to do with their biological nature.

Avian beastmen perched on nearby walls and rooftops, taking in every bit of the scene. Several bird-beastmen flapped their wings and flew off—they were the natural scouts and information messengers.

It was precisely because of these avian beastmen that Shang Feifan's business had spread throughout the entire city within a single day.

The magistrate and the patrol squad arrived.

As soon as they stepped foot on the scene, they tried to disperse the beastmen lined up to buy little bread and recipes.

The beastmen didn't dare offend them, so they could only disperse while hurling muted curses, though several daring souls didn't go far, lingering nearby to crane their necks and watch how the aftermath would play out.

The thug leader crawled on the ground toward the magistrate, weeping and crying for justice, claiming that they had merely come to check the trading qualifications of this household when they were assaulted by this foreign merchant of unknown origin.

chunks.chineseText:
治安官和巡逻队看到满地伤的混混们，也脸皮抽搐。心中暗叫：这次的任务麻烦了。这个姓商的厨子兼冒险者一看就不是怕事的。

治安官绷着脸皮，走进院子中，找主事人。

商非凡一脸不耐烦地走过来。

不等治安官质问，就先一步：“你们来得正好。外面那些就是闹事的混混，他们过来威胁勒索我们，进门就打砸抢，一个个比土匪还土匪。我相信你们摩罗城的治安，才打算在这里拍卖食谱，你们赶紧把这些地痞无赖都给抓走！”

治安官噎住，差点立正接令。商非凡的气势太强，压迫得他十分难受。

“外面那些兽人过来干什么，我们自然会调查。但你们把那么多人打伤，却是所有人都看到的事实。现在，你得跟我们走一趟。首先交代清楚你们有没有开店资格，其次交代你们打伤人的经过，还有税务方面……”

商非凡：要不要把这些人也全都揍一遍？但动手的话，拍卖食谱的生意似乎也会完蛋。

要么别卖食谱了，动手抢劫更快……

虎不帅走过来，按住蠢蠢欲动的商非凡的手，对治安官亮出一物。

“这是我的行商资格，这个院子是我租的，这位只是我的合作者，这里的生意方面都由我负责。”

治安官下意识看向虎不帅摊开的手掌，就见这名年轻兽人的手掌心中躺着一枚骨牌。

治安官看到骨牌的颜色，心里就咯噔了一下。

虎国王室为了让国境范围内的大小贵族包括管事人员都能第一时间分辨出王室和贵族的身份，对骨牌颜色有强行规定。

王室的骨牌都是金色。

贵族根据爵位不同，从高到低，骨牌颜色从深紫到浅紫。

普通民众的骨牌都是白色。

除此之外，还有一些其他颜色的骨牌，比如特别调查局调查官的骨牌就是黑色，军队的将官是血红色，职业特殊者则是绿色和蓝色。

虎不帅现在拿出的骨牌就是深蓝色，且深蓝色的骨牌上还有两道金线。

这说明虎不帅的职业必定与王室有关，且身份不低。

治安官非常不想接过这枚骨牌，他觉得烫手，但又不得不接过来查看。

果然，这不是一枚身份骨牌，而是资格骨牌，上面明确刻写着“虎国境内可自由行商”字样，骨牌背面还刻印着虎王的小王印。

可以说只要有这么一枚骨牌，虎不帅在虎国境内任何地方行商都是合法的，他不管做什么买卖开什么店铺都不需要向当地权力者另行申请，就连税收，他都能享有最优惠那档，只要不达到一定数额，都可以免税。

治安官在心中暗骂一声，恭恭敬敬地把骨牌递还给虎不帅。

虽然不知道虎不帅的明确身份，但能得到这种最高等级、由虎王亲自盖印认可的自由行商令牌，足以证明这名年轻兽人的身份地位，最重要的是他得到了虎王喜爱。

虎王大王印和私人用的小王印是什么模样，早就发到各个领地让众兽人牢记。

而敢于冒充虎王王印的傻大胆不能说没有，可敢这么堂而皇之在大城市里拿出来的，九成九不会是骗子。

况且这种王印都有特别的验证方法，作为小小的治安官，他没办法验证，但这座城的主人彘庞男爵有。

治安官几秒之内就想通关窍，也决定了绝不得罪虎不帅的想法。

不管派他过来的人知不知道虎不帅的身份底细，他都决定不掺和在里面，只把这个案子当做最普通的混混闹事案来判。

治安官当着虎不帅和商非凡的面，就转身去和巡逻队队长小声说话。

过了一会儿，治安官走过来：“事情我们已经知道。具体如何处理，我们会报上去。请你们在案子结束前暂时不要离开摩罗城。”

虎不帅点头：“好。”

商非凡：我已经做好战斗准备，就连游戏系统都给我发布了新任务，让我解决这次混混闹事事件，可现在……这算是解决了吗？

叮咚，脑载系统告诉他，这个任务真解决了，他得到了五点贡献点。

加上找到药剂市场投毒案真相得到的奖励，他现在重新结余了22个贡献点。

商非凡看到如此平静的局面，有点小失望。他就差一个借口，可惜……

治安官走出院门在附近找了两辆车子，和巡逻队的人一起动手，把那些瘫在地上的混混们抬上车子，走人。

哀嚎痛苦的混混们惊讶极了：就这样？！他们的伤都白伤了？拜托睁大你们的眼睛看清楚，他们平均每人都至少断了一条腿或一条胳膊，这事怎么能就这么结束？

但治安官和巡逻队长什么话也没说，混混们敢叫，他们就拿治安棍抽他们，抽了几下，就全都老实了。

围观的兽人们也看得一头雾水，感觉就像是雷声大雨点小，不，他们连雨点都没看到。

“我说这商厨底气怎么那么足，不但不把那些混混放心上，还把他们打得满地找牙，原来是背后有靠山！”

“真没看出来，之前他们租下这个院子，就那么点人，我还以为他们是小地方来的小商队。”

“你没见上午有炼药师来捧场，来了可不止一个两个。也就是那谁眼皮子太浅，还没搞清楚游来的是巨鲨还是小鱼，就敢上嘴咬。”

“再等等看吧。”

“等什么？一张价值万金的配方现在就卖二十银，过了这个村可就没这个店了。难道要等到那些贵族插手垄断的时候吗？我去排队。”

“哎？你说的对。等等我，我也去！”

院子里，帮工的兽人迅速把搞乱的院子收拾整齐。

商非凡看看天色，眼看就要到傍晚，外面排队的人也散得差不多，就让收拾完的帮工先回家，等明天早上再来。

那些掉落到地上的小面包不可能再拿出去卖，商非凡也不打算自己吃。

倒是那些帮工舍不得扔掉那些只是滚到地上的小面包，商非凡大手一挥，允许那些帮工带回去。

帮工们高兴坏了，平分了那些其实没什么大碍的小面包，都打算带回去让家人尝尝。

等帮工们离开，商非凡这才转头看向虎不帅，伸手，捧住虎不帅的脸，左看右看。

虎不帅挣扎：干嘛？

“你刚才很帅。”商非凡觉得自己心脏被击中。刚才按住他、为他出头的不帅特别有男友力！

虎不帅满头问号：他刚才哪里帅？这人眼睛没问题吧？

商非凡看虎不帅，怎么看怎么好。

忍住吧嗒人脸蛋的强烈冲动，老商松开手，抬手揉了揉虎不帅的头发。

虎不帅：“……我离开时，考虑到今后，就跟虎王求了这么一个自由行商令。”

“未雨绸缪，很聪明。”商非凡真心夸赞。

虎不帅听到一个熟悉的但兽人世界没有的成语，在心里笑了下。

“我们现在还不适合和摩罗城的各方势力对上。毕竟你的初衷只是想要利用手中食谱赚点快钱，那我们也没必要在摩罗城惹事。”

虎不帅又轻声说：“我们只有两个人，你还带着一个小幼崽。”
chunks.englishText:
When the sheriff and the patrol officers saw the thugs lying scattered across the ground in groaning heaps, their faces twitched uncontrollably. They cursed in their hearts—*this assignment just became a massive headache.* The cook-cum-adventurer named Shang was clearly not someone who feared trouble.

With a rigid face, the sheriff strode into the courtyard to find the person in charge.

Shang Feifan walked over, his face brimming with impatience.

Before the sheriff could even open his mouth to question him, Shang Feifan beat him to it: "You arrived just in time! Those thugs outside came over to harass, threaten, and extort us! The moment they stepped through the door, they started smashing and looting like common bandits. I only decided to hold a recipe auction here because I trusted the public security of Molo City, so hurry up and arrest all these riffraff!"

The sheriff choked on his words, nearly snapping to attention to accept the order. Shang Feifan’s aura was far too domineering, pressing down on him with uncomfortable intensity.

"As for why those beastmen outside came here, we will naturally investigate," the sheriff said, regaining his footing. "However, the fact that you injured so many people was witnessed by everyone present. Right now, you must come with us. First, you need to clarify whether you possess the proper business licensing; second, explain how you inflicted these injuries; and third, address the matter of taxes..."

Shang Feifan mused silently: *Should I just beat these guys up as well? But if I raise my fists now, the recipe auction business will probably go up in smoke.*

*Or maybe I shouldn't bother selling recipes at all—robbing people directly would be so much faster...*

Hu Bushuai stepped forward, placing a steady hand over Shang Feifan's restless wrist to hold him back, before flashing an object at the sheriff.

"This is my merchant permit. I rented this courtyard, and he is merely my business partner. All commercial operations here are my responsibility."

The sheriff instinctively glanced down at Hu Bushuai’s open hand. Resting in the young beastman's palm was a bone token.

The moment the sheriff saw the color of that token, his heart sank.

To allow noble lords and administrative officials across the realm to instantly discern royal and noble identities, the Tiger Kingdom's royal family enforced strict regulations regarding the colors of identity tokens.

Royal bone tokens were always gold.

For nobles, depending on their rank, the tokens ranged from deep purple down to light purple.

Common citizens held white bone tokens.

Aside from these, there were a few special colors. For instance, investigators from the Bureau of Special Investigation carried black tokens, military generals carried blood-red ones, and individuals with specialized occupations carried green or blue tokens.

The token Hu Bushuai held out right now was deep blue—and running through the deep blue surface were two distinct threads of pure gold.

This indicated that Hu Bushuai’s profession was undoubtedly linked to the royal family, and his status was anything but low.

The sheriff desperately wished he didn't have to take the token; it felt like a burning coal in his hands. Yet, he had no choice but to receive it and inspect it closely.

Sure enough, this was not a mere identity token, but a credential token. Explicitly carved upon its surface were the words: *Authorized to Trade Freely Within the Kingdom of Tigers.* On the reverse side was stamped the minor royal seal of the Tiger King himself.

It was no exaggeration to say that with this single token, Hu Bushuai possessed the legal right to trade anywhere within the Tiger Kingdom. Whatever business he conducted or shop he opened, he did not need to seek additional approval from local authorities. Even in terms of taxation, he enjoyed the most favorable rate—remaining entirely tax-exempt below a certain threshold.

The sheriff cursed fiercely in his mind before respectfully handing the bone token back to Hu Bushuai.

Although he did not know Hu Bushuai's exact identity, obtaining a top-grade token of free trade personally stamped and recognized by the Tiger King proved the young beastman's extraordinary background. Most importantly, it proved he enjoyed the royal favor of the Tiger King.

The design of the Tiger King's grand seal and private minor seal had long been distributed to every fiefdom, etched into the minds of every beastman official.

While one couldn't say there were no reckless fools brave enough to forge royal seals, nineties out of a hundred who dared to flaunt such a token so brazenly in a major city were definitely not impostors.

Furthermore, royal seals possessed specialized methods of verification. As a mere sheriff, he lacked the authority or means to verify it, but the master of this city, Baron Zhi Pang, certainly did.

Within seconds, the sheriff figured out the stakes and decided that he would rather die than offend Hu Bushuai.

Regardless of whether the person who sent him here knew about Hu Bushuai’s background, he decided not to get caught in the crossfire. He would handle this strictly as an ordinary case of local thugs causing a disturbance.

Right in front of Hu Bushuai and Shang Feifan, the sheriff turned on his heel and walked over to whisper hushed instructions to the patrol captain.

A moment later, the sheriff returned. "We now understand the situation. As for the specific details of how this will be handled, we will report it to our superiors. Please refrain from leaving Molo City until the case is concluded."

Hu Bushuai nodded. "Very well."

Shang Feifan stood there, mentally bewildered: *I was completely ready for a fight! Even the game system issued a new quest asking me to resolve this thug disturbance... But now? Does this count as resolved?*

*Ding-dong!* 

The brain-hosted system chimed to inform him that the quest had indeed been completed, awarding him 5 contribution points.

Adding that to the reward he had obtained from uncovering the truth behind the potion market poisoning case, his contribution point balance was now back up to 22 points.

Seeing how peacefully everything had ended, Shang Feifan felt a faint pang of disappointment. He had been just one excuse away from a good brawl, but alas...

The sheriff walked out of the courtyard and requisitioned two carts nearby. Working alongside the patrol officers, they heaved the paralyzed, groaning thugs onto the carts and departed.

The wailing thugs were utterly dumbfounded. *That's it?! Are our injuries just going to be ignored?! Open your eyes and look closely, for pity's sake! Every single one of us has at least one broken arm or leg! How could this possibly end like this?!*

Yet neither the sheriff nor the patrol captain offered a single word of explanation. Whenever the thugs dared to cry out, the officers simply lashed them with their batons. After a few strikes, every last one of them fell obediently silent.

The watching crowd of beastmen was equally bewildered. It felt like a massive buildup with zero payoff—in fact, they hadn't even seen a single drop of rain fall.

"I was wondering why that Chef Shang was so full of confidence, paying those thugs no mind at all and beating them till they were spitting teeth! Turns out he has a massive mountain backing him!"

"Who would have guessed? When they first rented this yard with so few people, I honestly thought they were just a small merchant team from some backwater town."

"Didn't you see the alchemists coming over to show support this morning? And it wasn't just one or two! That fool who sent those thugs was just too shortsighted—he couldn't even tell if he was biting a giant shark or a tiny minnow before snapping his jaws."

"Let's wait and see a bit longer."

"Wait for what? A recipe worth ten thousand gold is selling for twenty silver right now! Once this ship sails, there won't be another chance! Are you going to wait until the nobles step in and create a monopoly? I'm going to get in line!"

"Hey! You make a good point! Wait for me, I'm queuing up too!"

Inside the courtyard, the hired beastman helpers quickly tidied up the mess.

Shang Feifan checked the sky and saw that dusk was fast approaching. Since the line outside had mostly dispersed, he let the workers head home early after finishing up, telling them to return the next morning.

The small buns that had fallen onto the ground could no longer be sold, nor did Shang Feifan intend to eat them himself.

However, the hired hands couldn't bear to see buns that had merely rolled on the floor go to waste. Shang Feifan gave a generous wave of his hand, allowing them to take the fallen pastries home.

The workers were overjoyed. They divided up the perfectly edible buns among themselves, eager to let their families taste the treat.

Once the workers had left, Shang Feifan turned to look at Hu Bushuai. He reached out and gently cupped Hu Bushuai’s face in his hands, turning his head left and right to inspect him.

Hu Bushuai wriggled uncomfortably. "What are you doing?"

"You were really cool just now," Shang Feifan said, feeling a sudden fluttering in his chest. The way Hu Bushuai had held him back and stood up for him earlier had radiated pure boyfriend energy!

Hu Bushuai’s head was filled with question marks. *Where was I 'cool'? Is there something wrong with his eyes?*

Yet, as Shang Feifan gazed at Hu Bushuai, the young beastman looked perfect no matter how he viewed him.

Suppressing the strong urge to plant a kiss on the beastman's cheek, Old Shang released his face and reached up to ruffle Hu Bushuai’s soft hair.

Hu Bushuai said, "...When I left, I took future complications into account, which is why I asked the Tiger King for this free trade permit."

"Planning ahead—very clever," Shang Feifan praised sincerely.

Hearing a familiar idiom that didn't exist in the beastman world, Hu Bushuai smiled softly to himself.

"It isn't wise for us to clash directly with the various factions of Molo City right now," Hu Bushuai murmured softly. "After all, your original intention was merely to use the recipes in your hands to make some quick cash. There's no need for us to stir up trouble here."

He added gently, "There are only two of us, and you're carrying a little cub with you."

chunks.chineseText:
商非凡：对于可以不断重生的玩家来说，人数就不是问题。逃跑也不是问题，他死了就可以直接回到天残谷。

不过他现在还不想暴露玩家身份，更不想让虎不帅知道他只是一个外来者，更更不想再花两个月时间从天残谷跑到虎不帅身边。

哦，对了，他还有回城功能！

他之前设定的回城地点就在城外一座小山丘后面。

但他不能只顾自己，他还得考虑到虎不帅，他不可能丢下不帅一个人在敌营。

战意迅速下降的商非凡轻轻推了推虎不帅的背：“去看看那些抄写匠抄写得怎样了，我们该去发配方了。”

以前，老商特别不理解有些人为什么会疯狂迷恋二次元的纸片人，或者养电子宠物都能养得不惜投入。

现在……他只想把虎不帅的数据全部复制下来，不，不要复制，他不想再有一个虎不帅出现，他要全部截取虎不帅的数据，带回现实世界，让他永远陪伴自己。

也许他该在现实世界认真去找找游戏商的服务器地址了。

否则这个游戏突然停游怎么办？
chunks.englishText:
Shang Feifan knew that for players capable of endless rebirth, numbers were no longer an issue. Neither was escaping; the moment he died, he could respawn directly back at the Heavenly Cripple Valley. 

However, he did not want to expose his player identity just yet, nor did he want Hu Bushuai to discover that he was merely an outsider. Above all, he certainly didn't want to waste another two months traveling all the way from the Heavenly Cripple Valley back to Hu Bushuai's side.

Oh, right! He still had the town-recall function!

His previously set recall point was located just behind a small hill outside the city.

Yet, he couldn't just look out for himself—he also had to consider Hu Bushuai. There was no way he could abandon Bushuai all alone in the enemy camp.

With his battle intent rapidly plummeting, Shang Feifan gently nudged Hu Bushuai's back. "Go check and see how those scribes are doing with the copying. It's time for us to go distribute the formulas."

In the past, Lao Shang could never understand why some people would fanatically obsess over 2D paper cutout waifus, or pour countless resources into raising virtual digital pets without a second thought.

Right now... he just wanted to copy all of Hu Bushuai's data—no, scratch that, he didn't want another Hu Bushuai coming into existence. He wanted to intercept all of Hu Bushuai's data completely and take it back to the real world, so that he could keep him company forever.

Perhaps he really ought to seriously track down the game developer's server address in the real world. 

Otherwise, what would he do if this game suddenly shut down its servers?

chunks.chapterTitle: 第53章 分钱、历史、寻宝指引 (Part 1)
chunks.chineseText:
第53章 分钱、历史、寻宝指引

此后直到拍卖会来临的当天，都没有人再上门找事。

就在这四天内，商非凡光是靠卖小面包的配方就卖出了1266份，共计获得25320银达鲁。

商非凡数着满桌钱币，心情愉快，他敢说他现在肯定是玩家中最有钱的一个。

等今天他就联系老伏，把一百银砸到他脸上。

“给，你的分成。”商非凡把一个装满银达鲁的袋子推到虎不帅面前。

虎不帅震惊，连忙拒绝：“不用。这是你赚的，不用分给我。”

商非凡拿起那个钱袋往虎不帅怀里一塞：“如果没有你那个自由行商令，你以为我这份生意能做得这么安稳？你就当收保护费。”

虎不帅哭笑不得，把钱袋还回去：“不用，真的。”

商非凡又丢回去，还往里面又多塞了一大把：“三分之一嫌少是吧，那我分你一半。”

“不是……”

“以后我们还有更多合作机会。你那个自由行商令以及你的身份，对我会有极大帮助。还是你打算这次过后就跟我散伙？”商非凡一脸我就赖上你的无赖脸。

虎不帅非常不擅长应对这种人，他只能把钱袋里的钱倒出大半，收起大约十分之一的分账：“这些就够了。我的身份能给你带来一定便利，但也会带来很多麻烦。”

商非凡把袋子抢过来，把虎不帅倒出来的钱又装回去：“行吧，以后都按照三成的分账分给你。这次你就收一半。你再拒绝，我就把钱撒到大门口。”

虎不帅：“……”

商非凡又抓了十来个银达鲁塞给阿呆，这是他给儿砸的零花钱。

阿呆已经知道金钱的魅力，抱着钱币就想给老商打个滚。

虎不帅好笑，找了一个小号钱袋送给阿呆。

商非凡看虎不帅收下钱袋，这才高兴。他就喜欢给喜欢的人塞钱，他是粗人，觉得什么都没有比给钱更实惠。如果钱财无用，他就给武器给粮食。

把桌上的钱币全都装好，老商把他那一份扔进广场空间。

虎不帅看到偌大的钱袋凭空消失，只眨了眨眼睛，什么都没问。

商非凡又提出一个钱箱，这是卖小面包的零碎钱。

比起配方收益，小面包实物这边差不多就是收支平衡，因为鲜奶和蜜糖都是昂贵货，他们又是买一送一，扣除工钱和房租钱后，基本没赚钱。

“想要这种常见食物价格变得平民化，还是得扩大养殖和生产才行。”商非凡拨弄钱箱里一大堆铜达铢，又抓了一把塞到阿呆的小钱袋里。

虎不帅一边在心里想这就是个会宠坏孩子的爸爸，一边说：“土地、种子、环境、养殖和种植方法，我们首先就卡在最关键的土地和环境上。虫族诅咒不除，兽人大陆的土地就不能完全恢复。”

“那这个所谓的虫族诅咒要怎么去除？”商非凡丢开钱箱，懒得数了。

虎不帅摇头：“我也不知道。有人说需要神血复苏的那天，等到传说中的治愈系或者光明系的神血大祭司出现，也许就能祛除大地中的诅咒。”

“那虫族诅咒又是怎么来的呢？”了解到根源，也许就能从根源下手。

虎不帅现在已经九成认定商非凡就是穿越来的老乡，开始有意无意地给他补充常识：“传说兽人大陆原本是一块非常巨大的、看不到边沿的大陆，当时兽人大陆上生活着兽人族、鸟人族、虫人族、水生族，还有植物人族。

同一个家庭里的亲人都能争斗不休，更不要说是不同种、不同族的外人。

一开始大家为了生存资源争斗，争斗多了，就会累积仇恨。一个部落打不过另一个部落，就会结交别的部落，共同去攻打敌人，如此争斗就变成了战斗，逐渐演化成战争。”

虎不帅上辈子给小朋友当老师，给小孩子说故事说习惯了，现在给商非凡讲述历史，就带出了那么一点给小朋友讲故事的味道。

商非凡很喜欢虎不帅的声音，听得津津有味。

阿呆也坐在一边歪头听讲。

虎不帅揉揉阿呆的方脑袋，“除了喜欢安静的植物人族以及对陆地不是特别感兴趣的水生族，兽人族、鸟人族和虫人族都希望成为兽人大陆的主宰者，他们势力和实力相当，不是今天你压倒我，就是明天我压倒你。有很长一段时间，大家都是轮流当兽人大陆的帝皇。”

“帝皇？”

“对，现在没有帝，只有王。但在很早以前，当整个大陆统一的时候，就有帝皇的存在。兽人们也默认只有统一整个兽人大陆才能称帝。”

“大繁华纪有帝皇吗？”

“没有。大繁华纪是多种族联盟制，只有盟主，没有帝皇。盟主的任期最长只有三十年，每十年选举一次。如果大家不满意盟主，可以在任期内就推翻他并要求改选。”

虎不帅简单说了一些大繁华纪的政府架构，就又回到虫族诅咒的传说上。

“虫人在兽人大陆不太受欢迎，这是因为历史原因。这个历史原因就牵扯到虫族诅咒，但只要研究过历史的人就知道，虫人族也是受害者。

在兽人大陆的中古时期，兽人族和鸟人族联手，共同对付虫人族。虫人族虽然数量众多，但也经不起两大种族联手，尤其鸟人族大多还是虫人族的天敌，很多鸟人族都天生克制虫人族。

虫人族大祭司一怒之下，就对两族施以诅咒，诅咒兽人大陆的土地只能长出野草，可以充当粮食的植物都无法结果。

但这个诅咒也惹怒了不喜欢战争的植物人族。虽然传说中虫人族克制植物人族，但植物人族也有办法让虫人族灭绝。

因为受到三大种族的针对，虫人族无奈之下只能退出兽人大陆，退到海中岛屿上。虫人族大祭司留下的诅咒也被破解。

很可惜这部分的历史缺失了很多，没人知道那个诅咒是怎么破解的。另外，根据宫廷图书馆一些古老书籍记载，虫人族很可能在海的另一边找到了一片新的大陆，并命名为虫人大陆。”

商非凡举手：“这么说这个世界不止兽人大陆，她一共有多少个大陆？”

虎不帅摇头：“不知道。也许在大繁华纪或者之前有强者曾经探索出这个世界到底有多大，以及有多少个大陆，但大战纪摧毁了太多历史记载，更让文明大大倒退。

导致现在的我们也不知道我们生活的这个世界到底有多大，只知道兽人大陆的海洋非常广阔，海中有无数小岛。

但海洋非常危险，除了本身就充满闪电、巨浪和狂风暴雨的危险海域，生活在大海里的海族不喜欢陆生族的大船，会攻击大船和陆生族，也会攻击鸟人族。

这些都导致兽人无法越过海洋找到其他大陆。凡是走出去的兽人和鸟人族都没有回来的。”

商非凡想到游戏系统称这个世界为天河星，会不会土著兽人都不知道他们星球的名字？

虎不帅忽然道：“虫族诅咒并不是虫人族诅咒。”

“嗯？”商非凡没能立刻反应过来。
chunks.englishText:
### Chapter 53: Splitting Profits, Ancient History, and Treasure Map Guidance

From that day on until the day of the auction, no one came looking for trouble again.

Over those four days alone, Shang Feifan managed to sell 1,266 copies of the small bread recipe, earning a grand total of 25,320 silver Dalu.

Counting the table piled high with silver coins, Shang Feifan was in a splendid mood. He dared to say he was currently the wealthiest player in the entire game.

*Later today, I'll contact Old Fu and slap a hundred silver right onto his face!*

"Here, your cut," Shang Feifan said, pushing a heavy pouch stuffed with silver Dalu toward Hu Bushuai.

Hu Bushuai was shocked and quickly waved his hands in refusal. "There's no need. You earned this money yourself, you don't need to share it with me."

Shang Feifan picked up the coin pouch and shoved it firmly into Hu Bushuai’s arms. "If it weren't for your free trade permit, do you think I could have run this business so peacefully? Just think of it as collecting protection money."

Hu Bushuai didn't know whether to laugh or cry as he tried to return the pouch. "No, really, it's fine."

Shang Feifan threw it back, even grabbing a large handful of additional coins and stuffing them inside. "A third is too little for you? Fine, I'll give you half!"

"That's not it..."

"We'll have plenty more opportunities to cooperate in the future. That free trade permit of yours and your status are going to be of massive help to me. Or are you planning to part ways with me after this?" Shang Feifan put on an unabashedly rogue expression that screamed, *I'm sticking to you no matter what.*

Hu Bushuai was utterly terrible at dealing with people like this. In the end, he could only pour out most of the money from the pouch, taking roughly a ten-percent cut. "This is more than enough. My identity can bring you a certain degree of convenience, but it can also bring a lot of trouble."

Shang Feifan snatched the pouch back and shoved all the coins Hu Bushuai had poured out right back inside. "Fine, from now on, everything will be split with a thirty-percent cut for you. But for this time, you take half. If you refuse again, I'm tossing all this money out the front door!"

Hu Bushuai: "..."

Shang Feifan then grabbed a dozen or so silver Dalu and stuffed them into A'Dai's hands—this was pocket money for his little son.

A'Dai had already learned the charm of money. Clutching the coins tightly, he looked ready to do a somersault on the spot for Old Shang.

Amused, Hu Bushuai fished out a smaller coin pouch and handed it to A'Dai as a gift.

Watching Hu Bushuai accept the money pouch at last, Shang Feifan beamed with satisfaction. He simply loved giving money to the people he cared about. He was a practical man; to him, nothing was more genuine than giving cash. If money was useless, he would give weapons or food instead.

After packing up all the coins on the table, Old Shang tossed his own share into his square inventory space.

Seeing the massive pouch of money vanish into thin air, Hu Bushuai merely blinked, asking no questions.

Shang Feifan then pulled out another cash box containing the loose change earned from selling the actual physical bread.

Compared to the lucrative profits from selling recipes, the physical bread side had merely broken even. Fresh milk and honey were expensive commodities, and because they ran a "buy one, get one free" deal, after deducting labor and rent, they barely made a profit.

"If we want the price of everyday food like this to become affordable for ordinary people, we'll still have to expand livestock farming and production," Shang Feifan mused, fiddling with the mountain of copper Dazhu in the box before scooping up another handful to stuff into A'Dai's tiny pouch.

Hu Bushuai thought to himself that this was precisely how doting fathers spoiled their children, but aloud he said, "Land, seeds, environment, livestock breeding, and farming techniques... we're stuck right at the most critical hurdles: the land and the environment. Unless the Zerg Curse is lifted, the soil of the Beastman Continent cannot fully recover."

"Then how do we lift this so-called Zerg Curse?" Shang Feifan pushed the cash box aside, too lazy to keep counting.

Hu Bushuai shook his head. "I don't know either. Some say that on the day divine blood awakens, when a legendary Grand Priest of the Healing or Light attribute possessing divine blood appears, the curse upon the earth might finally be cleansed."

"And where did this Zerg Curse come from in the first place?" Shang Feifan asked. *If I understand the root cause, maybe I can tackle it at the source.*

By now, Hu Bushuai was ninety percent certain that Shang Feifan was a fellow reincarnator from his old world. Intentionally or otherwise, he began filling in his common knowledge: "Legend has it that the Beastman Continent was originally a colossal landmass with no visible boundaries. At that time, the continent was inhabited by the Beastman Clan, Avian Clan, Insectoid Clan, Aquatic Clan, and Plant-folk Clan.

"Even family members sharing the same bloodline fight endlessly among themselves, to say nothing of different races and species.

"In the beginning, everyone fought over survival resources. As conflicts accumulated, deep hatred took root. When one tribe couldn't defeat another, it would ally with neighboring tribes to attack their common enemy. Thus, skirmishes escalated into battles, and battles gradually evolved into full-scale war."

Having spent his past life as a school teacher accustomed to telling stories to young children, Hu Bushuai's tone as he recounted history carried a gentle, narrative charm.

Shang Feifan thoroughly enjoyed the sound of Hu Bushuai’s voice, listening with rapt attention.

A'Dai sat beside them as well, tilting his blocky head as he listened intently.

Hu Bushuai patted A'Dai's square head and continued, "Aside from the peace-loving Plant-folk Clan and the Aquatic Clan, who weren't particularly interested in the mainland, the Beastmen, Avians, and Insectoids all strived to become the absolute rulers of the Beastman Continent. Their power and foundation were evenly matched—one day one race would dominate, and the next day another would take the lead. For a long period in history, the various races took turns ruling as emperors of the Beastman Continent."

"Emperors?"

"Yes. Nowadays, there are no emperors, only kings. But long ago, when the entire continent was unified, supreme emperors existed. The beastmen still implicitly hold that one can only claim the title of Emperor if they unify the entire Beastman Continent."

"Were there emperors during the Era of Great Flourishing?"

"No. The Era of Great Flourishing operated under a multi-racial alliance system. There were only Alliance Leaders, not emperors. An Alliance Leader could serve a maximum term of thirty years, with elections held every ten years. If the people were dissatisfied with an Alliance Leader, they could overthrow him during his term and demand a re-election."

Hu Bushuai briefly explained the governmental structure of the Era of Great Flourishing before returning to the legend of the Zerg Curse.

"The Insectoids are not particularly popular on the Beastman Continent, and that stems from historical reasons. This history is intertwined with the Zerg Curse, but anyone who has studied history knows that the Insectoid Clan was also a victim.

"During the Middle Antiquity Period of the Beastman Continent, the Beastman Clan and Avian Clan joined forces to wage war against the Insectoid Clan. Although the Insectoids were vast in numbers, they could not withstand the combined might of two major races—especially since most Avians were natural predators of the Insectoids, possessing inherent advantages over them.

"In a fit of fury, the Grand Priest of the Insectoid Clan laid a devastating curse upon both races: the soil of the Beastman Continent would grow nothing but wild weeds, and any plants capable of yielding food would fail to bear fruit.

"However, this curse also angered the Plant-folk Clan, who detested war. Although legend claims the Insectoids countered the Plant-folk, the Plant-folk possessed their own means to drive the Insectoids to extinction.

"Targeted by three major races at once, the Insectoid Clan had no choice but to retreat from the Beastman Continent, withdrawing to islands far out at sea. The curse left behind by their Grand Priest was eventually broken as well.

"Unfortunately, much of that historical record has been lost. No one knows how the curse was originally broken. Furthermore, according to ancient books preserved in the royal library, it is highly probable that the Insectoid Clan discovered a new continent on the other side of the ocean and named it the Insectoid Continent."

Shang Feifan raised his hand. "So you're saying there's more than just the Beastman Continent in this world? How many continents are there in total?"

Hu Bushuai shook his head. "I don't know. Perhaps during the Era of Great Flourishing or even earlier, powerful experts explored the true scale of this world and mapped its continents. But the Era of Great Warfare destroyed far too many historical records and caused civilization to regress tremendously.

"As a result, none of us today know how vast our world truly is. We only know that the ocean surrounding the Beastman Continent is immensely vast, scattered with countless islands.

"Yet the ocean is exceedingly dangerous. Beyond the hazards of lightning, giant waves, and raging tempests, the Sea Clan inhabiting the depths detests the massive ships of land-dwellers. They attack surface vessels and land-dwellers, and they attack the Avian Clan as well.

"Because of this, no beastman has ever been able to cross the ocean to find other continents. Any beastman or avian who ventured deep into the sea has never returned."

Shang Feifan recalled that the game system referred to this planet as "Tianhe Star." *Do the native beastmen not even know the true name of their own planet?*

Suddenly, Hu Bushuai spoke up: "The Zerg Curse is not an Insectoid Curse."

"Hmm?" Shang Feifan couldn't immediately process his words.
